  • --skip <index>, --unskip <index>: Controls stages by runtime stage index; the index is based on what is displayed in status/hmcheck_list.
  • --no-write <path ...>: Prohibits writing to existing files or directories within the workspace; wildcard paths can be used for non-existent targets. See Parameter Description for security restrictions.

docs.title: 4. Common Actions in the TUI
docs.text:
status
current_tips
loop

When a stage fails, first check the specific files and next steps returned by the Checker, then fix them and invoke:

tool_invoke Check
tool_invoke Complete

If the check process has no output:

tool_invoke StdCheck lines=-1
tool_invoke KillCheck

For a complete command reference, see Human-Machine Collaborative Verification and TUI.

docs.title: 5. Artifacts and Next Steps
docs.text:
Default artifacts are located in <workspace>/unity_test/, and toffee-test reports (if tests have been run) are located in <workspace>/uc_test_report/. The workflow determines the specific documentation and test file names; do not assume that Bug, waveform, or coverage files will necessarily be generated.

  • To involve an external Code Agent: Read MCP Integration.
  • To centrally manage multiple tasks: Read Master Mode.
  • To modify stages, tools, or Checkers: Start with Custom Development Quick Start.

docs.title: Human-in-the-Loop Verification
docs.text: UCAgent allows pausing during stage execution, testing, or Checker failure, enabling manual repair of files or the environment before allowing the Agent to continue. Normal mode and MCP mode use the same set of PDB commands; Master mode places common operations on the Web page.

docs.title: 1. When to Intervene
docs.text:
Situations suitable for human intervention include:

  • Specifications, feature points, or test plans require human confirmation;
  • Test environment, dependencies, or simulator configuration need modification;
  • Checker failure information is clear, but the model has not fixed the issue;
  • The check process times out, requiring log inspection and termination before retrying.

A test failure itself does not equal a DUT defect. First, confirm that the fixture, reference model, API, reset/timing, and assertions are correct, then decide whether to record a Bug.

docs.title: 2. Pausing and Checking Status
docs.text:
When using LangChain direct connection, press Ctrl+C to pause; for external Code Agents, pause according to their client operations. After returning to the UCAgent console, the common commands are:

status
current_tips
task_detail
changed_files

status displays stage progress, current_tips displays the current stage task and Checker requirements, task_detail views stage details, and changed_files views recent modifications.

docs.title: 3. Checking, Fixing, and Continuing
docs.text:
1. Read the artifact, location, expected, and next_action returned by Check.
  2. Manually edit files or fix the environment, running a single pytest case if necessary.
  3. Re-check:
tool_invoke Check
  1. After the check passes, record the work for this stage, then proceed:
tool_invoke SetCurrentStageJournal journal='Fixed fixture, related tests and Check all passed'
tool_invoke Complete

Complete requires that the current stage already has a log; if prompted that reference files are unread, use ReadTextFile to read the listed files first. If human review is required, confirm according to the next section and then call Complete again.

  1. Continue the Agent loop:
loop
loop Fixed fixture, please re-run failed cases and complete the current stage

If Check has no output for a long time:

tool_invoke StdCheck lines=-1
tool_invoke KillCheck
tool_invoke Check

StdCheck and KillCheck target only the running check process; check the output first, then decide whether to terminate.

docs.title: 4. Forced Human Review
docs.text:
You can make a stage wait for human confirmation after the Checker passes:

hmcheck_set 2 true
hmcheck_set all true
hmcheck_set 2 false
hmcheck_cstat
hmcheck_list

The stage index is the flattened index of the current runtime; do not directly apply the numbering from another configuration. Use the index displayed by status or hmcheck_list as the reference.

After pausing, confirm the artifacts and test results, then approve or reject the review:

hmcheck_pass Checked specifications and test coverage
hmcheck_fail Need to add boundary cases

You can also approve the review and continue in one step:

hmcheck_pass_and_continue Confirmed

HM is the human review switch. LFail/LPass on the Web page are LLM failure suggestion and pass review switches, which are not the same function as the human confirmation of hmcheck_pass/hmcheck_fail.

docs.title: 5. Permissions and Stage Control
docs.text:
View or adjust Agent writable paths:

list_rw_paths
add_write_path unity_test/
add_un_write_path Adder/
del_write_path unity_test/
del_un_write_path Adder/

Workflow stage control:

skip_stage 3
unskip_stage 3
tool_invoke GoToStage 2

skip_stage, unskip_stage, and GoToStage all use stage indices; GoToStage can only return to stages already reached. When starting from the command line, you can also use --skip, --unskip, and --force-stage-index; see Parameter Description for details.

docs.title: 6. Common Commands Table
docs.text:
Command Function Example status View overall status status task_detail View stage details task_detail 2 current_tips Get current stage guidance current_tips tool_list List available tools tool_list tool_invoke Invoke tool in PDB tool_invoke RunTestCases target='',timeout=120 hmcheck_set Set human review hmcheck_set 2 true hmcheck_pass / hmcheck_fail Pass or reject human review hmcheck_pass Confirmed skip_stage / unskip_stage Skip or restore stage skip_stage 3 loop Continue model loop loop help View current version commands help quit Exit process quit

Entering q, exit, or quit in the TUI first returns to the PDB console; you must enter quit again to terminate the process.

The parameter format for tool_invoke is:

tool_invoke <tool_name> [arg1,arg2,key=value,...]

Parameters are separated by commas, strings use Python quotes, and boolean values use True/False. RunTestCases.target is relative to the current test directory (default unity_test/tests/); do not add the directory prefix again. For example:

tool_invoke RunTestCases target='test_adder.py::test_add',timeout=120

docs.title: 7. Master Page
docs.text:
The Dashboard, Task, and Agent pages of Master allow viewing logs, stage files, and Diffs, and batch setting HM, Skip, LFail, and LPass. Page operations are similar to local commands in function, but the entry point and permissions are determined by Master configuration; see Web Master User Guide for details.

Whether the Web Terminal retains the local terminal simultaneously depends on whether the sub-Agent uses --web-console or --web-terminal; see Parameter Description for the differences.

docs.title: 8. Recovery Principles
docs.text: UCAgent saves stage history in the workspace. After the process exits, ensure that the old UCAgent and Code Agent have stopped, then restart with the same workspace, DUT, and configuration. After startup, first execute status to confirm the current stage and history, then enter loop or let the external Agent continue. Do not directly delete .ucagent/, test reports, or workflow artifacts for the sake of "recovery".

docs.title: Parameters and Options
docs.text:
The usage of UCAgent is:

ucagent <workspace> <dut_name> [options]

docs.title: Input and Output
docs.text:
• workspace: The working directory. workspace/<DUT_DIR> should be the DUT Python package directory exported by the picker, containing the README and source files required for verification; for example, workspace/Adder/.
    • workspace/<DUT_DIR>/README.md: DUT verification requirements and objectives
    • workspace/<DUT_DIR>/*.md: Other reference files
    • workspace/<DUT_DIR>/*.{v,sv,scala}: Source files used for Bug analysis
    • Other files related to verification (e.g., provided test instances, requirement specifications, etc.)
  • dut_name: The name of the Design Under Test, i.e., , for example: Adder

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• The workflow prepares Guide_Doc/ in the workspace and generates <output>/tests/, documentation, and test reports by stage; uc_test_report/ will only appear after the corresponding tests are actually executed. The default <output> is unity_test.

For a detailed explanation of the output, refer to Result Analysis and Process Summary

docs.title: Positional Arguments
docs.text: Parameter Required Description Example workspace Required for normal tasks Working directory; can also be a local .tar.gz or HTTP(S) archive URL ./output dut Required for normal tasks DUT name (subdirectory name under the working directory); not required for entry points like information queries Adder

docs.title: Execution and Interaction
docs.text:
Option Short Value/Type Default Description --stream-output -s flag Off Stream output to the console --human -hm flag Off Enter manual input/breakpoint mode at startup --interaction-mode -im standard/enhanced/advanced standard Interaction mode; enhanced includes planning and memory management, advanced includes adaptive strategies --tui flag Off Enable terminal TUI interface --web-console [host[:port]] [password] Off Enable browser Web UI (standalone mode). Default localhost:8000. Note: Provides only the Web interface, not local command-line interaction --web-terminal [host[:port]] [password] Off Start Web Terminal server. Default 127.0.0.1:8818. Provides both Web terminal and local command-line interaction --loop -l flag Off Enter the main loop immediately after startup (can be used with --loop-msg) --loop-msg str Empty The first message injected when entering the loop --seed int Random Random seed (automatically random if not specified) --sys-tips str Empty Override system prompt --icmd str (repeatable) [] Initial commands to execute at startup, can be used multiple times --no-history flag Off Disable loading history from the working directory --exit-on-completion -eoc flag Off Automatically exit the agent after task completion (after successful Exit tool call)

--web-console provides a standalone Web session; --web-terminal can be used simultaneously with the local terminal. For example:

ucagent --web-console '127.0.0.1:8000 mysecret'
ucagent ./output Adder --web-terminal '127.0.0.1:8818 mysecret'

See Web Master User Guide for the Master's Dashboard, Launch, Task, and Agent pages.

docs.title: Configuration and Templates
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --workspace-base path /tmp/ucagent_workspace_base Base directory for extracting archive workspaces; the effective workspace is <base>/<archive-name>/workspace --config path None Path to the configuration file, e.g., --config config.yaml --plugin name/path (repeatable) [] Activate installed plugin ID or local plugin project path --plugin-workflow [plugin:]workflow None Use the workflow configuration layer declared by the activated plugin; can be used with --config --list-plugins flag No List plugins discoverable via entry points and plugin.search_paths then exit --validate-plugin name/path (repeatable) [] Validate plugin manifest, compatibility, dependencies, commands, and resources then exit --template-dir path None Custom template directory --template-overwrite flag No Allow overwriting existing content when rendering templates to the workspace --template-cfg-override path (repeatable) [] Override template configuration from YAML files, can be used multiple times --output dir unity_test Output directory name --override A.B.C=VALUE[,X.Y=VAL2,...] None Override configuration using dot-path notation, can be used repeatedly; values are parsed as Python literals, booleans should be written as True/False, unparsed values are treated as strings --gen-instruct-file -gif file AGENTS.md Generate a guidance file for external Agents under the workspace (overwrites if exists) --guid-doc-path path (repeatable) None Select custom Guide_Doc directory or append files --use-skill / --no-use-skill flag On Explicitly enable/disable SKILL; uses configuration value if not specified, built-in configuration defaults to on --extra-skill-path path None In addition to the default SKILL, use SKILLs from the specified path; cannot be used with --no-use-skill --backend str None Specify backend (overrides configuration file settings) --emulate-config flag No Only simulate the configuration process, do not actually run each stage

docs.title: Planning and ToDo
docs.text:
Option Short Value/Type Default Description --force-todo -fp flag No Enables the ToDo tool in standard mode and includes ToDo information in each round's prompt --use-todo-tools -utt flag No Enables ToDo-related tools (not limited to standard mode)

The ToDo tool is used to record plans and does not replace stage verification. Step indices start from 1; a new plan requires 2–20 steps. See the Tool List for tool purposes.

docs.title: External and Embedded Tools
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --ex-tools -et name1[,name2...] None Comma-separated list of external tool class names (e.g., SqThink); can be used multiple times --no-embed-tools true_or_false (value optional) true Disables built-in retrieval/memory embedded tools; a bare argument or true disables them, while passing false enables them

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --log flag No Enables logging --log-file path Auto Log output file (uses default if not specified) --msg-file path Auto Message log file (uses default if not specified)

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --mcp-server flag No Starts the MCP Server (including file tools) --mcp-server-no-file-tools flag No Starts the MCP Server, omitting the file operation tool group; retains basic ReadTextFile --mcp-server-host host 127.0.0.1 Server listening address --mcp-server-port int 5000 Server port; use -1 to automatically select an available port

docs.title: Stage Control and Security
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --force-stage-index int 0 Specifies the runtime stage index; rollback resets saved data for that stage and subsequent stages --skip int (repeatable) [] Skips the specified stage index; can be provided repeatedly --unskip int (repeatable) [] Unskips the specified stage index; can be provided repeatedly --no-write -nw path1 path2 ... None Prohibits writing to specified files or directories; paths must be within the workspace, and non-wildcard paths must already exist --ref str (repeatable) [] Specifies reference files that a stage needs to read; format: [stage_index:]file_path1[,file_path2] --append-py-path -app path (repeatable) [] Adds Python paths or files for module loading

docs.title: Master API and Distributed
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --as-master [ip[:port]] Off Starts as a Master API server; uses default values if no address is specified --master host[:port] [key] [] Connects to a Master API server; access_key can be specified; can be used multiple times --as-master-persist [path] /tmp/ucagent_master Master uses a persistent workspace directory (used with --as-master) --as-master-key str None Access key required for client registration (used with --as-master) --as-master-password str None HTTP Basic Auth password to protect the Master API (used with --as-master) --client-id str None Client identifier used when connecting to the Master (used with --master) --export-cmd-api [ip[:port]][ passwd] Off Starts a CMD API server, default 127.0.0.1:8765; a password can be specified to enable HTTP Basic Auth

docs.title: Context Management
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --enable-context-manage-tools flag Off Enables context management tools; applicable to scenarios requiring explicit context management, such as API mode

docs.title: Version and Checks
docs.text: Option Short Value/Type Default Description --check flag No Checks for the existence of default configuration, language directories, templates, and Guide_Doc, then exits --version flag Prints the version and exits --upgrade [pip_args] No Upgrades UCAgent from the GitHub main branch; optional additional pip arguments can be passed --hook-message str None Hook continue/complete key for custom prompt handling (used by Code Agent)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Run a prepared DUT directly:

ucagent ./output Adder -s -hm --tui --loop

Use the command-line backend to invoke verification tools via MCP:

ucagent ./output Adder --mcp-server-no-file-tools \
  --backend opencode -s -hm --tui --loop

Temporarily override configuration:

ucagent ./output Adder --config config.yaml \
  --override 'runtime_options.need_ref_model=True' \
  --override 'conversation_summary.max_tokens=16384'

--override is processed after YAML loading; boolean values use Python's True/False; YAML uses true/false. Commas within each parameter are used to separate assignments and are not suitable for passing lists or strings containing commas; such values should be written to the configuration file. See Workflow Configuration for configuration priority and list replacement rules.

docs.title: Environment Variable Description
docs.text: UCAgent supports configuring various parameters via environment variables. Environment variables are used to override the default values in the built-in configuration file; keys explicitly written in the user configuration file take precedence over the configuration file.

docs.title: Model Configuration
docs.text: Environment Variable Name Description Default Value OPENAI_MODEL OpenAI chat model name None (must be configured) OPENAI_API_KEY OpenAI API key None (must be configured) OPENAI_API_BASE OpenAI API base URL None (must be configured) OPENAI_CONTEXT_SIZE Context window size (in tokens) for the model used by the command-line backend, rendered into the context window configuration of each backend; if not set, the backend default value is used Not set OPENAI_OUTPUT_SIZE Maximum output limit (in tokens) for a single response of the model used by the command-line backend, effective only for opencode/kilo backends when a context window is declared Not set OPENAI_API_MODE OpenAI API mode used by the LangChain backend: auto, responses, or chat_completions auto OPENAI_RESPONSES_PROBE_TIMEOUT Timeout in seconds for the Responses API capability probe at startup, must be a positive number 10 OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT Reasoning effort for the LangChain backend; passed as-is according to the string supported by the current OpenAI or compatible model service xhigh OPENAI_TEMPERATURE OpenAI model temperature parameter Not set OPENAI_TOP_P OpenAI model top_p parameter Not set ANTHROPIC_MODEL Anthropic Claude model name claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Anthropic API key None (must be configured) GOOGLE_GENAI_MODEL Google Gemini model name gemini-2.5-pro GOOGLE_GENAI_API_KEY Google Generative AI API key None (must be configured)

docs.title: Embedding Model Configuration
docs.text: Environment Variable Name Description Default Value EMBED_MODEL Vector embedding model name None (must be configured) EMBED_OPENAI_API_KEY OpenAI API key for the embedding model None (must be configured) EMBED_OPENAI_API_BASE OpenAI API base URL for the embedding model None (must be configured)

docs.title: Langfuse Monitoring Configuration
docs.text: Environment Variable Name Description Default Value ENABLE_LANGFUSE Whether to enable Langfuse tracing monitoring false LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY Langfuse public key None (must be configured) LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY Langfuse secret key None (must be configured) LANGFUSE_URL Langfuse service address http://localhost:3000

docs.title: Conversation Summary Configuration
docs.text:
Environment Variable Name Description Default Value SUMMARY_MAX_CTX_TOKEN Estimated context token limit that triggers compression; 0 disables this trigger condition 204800 SUMMARY_MAX_SUM_TOKEN Output token limit for each summary generation, must be greater than 0 8192 SUMMARY_MAX_KEEP_MSG Context message count limit that independently triggers compression; 0 disables this trigger condition 100 SUMMARY_TAIL_KEEP_MSG Number of recent messages retained for the LLM 1

SUMMARY_MAX_CTX_TOKEN and SUMMARY_MAX_KEEP_MSG are two independent trigger conditions; exceeding either one will trigger compression. Context tokens are estimated values before the model call; if the model service returns usage during execution, the LangChain backend will calibrate subsequent estimates using the most recent actual input tokens. In status, ProviderTokens displays the server-side cumulative tokens as input/output/total, Context displays the current estimated value and threshold, and Compression displays the reason for the most recent compression and the size before and after.

docs.title: LLM Rate Limiting Configuration
docs.text: Environment Variable Name Description Default Value ENABLE_LLM_RATE_LIMIT Whether to enable LLM request rate limiting false LLM_MAX_RPS Maximum requests per second for LLM 10

docs.title: LLM Auxiliary Suggestion Configuration
docs.text: Environment Variable Name Description Default Value ENABLE_LLM_FAIL_SUGGESTION Whether to enable intelligent suggestions for stage failures false FAIL_SUGGESTION_MODEL Model name used for failure suggestions None (must be configured) FAIL_SUGGESTION_API_KEY API key for failure suggestions None (must be configured) FAIL_SUGGESTION_API_BASE API base URL for failure suggestions None (must be configured) FAIL_SUGGESTION_MFCOUNT Minimum number of failures to trigger failure suggestions 3 FAIL_SUGGESTION_TEMPERATURE Temperature parameter for the failure suggestion model Not set FAIL_SUGGESTION_TOP_P Top_p parameter for the failure suggestion model Not set ENABLE_LLM_PASS_SUGGESTION Whether to enable intelligent review for stage passes false PASS_SUGGESTION_MODEL Model name used for pass review None (must be configured) PASS_SUGGESTION_API_KEY API key for pass review None (must be configured) PASS_SUGGESTION_API_BASE API base URL for pass review None (must be configured) PASS_SUGGESTION_TEMPERATURE Temperature parameter for the pass review model Not set PASS_SUGGESTION_TOP_P Top_p parameter for the pass review model Not set

docs.title: Process Control Configuration
docs.text:
Environment Variable Name Description Default Value HUMAN_CHECK_CK Whether to enable human review of check points when verifying complex DUTs false UC_ENV_CMD_BACKEND_EX_ARGS Additional arguments for command-line backend execution None

loop_settings.max_stalled_rounds in ucagent/setting.yaml controls the stall protection for the external Agent loop, with a default value of 0 (disabled). It is only enabled when manually set to a positive integer via the configuration file or --override loop_settings.max_stalled_rounds=VALUE. Once enabled, accumulation occurs only if Check/Complete is actually called within a round, and the stage, Checker, and Checker explicit structured diagnostics are all identical to the previous counting round. Stage or batch progression, check passes, or diagnostic changes will reset the counter; rounds with no new checks are not counted. Upon reaching the threshold, UCAgent pauses --loop and waits for human intervention, without exiting the task, modifying artifacts, or adding fields to status. Other values must be non-negative integers.

docs.title: Test Tool Configuration
docs.text: Environment Variable Name Description Default Value UC_TEST_RCOUNT Number of repeated executions for test cases 3 UC_IS_IMP_TEMPLATE Whether it is an implementation layer test template false UC_SEED_MODEL Retrieval mode for random test seeds: manual returns the literal value passed to ucagent.get_seed(seed) as-is; random returns a brand new random seed; time generates based on the current time; uniform:<min>:<max> takes a uniform value within the closed interval; normal:<mu>:<sigma> takes a value from a Gaussian distribution and clamps it to [0, 2^31-1]. Invalid values will result in an error directly manual

docs.title: TUI (Interface and Operations)
docs.text: UCAgent includes a built-in terminal user interface (TUI) based on Textual, designed for local interactive observation of task progress, message streams, and console output, as well as for directly entering commands (such as entering/exiting loops, switching modes, and executing debug commands).

docs.title: Interface Components
docs.text:
The TUI interface components are illustrated in the figure below.

  • Mission Panel (Left)

    • Phase List: Displays the phases of the current task (index, title, phase skills (when skills are enabled), failure count, duration). Color meanings:
      • Green: Completed phases
      • Red: Current active phase
      • Yellow: Skipped phases (displayed as "skipped")
    • Changed Files: Recently modified files (including modification time and relative time, e.g., "3m ago"). More recent files are displayed in green.
    • Tools Call: Tool invocation status and counts. Busy tools are highlighted in yellow (e.g., SqThink(2)).
    • Daemon Commands: List of commands running in the background (with start time and elapsed duration).

  • Status Panel (Top Right)

    • Displays a summary of API and agent status, as well as current panel size parameters (useful for reference when adjusting the layout).

  • Messages Panel (Top Right Center)

    • Real-time message stream (model replies, tool outputs, system prompts).
    • Supports focus and scroll control; the title displays the "current/total" message position. For example: Messages (123/456).
  • Console (Bottom)
    • Output: Area for command and system output, supporting paginated viewing.
    • Input: Command input line (default prompt "(UnityChip) "). Provides history, completion, and busy status indicators.

Note: The interface automatically refreshes once per second (without affecting input). When messages or output are too long, it enters paginated or manual scrolling mode.

docs.title: Operations and Shortcuts
docs.text:
Global Operations

  • Enter: Executes the current input command; does nothing if the input is empty. Enter q/Q/exit/quit to exit the TUI and return to the PDB console.
  • Ctrl+C: Cancels the currently running command; exits the TUI if no command is running.
  • Esc:
    • If browsing Messages history, exits manual scrolling and returns to the end;
    • If Output is in paginated view, exits pagination;
    • If the help panel is open, closes the help panel;
    • Otherwise, clears the input line and focuses on the bottom input box.
  • Tab: Command completion; press Tab again to cycle through candidates.
  • Shift+Left: Clears the input line.

Panel Resizing

  • Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right: Decreases/increases the width of the left Mission panel.
  • Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down: Increases/decreases the height of the bottom Console output area.
  • Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J / Ctrl+K / Ctrl+L: Vim-style panel adjustment shortcuts, functionally equivalent to Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Down / Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Right (i.e., h=left j=down k=up l=right).

Console Operations

  • Up / Down:
    • If Output is in paginated mode, used for page navigation;
    • Otherwise, used for command history navigation (places historical commands into the input line, which can be edited and executed with Enter).
  • PageUp / PageDown: Pages through the Console Output.
  • Shift+Right: Clears the Console Output.

Pagination Mode Note: When Output enters paginated viewing, a prompt "PageUp/PageDown: scroll, Esc: exit" appears at the bottom. Esc exits pagination and returns to the input state.

Messages Panel Operations

  • Up / Down (when Messages panel is focused): Manually scrolls the message list.
  • Esc (when Messages panel is focused): Exits manual scrolling and resumes automatic following of the latest messages.

Themes and Help

  • Ctrl+T: Opens the theme selector dialog. Press Enter to confirm the selected theme, or Esc to cancel and restore the original theme.
  • F1: Shows/hides the shortcut key help panel.

After exiting the TUI, the UCAgent process remains running. To terminate the process, enter quit in the returned PDB console. If a task is currently executing, use Ctrl+C to cancel it and wait for the return before exiting.

docs.title: Commands and Usage
docs.text:
• Regular Commands: Type directly and press Enter, e.g., loop, tui, help, etc. (handled by the internal debugger).
  • History Commands: Use Up / Down to select a historical command, then press Enter to execute.
  • Clear Screen: Type clear and press Enter to clear only the Output (does not affect message records).
  • Background Commands: Appending & to the end of a command runs it in the background; completion is indicated in the Output area. Current background commands can be viewed via list_demo_cmds.
  • Executing System Commands: Input that cannot be recognized as a PDB command is executed directly as a shell command; input prefixed with ! forces evaluation as a Python expression (native PDB behavior), and this mode prioritizes scrolling to the latest output after execution.
  • Listing Background Commands: list_demo_cmds displays the list of running background commands and their start times.

docs.title: Message Configuration (messages_config)
docs.text:
• Purpose: View or adjust the message compression strategy during runtime. The token limit and message count limit are two independent trigger conditions; exceeding either one triggers compression.
  • Commands:
    • messages_config to view the current configuration
    • messages_config to set a configuration item
  • Configurable Items:
    • max_tokens: The estimated context token limit that triggers compression; set to 0 to disable this condition
    • max_keep_msgs: The context message count limit that triggers compression; set to 0 to disable this condition
    • max_summary_tokens: The output token limit for the summary model, must be greater than 0
    • tail_keep_msgs: The number of most recent messages to keep as-is after each compression
  • Examples:
    • messages_config
    • messages_config max_keep_msgs 200
    • messages_config max_tokens 131072

status displays the message compression status using only three compact fields: ProviderTokens displays server-side cumulative tokens as input/output/total, Context displays estimated tokens and message count as current value/threshold, and Compression displays the reason for the most recent compression and the size before and after. If the server does not return usage, ProviderTokens displays unavailable; use messages_config to view detailed configuration.

Other Notes

  • Auto-completion: Supports completion for command names and some parameters; if there are too many candidates, they are displayed in batches, and Tab can be pressed multiple times to view remaining items.
  • Busy Indicator: During command execution, the input box title rotates to display (wait.), (wait..), (wait...), indicating processing is in progress.
  • Auto-scrolling: Both the Messages panel and Console output area support smart auto-scrolling. By default, it automatically follows the latest content; using the mouse wheel or keyboard paging enters manual scrolling mode, keeping the current position unchanged; when manually scrolling to the end, it automatically resumes following mode. You can also press Esc to directly exit manual scrolling.
  • Error Tolerance: If certain UI operations encounter exceptions (e.g., the terminal does not support certain control sequences), the TUI will attempt to fall back to a safe state and continue running.

docs.title: Using with Web Master
docs.text:
TUI and Web are not mutually exclusive; it is recommended to combine them based on the scenario:

  1. TUI is suitable for local quick debugging and fine-grained command input.
  2. Web Master is suitable for cluster observation, hosted task operations, and remote collaboration.

Collaboration Recommendations:

  1. Use the Launch page to complete file preparation and compilation startup.
  2. Use the Task page to track startup and logs.
  3. Enter the Agent page to execute phase batch control and result review.
  4. When local immediate fixes are needed, switch back to TUI or the local terminal.

Notes:

  1. When web-terminal is enabled, it can run in parallel with the local terminal.
  2. For multi-terminal session scenarios, it is recommended to distinguish tasks using different URLs or tabs.

docs.title: How to switch models?
docs.text:
You can temporarily switch models using environment variables:

export OPENAI_MODEL="<model_name>"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="<api_key>"
export OPENAI_API_BASE="https://<provider>/v1"

You can also modify fields such as openai.model_name in the project's config.yaml, or specify a different configuration file using --config <path>. For configuration priority, see Workflow Configuration; for model environment variables, see Parameter Description.

docs.title: How to use --no-embed-tools?
docs.text:
The current CLI disables embedded/retrieval tools by default. Writing --no-embed-tools bare or passing true both disable the tools; to enable them, use:

--no-embed-tools false

Embedded tools are not a prerequisite for standard file tools or testing tools.

docs.title: UCAgent exited midway, how to recover?
docs.text: First, confirm that the old UCAgent and any external Code Agent have exited, then restart with the same workspace, DUT, and configuration. Enter status to confirm the current phase, then enter loop or let the external Agent continue. Do not delete .ucagent/ or output artifacts unless you explicitly intend to start over.

docs.title: What to do if a Check fails?
docs.text:
First, read the artifact, location, observed, expected, and next_action returned by the Checker. If necessary, use:

tool_invoke StdCheck lines=-1
tool_invoke KillCheck

After fixing, re-run the tests, Check, and Complete. Test infrastructure failures should be fixed to Pass first; only reproducible DUT failures with correct assertions should be recorded as Bugs.

docs.title: Why is config.yaml not found at startup?
docs.text:
config.yaml is a project configuration file, not a file necessarily provided by pip installation. You can:

  • Create your own config.yaml in the workspace and pass --config config.yaml;
  • Use the configuration and Makefile from the source repository;
  • Omit --config to use the layered default configuration.

docs.title: Why is --no-write not taking effect?
docs.text: The target must be located within the workspace. Regular files or directories must already exist; wildcard paths can match targets that have not yet been created. This option restricts UCAgent tool writes but does not prevent you from manually modifying files in an external shell.

docs.title: How to choose text file tools?
docs.text:
The current text file tools are:

  • EditTextFile: Create, overwrite, or append to a complete text file;
  • ReplaceStringInFile: Replace a unique segment of text in an existing file;
  • DeleteTextLines: Delete multiple complete line blocks at once.

First use ReadTextFile to get the current content; pass expected_sha256 when concurrent protection is required.

docs.title: How to distinguish between CK, TC, and Bug?
docs.text: CK stands for functional check point, and TC stands for test case. Dynamic Bug entries should be associated with accurate FG/FC/CK and the failing TC; test infrastructure failures should not be recorded as DUT Bugs.

docs.title: How to troubleshoot MCP connection failures?
docs.text:
Confirm:

  1. UCAgent is using --mcp-server or --mcp-server-no-file-tools;
  2. The client address is http://<host>:<port>/mcp;
  3. The client port matches --mcp-server-port;
  4. For remote scenarios, --mcp-server-host, firewall, and permissions allow the connection.

The command-line backend must also have MCP parameters enabled; otherwise, the CLI will refuse to start.

docs.title: LLM Check and Refinement
docs.text:
The UCAgent Checker first uses deterministic rules to verify stage artifacts. The optional LLM Check provides two types of assistance on top of this:

  • Fail Refinement: After a stage Check fails, it analyzes the current diagnosis and provides repair suggestions.
  • Pass Check: After the Checker passes before stage completion, an independent model reviews the results; the review model must call ApproveStagePass to approve the stage.

Both features are disabled by default. They do not replace the Checker, nor do they automatically convert test infrastructure failures into DUT Bugs.

docs.title: 1. Minimal Configuration
docs.text:
Fail Refinement:

export ENABLE_LLM_FAIL_SUGGESTION=true
export FAIL_SUGGESTION_MODEL="<model_name>"
export FAIL_SUGGESTION_API_KEY="<api_key>"
export FAIL_SUGGESTION_API_BASE="https://<provider>/v1"

Pass Check:

export ENABLE_LLM_PASS_SUGGESTION=true
export PASS_SUGGESTION_MODEL="<model_name>"
export PASS_SUGGESTION_API_KEY="<api_key>"
export PASS_SUGGESTION_API_BASE="https://<provider>/v1"

It is recommended to use a model or API quota different from the main model to distinguish between verification execution and result review. The API parameters for Fail and Pass are configured independently; if using launch.default_env in ucagent/setting.yaml, sub-Agents can also inherit these variables.

The same configuration can be written into the project YAML:

vmanager:
  llm_suggestion:
    check_fail_refinement:
      enable: true
      clss: ucagent.stage.llm_suggestion.OpenAILLMFailSuggestion
      args:
        model_name: "<model_name>"
        openai_api_key: "<api_key>"
        openai_api_base: "https://<provider>/v1"
        min_fail_count: 3
      bypass_stages: []
      target_stages: []
      default_apply_all_stages: true
    check_pass_refinement:
      enable: true
      clss: ucagent.stage.llm_suggestion.OpenAILLMPassSuggestion
      args:
        model_name: "<model_name>"
        openai_api_key: "<api_key>"
        openai_api_base: "https://<provider>/v1"
      bypass_stages: []
      target_stages: []
      default_apply_all_stages: true

The enable field in the configuration file can also use environment variable placeholders, for example enable: $(ENABLE_LLM_FAIL_SUGGESTION: false). Do not write secrets into documentation, logs, or runtime snapshots.

docs.title: Fail Refinement
docs.text:
When the Checker for the current stage returns a structured failure diagnosis, and Fail Refinement is enabled for that stage, UCAgent accumulates the count of consecutive failures. By default, the suggestion model is called only after 3 consecutive failures; before reaching the threshold, the regular Checker results are retained. A successful Check resets the consecutive failure count to zero.

The suggestion model receives the current stage task and failure report, and can use read-only inspection tools to read relevant files. It returns an action suggestion, and the Agent still needs to apply the suggested fix and re-run Check.

docs.title: Pass Check
docs.text:
When the Checker in the Complete path passes, and Pass Check is enabled for the current stage, UCAgent passes the stage task, check results, and stage Diff to the review model. The review model needs to:

  • Return specific repair suggestions and reject approval if issues are found;
  • Call ApproveStagePass(pass_or_not=true) if there are no issues.

If approval is not obtained, the stage will not proceed. Each Pass Check trigger results in a model call, so it is recommended to use it only for critical stages such as specification, coverage, test implementation, or Bug reporting.

docs.title: 3. Stage Filtering
docs.text:
Each suggestion configuration supports:

Field Function bypass_stages Always skips the listed stages; highest priority target_stages If non-empty, enables the feature only for the listed stages default_apply_all_stages Whether to apply to all stages when target_stages is empty; defaults to true

The evaluation order is: first check bypass_stages, then target_stages, and finally default_apply_all_stages. You can also toggle LFail/LPass per stage on the running Agent page; stage-level settings override the global filtering results.

Example:

check_pass_refinement:
  enable: true
  target_stages: [functional_specification_analysis, comprehensive_verification_and_bug_analysis]
  default_apply_all_stages: false

Stage names must use the name from the current configuration, not the page title or stage index.

docs.title: 4. Common Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Applies To Default Description model_name Fail/Pass None Review model name openai_api_key Fail/Pass None API Key openai_api_base Fail/Pass None OpenAI-compatible API address min_fail_count Fail 3 Number of consecutive failures before calling the model summary_trigger_tokens Fail/Pass Fail 32768, Pass 65536 Trigger threshold for conversation summary in the suggestion model summary_keep_messages Fail/Pass 10 Number of messages to retain after summarization ignore_labels Fail/Pass <think>...</think> Tag pairs to filter from suggestion text temperature, top_p Fail/Pass Not set Sampling parameters passed to the suggestion model

docs.title: 5. Troubleshooting and Cost
docs.text:
• No suggestion output: First check ENABLE_LLM_*_SUGGESTION, the corresponding model variables, and the API address, then confirm that the current stage is not filtered out.
  • Fail suggestion does not appear immediately: By default, 3 consecutive failures are required; you can adjust min_fail_count, but do not use it to mask unresolved Checker failures.
  • Pass Check does not proceed: Check the review model's return value to confirm it called ApproveStagePass(true) when there were no issues; fix the issues and re-run Complete.
  • Suggestion model calls increase latency and cost. Prioritize enabling it for critical stages, and set reasonable API timeouts and context summary thresholds.
  • Regular Checker results are always the source of truth. LLM suggestions can only help locate issues; they cannot replace tests, source code, reports, or waveform evidence.

Configuration fields and default values are subject to the current version of ucagent/setting.yaml; to modify the implementation or add new review strategies, refer to ucagent/stage/llm_suggestion/ and Workflow Configuration.

docs.title: Web Master User Guide
docs.text:
This document provides the complete operational workflow for UCAgent Web Master:

  1. Access the Master dashboard to view Agent status
  2. Create and compile tasks on the Launch page
  3. Manage task lifecycle on the Task page
  4. Perform batch stage operations and review results on the Agent page

docs.title: 1. Feature Overview
docs.text:
Web Master is not just a status display; it is a complete task management entry point. Core capabilities include:

  1. Dashboard: Agent list, filtering, sorting, pagination, and offline policies
  2. Launch: Workspace creation, file import/upload, module parsing, compilation, and launch parameter preview
  3. Task: Hosted task list, status filtering, log viewing, stop/delete
  4. Agent: Stage quick actions (HM/Skip/LFail/LPass), stage file viewing, and Diff comparison
  5. Web Terminal: Online terminal access (can run in parallel with local terminals)

docs.title: 2.1 Starting Master
docs.text:
Master retains a local PDB console for executing Master API, task, terminal, status, and file management commands, but it does not initialize, probe, or invoke API/command-line model backends. When executing model work commands such as loop, chat, or next_round, BlankBackend directly returns "not supported" and does not invoke the model.

# Source repository: temporary workspace

make as_master

# Recommended: persistent workspace

make as_master_persist

# Installed command

ucagent --as-master-persist --as-master

Default access address:

http://localhost:8800

If password protection is required:

ucagent --as-master-persist --as-master --as-master-password "your_password"

Starting Master itself does not require a model address, API Key, or model name. If you need to launch child Agents from the Launch page, you can configure model variables in the Master process environment; these are only used to construct the launch environment for child Agents.

The --backend flag in Master mode is used to set the default backend when launching child Agents from the Launch page; the current Master process always uses a model-less backend.

docs.title: 2.2 Connecting Agent to Master
docs.text:
ucagent ./output Adder --master 127.0.0.1:8800 your_key

Example:

ucagent ./output Adder --master 127.0.0.1:8800

docs.title: 3.1 Common Operations
docs.text:
1. Search Agents (ID/Host/Mission)
  2. Filter by status (online/offline)
  3. Sort by fields (last_seen/progress, etc.)
  4. Paginate through large-scale Agent lists
  5. Batch delete offline Agents

docs.title: 3.2 Offline Cleanup Policy
docs.text:
You can enable Auto-delete offline and set the check interval and threshold time to reduce interference from zombie instances on the panel.

Recommendations:

  1. Development environment: Shorter threshold (e.g., 5-10 minutes)
  2. Shared environment: Longer threshold (e.g., 30-60 minutes)

docs.title: 4.1 Standard Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a Launch Workspace
  2. Upload or import RTL/Spec/Requirement/Config files
  3. Mark the main RTL and parse modules
  4. Select DUT name and module, then execute compilation
  5. Check the command preview and launch the hosted task

docs.title: 4.2 Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Recompile after every adjustment to the main module
  2. Retain version tags for Requirement and Config to facilitate traceability
  3. Review the Command Preview before launching to confirm backend/master/export-cmd-api parameters

docs.title: 4.3 Parallel Task Limit and Waiting Queue
docs.text:
master_api.max_task_count controls the maximum number of tasks Master can execute simultaneously, defaulting to 100:

  1. Tasks launched after reaching the limit enter the waiting state and do not occupy execution quota
  2. Once a task finishes and releases quota, waiting tasks are automatically launched in launch order
  3. Waiting tasks are only listed in the Launch Queue panel on the Task page (including task ID, DUT, creation and enqueue time, etc.); the main task list does not display waiting tasks
  4. The Launch Queue panel supports drag-and-drop or ▲▼ buttons to adjust the launch order of waiting tasks; resubmitted tasks are placed at the end of the queue
  5. The Waiting statistic on the Master page is displayed at the same level as TOTAL/ONLINE/OFFLINE to show the current number of waiting tasks
  6. The Task page summary bar persistently displays the current maximum concurrency (master_api.max_task_count)
  7. Waiting tasks can be cancelled in the Launch Queue panel; cancellation deletes the task record and its workspace directory

docs.title: 5.1 Page Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Filter by status, keyword, and DUT (waiting tasks are only displayed in the Launch Queue panel, see 4.3)
  2. Paginate through tasks
  3. View task details (command, registration status, PID)
  4. View stdout/stderr logs
  5. Stop tasks and delete records
  6. Adjust the launch order of waiting tasks and cancel waiting tasks in the Launch Queue panel (see 4.3)

docs.title: 5.2 Typical Troubleshooting Path
docs.text:
1. Task stuck in starting: First check the command and environment variable expansion results
  2. Task failed: Prioritize checking stderr, then check workspace and DUT parameters
  3. Agent not registered: Check --master address, key, and network connectivity
  4. Task always waiting: Parallel tasks have reached the master_api.max_task_count limit; the queue position is visible in the details page, wait for automatic launch or cancel the task

docs.title: 6.1 Stage Quick Controls
docs.text:
The page supports single-stage quick toggles:

  1. HM: Human review toggle
  2. Skip: Skip toggle
  3. LF: LLM Fail Suggestion toggle
  4. LP: LLM Pass Suggestion toggle

docs.title: 6.2 Stage Batch Controls
docs.text:
You can select multiple stages and batch set:

  1. HM On/Off
  2. Skip/Unskip
  3. LFail On/Off
  4. LPass On/Off

docs.title: 6.3 Stage Artifact Review
docs.text:
For stage output files, you can:

  1. View content
  2. View Diff (comparison between current result and changes)
  3. Quickly locate artifacts corresponding to failed stages

docs.title: 7.1 Two Common Modes
docs.text:
1. web-console: Browser console mode (independent Web entry)
  2. web-terminal: Web terminal mode (can run in parallel with local terminals)

docs.title: 7.2 Multi-Session Recommendations
docs.text: When enabling multiple terminal sessions, it is recommended to distinguish tasks via different URLs/tabs to avoid accidental operations.

docs.title: 8. Proxy and Network Notes
docs.text:
Master supports unified proxy forwarding to task/agent cmd, terminal, and web-console access paths.

When connection issues occur, troubleshoot in the following order:

  1. Master page visible but sub-pages fail: Check proxy paths and authentication
  2. Page opens but WS is unstable: Check if the reverse proxy/gateway allows websocket
  3. Local connects but remote does not: Check binding address (127.0.0.1 vs 0.0.0.0)

docs.title: 9. Security and Permission Recommendations
docs.text:
1. Always enable password protection for public or shared networks
  2. Use gateway authentication and TLS when exposing externally
  3. Regularly clean up offline Agents and invalid task records

docs.title: Q1: Why does Launch compilation succeed but task launch fail?
docs.text:
Prioritize checking:

  1. Whether the backend is available
  2. Whether launch environment variables are complete
  3. Whether the master address and key are correct

docs.title: Q2: Why does Task show running, but the Agent page cannot be opened?
docs.text: This is usually due to registration delay or proxy chain issues; first check the registration status and logs in Task details.

docs.title: Q3: When to use TUI and when to use Web?
docs.text:
1. TUI: Local quick debugging, fine-grained command operations
  2. Web: Centralized management, multi-task operations, remote collaboration

docs.title: Skill SKILL
docs.text: Skills bundle reusable task methods, scripts, and reference materials into a single directory. The Agent first lists available skills and then reads SKILL.md on demand, avoiding loading all instructions into the context at once. Skills are used to accelerate and guide tasks; when skills are disabled, the workflow must still provide complete task instructions, tool paths, and the same Checker acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Enabling and Configuration
docs.text:
Built-in configuration enables skills by default; if no CLI switch is passed, the skill.use_skill value in the hierarchical configuration takes precedence. You can explicitly override this:

ucagent <workspace> <DUT> --use-skill
ucagent <workspace> <DUT> --no-use-skill

You can disable it in the configuration file:

skill:
  use_skill: false

--extra-skill-path <path> appends custom skills and enables skill support; it cannot be used simultaneously with --no-use-skill. During initialization, skills are copied to the workspace .ucagent/skills/, with additional skills located in the ext/ subdirectory. Tools read and execute the workspace copies; after modifying skills in the source code, you must restart and re-copy them to use the new content.

docs.title: Stage Skills and General Skills
docs.text:
Example stage configuration:

stage:
  - name: static_analysis
    desc: "Analyze static defect candidates"
    task:
      - "Read source code and requirements, complete static analysis according to Guide_Doc/dut_bug_analysis.md"
    skill_list:
      - unitytest/static-bug-analysis
    force_use_skill: true
Configuration Usage Requirement Skills enabled and stage skill_list is non-empty Forced by default; usage evidence must be satisfied before Complete Stage sets force_use_skill: false Stage-specific skills are optional skill_list is unconfigured or empty SetSkillUsage is not required; stage skill gate is not enforced skill.general_skill_list General skills are always optional Skills globally disabled All stage skill gates are disabled; other acceptance requirements are executed as usual

The skill gate applies to Complete and does not block intermediate Check calls. Disabling skills should not block tasks due to the absence of .ucagent/skills/.

docs.title: Usage Flow and Evidence
docs.text:
Mandatory stage skills are used in the following order:

  1. Call ListSkill to list currently available skills.
  2. Use UCAgent's ReadTextFile to read the returned workspace SKILL.md path.
  3. Execute the task according to the skill method; if scripts are needed, execute them via RunSkillScript.
  4. Call Check to verify the current artifact.
  5. After the current Check passes, call SetSkillUsage to confirm usage.
  6. Call Complete to finish the stage.

ListSkill and ReadTextFile generate real list/read records respectively; RunSkillScript registers script usage only after the entire call succeeds. SetSkillUsage cannot fabricate these records via model declaration. It can confirm executed text methods only after both list/read records and a currently passing Check are present.

When a method has been applied, the tool parameters for SetSkillUsage are as follows:

{
  "skill_usage": {
    "unitytest/static-bug-analysis": {
      "list": true,
      "read": true,
      "use": true
    }
  }
}

If the current stage has no objects for skills to process, after executing its no-applicable-objects branch and passing Check, submit use: false and a non-empty reason explaining the specific cause. This reason cannot replace list/read, skip the current check, or override an observed use: true; nor can it be used to fabricate bugs or artifacts to satisfy the skill gate. Do not fill in reason when use: true.

docs.title: Related Tools
Skill Directory and Metadata
docs.text:
analysis/
├── SKILL.md
├── scripts/                  # Optional
│   ├── analyze.py
│   ├── __init__.py           # Optional stage hook
│   └── script_runner.json    # Optional runner mapping
└── references/               # Optional auxiliary materials

The first line of SKILL.md must be --- directly, and the frontmatter must include at least name and description:

---
name: analysis
description: Analyze input materials, generate and check results according to project conventions
metadata:
  category: analysis
---

# Analyze Input Materials

## Objectives and Inputs

List applicable tasks, input files, and prerequisites.

## Execution Steps

Describe which materials to read, how to analyze, when to call scripts, and how to verify.

## Output and Acceptance

Describe allowed write paths, complete artifact formats, and remediation steps after failure.
  • name: No more than 64 characters, using only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, and must satisfy naming validation.
  • description: Describes applicable tasks, up to 1024 characters; excess content is truncated. The description helps the Agent select skills but does not automatically trigger scripts.
  • metadata: Optional string key-value mapping; keys and values are converted to strings at runtime.

The body must provide executable steps and real script parameters. Mandatory format and evidence rules must also be available in stage tasks, Guide_Doc, and templates to avoid losing acceptance criteria when skills are disabled.

docs.title: Script Execution Environment
docs.text:
Script processes use the DUT workspace as the current directory. RunSkillScript uses shlex to split arguments, then launches the process with the runner and argv, with shell=False; do not rely on pipes, redirection, or shell variable expansion.

  • .py files use the Python interpreter running UCAgent; .sh and .bash files use Bash.
  • Other scripts specify a single executable program in scripts/script_runner.json as {"filename": "executable"}; runner arguments are not allowed.
  • Environment variables DUT and OUT come from the resolved configuration in .ucagent/runtime_config.json.
  • RunSkillScript reads ucagent_python_path from the snapshot, places it at the beginning of the subprocess PYTHONPATH, deduplicates, and preserves other import paths.

Python skill scripts that need to import ucagent must be executed via RunSkillScript. Scripts should use load_runtime_config(workspace) to read runtime configuration; do not re-interpret original functional environment variables or guess the UCAgent source directory from the copied script location. If import paths in the snapshot are missing, non-absolute, or invalid, restart UCAgent to regenerate the snapshot.

docs.title: Stage Hook (Advanced)
docs.text:
Skills can provide setup_vstage(stage) in a non-empty scripts/__init__.py, wrapping existing methods of the current stage via stage.add_hook(method_name, hook_func). Skills in both stage-specific skill_list and skill.general_skill_list participate in hook loading and are deduplicated.

Hooks only affect the current stage instance. Registration must remain idempotent to avoid hidden operations during import; also, do not place mandatory behavior only in hooks, which would prevent task completion if skills are disabled.

When developing and testing skills, verify at least three scenarios: enabled, disabled, and missing skill directory. See Workflow Configuration for configuration methods in workflows, and Custom Tools for tool and path policies.

docs.title: Xpra GUI Applications and Interactive Console
docs.text:
The CMD WebUI can display server-side graphical applications in the browser via Xpra, or run interactive commands through a graphical terminal. The Xpra button on the Agent Dashboard opens the session management page; clicking Create session opens the creation dialog; the Open link for each session directly opens the application display page. The display page uses the UCAgent interface, reusing the protocol and rendering libraries of the official HTML5 client, and no longer displays the official connection form.

Sessions belong to the CMD service that created them. They do not discover, take over, or delete Xpra sessions started by other users or services on the same machine. Web Terminal, Web Console, and Xpra use independent connections and can run simultaneously.

docs.title: Installation and Startup Requirements
docs.text:
Install the Xpra server, X11 service support, a virtual display program (such as Xvfb), and the official xpra-html5 client in the environment where the CMD service runs. Console mode also requires a graphical terminal, which defaults to xterm. Real integration verification uses Xpra 6.5.5 as the baseline.

The CMD service and target applications can be deployed on Linux hosts or Docker containers that have the above dependencies. Users access the session management page and application display page via a browser. Direct connection and Master proxy access have been verified on macOS using Chrome and WebKit.

The CMD service can still start if Xpra is missing, and other APIs remain available. The management page will display prompts indicating missing programs or resources. The status endpoint checks executables, versions, and explicitly configured resource paths; when actually creating a session, it further checks whether the server and HTML5 service can start.

Follow the CMD service's startup and authentication settings, for example, execute in PDB:

cmd_api_start --passwd your-password

Access http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/xpra/ directly, using the same Basic authentication as other CMD APIs. If the CMD service has no password configured, Xpra also allows passwordless access. HTML5 pages, resources, and WebSockets are also subject to this policy; passwords are not written into the connection URL. After entering the management page and completing CMD or Master login, clicking Open will automatically check access permissions and connect based on the session ID in the URL, without requiring re-entry of the Xpra host, port, username, or password. The session ID itself does not grant access permissions; unauthenticated new browsers must still complete the login for the current entry point first.

Some browsers do not include the page's Basic authentication header in the WebSocket handshake. Before each connection, the display page obtains a connection Cookie with a 5-minute validity period via an authenticated HTTP request; the Cookie uses HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, and also uses Secure under HTTPS, and is only applicable to the WebSocket of the current session and current proxy path. It cannot be used to call management interfaces, nor can it be used by other sessions; once the connection is established, it will not be disconnected due to Cookie expiration, and it is automatically re-issued upon reconnection. Command-line WebSocket clients can still directly use Basic authentication.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Place the following settings in the UCAgent configuration file; fields are read from the currently effective configuration, and the CMD service must be restarted after modifications:

cmd_api:
  xpra:
    executable: xpra
    max_sessions: 5
    terminal_command: [xterm, -e]
    html_dir: null
    startup_timeout: 20
    shutdown_timeout: 5
    presets:
      - label: Terminal
        name: Terminal
        mode: console
        command: bash -l
        cwd: .
        env: {}
        idle_timeout: -1
      - label: Browser
        name: Browser
        mode: gui
        command: chromium --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check about:blank
        cwd: .
        env: {}
        idle_timeout: -1
      - label: Codex
        name: Codex
        mode: console
        command: codex
        cwd: .
        env: {}
        idle_timeout: -1
      - label: OpenCode
        name: OpenCode
        mode: console
        command: opencode
        cwd: .
        env: {}
        idle_timeout: -1
      - label: Qwen Code
        name: Qwen Code
        mode: console
        command: qwen
        cwd: .
        env: {}
        idle_timeout: -1
Field Purpose executable Xpra program name or executable file path max_sessions Number of simultaneously active sessions, default 5; must be a positive integer terminal_command List of startup arguments for the Console graphical terminal, followed by the appended application command and its arguments html_dir Official HTML5 resource directory, must contain index.html; null uses Xpra's built-in resources startup_timeout Seconds to wait for the HTML5 service to be ready, must be a positive number shutdown_timeout Seconds to wait for the associated Xpra to stop normally, forcibly reclaims after timeout presets List of shortcut buttons for the creation form; [] hides all buttons. A custom list completely replaces the default list

Xpra uses a private temporary directory and Unix socket, and does not open an additional Xpra TCP port. Sessions isolate Xpra's system/user configuration directories to prevent listening settings or additional startup commands within them from bypassing CMD management; adjust this feature via the above UCAgent configuration.

docs.title: Creation Shortcut Buttons and Code Agent
docs.text:
The creation form provides Terminal, Browser, Codex, OpenCode, and Qwen Code shortcut buttons by default. Clicking Create session opens the creation dialog, which provides these shortcut buttons. Clicking a button completely fills in the name, mode, command, working directory, environment variables, and idle timeout; only after confirming or modifying the parameters and clicking Create session will the program start. The buttons themselves do not start sessions, nor do they occupy quota.

Terminal uses Console mode to start bash -l, displaying an interactive shell through the configured graphical terminal; the command can be changed to installed shells such as zsh -l. Browser uses GUI mode to start chromium --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check about:blank; the command can be changed to the actual browser path or programs like Firefox. The browser runs in the environment where the CMD service is located, and the corresponding programs need to be installed there; the accessed network and files also come from that service environment.

Each presets entry includes required label (button text) and command; other fields are consistent with the creation interface: name defaults to an empty string, mode defaults to gui, cwd defaults to ., env defaults to {}, and idle_timeout defaults to -1. Code Agent presets should explicitly use mode: console to run the interactive interface through the configured graphical terminal. The command can be modified to the absolute path of the executable file, or parameters supported by that CLI can be appended; the working directory must still be located within the workspace.

codex, opencode, and qwen must be installed in the environment where the CMD service actually runs and be findable via its PATH; if CMD runs in a container, CLI installations on the host machine will not automatically appear in the container. Presets use interactive startup commands; the CLI's own first-time login, model configuration, and authorization are still completed by that CLI. If the command is missing, the creation interface and page will prompt to install the program or correct the path.

Preset parameters are sent to the browser via the authenticated API for user viewing and editing. Do not put API keys, tokens, or passwords in preset commands or env; set the required credentials in the CMD runtime environment, and let child processes inherit them. Shortcut buttons do not modify the Code Agent's login configuration or approval options.

The preset list can still be read even if Xpra or the target CLI is missing. If the format is invalid, the page displays a configuration error, and the manual creation form remains available. Restart the CMD service after modifying the configuration.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
All interfaces uniformly use the /api/xpra/ prefix.

Method Path Description GET /api/xpra/ Session management page GET /api/xpra/status Program availability, version, Console terminal availability, and diagnostics GET /api/xpra/presets Returns {"presets": [...]}, for the creation page to fill parameters; follows CMD/Master authentication GET /api/xpra/sessions List of owned sessions, active count, maximum count POST /api/xpra/sessions Create session; returns 201 after the HTML5 service is ready GET /api/xpra/sessions/{id} Single session details, recent errors, and length-limited logs DELETE /api/xpra/sessions/{id} Stop and delete the owned session POST /api/xpra/sessions/{id}/connect Check the session and issue or refresh the connection Cookie for the current browser, returns 204 on success; still requires CMD/Master HTTP authentication GET /api/xpra/sessions/{id}/view HTML5 display page with automatic connection GET / HEAD /api/xpra/sessions/{id}/client/{path} UCAgent application display interface and official protocol, rendering resources WebSocket /api/xpra/sessions/{id}/client/ Screen, keyboard/mouse, and client protocol interaction

Create a GUI session:

curl -u :your-password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Clock","mode":"gui","command":"xclock","cwd":".","env":{}}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/xpra/sessions

Creating a Console session uses the same interface and fields, for example:

{
  "name": "Interactive shell",
  "mode": "console",
  "command": "bash -l",
  "cwd": ".",
  "env": {"TERM": "xterm-256color"},
  "idle_timeout": 300
}

command is required; mode defaults to gui, name defaults to the startup program name, cwd defaults to the workspace root directory, and env defaults to an empty object. The working directory must exist and be located within the workspace; symbolic links cannot point to external directories.

Commands are split into arguments by quotes and do not automatically interpret shell expressions. When pipes, redirections, or shell initialization are needed, explicitly submit bash -lc 'your command'. Console mode appends the split arguments after terminal_command; GUI mode directly starts the application.

Sessions include id, name, mode, command, cwd, idle_timeout, status, created_at, viewer_path, and last_error; details also include log_tail with up to 200 lines of output. viewer_path is resolved relative to the current /api/xpra/ base address. created_at is a Unix timestamp. Environment variable values are not returned as session fields; known credentials and submitted environment variable values are masked in captured logs.

docs.title: Display Page Operations
docs.text:
Clicking Open launches the application directly. The Console defaults to filling the available display area, while the GUI retains the application's own window size and adjustment capabilities. The top bar displays the actual connection status and provides Reconnect, Full screen, Sessions, Exit, and a window switch list; minimized applications can be restored via the window list.

In the Console, drag the mouse to select text, then right-click to choose Copy selection to copy to the local clipboard; right-click to choose Paste to paste local clipboard text into the terminal. Support for ⌘C / ⌘V and Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+V is also available; ordinary Ctrl+C remains for terminal interruption. Opening a menu does not change the current selection, and the copy button is unavailable when no text is selected.

When the browser requires clipboard permissions, you must allow this visit. If standard HTTP, browser restrictions, or permission denial occur, a manual copy/paste window will open. You can also directly select Paste text…, perform the browser's paste operation in the local text box, and then click Paste into terminal. Content in the text box is not sent to the application before submission. Pasted text is sent as-is; newlines in the text may trigger terminal execution.

In the Console, hold a modifier key (Shift, Control, Command, or Alt) and right-click; the right-click is still handed to the remote application for its own menu or mouse functions. Right-clicks in GUI mode are always handed to the remote application; local browser menus do not pop up in the application area. Top navigation and buttons retain the browser's right-click behavior.

Clicking Exit and confirming will stop the application, delete the current session, and return to the session management page of the current entry; the current client will disconnect. During exit, automatic reconnection is paused; if it fails, the reason is displayed and retry is allowed. Closing the browser tab retains the application based on the idle timeout setting for that session.

Refreshing the page re-verifies and automatically connects. In case of temporary disconnection, automatic retry occurs up to 5 times, displaying the retry progress. If the session is deleted, exited, or access is denied, the specific reason and operation prompt are displayed without redirecting to the official connection page. Clicking Reconnect manually initiates a new connection. The initial connection does not proactively read the local clipboard or request audio permissions; clipboard interactions are triggered by user copy/paste operations.

Each session allows only one client control simultaneously. Newly opened display pages automatically preempt the original connection; the original page displays the Session opened in another client prompt and Take back button, stopping automatic reconnection. Clicking Take back reclaims the current page, and the other page receives the same prompt. Direct connection, Master task proxy, and agent proxy all adhere to this rule.

docs.title: Lifecycle and Error Handling
docs.text:
Status includes starting, running, stopping, exited, and failed. Sessions in starting, running, or stopping states occupy active quotas; exited or failed sessions do not occupy quotas but can still be viewed for logs or deleted.

An idle_timeout can be set during creation, in integer seconds: -1 (default) means no timeout, a positive integer means the application exits automatically if no connected client has been present for that many seconds; 0, other negative numbers, non-integers, or values exceeding 4294967 are invalid. Timing starts when the session service is ready and no client is connected; it is cancelled upon client connection and restarted after the last client disconnects. The session does not timeout even without keyboard/mouse input while a client maintains the connection; polling the management page, viewing details, and loading resources do not count as client connections. New clients during preemption continue the session.

After idle timeout exit, an exited record is retained in the list for viewing logs and deletion; active quotas and process resources are released. With -1, closing the browser or losing network connection retains the application; with a finite timeout, it can be reopened before expiration. Upon application exit, the session ends; deleting the session, stopping the CMD service, or normally exiting UCAgent cleans up associated Xpra, child processes, and temporary resources. Old sessions are not restored after service restart.

Interface failures return structured diagnostics via detail:

{
  "detail": {
    "error_code": "XPRA_SESSION_LIMIT",
    "message": "The maximum number of active Xpra sessions has been reached.",
    "next_action": "Delete an unused session or increase cmd_api.xpra.max_sessions."
  }
}
Status Code Typical Cause Action 401 Missing or incorrect CMD / Master credentials Use authentication info from the current entry 404 Session does not exist or has been deleted Refresh the list and open an existing session 409 Capacity limit reached or creation cancelled by a stop operation Delete idle sessions, or retry creation 422 Invalid command, working directory, environment variable, or request field Correct input based on diagnostics 502 Unable to connect to upstream Xpra Check session status and logs, then reconnect 503 Missing program, terminal, HTML5 resources, or server capabilities; session not running Install/configure running conditions based on diagnostics, or create a new session 504 Startup did not complete within the time limit Check logs, fix the display environment, and adjust startup wait time if necessary

Creation failure returns a queryable session_id and logs; if submission parameters are invalid or the program does not exist, a session ID may not be allocated yet. The management page and display page directly display the error reason and next steps.

docs.title: Master Proxy and Existing Terminals
docs.text:
When accessing via an existing Master CMD proxy, prepend /task/{task_id}/cmd or /agent/{agent_id}/cmd to the above addresses, for example:

/task/{task_id}/cmd/api/xpra/
/agent/{agent_id}/cmd/api/xpra/sessions/{id}/view

The management page, HTML5 resources, and WebSocket use the same proxy prefix. The browser uses Master authentication, providing corresponding credentials for the upstream CMD connection to Master. HTTPS pages automatically use WSS; when deployed behind an external reverse proxy, WebSocket Upgrade should continue to be allowed.

Agents update CMD proxy credentials to the connected Master via actual registration and heartbeat; Master uses these in memory for HTTP/WebSocket forwarding and does not return or save this password in the Agent list, details, or persisted Agent snapshots. Master credentials are restored by new heartbeats after Master restart.

Existing terminals maintain an independent /ws service; Master maintains /terminal/ws and /web-console/ws. Xpra uses /api/xpra/sessions/{id}/client/ under CMD; deleting, refreshing, or reconnecting Xpra does not take over the terminal connection nor terminate the terminal process.

docs.title: Full Runtime Integration Test
docs.text:
In a Linux environment with the project's full dependencies, picker, Verilator, Xpra server, official HTML5 resources, Xvfb, xterm, and xclock installed, run:

UCAGENT_RUN_XPRA_INTEGRATION=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_api_xpra_full_runtime.py

The test first exports and compiles a real DUT package from Adder RTL using picker and Verilator, then loads the default verification workflow via the formal CLI, verifying coexistence of Web Terminal, Web Console modes, and CMD API/Xpra. It checks real PDB command execution, terminal input/output, Master authentication proxy after actual heartbeat registration, GUI/Console session creation/deletion, and process cleanup after normal UCAgent exit. Web Terminal and Web Console for the same Agent follow the mutual exclusion limits of the CLI; tests can be run separately across multiple Agents. The test uses the project's built-in blank backend, does not initiate model requests, and does not replace Agent, PDB, or workflow objects. This test is skipped unless explicitly enabled; standard unit tests do not require local Xpra server installation.

docs.title: Custom Development
docs.text: When customizing a workflow, first define tasks and acceptance criteria, then add tools, guidance documents, and templates as needed. It is recommended to run the Mini Example first to understand how each component collaborates by comparing it with the actual files.

docs.title: Learning Path
docs.text:
1. Read Getting Started with Custom Development to understand the components of a minimal workflow.
  2. Run the Mini Example to observe how the two stages generate and accept documents.
  3. Adjust stages, inputs, and outputs according to the Workflow Configuration.
  4. When new capabilities are needed, write Tools and Checkers.
  5. When independent installation and delivery of extensions are required, use Plugins.

docs.title: Lookup by Problem
docs.text:
Problem to Solve Documentation Understand component responsibilities and execution process Architecture and How It Works Configure stages, template variables, skip, and human review Workflow Configuration Write runtime guidance documents and initial files Template Files and Generated Artifacts Add computation, file, or external service capabilities Custom Tools Find the purpose of built-in tools Tool List Verify files, formats, business rules, and batch progress Custom Checker Run a complete example that does not depend on RTL Mini Example Package and publish Tools, Checkers, Skills, or workflows Plugin Development and Publishing

When using UCAgent for the first time, complete Installation and Getting Started with Normal Mode first. CLI parameters are documented in Parameter Description.

docs.title: Getting Started with Custom Development
docs.text:
Creating a workflow typically requires four types of resources:

  • Workflow Configuration: Defines stage order, tasks, reference files, outputs, and Checkers;
  • Tools: Enable the Agent to read, compute, test, or invoke domain services;
  • Guide_Doc/Templates: Specify output structure, tags, and evidence formats;
  • Checker: Accept stage artifacts using deterministic rules.

It is recommended to first run the Mini Example, then replace the Calculator in the example with your own input.

docs.title: 1. Minimum Directory Structure
docs.text:
MyWorkflow/
├── Guide_Doc/
├── mini.yaml
├── my_tools.py
├── my_checkers.py
├── __init__.py
└── README.md

The Makefile is optional and is responsible only for preparing the workspace and constructing the startup command.

docs.title: 2. Workflow Configuration
docs.text:
Below is the minimal structure consistent with the current parser:

ex_tools:
  - "my_tools.CountWords"

template_overwrite:
  PROJECT: "Calculator"

mission:
  name: "{PROJECT} Document Generation"
  prompt:
