    system: "You are a technical documentation engineer."

stage:
  - name: analyze_project
    desc: "Analyze project"
    task:
      - "Read {PROJECT}/README.md"
      - "Write {OUT}/{PROJECT}_analysis.md"
    reference_files:
      - "Guide_Doc/project_analysis_guide.md"
    output_files:
      - "{OUT}/{PROJECT}_analysis.md"
    checker:
      - name: markdown_check
        clss: "UnityChipCheckerMarkdownFileFormat"
        args:
          markdown_file_list: "{OUT}/{PROJECT}_analysis.md"
          no_line_break: true
    skill_list: []
    force_use_skill: false

Field descriptions:

  • ex_tools registers the full import path of external tool classes;
  • template_overwrite provides custom template values such as {PROJECT}; the output directory is specified via the CLI option --output;
  • mission.prompt.system is the global system prompt;
  • stage is a list of stages executed in order; stages can nest stage sub-stages;
  • reference_files and output_files use relative paths within the workspace;
  • checker[].args are passed to the Checker constructor, while extra_args are used to add new attributes after instantiation and cannot override existing attributes;
  • skill_list enters the stage skill gatekeeper only if skills are enabled and the list is non-empty. Skills are forced by default; set force_use_skill: false to make them optional.

Configuration loading and list replacement rules are documented in Workflow Configuration.

docs.title: 3. Providing Tools
docs.text:
The my_tools.CountWords in the example configuration must be an importable, zero-argument instantiable tool class. It is recommended to inherit from UCTool, define parameters using Pydantic BaseModel, and implement the real _run behavior.

First, refer to the complete implementation in Customize Tools to verify local invocation and MCP schema conversion, then register it in ex_tools. If only tasks and documentation specifications need adjustment, existing tools can be used without creating new tool classes.

docs.title: 4. Defining Acceptance
docs.text:
The above Markdown Checker validates format; if tasks also require word count, specific sections, or business rules, corresponding Checkers must be added. The Mini Example provides WordCountChecker and RequiredSectionsChecker.

Custom Checkers must validate real artifacts and clearly indicate location, expected conditions, and remediation actions upon failure. A complete, usable file existence check example is available in Custom Checker; do not use placeholder implementations that unconditionally return True to accept a stage.

docs.title: 5. Writing Guide_Doc and Skills
docs.text:
Guide_Doc should describe the complete format and examples that the Agent must produce at the current stage, using runtime relative paths, such as Guide_Doc/project_analysis_guide.md. If skills are used:

  • The first line of SKILL.md must be ---, and the frontmatter must contain at least name and description;
  • Scripts are placed in scripts/ and executed via RunSkillScript;
  • RunSkillScript loads ucagent_python_path from the runtime snapshot to prepare import paths for Python scripts; scripts read the already-parsed runtime configuration;
  • If a skill is disabled or its directory does not exist, the stage must still be completable using ordinary tools and Checkers.

docs.title: 6. Launching Custom Workflow
docs.text:
Taking examples/MiniWorkflow as an example, the startup commands are:

cd examples/MiniWorkflow
make test
make run ARGS="--loop"

Equivalent core command:

PYTHONPATH=. ucagent ./output/ Calculator \
  --config ./mini.yaml \
  --guid-doc-path ./Guide_Doc/ \
  -s -hm --tui --loop

First, configure the model according to Direct Usage. PYTHONPATH=. makes my_tools and my_checkers in the current directory importable; --guid-doc-path specifies the custom Guide_Doc. The Makefile cleans and prepares output/; before manually executing the core command, Calculator/ must also be copied into the workspace.

When execution requires an external Code Agent, use make run ARGS="--mcp-server --backend=codex", then connect according to MCP Access. Here, full file tools are enabled to satisfy the EditTextFile requirement in the Mini task.

After launch, use status, current_tips, and tool_list to check the task; stages must pass Check/Complete upon completion. For more complete configurations, see Mini Example.

docs.title: Architecture and Operation
docs.text: UCAgent defines tasks using configuration, executes operations using tools, and accepts outputs using Checkers. The backend handles model interaction; the Stage Manager manages the current stage, checks, and progression. This chapter explains the component relationships that need to be understood for custom development.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
Component Responsibility Primary Code Entry Point VerifyAgent Loads configuration, prepares workspace, assembles backend, tools, and stages ucagent/verify_agent.py Backend Interacts with the model or a Code Agent via CLI ucagent/abackend/ StageManager / VerifyStage Provides stage tasks, manages Check, Complete, history, and skip states ucagent/stage/ Tool Reads, edits, computes, runs tests, or calls external services ucagent/tools/ Checker Determines if a task meets requirements based on files, configuration, test results, and evidence ucagent/checkers/ Guide_Doc / Template Provides run instructions, complete format examples, and initial files ucagent/lang/<lang>/doc/, template/ Skill (Optional) Provides task methods and scripts to help fulfill a set of acceptance requirements ucagent/lang/<lang>/skills/

Tools execute actions, while Checkers verify results. For example, a write file tool succeeding only indicates that the write is complete; whether the document content complies with rules is still determined by the corresponding Checker.

docs.title: From Startup to Execution
docs.text:
1. Load configuration layer by layer, parsing environment variables and template variables. See Workflow Configuration for the complete order.
  2. Prepare runtime Guide_Doc, initial templates, optional skills, and configuration snapshots.
  3. Assemble backend, tools, and stages to restore available task states.
  4. Enter the console or execution loop. The Agent reads the current task and reference materials, calling tools to generate outputs.
  5. The Agent calls Check to get feedback, fixing failed items; calls Complete to request final acceptance and progression.
flowchart TD
    A[Enter Current Stage] --> B[Read Tasks and Reference Files]
    B --> C[Call Tools and Generate Outputs]
    C --> D{Check or Complete}
    D --> E[Check References, Outputs, and Checker]
    E --> F{Check Passed?}
    F -- No --> G[Fix Based on Diagnosis]
    G --> C
    F -- Check --> H[Return Check Result or Next Batch]
    H --> C
    F -- Complete --> I{Final Acceptance and Stage Gate Passed?}
    I -- No --> G
    I -- Yes --> J{More Stages?}
    J -- Yes --> A
    J -- No --> K[Workflow Complete]

Check does not advance the stage, but batch Checkers can switch to the next batch after passing. Complete performs its own final check; ordinary stages do not require calling Check first. The "No Applicable Work" branch of skills additionally requires the current Check to pass; see Skills.

docs.title: How Stages Accept
docs.text:
• reference_files declares reference files that need to be read. Read records are generated by the ReadTextFile tool; file reads by external clients are not logged.
  • output_files declares required output paths or patterns. File existence is just the first condition; content rules are verified by the Checker.
  • checker executes in configuration order, returning a diagnosis upon the first failure.
  • Complete also requires applicable skills and human review for the current stage.

Checkers do not automatically pass just because the Agent claims "completed." Custom Checkers should verify observable facts and return specific locations, expected conditions, and next steps on failure. Lifecycle and batch rules are detailed in Custom Checkers.

docs.title: Boundaries of Configuration and Resources
docs.text:
Variables like {DUT} and {OUT} in workflow configurations are rendered after configuration loading. Guide_Doc is a file that must be read during runtime; initial templates are copied to the workspace via the template rendering process. Files listed in reference_files do not automatically imply their contents undergo variable substitution. See Template Files and Generated Outputs for writing guidelines for both resource types.

Skills can accelerate tasks, but when skills are disabled or the skill directory is missing, the stage must still have a complete task description, standard tool paths, and identical acceptance criteria.

The Master page and task management mechanism are described in Web Master User Guide. When beginning to write extensions, continue reading Custom Development Introduction and Workflow Configuration.

docs.title: Workflow Configuration
docs.text: A workflow consists of a set of stages executed in sequence. Each stage describes tasks, reference files, expected outputs, and a Checker; the Agent can call Check to view feedback, then use Complete to perform final acceptance and proceed. If a stage fails, it should first be fixed according to the Checker's diagnosis before retrying.

docs.title: 1. Default Workflow
docs.text:
The default Chinese configuration is located at ucagent/lang/zh/config/default.yaml, which currently has 20 top-level stages; indented entries are sub-stages. The runtime Stage Manager flattens parent and child stages, therefore indices used by --skip, hmcheck_set, and GoToStage must be based on the current status or hmcheck_list in the active run.

Top Index Stage Default Status 0 requirement_analysis_and_planning Executing 1 dut_function_understanding Executing 2 functional_specification_analysis: FG, FC, CK, line-by-line mapping sub-stages Executing 3 functional_specification_refine Executing 4 static_bug_analysis Executing 5 dut_wrapper_implementation: DUT creation, pytest fixture Executing 6 coverage_model_implementation: coverage groups, coverage points, batch implementation Executing 7 test_environment_implementation: env, Bundle, Mock, and fixture Partially human-checked, default skip 8 basic_api_implementation Executing 9 reference_model_implementation Executing when NEED_REF_MODEL=true 10 reference_model_fixture_imp Executing when NEED_REF_MODEL=true 11 basic_api_functional_test Executing 12 create_test_case_templates Executing 13 comprehensive_verification_and_bug_analysis: batch implementation of test cases Executing 14 refine_test_cases_based_on_functional_points Executing 15 static_bug_validation Executing 16 line_coverage_analysis_and_improvement Default skip 17 generate_random_test_cases Executing 18 verification_review_and_summary Executing 19 record_and_report_bugs Executing

In the default configuration, human_check_env_specification, human_check_env_implementation, and line_coverage_analysis_and_improvement use skip: true; whether they actually execute is also subject to environment variables and project override configurations. Formal, Vibe, and Increment are independent configurations with different stage counts and names, and cannot be applied using the table above.

docs.title: 2. Stage Fields
docs.text:
The minimum stage structure is as follows:

stage:
  - name: analyze_project
    desc: "Analyze project and generate report"
    task:
      - "Read {DUT}/README.md"
      - "Write results to {OUT}/{DUT}_analysis.md"
    reference_files:
      - "Guide_Doc/project_analysis_guide.md"
    output_files:
      - "{OUT}/{DUT}_analysis.md"
    checker:
      - name: markdown_check
        clss: "UnityChipCheckerMarkdownFileFormat"
        args:
          markdown_file_list: "{OUT}/{DUT}_analysis.md"
          no_line_break: true
    skill_list: []
    force_use_skill: false
    skip: false
  • name: Stable stage identifier. LLMs recommend using it for filtering, history, and logs.
  • desc: Stage title; may contain template variables provided by the Checker.
  • task: Task list for the Agent. Clearly specify input, actions, output format, and completion criteria.
  • reference_files: Relative paths or globs in the workspace that the stage needs to read. If required reference files are missing at runtime, fix the configuration or input.
  • output_files: Paths or globs that must exist as outputs of the stage; each pattern must match a path; content correctness is still verified by the Checker.
  • checker: Verification gates executed in sequence. Complete can only proceed after all gates pass.
  • stage: List of sub-stages. A parent stage only enters parent stage acceptance after its sub-stages are completed.
  • skip: Whether to default skip; suitable only for stages clearly not applicable.
  • need_human_check: Wait for human review after passing the Checker.
  • skill_list: Specialized skills for the current stage. When a skill is enabled and the list is non-empty, a real list/read/use evidence is required by default; force_use_skill: false makes it optional.

docs.title: 3. Configuration Loading and Template Variables
docs.text:
Configuration is loaded in the following order, with later layers overriding earlier ones:

  1. ucagent/setting.yaml
  2. ~/.ucagent/setting.yaml
  3. ucagent/lang/<lang>/config/default.yaml
  4. Workspace ./.ucagent/setting.yaml
  5. File specified by --config (defaults to config.yaml if not specified)
  6. CLI arguments and --override

When selecting a plugin workflow, its configuration baseline is inserted after the language default configuration and before the workspace configuration; see Plugin Development and Release. The project configuration search scope includes the current startup directory, ~/.ucagent/, and the language configuration directory; relative --config paths are not default relative to the workspace.

List fields (especially stage, checker, reference_files) are replaced as a whole, not merged item by item by project name. When modifying default stages, copy the complete list and edit.

Common template variables:

Variable Meaning {DUT} DUT subdirectory name {OUT} Output directory under the workspace, default unity_test {WORKSPACE} Absolute path of the current workspace {GUIDE_DOC} Runtime Guide_Doc path in the workspace {DOC_GEN_LANG} Document language, from template configuration

{OUT} is determined by --output (default unity_test) during the first configuration render. To change the output path, use this option; do not just modify template_overwrite.OUT.

Environment variable substitution occurs during YAML loading, e.g., $(NEED_REF_MODEL: false); template variables like {DUT} and {OUT} are rendered after configuration parsing. Do not re-read raw environment variables at runtime to infer the already-parsed configuration.

docs.title: 4. Skip, Rollback, and Human Review
docs.text:
Temporarily skip a stage:

ucagent <workspace> <DUT> --skip <runtime_stage_index>
ucagent <workspace> <DUT> --unskip <runtime_stage_index>

Used during runtime:

skip_stage <runtime_stage_index>
unskip_stage <runtime_stage_index>
tool_invoke GoToStage index=<runtime_stage_index>
hmcheck_set <runtime_stage_index> true

The index is the flattened runtime index; do not continue using old numbers after modifying the workflow. GoToStage can only go back to stages already reached. Skipping a stage does not generate the files it should have produced; subsequent Checkers may fail as a result; only skip if the stage is confirmed not applicable.

docs.title: 5. Checker Configuration
docs.text:
Checker classes are specified via clss, short names are imported from ucagent.checkers, and full paths can point to custom modules:

checker:
  - name: word_count
    clss: "my_workflow.checkers.WordCountChecker"
    args:
      file_path: "{OUT}/{DUT}_analysis.md"
      word_min: 200
      need_human_check: false

args are passed to the constructor and cfg is automatically injected; extra_args are set via set_extra after instantiation, cannot override existing attributes, and cannot replace constructor parameters or dedicated setters. Whether need_human_check takes effect depends on whether the Checker's constructor handles it; alternatively, set need_human_check: true directly on the stage.

See Custom Checker for full implementation, lifecycle, and structured diagnosis of custom Checkers.

docs.title: 6. Batch Stages
docs.text:
Stages for feature coverage, test templates, test cases, and line mapping use UnityChipBatchTask to manage progress. When configuring batch tasks:

  • Set batch_size before constructing UnityChipBatchTask;
  • Use the current source document and test files as the source of truth; checkpoints are only for recovery;
  • Resynchronize source/generated tasks after source file changes, delete or mark expired tasks;
  • Complete the current batch with Check and expose the next batch; Complete is used only after all batches pass;
  • Failure diagnosis returns only a bounded missing range and the next step; do not dump the entire source or logs into the prompt.

The functional line mapping stage has additional constraints: file_list is the authoritative input; do not treat Guide_Doc as a mapping target; every non-empty physical line must have FG/FC/CK or a justified IGNORE; an interval can have at most 100 lines. See Guide_Doc/dut_line_func_map.md and functional_line_mapping_gap_analysis in the default configuration.

docs.title: 7. Custom Workflows
docs.text:
Do not modify default.yaml directly within the package. Instead, copy the complete stage list that needs modification in the project configuration, or use --override for targeted temporary overrides:

ucagent <workspace> <DUT> \
  --config config.yaml \
  --override 'runtime_options.need_ref_model=True'

When adding a new stage, provide the task, reference document, output, and Checker simultaneously; if the stage requires skills, ensure that the same goal can still be achieved using standard tools and Checker when skills are disabled. Stage-specific skills, Guide_Doc, templates, and scripts collectively form the runtime contract, and any change at any layer should be tested synchronously.

docs.title: 8. Runtime Snapshot
docs.text:
After configuration parsing, UCAgent writes .ucagent/runtime_config.json to the workspace. It contains only parsed, non-sensitive fields, such as DUT, OUT, runtime_options, current_test_report, and ucagent_python_path. Skill scripts should read this snapshot; do not guess the source code path from the script location or re-interpret environment variables. The ucagent_python_path in the snapshot must be an absolute path containing the current ucagent/__init__.py.

Next: Run the Mini Example first, then learn Custom Tools, Template Files, and Plugins as needed.

docs.title: Template Files and Generated Artifacts
docs.text: Templates and Guide_Doc are inputs to stage tasks. They instruct the Agent on what to generate, the format to use, and which conditions the Checker will verify; they themselves are not test results and cannot replace the Checker or test evidence.

docs.title: Relevant Directories in the Workspace
docs.text:
Using output/ as the workspace and the default output directory unity_test/ as an example:

output/
├── <DUT>/                  # DUT source code, README, and input materials
├── Guide_Doc/              # Runtime-copied guidance documents
├── unity_test/             # Documents, tests, and coverage definitions generated by the workflow
│   └── tests/              # pytest/toffee test files
├── uc_test_report/         # Reports generated by test tools (if tests are run)
└── .ucagent/               # Runtime configuration snapshots, history, and state

The --output flag can change the directory name of unity_test/. Specific files are determined by the current stage's configuration, template, and Checker, so do not treat the complete file tree from a single example as the fixed output for all workflows.

docs.title: Guide_Doc
docs.text:
Files in Guide_Doc/ are runtime reference materials, typically sourced from ucagent/lang/<lang>/doc/Guide_Doc/ or a custom --guid-doc-path. A stage can declare required files via reference_files; before the Complete state is reached, the stage's reference files and output files must satisfy the gate. Custom directories override the built-in Guide_Doc source (the last specified directory takes effect); file parameters are appended to the copy set by filename.

Guide_Doc should clearly specify:

  • The objective of the current stage, available inputs, and allowed write paths;
  • The complete format, field order, tags, and evidence requirements of the artifacts;
  • A complete reference example from title to end;
  • How to check inputs, fix artifacts, and re-call Check upon failure.

Runtime paths are always relative to the workspace. For example, when referencing a file in a prompt, write Guide_Doc/dut_test_case.md section 3, not the absolute path of this repository.

docs.title: Generation Templates
docs.text: Templates are initial files copied or rendered into the workspace. The template directory can be specified at startup using --template-dir, and existing targets can be overwritten using --template-overwrite. Template override configuration is passed via --template-cfg-override <yaml>; it handles only template variables and does not alter the stage Checker's judgment rules.

docs.title: Common Artifacts
docs.text:
The default UnityTest workflow typically generates the following categories of content in unity_test/, depending on whether the current stage is enabled:

  • *_basic_info.md, *_verification_needs_and_plan.md: DUT information, verification needs, and plans;
  • *_functions_and_checks.md: FG/FC/CK functional models, referenced by test and coverage definitions;
  • tests/*_api.py, tests/test_*.py: test interfaces, fixtures, and test cases;
  • *_function_coverage_def.py: functional coverage groups, coverage points, and sampling definitions;
  • *_line_coverage_analysis.md: line coverage results and regression analysis (requires corresponding stage configuration);
  • *_bug_analysis.md, *_test_summary.md: bug evidence and test summary (requires corresponding stage configuration).

uc_test_report/ is typically generated by RunUnityChipTest or the project's own Make targets and may include HTML and JSON reports. Only after tests are actually run can pass rates and coverage from the reports be treated as results.

docs.title: How to Add a Custom Guide_Doc
docs.text:
Create files in the workflow directory, for example:

MyWorkflow/
├── Guide_Doc/
│   └── project_analysis_guide.md
└── config.yaml

Declare it in the stage:

stage:
  - name: analyze_project
    desc: "Analyze project"
    reference_files:
      - "Guide_Doc/project_analysis_guide.md"
    output_files:
      - "{OUT}/{DUT}_analysis.md"
    task:
      - "Read Guide_Doc/project_analysis_guide.md"
      - "Write analysis results to {OUT}/{DUT}_analysis.md"

Paths in stage configuration are relative to the workspace; template variables such as {DUT} and {OUT} are replaced after configuration parsing. If a referenced file does not exist, is not read, or an output file is not generated, the stage check will fail and return the paths that need fixing.

docs.title: Tips for Writing Templates
docs.text:
1. Define the structure the machine needs to check first, then add explanatory text. Field names, heading levels, and tags must be unique and stable.
  2. Show the true end state in a complete example; do not provide only fragments and let the Agent infer missing sections.
  3. Clearly specify when optional branches are used, avoiding normal results like "no bugs" or "no coverage data" being mistakenly written as failures.
  4. Templates describe only the current contract. When formats change, update Guide_Doc, task prompts, Checker, skill assets, and tests in sync.
  5. Do not place API keys, access tokens, or other secrets in templates; runtime snapshots should only store non-sensitive configurations.

docs.title: MiniWorkflow Example
docs.text:
The minimal runnable example is located in the repository's examples/MiniWorkflow. It includes:

  • Guide_Doc/: stage reference documents;
  • mini.yaml: definition of two stages, tools, and Checker;
  • my_tools.py and my_checkers.py: extended implementations;
  • Makefile: prepares output/ and launches UCAgent.

Read Custom Development Quick Start first, then run the Mini Example. For modifying tools or Checker, refer to Customizing Tools and Checkers respectively.

docs.title: Custom Tools
docs.text: Tools provide the capabilities required for an Agent to execute tasks, such as parsing files, statistical analysis, running simulations, or accessing domain services. It is recommended to inherit UCTool to obtain call counting, timeout handling, progress feedback, and MCP conversion support; acceptance rules are located in Checker.

docs.title: A Runnable Tool
docs.text:
Save the following code as an importable my_tools.py:

"""Example tool that greets a named recipient."""

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from ucagent.tools.uctool import UCTool


class HelloArgs(BaseModel):
    """Arguments accepted by the Hello tool."""

    who: str = Field(min_length=1, description="Name of the recipient")


class HelloTool(UCTool):
    """Return a greeting for a named recipient."""

    name: str = "Hello"
    description: str = "Return a greeting for the specified recipient."
    args_schema: type[BaseModel] = HelloArgs

    def _run(self, who: str, run_manager=None) -> dict:
        """Build the greeting without external side effects."""
        return {"greeting": f"Hello, {who}!"}

Tools should have a unique name, a clear description, and an args_schema with field descriptions. Returning strings or structured data is acceptable; however, if the Agent needs to continue using fields, a dictionary should be returned as a priority. Do not perform actual tasks in the constructor.

docs.title: Registration and Invocation
docs.text:
Ensure the module is importable in the UCAgent startup environment, for example by using --append-py-path <module-directory>. Then register it in the project configuration:

ex_tools:
  - my_tools.HelloTool

Temporary registration can be done using --ex-tools my_tools.HelloTool. Both configuration and CLI external tools are assembled; the ex_tools list across configuration files still follows the overall replacement rule. Tool classes or factories must support zero-argument invocation.

Built-in short names are exported from ucagent.tools and are currently maintained via lazy export mapping in ucagent/tools/__init__.py. Project tools typically use the full module path. When runtime context, package resources, or independent distribution are required, use plugins.

Local testing:

from my_tools import HelloTool
from ucagent.tools.uctool import to_mcp_tool

tool = HelloTool()
assert tool.invoke({"who": "UCAgent"}) == {"greeting": "Hello, UCAgent!"}
mcp_tool = to_mcp_tool(tool)
assert mcp_tool.name == "Hello"

After startup, you can view tools using tool_list and invoke them using tool_invoke Hello who='UCAgent'.

docs.title: File Paths and Permissions
docs.text:
File tools should use the path and permission validation from BaseReadWrite to avoid relying on the current process directory or calling os.path.abspath() directly on user input:

"""Example workspace-aware text statistics tool."""

from pathlib import Path
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from ucagent.tools.fileops import BaseReadWrite
from ucagent.tools.uctool import UCTool


class TextLengthArgs(BaseModel):
    """Workspace-relative text file to inspect."""

    path: str = Field(description="Workspace-relative UTF-8 text file path")


class TextLength(UCTool, BaseReadWrite):
    """Count characters in a validated workspace file."""

    name: str = "TextLength"
    description: str = "Count characters in a UTF-8 text file inside the workspace."
    args_schema: type[BaseModel] = TextLengthArgs

    def _run(self, path: str, run_manager=None) -> dict:
        """Validate the input file and return its character count."""
        ok, error, real_path = self.check_file(path)
        if not ok:
            return {"error": error, "next_action": "provide an existing workspace-relative file"}
        try:
            text = Path(real_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (OSError, UnicodeError) as exc:
            return {"error": str(exc), "next_action": "provide a readable UTF-8 text file"}
        return {"path": path, "characters": len(text)}

The example above also requires initializing the workspace context and cannot be used directly as a zero-argument ex_tools. For independent testing, first execute tool = TextLength(), then call tool.init_base_rw(workspace, write_dirs=[], un_write_dirs=[]). It is recommended to use the plugin tool factory for formal extensions to receive the workspace and read/write strategy to complete initialization; standard ex_tools assemblers do not automatically inject these values.

get_real_path resolves workspace-relative paths; check_file validates the file and returns (ok, error, real_path). Write tools must use check_file(path, for_write=True, allow_missing=True) and handle parent directories, existing files, and rollback on failure. Do not bypass configured writable or no-write directories.

docs.title: Exposure via MCP
docs.text:
The to_mcp_tool function requires args_schema to be a Pydantic BaseModel and does not support LangChain injected arguments. Once added to the external tools list, the tool will be exposed via UCAgent's MCP Server:

  • --mcp-server: Includes the file operations tool group.
  • --mcp-server-no-file-tools: Omits this group; the basic ReadTextFile and external tools are still exposed, so custom tools must adhere to permissions themselves.
  • Default endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:5000/mcp, where the address is controlled by the MCP host/port parameters.

The console can also execute start_mcp_server [host] [port] or start_mcp_server --no-file-ops [host] [port].

The following example uses the MCP SDK installed as a dependency of UCAgent, without needing to install the fastmcp client package separately:

"""Call the Hello tool on a running UCAgent MCP server."""

import asyncio
from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamable_http_client


async def main():
    """Discover tools and invoke Hello within the client session."""
    async with streamable_http_client("http://127.0.0.1:5000/mcp") as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            print(await session.list_tools())
            print(await session.call_tool("Hello", {"who": "UCAgent"}))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Long Tasks and Debugging
docs.text:
Long tasks can report progress by calling self.put_alive_data(message) within _run. For MCP calls requiring log pushing, sync_block_log_to_client can be enabled. The default tool timeout in UCAgent comes from call_time_out in setting.yaml; the client also needs to configure sufficient call timeouts.

If a tool is not found, first check module imports, zero-argument construction, ex_tools, ignore lists, and args_schema. If a call fails, then check input paths, permissions, dependencies, and timeouts. Tests should cover success, missing files, invalid paths, and erroneous inputs, verifying both local invocation and MCP conversion.

For tool implementations in a complete workflow, see Mini Example; context and delivery methods for independent extensions are covered in Plugin Development and Release.

docs.title: Tool List
docs.text: This page lists the primary tools by purpose. The actually available tools are determined by the workflow, plugin, skill switch, and tool filter configuration; names and parameters are subject to the schema of this run. Use tool_list in the console to view current tools; see Customize Tools for custom implementations.

docs.title: Phases and Verification
docs.text:
Tool Purpose RoleInfo Retrieve role, system task, and constraints Status / CurrentTips / Detail View phase status, current task tips, and detailed information Check Check current phase; batch phases can advance to the next batch upon passing Complete Execute final checks and applicable gates; advance phase upon success GoToStage Return to a previously reached phase KillCheck Abort an ongoing check StageJournal / AllStageJournal / SetCurrentStageJournal Read or record phase logs StageDiff / StageCommit View or record phase artifact changes HumanHelp Request human assistance Exit Request exit according to current task rules

Check and Complete are not success declarations: they read the current artifacts and execute the Checker. The stage_args parameter in arguments is used for additional inputs supported by the current Checker; full_output: true can request the raw check result. See Workflow Configuration for verification rules.

docs.title: Files and Text
docs.text:
All paths should be relative to the current workspace. Writes are subject to UCAgent's writable directory and no-write configuration constraints.

Tool Purpose and Key Parameters ReadTextFile Read text; path, start (1-based), count. Also serves as phase reference files and skill read records ReadBinFile Read byte range of binary files PathList List directory structure by depth FindFiles Find files by filename pattern SearchText Search text or regex, with optional file, hit count, and context range limits EditTextFile Create or overwrite full text; supports append and expected_sha256 for concurrent modification checks ReplaceStringInFile Precisely replace unique non-empty text; supports line_blocks limit, SHA-256, and dry_run DeleteTextLines Delete single lines or closed intervals by physical line number from pre-deletion snapshot; supports SHA-256 CopyFile / MoveFile Copy or move files, with option to specify overwrite behavior DeleteFile Delete file; path and confirmation parameters provided by schema CreateDirectory Create directory GetFileInfo View file size, modification time, and other information

Example for DeleteTextLines.line_blocks: [1, [10, 20]] deletes line 1 and lines 10–20; [10, 20] deletes only two single lines. All ranges reference the original file; any out-of-bounds access will reject the entire operation. For ReplaceStringInFile, search blocks use nested closed intervals, e.g., [[10, 20]], requiring uniqueness across all specified blocks.

It is recommended to read files first and record SHA-256, then submit modifications; re-read and redo edits if concurrent conflicts occur.

docs.title: Testing, Commands, and Workspace
docs.text:
Tool Purpose RunPyTest Run Python tests, providing pytest parameters and timeout, and select stdout/stderr return RunUnityChipTest Run UnityChip/toffee tests and generate corresponding reports RunTestCases Run a set of test cases supported by the phase RunBashCommand Execute Bash commands in the workspace; ignored by default in tool filter configuration WorkDiff / WorkCommit View Git workspace differences or commit allowed files; ignored by default

Do not register test infrastructure errors as DUT bugs. Failed test cases that truly expose DUT defects should retain assertions and record evidence according to the current workflow.

The timeout input for RunPyTest defaults to 15 seconds; UCAgent also sets the tool-level call_time_out, defaulting to 300 seconds. Long tasks must consider both tool and client timeouts; specific behavior follows actual call configuration.

docs.title: Waveform Evidence
docs.text:
Tool Purpose WaveInfo Find test waveforms, analyze signals and clock alignment, and generate verifiable evidence receipts ApplyWaveInfoEvidence Update central waveform records in bug documents using verified receipts ReviewWaveInfoEvidenceBatch Prepare a batch of waveform contexts for review and atomically apply results after full audit

Waveform tools depend on the optional wavekit. Phases requiring waveform evidence must have dependencies and real test data. Exploratory queries cannot replace complete evidence; parameters, TC nodes, and bug document formats follow the current tool schema and runtime Guide_Doc/dut_bug_analysis.md.

By default, analysis files are selected in FST, VCD, FSDB order; runtime_options.waveform_analysis_format_priority can be configured. FSDB runtime dependencies, browser limitations, and readers for other formats are documented in Waveform Analysis Formats and Extensions.

docs.title: Skills, Planning, and Retrieval
docs.text:
Tool Purpose ListSkill / RunSkillScript / SetSkillUsage List skills, execute scripts, and register current phase skill evidence; see Skills CreateToDo Create or overwrite a plan, requiring 2–20 steps CompleteToDoSteps / UndoToDoSteps Complete or undo steps by index starting from 1 ResetToDo / GetToDoSummary / ToDoState Clear plan, read summary, or get status SemanticSearchInGuidDoc Perform semantic search on running guides and project reference materials MemoryPut / MemoryGet Write or retrieve memory by scope

ToDo tools require corresponding options to be enabled. Retrieval and memory tools depend on embedded models; currently disabled by default in CLI, can be enabled with --no-embed-tools false. Planning, memory, and skill usage cannot replace Checker verification.

docs.title: Assembly and MCP Scope
docs.text:
The --mcp-server-no-file-tools option omits the file operation tool group, retaining basic ReadTextFile, phase tools, and registered extension tools. Therefore, this option does not prohibit all file writes: external clients and custom tools must each comply with workspace permissions.

The default tools.ignore_tools configuration includes RunBashCommand, WorkDiff, and WorkCommit. Filter rules are jointly determined by tools.ignore_tools and tools.selected_tools; adjustments should be confirmed via tool_list and MCP tool discovery results. CLI options are documented in Parameter Description.

docs.title: Custom Checker
docs.text: A Checker is a deterministic gate for stages. After an Agent generates or modifies artifacts, you can call Check to receive feedback; a stage can only advance to Complete once all Checkers, referenced files, and output file gates pass. Checkers are responsible only for verifying facts and should not treat "appears complete" as a pass.

docs.title: When to Use a Custom Checker
docs.text:
Built-in Checkers are suitable for common Markdown, file, test, coverage, and batch task checks. When verifying business rules, you can write a custom Checker, such as:

  • Documents must contain specified titles and fields;
  • Generated configurations must reference existing files;
  • Every test item in a batch must have a corresponding artifact;
  • External commands must return success, and their output must meet explicit conditions.

Checkers should verify observable files, configurations, or command results. Do not rely solely on progress markers written by the Agent in documents, and do not relax test assertions just to allow a stage to pass.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
When VerifyStage creates a Checker, it passes the args from the configuration and the current cfg to the constructor, then sets the workspace and stage. The Stage Manager injects these later; therefore:

  1. __init__ must call super().__init__() first, only storing parameters and creating lightweight objects;
  2. Initialization depending on workspace, stage, Stage Manager, or file scanning should be placed in on_init();
  3. do_check performs real-time verification and returns (bool, result);
  4. get_template_data() can only return cached state and cannot scan files, advance batches, or write checkpoints;
  5. Every overridden do_check must have a meaningful docstring, as it will be displayed in stage information.

Minimal structure:

from pathlib import Path

from ucagent.checkers.base import Checker


class FileExistsChecker(Checker):
    """Check if the target file exists within the workspace."""

    def __init__(self, path: str, **kwargs):
        """Store the artifact path and optional human-review setting."""
        super().__init__()
        self.path = path
        self.set_human_check_needed(kwargs.get("need_human_check", False))

    def on_init(self):
        """Prepare cache state related to the stage."""
        return super().on_init()

    def do_check(self, is_complete=False, **kwargs) -> tuple[bool, object]:
        """Check the target file and return a pass result or structured diagnosis."""
        root = Path(self.workspace).resolve()
        target = (root / self.path).resolve()
        if Path(self.path).is_absolute() or not target.is_relative_to(root):
            return False, {
                "error_code": "INVALID_ARTIFACT_PATH",
                "error": "artifact path must be relative and remain inside workspace",
                "artifact": self.path,
                "next_action": "configure a workspace-relative artifact path",
            }
        if not target.is_file():
            return False, {
                "error_code": "FILE_MISSING",
                "error": f"required artifact is missing: {self.path}",
                "artifact": self.path,
                "expected": "a regular file",
                "next_action": "create the file, then call Check again",
            }
        return True, {"artifact": self.path}

get_path is used to append relative paths to the workspace but cannot replace full boundary checks. When receiving variable paths, you should resolve the real path as in the example above and confirm it remains within the workspace, including symbolic links pointing to targets.

docs.title: Configuring a Checker
docs.text:
Stage configuration specifies the class via clss, passes args to the constructor, and sets extra_args after instantiation via set_extra. Short names are exported from ucagent.checkers; custom classes use the full import path:

stage:
  - name: generate_documentation
    desc: "Generate project documentation"
    task:
      - "Read project materials and write documentation"
    output_files:
      - "{OUT}/{DUT}_documentation.md"
    checker:
      - name: required_sections
        clss: "examples.MiniWorkflow.my_checkers.RequiredSectionsChecker"
        args:
          file_path: "{OUT}/{DUT}_documentation.md"
          required_sections:
            - "Project Overview"
            - "Function Description"
          need_human_check: false

args in the configuration are automatically augmented with the current cfg; custom constructors receive it or other optional parameters via **kwargs. List fields are replaced entirely at each level, so when copying configuration, write out the full Checker list.

docs.title: Diagnosis Results
docs.text:
Return a concise result on pass. On failure, if a fix method can be determined, return a bounded structured diagnosis containing at least:

  • error_code: a stable machine-readable code;
  • error: the specific issue;
  • next_action: the next step to execute, such as a fix or tool call;
  • artifact, location, observed, expected: provide these when helpful, keeping content bounded.
return False, {
    "error_code": "DOCUMENT_TOO_SHORT",
    "error": "the document contains 450 words; at least 500 are required",
    "artifact": "unity_test/Adder_analysis.md",
    "observed": {"word_count": 450},
    "expected": {"minimum_word_count": 500},
    "next_action": "add at least 50 words of relevant content, then call Check",
}

If the result needs to retain the original command output, place the bounded diagnosis in the diagnostic field and limit the raw output to a reasonable size. Do not guess failure summaries from ordinary error, details, STDOUT, or STDERR fields; stage management will retain raw results without complete diagnoses. Callers can pass {"full_output": true} in stage_args to request the raw result simultaneously.

The is_complete parameter in do_check distinguishes intermediate Check from final Complete. Do not declare all batches complete prematurely in Check, and do not treat intermediate progress as final verification.

docs.title: Batch Checker
docs.text:
When processing test cases, features, or line mappings in batches, use UnityChipBatchTask instead of writing separate checkpoints and batch state machines:

UnityChipBatchTask is imported from ucagent.checkers.base. After completing input and artifact validation and synchronizing the task list, call:

return self.batch_task.do_complete(
    note_msg=[],
    is_complete=is_complete,
    fail_source_msg="generate artifacts for the missing source items",
    fail_gen_msg="remove generated items that are absent from the source",
    exmsg="read the current batch details before continuing",
)

This call is used within an existing batch Checker's do_check and cannot replace source data scanning and artifact validation. Actual implementation also requires:

  • Setting batch_size before constructing UnityChipBatchTask;
  • Preserving and synchronizing source_task_list, gen_task_list, tbd_task_list, and cmp_task_list;
  • Treating source files as the source of truth, using checkpoints only for recovery;
  • Removing or marking tasks as expired when source data changes; unknown, duplicate, or forged progress must fail;
  • Completing batch transitions with do_complete(), which saves progress and resets the consecutive failure count upon batch pass;
  • Returning clear diagnoses for empty source lists, invalid paths, and incomplete artifacts.

Function line mapping also requires file_list to be a unique set of files, not treating Guide_Doc as a mapping target; every non-empty physical line must have FG/FC/CK or a justified IGNORE, with a maximum of 100 lines per mapping block.

docs.title: Human Review and Stage Gates
docs.text:
A Checker can request human review via set_human_check_needed(True); this causes the stage to wait for human operation after the Checker passes. Stage reference_files, output_files, and skill gates are handled uniformly by the Stage Manager, so Checkers should not reimplement these gates.

Skill gates only take effect when skill support is enabled and the current stage's skill_list is non-empty. Setting force_use_skill: false makes skills optional for that stage; general_skill_list does not enter stage-mandated gates. When skills are disabled, Checkers must still be able to perform the same verification using ordinary tools and existing artifacts.

docs.title: Test Custom Checkers
docs.text:
Must cover:

  • File not found, empty files, and format errors;
  • Normal input, boundary values, and invalid input;
  • Workspace path boundaries;
  • Completeness and bounded content of diagnostic fields;
  • Synchronization behavior of batch tasks after adding, removing, or modifying source data.

See the repository for a runnable minimal implementation at examples/MiniWorkflow/my_checkers.py. For complete tool and workflow examples, see Custom Development Intro, Workflow Configuration, and Mini Example.

docs.title: Mini Example
docs.text: The examples/MiniWorkflow/ directory is a runnable two-stage workflow: the first stage analyzes the Calculator's README, and the second stage generates project documentation. It demonstrates the minimal combination of configuration, external tools, Guide_Doc, and custom Checkers.

docs.title: 1. Directory and Inputs
docs.text:
examples/MiniWorkflow/
├── Calculator/README.md
├── Guide_Doc/
│   ├── project_analysis_guide.md
│   └── documentation_template.md
├── mini.yaml
├── my_tools.py
├── my_checkers.py
└── Makefile

The mini.yaml file uses the current workflow fields: ex_tools, template_overwrite, mission, stage, reference_files, output_files, and checker. The startup command uses output/ as the workspace; since --output is not passed, the stage artifacts are actually located at examples/MiniWorkflow/output/unity_test/. When changing the output directory, pass --output <name> and verify the path using the current stage information.

docs.title: 2. Running
docs.text:
First, complete the source installation, activate the virtual environment, and then follow the direct usage to configure the model. Execute from the repository root:

cd examples/MiniWorkflow
make test
make run ARGS="--loop"

make test only checks if custom tools and Checkers can be imported. make run will clean and create output/, copy Calculator, and then start UCAgent:

PYTHONPATH=. ucagent ./output/ Calculator \
  --config ./mini.yaml \
  --guid-doc-path ./Guide_Doc/ \
  -s -hm --tui --loop

The --loop flag enables immediate execution in normal mode; running only make run will pause at the TUI, requiring input of loop to begin. PYTHONPATH=. is used to import my_tools and my_checkers from the current directory, which the Makefile sets automatically.

When an external Code Agent is required, use:

make run ARGS="--mcp-server --backend=codex"

This command does not automatically enter the model loop. In another terminal, enter examples/MiniWorkflow/output/ first, then follow MCP Access to configure and start Codex. The Mini task requires using EditTextFile, so full MCP file tools are enabled here.

You can also copy the entire MiniWorkflow/ directory to another directory and run it; the installed UCAgent will start via the ucagent command, while custom tools and Checkers are imported from the current example directory.

The example workflow does not require embedded tools by default; the current CLI's --no-embed-tools is already set to true by default, so there is no need to add this parameter again.

docs.title: 3. What the Workflow Does
docs.text:
Stage analyze_project:

  1. Reads Calculator/README.md and Guide_Doc/project_analysis_guide.md;
  2. Generates unity_test/Calculator_analysis.md (relative to workspace);
  3. Uses CountWords to provide statistics;
  4. Accepts using a word count and Markdown format Checker.

Stage generate_documentation:

  1. Reads the analysis document and Guide_Doc/documentation_template.md;
  2. Generates unity_test/Calculator_documentation.md (relative to workspace);
  3. Uses ExtractSections to check sections;
  4. Accepts using word count, required sections, and Markdown format Checkers.

All stages must pass through Check/Complete. If a Checker fails, fix it according to the returned file and field, then retry.

docs.title: 4. Viewing Results
docs.text:
cat output/unity_test/Calculator_analysis.md
cat output/unity_test/Calculator_documentation.md

The actual word count and content are determined by the model output; do not treat the word count ranges in the example as universal requirements for all workflows.

docs.title: Adding a Stage
docs.text:
Append a complete stage to the stage list in mini.yaml:

- name: generate_api_docs
  desc: "Generate API documentation"
  task:
    - "Read existing analysis and template, generate {OUT}/{PROJECT}_api.md"
  output_files:
    - "{OUT}/{PROJECT}_api.md"

Add a Checker for this stage if reliable acceptance is required.

docs.title: Adding a Tool
docs.text: Define a class inheriting UCTool in my_tools.py, describe parameters using Pydantic args_schema, and then register the full import path in ex_tools within mini.yaml. Tools must only access paths allowed within the workspace.

docs.title: Adding a Checker
docs.text: In my_checkers.py, inherit Checker; in the constructor, call super().__init__() first, and in do_check return (bool, result). Failure results should include a stable error_code, specific error, and next_action.

docs.title: 6. Further Learning
docs.text:
• Custom Development Intro: Build configuration, tools, and Checkers from scratch.
  • Workflow Configuration: Stages, template variables, batching, and stage indexing.
  • Custom Tools: Local tools and MCP schema.
  • Checkers: Lifecycle, diagnostics, and batching conventions.
  • Plugin Development and Release: Package workflow resources as installable plugins.

docs.title: Plugin Development and Release
docs.text:
UCAgent plugins are designed for independent delivery of domain capabilities. A single plugin may provide one or more of the following capabilities as needed: Tool, Checker, Skill, Guide_Doc, and workflow. These contributions are all first-level options, independent of one another, and do not require the plugin to provide a complete workflow. Plugins are standard Python distributions: they are automatically discovered via standard entry points after installation, and can also be discovered via explicitly configured search paths during source development. Plugins are imported and activated only after being selected by the user; UCAgent does not scan or execute arbitrary workspace Python files.

The plugins/RTL2Spec/ directory provides a documentation generation plugin; plugins/DesignWithPPA/ demonstrates combinations of custom Tools, Checkers, templates, Skills, and workflows.

docs.title: Co-located Optional Plugins
docs.text:
The plugins/ directory is used to maintain plugins developed alongside UCAgent and packaged independently. Installing the core package does not install or enable these plugins. Plugin development should be confined to their own directories: dependencies, entry points, configurations, resources, tests, and maintenance commands are managed by the plugin itself, without adding plugin content to the core's dependency list, default configurations, or Tool/Checker export tables.

Content Maintenance Location Plugin API, loading mechanism, license, copyright notices, general contribution process, and vulnerability reporting channels UCAgent core and repository root directory Manifest, packaging configuration, dependencies, implementation, workflows, resources, and tests Individual plugin directories Plugin-specific ignore rules, editing conventions, file attributes, and usage/maintenance instructions Individual plugin directories, inheriting repository-wide rules Core and repository public CI Root directory .github/workflows/ Plugin installation, verification, packaging, and installed-state test commands Scripts or Makefiles in plugin directories

Subdirectory .gitignore, .editorconfig, and .gitattributes files do not represent independent repositories and are not required for plugin execution; retain them only based on actual maintenance needs to avoid spreading plugin-specific rules across the entire repository. Plugin maintainers use the same UCAgent commit to execute plugin verification locally; adding new plugins does not require adding root directory CI workflows. Only when public plugin interfaces or repository-level infrastructure change should corresponding core files be synchronized.

The current co-located plugins are listed below. See the corresponding README for runtime dependencies, examples, and maintenance commands for each plugin:

Project Plugin ID / Workflow Primary Purpose DesignWithPPA design-with-ppa:unit-design-tdd Test-driven RTL design and PPA optimization RTL2Spec rtl2spec:xiangshan-design-document Deliver Chinese design and functional checkpoint documentation based on XiangShan source and RTL generation evidence

First install the core, then install plugins on-demand from the UCAgent repository root, for example:

python -m pip install ./plugins/RTL2Spec
ucagent --validate-plugin rtl2spec

Explicitly select --plugin rtl2spec and --plugin-workflow rtl2spec:xiangshan-design-document at runtime. During source development, you can replace the plugin ID with --plugin ./plugins/RTL2Spec; no prior installation of the plugin is required. The workspace is independent of the plugin implementation; selected workflows automatically locate and copy accompanying guide documents and other resources.

docs.title: Repository Policy and Plugin-Specific Notes
docs.text:
Co-located plugins use the root directory's LICENSE, NOTICE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md. General contribution processes, code of conduct, and vulnerability reporting channels are maintained only in the root directory; plugins reference these via links, requiring no duplicate files in each plugin. CLA and CCLA terms also follow repository conventions. License and attribution statements attached to third-party code or assets must still be retained.

Plugin-specific content remains in the plugin directory: README.md introduces installation and usage only; implementation structure, tests, and packaging commands are written to docs/development.md. Workflow details, tool interfaces, and troubleshooting content are placed in docs/ as needed. Plugin-specific technical notes are not written into the repository's general policy files.

docs.title: Licenses in Distribution Packages
docs.text:
Co-located plugins adopt the Apache-2.0 license from the root directory LICENSE; distribution package metadata must remain consistent with this. The source repository maintains only the root directory license and copyright notices; during the setuptools build process, the plugin's setup.py copies the root directory LICENSE and NOTICE.md, which are cleaned up after the build completes. The sdist includes these two files and build scripts; when building a wheel from an unpacked sdist, the bundled copies are used without accessing the UCAgent repository. The wheel stores the copies in .dist-info/licenses/. Actual examples are provided in the setup.py of RTL2Spec and DesignWithPPA.

Declare in the plugin's pyproject.toml:

[project]
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE", "NOTICE.md"]

Paths in license-files are relative to the plugin project directory and cannot be written as ../../LICENSE. Files must be prepared before setuptools reads project configuration, supporting standard installation, editable installation, and source distribution rebuild. Before release, verify that text in sdist and wheel matches the root directory files byte-for-byte; do not maintain a second copy of the license manually.

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text:
A plugin typically has four names serving directory, Python packaging, plugin selection, and code import respectively:

Co-located plugin project directories are recommended to use PascalCase (camel-up), such as DesignWithPPA and RTL2Spec. This is a directory style convention; the loader does not depend on directory name casing.

Level DesignWithPPA Example RTL2Spec Example Purpose Project Directory DesignWithPPA RTL2Spec File system path Distribution Name ucagent-design-with-ppa ucagent-rtl2spec pip installation and distribution metadata Plugin ID design-with-ppa rtl2spec entry point, manifest, CLI selector Python Package Name design_with_ppa rtl2spec Python import path

The Plugin ID must match ^[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$: use lowercase letters and numbers, with separators -, _, and . appearing only between non-empty segments. IDs must remain unique within the same Python environment and single UCAgent run. Plugins should not retain compatibility entry points for deprecated names, as this can cause ambiguity in discovery results and configuration.

The manifest name, the key and provider in the ucagent.plugins entry point, and the Plugin.name returned by the provider must be completely consistent. The manifest entry and the value of the entry point should also point to the same provider. Project directories and Python package names need not match the Plugin ID literally; casing in documentation examples and the ucagent- prefix are not additional loading rules. --plugin accepts Plugin IDs or project paths, but cannot be replaced by distribution names or Python package names. Workflow names follow the same ID character rules, are unique within their parent plugin, and are selected as <Plugin ID>:<Workflow Name>.

docs.title: Standard Project Structure
docs.text:
DesignWithPPA/
├── ucagent-plugin.toml
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── Makefile
├── cases/
├── scripts/
├── src/
│   └── design_with_ppa/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       ├── plugin.py
│       ├── ppa.py
│       ├── assets/
│       ├── checkers/
│       ├── workflows/
│       ├── Guide_Doc/
│       ├── templates/
│       └── skills/
└── tests/

Create only actual resource directories for release. Pure Tool, pure Checker, pure Skill, pure Guide_Doc, or pure workflow plugins are all valid. Additional contributions can be added in the same distribution later without modifying the UCAgent core package. Runtime scripts can be placed in scripts/ within the package; test and maintenance configurations belong in the plugin project root. Co-located plugins follow the same structure, with the project root located at plugins/<Project Directory>/. The loader locates the project via the manifest, independent of the parent directory name. The standard structure does not require empty directories to be retained.

docs.title: Local Source Manifest
docs.text:
The source project root must include ucagent-plugin.toml:

schema_version = 1
name = "design-with-ppa"
entry = "design_with_ppa.plugin:get_plugin"
python_path = "src"

The manifest allows only these four fields:

  • schema_version: must be 1 for the current version;
  • name: the stable Plugin ID, must match Plugin.name returned by the provider exactly;
  • entry: the provider in module.path:provider format;
  • python_path: the Python import root relative to the project root.

The manifest and python_path are used only for local source loading. Installed wheels use distribution entry points and do not depend on the local manifest, though the same project manifest can be retained in the wheel for source development and review.

docs.title: Installed Automatic Discovery
docs.text:
The plugin's pyproject.toml must register the ucagent.plugins entry point:

[project]
name = "ucagent-design-with-ppa"
version = "0.2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
  "UCAgent>=26.9.2.dev14",
  "vcdvcd>=2.3.5,<3.0.0",
]

[project.entry-points."ucagent.plugins"]
design-with-ppa = "design_with_ppa.plugin:get_plugin"

Both the core and plugin must be installed in the same Python environment. Install the core first according to UCAgent instructions, then install the plugin's local directory, wheel, or published distribution package; do not assume the example package is published on PyPI. requires_ucagent and the distribution package's UCAgent dependency ranges should be consistent, using the lower bound of a version verified in practice.

After installation, Python's distribution metadata provides discovery information. For example, run from the UCAgent root directory:

python3 -m pip install ./plugins/DesignWithPPA
ucagent --list-plugins
ucagent --validate-plugin design-with-ppa
ucagent <workspace> <dut> --plugin design-with-ppa

--list-plugins reads only entry point names and the local manifest, without importing the provider. --validate-plugin imports the selected provider and verifies the plugin API, UCAgent version, Python dependencies, external commands, and resources. UCAgent does not automatically install dependencies at runtime; missing items are returned as actionable errors.

docs.title: Source State Configuration Search
docs.text:
When no plugins are installed, add plugin.search_paths in any valid configuration layer:

plugin:
  search_paths:
    - "/opt/ucagent-plugins"
    - "{WORKSPACE}/local-plugins"

This field must be a string list, processed through normal configuration layering and {WORKSPACE} template resolution. Each path may:

  • Directly point to a plugin project containing ucagent-plugin.toml;
  • Point to a collection directory containing multiple plugin projects, where UCAgent checks only its immediate subdirectories.

Paths must exist; full directory tree recursion is not performed. Upon discovery, only the strict manifest is read, and a provider is imported only after an exact match on name. If an installation entry point and a search path share the same ID, startup will list both the installed distribution and the local manifest path with an ambiguity warning; silent selection based on source priority is not permitted.

Relative search paths are relative to the current working directory when UCAgent is started. For user-level or workspace configurations requiring cross-directory stability, use absolute paths or the {WORKSPACE} template.

To force debugging of a specific source copy, pass the project path directly:

ucagent --validate-plugin /opt/ucagent-plugins/DesignWithPPA
ucagent <workspace> <dut> \
  --plugin /opt/ucagent-plugins/DesignWithPPA

Example using stable IDs for configuration:

ucagent --config config.yaml --list-plugins
ucagent <workspace> <dut> \
  --config config.yaml \
  --plugin design-with-ppa

The configuration list is processed according to UCAgent's overall replacement semantics. When workspace configuration overrides user configuration, write out the complete expected search path list.

docs.title: Provider and Runtime Context
docs.text:
A Provider returns ucagent.plugins.Plugin:

from pathlib import Path

from ucagent.plugins import CommandRequirement, Plugin, PluginContext

from .checkers import TimingBudgetChecker
from .my_tool import MyTool


def create_tools(context: PluginContext):
    return [
        MyTool(
            workspace=str(context.workspace),
            output_dir=context.output_dir,
            write_dirs=list(context.write_dirs),
            un_write_dirs=list(context.un_write_dirs),
        )
    ]


def get_plugin():
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    return Plugin(
        name="design-with-ppa",
        version="0.2.0",
        description="Pre-layout PPA analysis and design workflows.",
        root=root,
        tool_factories=(create_tools,),
        checkers=(TimingBudgetChecker,),
        guide_doc_paths=(root / "Guide_Doc",),
        skill_paths=(root / "skills",),
        requires_ucagent=">=26.9.2.dev14",
        python_requirements=("vcdvcd>=2.3.5,<3.0.0",),
        command_requirements=(
            CommandRequirement("Yosys", ("yosys",)),
            CommandRequirement("OpenSTA", ("sta", "opensta")),
        ),
        assets=(root / "assets" / "reference.lib",),
    )

All Plugin capability fields default to empty:

Field Contribution Contract tool_factories Creates one or more UCTool instances; does not depend on workflows checkers Registers one or more Checker subclasses; does not depend on Tools or workflows guide_doc_paths Includes runtime Guide_Doc files or directories when the plugin is activated skill_paths Copies the Skill collection directory when the plugin is activated and Skill functionality is enabled workflows Optional complete configuration entry points and workflow-specific resources

All capability fields are allowed to be empty, facilitating the initial release and validation of plugin metadata, dependencies, and asset contracts before gradually adding capabilities. Actual release versions should provide at least one capability or asset useful to the user.

PluginContext is passed to the tool factory after configuration parsing and contains:

Field Contract workspace Absolute Path of the current workspace output_dir Relative output directory within the workspace write_dirs Tuple of final resolved writable directories un_write_dirs Tuple of final resolved non-writable directories cfg Final resolved, frozen UCAgent configuration; must not be written to logs or reports in whole plugin_root Absolute Path of the current plugin provider package directory

Tools must inherit UCTool, use Pydantic BaseModel as args_schema, and adhere to workspace path and read/write strategies. A factory may return a single tool or a list of tools. UCAgent will reject non-UCTool instances, tools with duplicate names across plugins, and tools sharing names with core or external tools. Plugin tools enter the same standard filtering process as Agent and MCP tools; therefore, both tools.ignore_tools and tools.selected_tools will take effect.

docs.title: Checker
docs.text:
Each item in checkers must be a subclass of ucagent.checkers.base.Checker. After activating a plugin, any valid configuration file can reference it by its short name, regardless of whether the configuration belongs to the plugin's workflow:

stage:
  - name: timing_budget
    desc: Check the timing budget
    task: []
    checker:
      - name: timing_budget_check
        clss: TimingBudgetChecker
        args: {}

UCAgent explicitly passes the plugin Checker registry to the stage parser, without writing the class to the global ucagent.checkers module. Checker class names must be unique across all activated plugins and cannot match core Checker names. Full dotted paths can still be used for regular importable classes, but formal checkers declarations provide startup type checking, short-name referencing, conflict detection, and plugin summaries.

docs.title: Isolated Execution Code Generation
docs.text:
Checkers must not import or execute workspace-generated Python modules in the UCAgent main process. When verifying Python DUTs, coverage definitions, test configurations, or other generated code, use RunTestCases; if checking structures obtainable only via execution is required, use a subprocess with timeouts, output limits, and side-effect isolation.

When starting an isolated subprocess with python -I, do not rely on PYTHONPATH: the isolated mode ignores this environment variable. The parent process must explicitly pass trusted import roots to the subprocess, which must add them to sys.path. These roots must include at least:

  • The precise UCAgent import root derived from the currently loaded ucagent package location;
  • The current running source plugin import root;
  • The target generated module directory and workspace, added only after the above trusted runtime paths.

Import order is part of the safety contract. The current UCAgent root must precede the workspace to prevent a similarly named ucagent package in generated directories from shadowing the running implementation. Do not guess the UCAgent path from the current directory name, repository name, environment variables, or another installed distribution; source runs, editable installs, and wheel installs must all resolve to the same running package.

Testing for such Checkers must simultaneously prove: the source plugin can import the current UCAgent in an isolated subprocess; the target module does not appear in the parent process's sys.modules; modifications to environment variables, module global state, and bytecode in the subprocess do not pollute the main process or workspace; and import failures, timeouts, and excessive output return bounded diagnostics.

docs.title: Independent Guide_Doc and Skill
docs.text:
guide_doc_paths and skill_paths are plugin-level contributions that take effect upon selecting the plugin, without requiring the selection of --plugin-workflow. A Guide_Doc may declare a single file or directory; Skill paths must be collection directories containing at least one valid SKILL.md. Each Skill's YAML frontmatter must include a standardized name and a non-empty description, with name matching the directory name. Guide_Doc contributions require the final configuration's guide_doc.enable to be true; disabling the special runtime Guide_Doc mode will explicitly reject Doc plugins without copying files to unused locations. Plugin Skills are copied to:

<workspace>/.ucagent/skills/ext/<plugin-id>/

Skills are always optional capabilities. Setting the final configuration skill.use_skill: false or CLI --no-use-skill will skip all plugin Skill copying, tool usage, and evidence gates, but will not disable the same plugin's Tools, Checkers, Guide_Docs, or workflows. Plugin-level Guide_Doc contributions will still load normally. Stage configurations reference copied plugin Skills via ext/<plugin-id>/<skill-relative-path>.

docs.title: Guide_Doc Core Guide
docs.text:
Plugins or plugin workflows can precisely select how to reuse the Guide_Doc file provided by the current language's default configuration via guide_doc.core_copy_policy in their own configuration YAML:

guide_doc:
  core_copy_policy:
    default_action: ignore
    retain:
      - dut_fixture.md
      - dut_test_case.md
    override:
      - dut_api_instruction.md
    ignore:
      - dut_bug_analysis.md

All four fields must be present simultaneously, with the following meanings:

Field Behavior default_action Core documents not appearing in any list default to retain or ignore retain Copy and retain the core document; startup fails if the plugin provides a different file at the same path override Do not copy the core document; instead, copy the plugin-provided file at the same path; startup fails if the plugin does not provide it ignore Do not copy the core document; the plugin must also not provide a file at the same path

List items are exact POSIX file paths relative to the current language's default Guide_Doc root directory. Paths must use canonical form; they cannot be absolute paths, contain .., backslashes, leading/trailing whitespace, or duplicates; the three action lists must also be disjoint. Explicitly listed paths must indeed exist in the current language's default documentation. Plugin-added documents that do not conflict with the core do not need to be listed in the policy and will be copied normally.

This configuration follows the standard configuration layering rules: a plugin workflow YAML can declare defaults, and workspace configuration, explicit --config, and CLI --override can further override it. Lists use full replacement semantics, so when overriding an action list, the complete list required for that layer should be provided. When no policy is declared, the core defaults to all retain, maintaining the original behavior of standard workflows.

Documents contributed by the plugin itself can be selected via guide_doc.plugin_copy_policy. This policy is suitable for selectively exposing only the language or target documents required by the current workflow in the final configuration: template variables are replaced before policy parsing:

guide_doc:
  plugin_copy_policy:
    default_action: ignore
    retain:
      - "{RTL_CODING_GUIDE_FILE}"
      - shared_test_contract.md
    ignore: []

All three fields must be present. default_action and explicit actions can only be retain or ignore; path rules are the same as the core policy, and explicit paths must be provided by the currently activated plugin. The ignore action also deletes old plugin documents at the same path in the workspace, preventing the reading of expired resources after configuration switching. Whether plugin and core documents at the same path are replaced is still determined by guide_doc.core_copy_policy's retain/override/ignore.

docs.title: Workflows and Their Exclusive Resources
docs.text:
Plugins can declare PluginWorkflow to bind future workflows and packages:

from ucagent.plugins import CommandRequirement, PluginWorkflow

workflow = PluginWorkflow(
    name="unit-design-tdd",
    config_file=root / "workflows" / "unit-design-tdd.yaml",
    guide_doc_paths=(root / "Guide_Doc",),
    template_dir=root / "templates" / "unit_design",
    template_target="{OUT}",
    template_context_factory=build_template_context,
    skill_paths=(root / "skills",),
    command_requirements=(CommandRequirement("Picker", ("picker",)),),
    runtime_config_keys=("design_with_ppa.max_optimization_iterations",),
)

When calling, activate the plugin first, then select the workflow:

ucagent <workspace> <dut> \
  --plugin design-with-ppa \
  --plugin-workflow design-with-ppa:unit-design-tdd \
  --config config.yaml

Both --plugin-workflow and --config can be used simultaneously. Workflow configuration is an independent baseline layer and does not impersonate user configuration files; the final priority order is: core global, user global, core language default, plugin workflow, workspace settings, explicit --config, CLI --override. Short workflow names without a specified plugin ID are only allowed if unique within the activated plugin. Runtime metadata separately preserves explicit configuration, plugin and workflow selector, and workflow configuration sources. The same information is also written to launch_context in .ucagent/runtime_config.json; non-secret final configuration scalars explicitly declared by the plugin are written separately to plugin_options, without copying the full configuration or credentials to the runtime snapshot.

Resources and dependency fields of PluginWorkflow are optional:

Field Contract After Workflow Selection config_file Independent workflow configuration layer; must be a YAML file within the plugin root guide_doc_paths Appends this workflow's exclusive runtime Guide_Doc template_dir This workflow's template source directory template_target Workspace-relative target template, e.g., {OUT}; must not resolve to workspace root, escape paths, or overlap with read-only paths template_context_factory Optional trusted function; returns additional template variables based on final configuration and core template context, cannot override core values like DUT, OUT, WORKSPACE skill_paths Optional set of workflow Skills appended when Skills are enabled python_requirements Python dependencies checked only when this workflow is selected command_requirements External command capabilities checked only when this workflow is selected runtime_config_keys Explicitly allowed non-secret scalar paths to write into runtime snapshot plugin_options

Plugin-level dependencies are checked when the plugin is activated; workflow dependencies are checked only after the workflow is selected. Therefore, using only AnalyzePPA does not require Picker, but selecting unit-design-tdd then requires the picker console command. Do not declare speculative PyPI versions for unverified tools; instead, verify actual console commands, version output, and subcommands required by the workflow.

The guide_doc_paths and skill_paths of a workflow are appended to plugin-level resources only when that workflow is selected; duplicate declared paths are deduplicated. template_dir remains a workflow-exclusive resource because template rendering must remain consistent with the complete configuration entry for that run. Different Skill roots cannot contain Skills that would be copied to the same relative path within the same plugin; such target conflicts will cause startup failure rather than silently overwriting.

All declared workflow configurations, Guide_Doc, templates, Skills, and assets must exist and be located within Plugin.root; symbolic links must not escape. If a plugin's multiple Guide_Doc sources provide different content to the same path, startup will fail. When a plugin and core document share the same name, it is handled according to guide_doc.core_copy_policy; silent overwriting will not occur when override is not explicitly allowed. Identical retained files allow idempotent reuse. Plugin Skills are an optional acceleration path: under --no-use-skill, Skills are not copied, but workflow prompts, tools, and Checkers must still provide complete non-Skill paths while maintaining the same acceptance criteria. When template_target is specified, the renderer only includes and renders files owned by the template source, without traversing or rewriting other existing products in the target directory, and will also reject overlaps with specific read-only paths like {DUT} in un_write_dirs before writing.

template_context_factory(cfg, base_context) is called after merging at the final configuration layer, before stage and template rendering. It is suitable for selecting prompt variables, template filenames, and template content simultaneously based on already-parsed language, target platform, and other configurations.
