The return value must be a finite JSON mapping with non-empty string keys; the factory cannot override the core context. Dynamic values have higher priority than the static template_overwrite in the workflow YAML, but explicit --template-cfg-override can still override the final file render value.

Explicitly include non-Python resources in the package data of pyproject.toml, for example:

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
design_with_ppa = [
  "assets/*.lib",
  "assets/*.md",
  "workflows/*.yaml",
  "Guide_Doc/*.md",
  "templates/**/*",
  "skills/**/*",
]

sdist should also recursively include the same resource set via MANIFEST.in, as well as the local ucagent-plugin.toml and tests; it cannot rely solely on files that happen to exist in the source tree.

docs.title: Verification, Build, Install, and Publish
docs.text:
First, prepare external tools declared by the plugin. The following commands verify the same core and plugin source code from the UCAgent repository root:

python3 -m pip install -e .
python3 -m pip install build pytest
python3 -m pip install -e ./plugins/DesignWithPPA
python3 -m py_compile plugins/DesignWithPPA/src/design_with_ppa/*.py
python3 -m pytest -q plugins/DesignWithPPA/tests
ucagent --validate-plugin ./plugins/DesignWithPPA
python3 -m build ./plugins/DesignWithPPA

Other plugins should replace the above plugin path with their own project directory. The default process of python3 -m build first builds an sdist, then builds a wheel from the sdist, which can isolate the build/ cache existing in the source tree to prevent stale files from entering the release package. The equivalent uv build default process can also be used. Do not run python3 -m build --wheel only on source trees that may contain old caches.

Installation-state verification must also be performed on the generated wheel; it cannot rely solely on importing from the source directory:

python3 -m venv /tmp/design-with-ppa-verify
/tmp/design-with-ppa-verify/bin/python -m pip install .
/tmp/design-with-ppa-verify/bin/python -m pip install plugins/DesignWithPPA/dist/ucagent_design_with_ppa-*.whl
/tmp/design-with-ppa-verify/bin/ucagent --list-plugins
/tmp/design-with-ppa-verify/bin/ucagent --validate-plugin design-with-ppa
/tmp/design-with-ppa-verify/bin/ucagent <workspace> <dut> \
  --plugin design-with-ppa \
  --plugin-workflow design-with-ppa:unit-design-tdd

Release checklist:

  1. The name, entry point name, and Plugin.name must be completely consistent;
  2. Plugin.version must match the package version, and requires_ucagent must cover the actual tested version;
  3. Python dependencies must appear in both the package metadata and the Plugin.python_requirements verification declaration;
  4. External commands must provide accurate names and acceptable executable alternatives;
  5. The wheel must include copies of all configurations, documents, templates, Skills, scripts, assets, and root directory licenses and copyright notices;
  6. The sdist must include ucagent-plugin.toml, tests, copies of licenses and copyright notices, and all files required to build an independent wheel;
  7. Local paths, configuration search paths, and installation entry points must all be tested via the three discovery methods;
  8. Each Tool must be tested via direct invocation, failure boundaries, MCP schema conversion, and tool filtering;
  9. Each Checker must be tested via type validation, short name resolution, lifecycle, and name conflict tests;
  10. Independent Guide_Doc, Skill, and workflow must each pass activation tests when no other capabilities are provided;
  11. Each workflow must complete when Skills are enabled, explicitly disabled, and when the Skill directory does not exist;
  12. Installation-state tests must run from the wheel, not relying on the src path within the repository;
  13. After releasing a new version, update using python3 -m pip install --upgrade <package or wheel path>, then run ucagent --validate-plugin <plugin ID>.

docs.title: Common Failures
docs.text:
• available=[]: The plugin is not installed, and the final configured plugin.search_paths does not include the project or parent directory;
  • manifest name ... does not match: The local manifest ID does not match the provider's Plugin.name;
  • requires Python package: The current UCAgent Python environment is missing plugin dependencies or the version is unsatisfiable;
  • requires command: The external analysis tool is not in the current process's PATH;
  • resource must remain inside plugin root: The provider declares a path outside the package or an escaped symbolic link;
  • selector is ambiguous: Multiple entry points, local plugins, or workflows use conflicting names; the error will list candidate distributions or manifest paths. You should uninstall, remove search paths, or explicitly use a unique source project path;
  • Duplicate plugin Checker name: Two activated plugins declare a Checker with the same name;
  • conflicts with a core Checker: The plugin Checker class name occupies a core Checker short name;
  • Tool not in Agent/MCP: Confirm --plugin was passed, then check the final tools.ignore_tools and tools.selected_tools.

docs.title: Open Contract for Workflow Execution
docs.text:
Plugin workflows must include the specification files that the LLM actually needs to comply with in the current stage's reference_files, rather than relying solely on error messages after failure. For example, when using a line mapping Checker, the stage must simultaneously provide Guide_Doc/dut_line_func_map.md and the currently generated functional contract. Task prompts should also explicitly specify the single-line physical range using the complete start-end format, such as 10-10, rather than a single number like 10. Missing specification files will cause weaker models to repeatedly trial and error, and will count avoidable format errors as stage failures.

Stage configuration, template context, and capability dependencies are parsed and copied to the runtime workspace in a single pass during UCAgent startup. After modifying plugin YAML, Guide_Doc, or templates, you must restart the workflow and regenerate the workspace; a running Agent does not hot-load these files. When recovering or retrying, verify that the generated files match the current parsed configuration's source, hash, and language selection. Do not treat artifacts from an old workspace as evidence of the new configuration.

The command-line backend may inherently possess shell, file browsing, and external directory read capabilities. Relying solely on system prompts to require the model to adhere to workspace boundaries is insufficient. If the workflow requires testing, transformation, or analysis to be executed only by trusted Tools/Checkers, the backend configuration must simultaneously disable the native shell and reject paths outside the workspace. Reading and writing to the current workspace should still use the backend's restricted file tools, while testing and external commands should use public MCP Tools. Verify that disabled capabilities indeed return a refusal through a real backend session, rather than merely verifying that the configuration file contains the corresponding field.

Batch processing Checker stage documents are repeatedly edited by the model. After each refinement or addition, you must check that FG/FC/CK IDs are globally unique, parent-child paths are consistent, and line mapping references are closed on the complete document. Do not append a new description of the same CK under another FC, and do not check only the current batch while ignoring completed batches. When submitting refined progress, only use the complete CK path provided by CurrentTips for the current batch; after completion, re-fetch the next batch.

Batch processing templates must also distinguish between "covering a CK already declared by the model" and "testing a function already associated with a CK". Coverage groups typically declare all CKs at once before the template stage, but this does not mean all templates have been generated. The current Check only requires that historical completed items and the CurrentTips current batch have real test associations; future batches may be temporarily unassociated and must not be pre-associated and skipped. When source documents or test associations change, resynchronize progress from the current file and test report, rather than treating coverage declarations or old checkpoints as evidence of completion.

The coverage predicate itself is also independent evidence and cannot be substituted by the existence of a bin name for "condition implemented." Workflows implementing predicates in batches should write a unique explicit false placeholder for the complete CK set in the structure stage. During the implementation stage, distinguish placeholders from non-constant predicates via AST or equivalent source code evidence, allowing replacement only of CurrentTips's current batch. Constant-true callables, early implementation of future batches, and rolling back completed items to placeholders must all be rejected. Source code gates can only prove that a condition has been written; whether the predicate is reachable and matches real stimuli still requires proof from subsequent isolated pytest coverage hits.

When reusing a core batch processing Checker, first confirm that its "report passed" semantics align with the plugin workflow. Verify that the workflow can retain DUT bugs exposed by correct tests, while design generation workflows typically require all current tests to pass; the two cannot share the same final report judgment. If different semantics are needed, inherit UnityChipCheckerBatchTestsImplementation, replace only the current batch's report gate via _validate_current_batch_report(report), and continue reusing its source code resynchronization, precise node execution, checkpoint, and batch progression state machine. If the workflow does not use Bug documents, ensure _cached_document_preflight(target_tests) returns None, preventing irrelevant Bug document preflight checks from blocking test batches. The report gate must only check the status of the current precise node, CK association, and hit evidence; other CKs in the full coverage model not executed by this batch are normal misses in the local report and cannot be used to reject the current batch. When the gate fails, do not call batch completion or persist progress, and ensure regression tests cover "rebuilding the Checker after rejection still starts from the same batch."

When batch implementing Python tests, you must modify existing template functions specified by CurrentTips in-place, rather than appending a same-named def before or after the file. After each write, perform an AST-level top-level function name uniqueness check on the entire test file, and confirm that mark_function references this unique function; otherwise, the later definition will overwrite module attributes, causing pytest collection, coverage association, and the LLM's observed implementation to point to different functions, potentially hiding the real implementation behind an old placeholder assertion.

Fenced YAML in specification documents must be pre-validated with a real YAML parser. Natural language values containing colons, hashes, braces, templates, or other YAML syntax characters should be explicitly quoted; for example, packing: "element k occupies bits [8*k+7:8*k+0]", to prevent colons from being parsed as new mappings. Do not treat Markdown text that "looks like YAML" as valid evidence; when a Check fails, fix the specific field and re-parse the entire fenced block.

External tool dependencies should declare the real console command, version parameters, and required subcommands, returning a clear next step when missing, version mismatched, or subcommands unavailable. When using only Tools, do not load workflow-specific dependencies; only check capabilities when selecting the corresponding workflow. Temporary files generated by testing, transformation, and analysis should be managed by trusted Check/Complete child processes, with the stage LLM contacting only public source code languages, Python tests, and result summaries.

Cleanup entry points provided by plugins are development convenience features and should not be relied upon to determine deletion scope based on Git status. Cleanup targets must be listed output, build, and cache directories within the plugin root, and should refuse to expand scope via coverable workspace or output parameters; tracked source files and user modifications to source files must remain unchanged. Before release, verify in a temporary directory that "target caches are deleted, unrelated files are retained, and paths outside the plugin root are not touched."

docs.title: Waveform Analysis Format and Extensions
docs.text: WaveInfo automatically selects a reader based on the file extension, with built-in support for FST, VCD, and FSDB. File listing, signal query, event analysis, and evidence replay all use the same format configuration. This configuration only affects the search and selection of existing waveforms during analysis; it does not change the format generated by the simulator, SetWaveform, or test fixture.

docs.title: Manual Bug waveform replay in PDB
docs.text:
Run these commands in the UCAgent PDB console:

(UnityChip) waveform_replay
(UnityChip) waveform_replay 600
(UnityChip) waveform_replay --reanalyze 600
(UnityChip) waveform_replay --reanalyze --max-rounds 5 600

waveform_replay [timeout_seconds] uses the unique configured waveform gate with require_current_replay: true, including its dynamic Bug document and test directory, without calling an LLM. The same stage must have one matching DUT test-classification checker before that gate; the default workflow's final stage already satisfies this requirement. The optional argument is a positive integer timeout in seconds for the full test run, defaulting to the resolved cfg.call_time_out. The command works without switching stages and does not record Bugs or advance or complete stages. An active model turn blocks the command before tests or evidence changes begin.

It first runs that classification check, rerunning the full DUT suite and validating failures against BG/TC/CK associations. Correct DUT Bug reproducers remain Fail. Classification failures stop replay. It then replays each unique TC associated with nonzero-confidence dynamic Bugs once. Semantically unchanged records retain their analysis conclusions while current receipts, waveform paths, and viewing settings refresh atomically. Already-current evidence is not rewritten. With no valid dynamic Bugs, it validates the canonical empty document and reports that replay is unnecessary.

Console output and UCAgent logs use the [waveform_replay] prefix for the document, test directory, test timeout, classification result, per-TC progress and status, refresh count, elapsed time, and final SUCCESS, FAILED, or CANCELLED. Ctrl+C cancels execution. Missing or ambiguous configuration, classification failures, missing waveforms, invalid receipts, and write failures report the current operation and the complete diagnostic. Follow that diagnostic before retrying.

Changes to a TC's assertions, stimulus, or test source must fail that TC's replay even if its waveform is identical. Preserve its original analysis and re-analyze the associated Bugs. Changed test paths, function names, or parameterized node IDs must not be treated as equivalent automatically. Changes to source code, timelines, signal values, or other signed semantic inputs produce WAVEFORM_SEMANTIC_BATCH_REVIEW_REQUIRED, with requires_bug_reanalysis: true, exact TCs, changed files, and the complete review_batch_call for subsequent analysis. Follow that call to prepare all contexts with ReviewWaveInfoEvidenceBatch, re-analyze every associated Bug against the current TC, specification, source, and waveform evidence, then submit every completed review atomically and run Check once as directed. Other semantically unchanged records may already have refreshed during the failed command, with a separate progress log; each document write still follows the atomic commit contract.

Add --reanalyze to let the configured LLM resolve classification or replay failures: waveform_replay [timeout_seconds] --reanalyze [--max-rounds N]. Model work starts only after a failed check. The default limit is three reanalysis turns; --max-rounds requires --reanalyze and a positive integer. The test timeout applies to each full test run, not to the whole LLM task. Each turn receives the complete diagnostic and the canonical Bug/test guidance, reads Guide_Doc/dut_bug_analysis.md and Guide_Doc/dut_test_case.md, analyzes the current TC against the specification and source, and updates actual artifacts. Skills are optional; ordinary file tools and Guide_Doc provide the same repair path.

Confirmed DUT Bugs keep valid failing reproducers and receive updated BG/ROOT analysis and signed waveform evidence. When correcting an invalid TC proves that an association is no longer a DUT Bug, remove that TC/reference from the disproved association, retain BGs supported by other failing TCs, and remove only unsupported BGs, empty dynamic branches, unreferenced ROOTs, and unused central waveform records. Synchronize stale static dynamic-confirmation links and existing summaries/reports. A partial test report is never grounds for deleting historical findings; valid assertions, coverage, unrelated Bugs, and shared roots must be preserved. If only one association is disproved while the TC still reproduces another Bug, remove only that association and preserve the failing TC and supported findings. When no dynamic Bug remains, keep the canonical empty three-section document.

After every model turn the command reruns full classification and current replay, and validates any configured matching static Bug-link checks. It reports SUCCESS only when all of these checks pass. An LLM's claim of success cannot override failures. Logs include LLM REANALYSIS round i/N, the remaining diagnostics, and the final number of model turns. The command temporarily blocks stage validation/completion/navigation/exit tools and keeps CurrentTips focused on reanalysis, then restores their callbacks and the prior pause state. It does not run the Bug Recorder or publish records. Whenever automatic refresh or LLM work changes the dynamic/static analysis, it reloads every matching Recorder’s document view and invalidates previously accepted records, including after a partial edit followed by failure or cancellation. Submit the current Bugs again through the normal recording stage before publishing. Default replay remains available without model work; reanalysis reports a clear error for a disabled/busy model backend, backend failure, exhausted rounds, or cancellation. Changes already made by the LLM are retained for inspection and retry if validation fails or execution is cancelled.

docs.title: Default Suffixes for Test Artifacts
docs.text:
The test API template selects the artifact suffix via ucagent.get_default_subfix(dut, sub_type), where sub_type is either "waveform" or "coverage". The returned value does not include a leading dot:

dut.SIMULATOR Waveform Suffix Coverage Suffix verilator .fst .dat vcs .fsdb .vdb uvs .usdb .cdb

This function accepts a DUT instance or class, reads the simulator name from its attribute, and ignores case and leading/trailing whitespace. If the SIMULATOR attribute is missing, it defaults to Verilator. If the attribute is None, an empty string, a non-string, or an unknown name, an error is raised; an invalid sub_type also raises an error.

get_coverage_data_path(request, dut, new_path) and get_waveform_path(request, dut, new_path) return the suffixes used for unique artifact paths for each test. When creating artifacts, use new_path=True; when reporting coverage, use the same DUT with new_path=False to obtain the original path. For VCS, .vdb may be a directory; pass the full path. The fake DUT in the template phase and independent Mock DUTs retain the SIMULATOR declared in the original DUT class without needing to start a real simulator.

When adding a new simulator, add waveform and coverage to _SIMULATOR_DEFAULT_SUFFIXES in ucagent/util/test_tools.py and add the corresponding tests; no branches need to be added to the path templates. This mapping only defines naming rules; actual artifacts depend on DUT build and simulator support. New waveform formats still require registration of a reader as described in this page. Coverage parsing is provided by toffee-test, and when using VCS, ensure the used version supports .vdb. Selecting suffixes itself does not add coverage parsing capabilities.

docs.title: Format Priority
docs.text:
The default configuration is located in ucagent/setting.yaml:

runtime_options:
  waveform_analysis_format_priority: [fst, vcd, fsdb]

This can be overridden in workspace configuration or an explicitly specified configuration file, for example, to prioritize VCD analysis:

runtime_options:
  waveform_analysis_format_priority: [vcd, fst, fsdb]

The list defines the formats participating in the search: [vcd] searches only for VCD, disabling FST and FSDB. The list must be non-empty, extensions must be lowercase and without a dot, and duplicates are not allowed. This configuration follows the normal configuration hierarchy; the parsed value is written to runtime_options in .ucagent/runtime_config.json and is not re-read from environment variables at runtime.

WaveInfo first determines the latest toffee_tmp_* test session, then matches the exact test name and optional numeric dump suffix. Within the same session, it compares format priority first, then numeric suffix, file modification time, and path. Therefore, under default configuration, test_add001.fst takes precedence over test_add999.vcd. It will not use an older session to find a higher-priority format, nor will it replace the test name with a similar one. File extension case does not affect format recognition.

If the selected file is empty, corrupted, or missing parsing dependencies, the tool returns the file's path, format, and recovery suggestions without automatically switching to another format. To switch, first fix waveform generation or explicitly adjust analysis priority, then re-call WaveInfo. The format_priority in the listing and selection results displays the order used for the current analysis.

docs.title: Backend priority within each format
docs.text:
runtime_options.waveform_analysis_backend_priority independently configures the reader libraries for each format. Defaults:

runtime_options:
  waveform_analysis_format_priority: [fst, vcd, fsdb]
  waveform_analysis_backend_priority:
    fst: [pywellen, wavekit]
    vcd: [pywellen, wavekit]
    fsdb: [wavekit]

Format priority selects the waveform file; backend priority then selects an implementation for that same file. Lists must be nonempty, lowercase and distinct. A configured but unregistered backend fails when constructing WaveInfo. Override only vcd: [wavekit] to keep other built-in defaults; a single entry disables library fallback for that format. Values come from resolved cfg.runtime_options, are validated and saved in .ucagent/runtime_config.json, and are never re-read from environment variables during a call.

FST/VCD default to WellenFstReader / WellenVcdReader, with WavekitFstReader / WavekitVcdReader as alternatives. Concrete classes must carry a backend prefix. Dependencies are pywellen>=0.25.7,<0.26, wavekit>=0.7.0,<0.8.0, and the directly declared pylibfst>=0.2.1,<0.3.

Only ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError during factory construction or context entry permits the next backend. Corruption, permission errors, query errors, unsupported advanced options and failures after analysis starts propagate without retrying. Selection never changes the TC, session, file or format. If every backend is unavailable, the tool directs the task to an operator to repair the environment and retry.

The current pywellen Python API omits complete file time bounds and declared bit indices. The VCD implementation additionally scans declarations and timestamp markers without retaining trace data, preserving final timestamps with no signal changes. The FST implementation uses pylibfst only for names, indices and time bounds, then immediately closes that metadata handle. Signal values are decoded by pywellen. It loads selected signals on demand but retains each loaded signal's complete native trace; narrow windows use indexed binary search without copying every Python row. Catalog output is bounded, while native metadata enumeration remains complete. This does not eliminate large-file scanning or memory costs. Digital analysis supports declared indices, ascending/negative ranges, array paths, wide integers and X/Z; real/string variables are excluded from the digital catalog. Contiguous scalar declarations retain their original bit paths. If the binding exposes indistinguishable duplicate names, such as noncontiguous scalar declarations of one bus, analysis fails instead of guessing their correspondence. Native decoding panics become analysis errors with resource cleanup.

Operator logs use the [WaveInfo] prefix. The runtime log records backend_order, each backend_attempt, backend_unavailable reasons, backend_open_failed and backend_selected. Console/runtime analysis_started / analysis_finished entries identify the actual backend, TC, status and elapsed time. They do not dump backend_args. Backend identity is not added to LLM tool results. File inventory does not open a reader and therefore has no selected-backend entry.

docs.title: FSDB Runtime Dependencies and Online Viewing
docs.text:
FSDB uses WavekitFsdbReader to adapt wavekit. FSDB also requires the Verdi NPI runtime library libNPI.so; configure it before starting UCAgent using one of the following methods:

  • WAVEKIT_NPI_LIB: The full path to libNPI.so.
  • VERDI_HOME: The Verdi installation directory.
  • LD_LIBRARY_PATH: A search path containing the library and its runtime dependencies.

These variables are used by the FSDB runtime library and operate independently of the waveform analysis format priority configuration. If NPI is missing, WaveInfo reports to the verification task that waveform analysis cannot be performed and recovery actions are taken; the underlying exception is written to the UCAgent runtime log. Environment maintainers should check runtime library configuration according to this section. Format, reader, and dependency configurations are managed by environment maintainers. Runtime guides and tool descriptions only require the verification task LLM to call WaveInfo and handle the results.

docs.title: Metadata-based viewing
docs.text:
Viewing uses /wave/?meta=<workspace-relative JSON path> and pins the actual waveform selected for that analysis. Metadata for a.fsdb is stored beside it as a.fsdb.json. The file browser reads extensions from GET /api/waveform/viewers and posts {"waveform_file":"waves/a.fsdb"} to POST /api/waveform/metadata. This creates missing metadata and preserves existing final evidence settings.

A final WaveInfo tool call publishes metadata. Direct analyze() and replay only compute results. ApplyWaveInfoEvidence synchronizes the selected receipt's view, including repeated Apply calls. Batch refresh/review publishes after all preparation succeeds and rolls metadata back if the document commit fails. Ordinary Check does not write metadata. One current view is stored per waveform; independent signed receipts retain historical snapshots. Removing waveform/JSON files does not invalidate verified historical evidence, while online viewing reports the missing files. Links never search a newer session or substitute another format.

Example waves/a.fsdb.json:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "waveform_file": "a.fsdb",
  "signals": ["TOP.dut.clk", "TOP.dut.result"],
  "source_files": ["../rtl/Demo.sv", "../src/Demo.scala"],
  "dut_python_path": "../Demo/__init__.py",
  "test_file": "../unity_test/tests/test_demo.py",
  "test_case": "unity_test/tests/test_demo.py::test_saturation",
  "start": "100",
  "end": "200",
  "cursor": "150",
  "integrity_hmac": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
}

All file paths inside JSON are relative to its directory and use /. Parent references are allowed, but resolved files and symlinks must stay inside the selected workspace. waveform_file is a basename beside the JSON. The first five fields are required; an unresolved Python entry is null and unknown source associations use an empty list. Test association preserves the exact node ID. Final windows contain all three nonnegative decimal-string timestamps in native waveform ticks, avoiding JavaScript integer precision loss. Ordinary viewing can omit the window. Metadata is limited to 1 MiB and 64 unique signals.

Existing main DUT design files, Python entries and exact test sources are associated automatically. WaveInfo(source_files=[...], dut_python_path="...") accepts workspace-relative paths for associations determined by the LLM. Scanned source files are not all added as related material. Invalid explicit paths fail; unresolved optional automatic associations produce warnings rather than invented paths.

docs.title: Metadata integrity
docs.text:
Stored JSON requires a tool-generated integrity_hmac. The 64 hexadecimal digits above illustrate the format and cannot be copied as a working signature. HMAC-SHA256 authenticates the complete unsigned JSON content together with its workspace-relative destination, using a workspace-specific secret. Changes to signals, timestamps, associated files, test IDs or link targets, and copies to another workspace, fail verification. Whitespace and object-key order do not affect canonical signing; duplicate JSON keys are rejected. Online links must use the resolved workspace-relative JSON path, rather than a symlink alias, so browser and server resolve the same waveform directory.

Keys stay outside the workspace at the service user's ~/.ucagent/waveform_keys/, with directory mode 0700 and key mode 0600. Key filenames derive from SHA-256 of the resolved workspace path. Keys never enter metadata, tool output or runtime configuration. Verification does not recreate missing keys. Republish viewing metadata through the tools after moving a workspace or losing its key.

CMD verifies integrity before dispatch, returning Surfer metadata and creating Xpra sessions. Surfer receives authenticated semantic fields with the signature removed. The default Verdi launcher verifies again immediately before starting the application, catching modifications after opening the page. Missing signatures, mismatches or unavailable keys prevent viewing. Ordinary viewing never re-signs modified JSON. Republish final evidence with WaveInfo/ApplyWaveInfoEvidence; for ordinary viewing, remove the damaged JSON and select the actual waveform again.

Historical receipts independently sign semantic snapshots. Ordinary Check does not need live JSON or its signing key, so deleting waveform/JSON files or losing the viewing key does not invalidate verified history. This mechanism detects metadata changes by parties without the key; it does not authenticate waveform/source contents or protect against someone who can read the same operating-system user's private keys or invoke signing tools.

docs.title: Viewers and Xpra configuration
docs.text:
The resolved cmd_api.waveform_viewers mapping defaults to:

cmd_api:
  waveform_viewers:
    fst:
      kind: web
      url: /surfer/
    vcd:
      kind: web
      url: /surfer/
    fsdb:
      kind: xpra
      script: verdi/launch_verdi.py
      args: ["--meta", "{wave_meta}", "--verdi", "verdi"]
      env: {}
      idle_timeout: -1

A web URL is a same-origin page path starting and ending with /, without a query. Redirection passes the same meta. Surfer asynchronously reads GET /api/waveform/metadata?meta=..., loads the exact waveform and restores signals, window and cursor, retaining FST fallback conversion and progress reporting. Configure another extension with its own page or launcher. Unconfigured formats return 415 with a corrective action; invalid configuration returns 503.

An Xpra GET only serves a launch page. The page posts {"wave_meta":"waves/a.fsdb.json"} to the existing POST /api/xpra/sessions. The server validates metadata, builds argv from operator configuration and reuses existing authentication, quotas, ownership and diagnostics. JSON cannot supply commands, scripts or environment variables. Identical metadata contents and viewer configuration reuse a live session; concurrent creation is coalesced and exited sessions can be recreated.

Relative script paths resolve only under the actual running package's ucagent/scripts, including subdirectories. Traversal and symlink escapes are rejected. Working-directory/PATH lookup is not used. Absolute scripts are checked explicitly. Python scripts use UCAgent's sys.executable. args is an argv list; {wave_meta} becomes the validated absolute JSON path at launch and arguments are safely quoted. env is operator configuration. idle_timeout is -1 or positive integer seconds. Pass additional Verdi arguments after "--" in the default launcher's argument list.

The default verdi/launch_verdi.py looks for *.daidir/simv.kdb beside the metadata's DUT Python entry, then beside associated source files. It does not search unrelated design directories. A unique database is loaded with -dbdir, preserving the elaborated VCS design; compile the DUT with -kdb. Without a database, the launcher imports supported Verilog/SystemVerilog sources. Scala remains associated reference material. Ambiguous databases require explicit selection: add "--dbdir", "Adder/libDPIAdder.so.daidir" to cmd_api.waveform_viewers.fsdb.args before any "--" separator. The path is relative to the selected workspace; absolute paths within that workspace are also accepted. The database and its symbolic links must remain inside the selected workspace.

The launcher opens FSDB, adds signals and docks the waveform in the same Verdi window, restoring native-tick positions. Tcl queries wvGetFileTimeUnit and sets wvSetWindowTimeUnit to one native tick before applying timestamps. Unknown time scales fail rather than assuming ns or using log cycles. Temporary Tcl lives until Verdi exits; failures and exit codes reach Xpra diagnostics.

The runtime needs Xpra/X11, Verdi and a valid license. Substitute tests cover argv, paths, Tcl literals, multiple native scales and errors. Actual signal display/time positioning requires integration acceptance in a licensed environment. All interfaces preserve subworkspace selection and both Master task/agent CMD proxy prefixes.

docs.title: Surfer bus expansion and rebuilds
docs.text:
Multibit digital signals initially show a collapsed aggregate value. Click the triangle beside a signal to expand or collapse its individual bit traces. Labels follow the declared indices, including ascending, nonzero and negative ranges. The aggregate retains its selected number format and individual bits preserve X/Z states. Metadata-loaded and manually added buses share this behavior; scalar, clock, real, string and existing structured decoders keep their normal presentation.

The bundled Surfer is pinned to upstream commit 3ab79e7220f937cb3fadf1117f15d344e5f7e990. Its local native changes and EUPL-1.2 license are in ucagent/scripts/surfer/. bit_expansion.patch integrates bit_expansion.rs with native translators and initially closed compound rows; bit values come directly from waveform data.

Rebuilding requires Rust 1.90+, the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, patch and wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.113. Clone the pinned upstream revision and initialize its submodules: instruction-decoder at 02bdcbfd5663a72e4a0b1b9d54519412d417fab1 and f128 at e60de395f0d6454c1dc546b87f06a6358425b6b6. Keep the upstream Cargo.lock unchanged, then run:

python ucagent/scripts/surfer/rebuild.py --source /absolute/path/to/surfer

The script validates the lockfile, patched source and binding CLI version, builds with locked dependencies, and updates matching JS/WASM assets and their index.html integrity digests. Use --wasm-bindgen for a specific CLI path or --output for an existing preview bundle directory. Stop the service using that directory before publishing rebuilt assets.

Browser regression uses the real CMD service and bundled WASM to cover VCD/FST, Variables, full names, window/cursor restoration and initially collapsed, independently expandable buses:

UCAGENT_RUN_SURFER_BROWSER_TESTS=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_surfer_metadata_browser.py

Install Playwright Chromium/WebKit; UCAGENT_SURFER_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE can select a local Chrome. Native bit mapping tests are included in bit_expansion.rs. After copying it into patched upstream sources, run cargo test -p libsurfer --no-default-features translation::bit_expansion.

docs.title: Graphical integration without Verdi
docs.text:
tests/fixtures/fake_verdi.py is a Tk application that executes the actual default launcher's Tcl, draws selected signals/window/cursor, and records remote button or R key input. It accepts only explicitly marked JSON waveform fixtures. The fixture has an .fsdb filename to exercise dispatch; it neither contains nor decodes proprietary FSDB. Xpra, Xvfb, CMD REST, the HTML5 client and WebSocket transport use their real implementations.

On Linux with project test dependencies, Xpra, Xpra HTML5 assets, Xvfb and Python Tk installed, run the following. Containers should use an init process, such as docker run --init, to reap exited application descendants:

UCAGENT_RUN_WAVE_XPRA_INTEGRATION=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_waveform_xpra_runtime.py

The tests create temporary workspaces and private signing directories. They cover authentication, GET without launch, concurrent session reuse, quota, exit/reopen, process cleanup, metadata tampering and Tcl startup errors. Fixtures include Chinese/space/Tcl-special paths, RTL/Scala associations, a 10fs native scale and timestamps exceeding JavaScript's safe integer range.

For browser acceptance, start a fixture service in the same Linux runtime. Adjust the browser URL to the published port when using a container:

python tests/test_waveform_xpra_runtime.py --serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765 --info /tmp/wave-xpra-info.json

Install Playwright and Chromium/WebKit where browser tests run, then set these variables. Transfer the service info file's password value securely; do not commit the file or credentials.

export UCAGENT_WAVE_XPRA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765
export UCAGENT_WAVE_XPRA_PASSWORD='<password from the private info file>'
export UCAGENT_WAVE_XPRA_ARTIFACTS=/tmp/wave-xpra-screenshots
python -m pytest -q tests/test_waveform_xpra_browser.py

UCAGENT_XPRA_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE can select an installed Chrome executable. Browser tests follow /wave/?meta=... into the application, check rendered pixels and exact restored state, send keyboard input, verify reload/reconnect and repeated-open session reuse, and save screenshots. Interrupting or terminating the fixture service cleans sessions and temporary files. These tests validate transport and launch protocol; actual Verdi FSDB decoding, command compatibility and time positioning still need acceptance in a licensed runtime.

docs.title: Registering Other Formats
docs.text:
ucagent/util/waveform_formats/ is a Python package. Its public protocols and registry do not depend on a waveform parsing library. Each format implements its reader in a separate file; formats using the same library can share an adapter:

ucagent/util/waveform_formats/
├── __init__.py          # Public exports and built-in registration
├── protocols.py         # Reader, factory, scope, signal, and result contracts
├── registry.py          # Priority validation and extension dispatch
├── pagination.py        # Bounded, deterministic signal pages
├── queries.py           # Library-independent signal queries
├── adapter_pywellen.py  # Shared pywellen decoding and advanced options
├── adapter_wavekit.py   # Shared wavekit context and value-loading adapter
├── read_fst.py          # WellenFstReader / WavekitFstReader
├── read_vcd.py          # WellenVcdReader / WavekitVcdReader
└── read_fsdb.py         # WavekitFsdbReader

Import WaveformReader, WaveformReaderFactory, WaveformScope, WaveformSignal, WaveformSignalMatches, and WaveformValueChanges from the package entry point. These use structural typing: a function, callable object, or reader class can satisfy the signatures without inheriting from UCAgent or wavekit. WaveInfo consumes only this public protocol; wavekit's _load_value_changes is called only inside its dedicated adapter.

docs.title: Factory and reader interface
docs.text:
The following signatures define the essential inputs and outputs. Full method documentation is in protocols.py:

from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
from typing import Any, Literal, NotRequired, Protocol, TypedDict

BackendArgs = dict[str, Any] | Literal["help"]

class WaveformScope(Protocol):
    @property
    def full_name(self) -> str: ...

class WaveformSignal(Protocol):
    @property
    def full_name(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def base_name(self) -> str: ...
    @property
    def width(self) -> int: ...

class WaveformSignalMatches(TypedDict):
    signals: Mapping[Any, WaveformSignal]
    total: int
    offset: int
    limit: int
    extensions: NotRequired[dict[str, Any]]

class WaveformValueChanges(TypedDict):
    mapped: Iterable[tuple[int, int]]
    extensions: NotRequired[dict[str, Any]]

class WaveformReader(Protocol):
    @property
    def backend_name(self) -> str: ...
    def configure_backend(self, backend_args: BackendArgs) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
    @property
    def begin_time(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def end_time(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def top_scopes(self) -> Sequence[WaveformScope]: ...

    def get_matched_signals(
        self, path: str, *, offset: int = 0, limit: int = 100,
    ) -> WaveformSignalMatches: ...

    def load_value_changes(
        self,
        signal: WaveformSignal,
        value_mapping: Mapping[str, int],
        begin_time: int | None = None,
        end_time: int | None = None,
    ) -> WaveformValueChanges: ...

class WaveformReaderFactory(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, path: str, /) -> AbstractContextManager[WaveformReader]: ...
Interface Input and output contract factory(path) Takes a file path string, absolute or relative to the caller's current directory, and returns a context manager yielding a WaveformReader. Open exactly that file without substituting a format or searching for another file. backend_name / configure_backend(backend_args) Return the backend name for operator logs; process options once before queries. Accept {} for defaults and "help" for usage without traces. Reject invalid options with WaveformBackendArgumentError. begin_time / end_time Return the first and last inclusive timestamps. All times are nonnegative integer native simulation ticks, with full precision; do not convert them to DUT cycles or other time units. top_scopes Return the real top-level scopes, each exposing its full dotted full_name; return an empty sequence if there are none. get_matched_signals(path) Support exact dotted paths, *, recursive **, /{regex}/, and brace alternatives/ranges. Accept path and keyword-only offset=0, limit=100. Return signals, the actual match count total, echoed offset / limit, and optional extensions. Sort by full path and return [offset, offset + limit), preserving backend mapping keys. Empty or out-of-range pages have an empty signal map; invalid queries raise without loading traces. WaveformSignal full_name is the exact full path, including declared bit indices; base_name is the unqualified name; width is a positive integer bit width. Descriptors can carry native handles but must be passed back only to their originating reader and remain valid only within its context. load_value_changes(...) Takes a signal resolved by this reader, a four-state mapping, and optional window bounds. Returns a dictionary containing mapped and optional extensions, as specified below. Context exit Release files, native handles, and other resources after both successful and failed analysis. Clean up partially allocated resources if opening fails. Propagate dependency, file, and query errors for operator diagnostics.

value_mapping contains all four lowercase 0, 1, x, and z keys with integer bit values, such as {"0": 0, "1": 1, "x": 0, "z": 0}. Map each source bit and assemble the unsigned integer in declared bit order. mapped is an iterable of ascending (timestamp, mapped_integer) pairs. Retain source transitions even when their mapped values are equal: WaveInfo reads value, X mask, and Z mask separately and aligns their timestamps. An empty signal trace returns an empty iterable.

begin_time=None and end_time=None leave the respective bound unlimited. For a bounded start, retain the latest state at or before begin_time with its original timestamp. The end is exclusive: return only transitions strictly before end_time. This preserves the preceding state when a change occurs at the start of an explicit analysis window. Repeated loads must not modify metadata or interfere with subsequent loads of the same signal.

docs.title: Paging and summaries for large signal sets
docs.text:
get_matched_signals(path, *, offset=0, limit=100) returns at most 100 signals by default, covering the sorted range [0, 100). offset must be a nonnegative integer and limit an integer from 1 to 1000. total counts all query matches, not the page size. Return exactly min(limit, max(total - offset, 0)) descriptors. Empty queries and out-of-range offsets return an empty signals mapping with the actual total and requested bounds. Sort consistently by full_name within the same file; do not repeat or skip signals or invalidate descriptors from other pages.

Libraries without native paging can use the public paginate_signal_matches(mapping, offset=..., limit=...) helper, preserving keys and descriptor objects. The built-in wavekit adapter uses this helper: it still obtains the underlying library's full match mapping, but returns only the selected page to WaveInfo and the LLM. A library with native paging can implement the same contract directly without building all descriptors. Generate query extensions for the current page instead of placing all omitted hierarchy/relationship details inside extensions.

Local and MCP WaveInfo calls expose three catalog arguments, used when pattern is omitted:

Argument Default Purpose signal_query "**" Catalog query using exact paths or reader query syntax, such as TOP.dut.**. signal_offset 0 Starting index in the sorted signal catalog. signal_limit 100 Maximum signals per page, from 1 to 1000.

For example, request the second page:

result = tool.analyze(
    test_case_name="tests/test_demo.py::test_add",
    signal_query="TOP.dut.**",
    signal_offset=100,
    signal_limit=100,
)

With 250 matches, the catalog summary is as follows. The actual signals field contains the 100 full paths and widths on this page:

signal_catalog:
  query: TOP.dut.**
  total: 250
  offset: 100
  limit: 100
  shown: 100
  end_offset: 200
  remaining: 50
  has_more: true
  next_offset: 200
  truncated: true
  next_call:
    test_case_name: tests/test_demo.py::test_add
    signal_query: TOP.dut.**
    signal_offset: 200
    signal_limit: 100
    include_extensions: false
    backend_args: {}

Pass signal_catalog.next_call directly to WaveInfo; it retains the exact TC, query, page size, extension option and backend_args. Pages are [0, 100), [100, 200), then [200, 250); the final page has no next_call. An out-of-range offset returns an empty page and a recovery call starting at 0. No matches prompt a broader signal_query. waveform_info.signal_count always counts the entire waveform.

signal_query_summary provides the same counts for catalog, clock, event, and context queries. When more matches remain, it supplies a catalog-mode next_call. Clock hints and similar-signal suggestions use only the current bounded catalog page; absence from that page does not prove a signal is missing. Top-level scope names are limited to 100, with top_scope_count, top_scopes_remaining, and top_scopes_truncated describing omitted scopes.

Catalog paging is independent of the event-analysis bound max_signals. Each event query loads at most max_signals + 1 descriptors to detect overflow and uses the actual total to validate the complete match set. The union across patterns, context signals, and clocks must still satisfy max_signals. Overflow returns the true count, a bounded preview, and catalog_call; it cannot report successful analysis of only the first page. Browse and narrow pattern before analyzing events. Nondefault catalog arguments combined with a nonempty pattern fail explicitly. Nondefault catalog arguments also require test_case_name.

docs.title: Input and output examples for both methods
docs.text:
These examples also appear in the Protocol method docstrings on WaveformReader. First query one signal:

matches = reader.get_matched_signals("TOP.dut.data[7:0]", offset=0, limit=100)

In the representative output, data_signal is a descriptor produced by this reader. The mapping key data illustrates a backend identity. Related signal paths in extensions do not automatically become matches or event triggers:

from types import SimpleNamespace

data_signal = SimpleNamespace(
    full_name="TOP.dut.data[7:0]", base_name="data", width=8,
)
result = {
    "signals": {"data": data_signal},
    "total": 1,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 100,
    "extensions": {
        "hierarchy": {"TOP.dut.data[7:0]": {"parent_scope": "TOP.dut"}},
        "related_signals": {"TOP.dut.data[7:0]": ["TOP.dut.valid", "TOP.dut.ready"]},
    },
}

Use the descriptor inside signals to load changes. Assume source states are 0: 8'b00000000, 10: 8'b00000011, 20: 8'b0000xz01, and 30: 8'b11111111:

signal = matches["signals"]["data"]
changes = reader.load_value_changes(
    signal,
    {"0": 0, "1": 1, "x": 0, "z": 0},
    begin_time=15,
    end_time=30,
)

The output retains the state at 10 before the requested start of 15 and excludes the end at 30:

result = {
    "mapped": [(10, 3), (20, 1)],
    "extensions": {
        "raw_values": [[10, "00000011"], [20, "0000xz01"]],
        "quality": {"source": "native", "gaps": []},
    },
}

With X-mask mapping, the same input produces mapped rows [(10, 0), (20, 8)]; Z-mask mapping produces [(10, 0), (20, 4)]. Without extensions, the methods return {"signals": page, "total": total, "offset": offset, "limit": limit} and {"mapped": rows} respectively; an empty extensions field is not required.

docs.title: Adapting another library and registering it
docs.text:
The following example belongs in a plugin's read_wlf.py. my_wlf_library is illustrative: assume its metadata and queries satisfy the contract above, read_mapped implements four-state mapping, source-transition retention, and window semantics, query_metadata(path, page_signals) returns JSON-serializable hierarchy/relationship information for only the current page, and signal_quality returns JSON-serializable quality information. Adapt actual library objects and semantics inside the format module. If a library supports only some query forms, implement the remaining forms in the adapter. The backend constructor must clean up partially opened resources when opening fails.

# my_plugin/readers/read_wlf.py

from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
from ucagent.util.waveform_formats import (
    WaveformSignalMatches, WaveformValueChanges, WaveformBackendArgumentError,
    paginate_signal_matches,
)

class ExampleWlfReader(AbstractContextManager):
    """Adapt the chosen WLF library to the UCAgent reader contract."""

    backend_name = "example"

    def configure_backend(self, backend_args):
        """Accept defaults and describe the supported advanced options."""
        if backend_args == "help":
            return {"options": {}, "examples": [{"backend_args": {}}]}
        if backend_args != {}:
            raise WaveformBackendArgumentError('Use backend_args="help".')
        return {}

    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.path = path
        self.backend = None

    def __enter__(self):
        from my_wlf_library import Reader

        self.backend = Reader(self.path)
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
        self.backend.close()
        return False

    @property
    def begin_time(self):
        return self.backend.begin_time

    @property
    def end_time(self):
        return self.backend.end_time

    @property
    def top_scopes(self):
        return self.backend.top_scopes

    def get_matched_signals(self, path, *, offset=0, limit=100) -> WaveformSignalMatches:
        page = paginate_signal_matches(
            self.backend.find_signals(path), offset=offset, limit=limit,
        )
        page["extensions"] = self.backend.query_metadata(path, page["signals"])
        return page

    def load_value_changes(
        self, signal, value_mapping, begin_time=None, end_time=None,
    ) -> WaveformValueChanges:
        return {
            "mapped": self.backend.read_mapped(
                signal, value_mapping, begin_time=begin_time, end_time=end_time,
            ),
            "extensions": {"quality": self.backend.signal_quality(signal)},
        }

# Plugin initialization

from ucagent.tools import WaveInfo, register_waveform_reader
from my_plugin.readers.read_wlf import ExampleWlfReader

register_waveform_reader("wlf", ExampleWlfReader, backend="example")
tool = WaveInfo(
    workspace="/path/to/workspace",
    test_dir="unity_test/tests",
    format_priority=["fst", "vcd", "fsdb", "wlf"],
    backend_priority={"wlf": ["example"]},
)
result = tool.analyze(test_case_name="test_add")

register_waveform_reader(format_name, factory, *, backend="default") accepts lowercase extension and backend names without a dot. Registration does not open files or import parsing dependencies. Register during application/plugin initialization before constructing WaveInfo. One format can have multiple backend names; duplicate (format_name, backend) entries cannot replace existing implementations. Single-backend plugins can use "default"; other configured names must be registered. Configure both priorities for a full workflow:

runtime_options:
  waveform_analysis_format_priority: [fst, vcd, fsdb, wlf]
  waveform_analysis_backend_priority:
    wlf: [example]

Load optional dependencies only when the factory is called or its context is entered. Default FST/VCD implementations share adapter_pywellen.py; their wavekit alternatives and FSDB share adapter_wavekit.py. Without advanced options, query/load methods return only standard fields. New formats share discovery, analysis, receipt, and replay workflows; registering an analysis reader does not add browser decoding capabilities.

docs.title: Advanced options and help
docs.text:
Local and MCP backend_args: dict | Literal["help"] defaults to {}. Objects can contain nested JSON data; non-string top-level keys, native objects and NaN/Infinity are rejected. Options apply only to the current reader. They do not select libraries, invoke arbitrary methods/code or change standard evidence semantics. Nonempty options and "help" require test_case_name; omit event pattern for help.

help_result = tool.analyze(
    test_case_name="tests/test_demo.py::test_add",
    backend_args="help",
)
catalog = tool.analyze(
    test_case_name="tests/test_demo.py::test_add",
    signal_query="TOP.dut.**",
    signal_limit=100,
    backend_args={"signal_metadata": True},
    include_extensions=True,
)
analysis = tool.analyze(
    test_case_name="tests/test_demo.py::test_add",
    pattern=[{"signal": "TOP.dut.data[7:0]", "event": "unknown"}],
    start_step=10,
    end_step=30,
    backend_args={"statistics": True},
    include_extensions=True,
)

After entering the selected reader, the tool calls configure_backend() before catalog queries or event analysis. It passes a deep copy; a backend must not affect other calls. "help" returns only status: advanced_help, file selection and usage under extensions.backend. Explicit help is shown even with include_extensions=False and cannot become event evidence. Example pywellen help:

extensions:
  backend:
    options:
      signal_metadata:
        type: boolean
        default: false
        description: Return declaration metadata for the current page.
      statistics:
        type: boolean
        default: false
        description: Return source-state counts for each loaded signal and window.
    examples:
      - backend_args:
          signal_metadata: true
        include_extensions: true
      - backend_args:
          statistics: true
        include_extensions: true

Current pywellen signal_metadata returns parent scope, declaration type, direction, declared/selected indices, enum and VHDL type under extensions.signal_queries[query].signal_metadata for the selected page. When present, enum_type is the array [type_name, [[bit_value, label], ...]]; otherwise it is null. statistics returns source_states, unknown_states, first/last timestamps and load bounds under extensions.value_changes[signal][channel].statistics. Counts include the prior state needed to reconstruct the window start and are not event counts. Both options accept only booleans and default to false. Wavekit currently reports empty help options, accepting only {} and "help".

Ordinary advanced output follows the default-hidden policy: extensions_available announces fields; include_extensions=True reveals contents. Call-scoped configure_backend() results go under extensions.backend; other results retain their query-page/signal/mapping/window scope. Extensions cannot bypass pagination. Unsupported options return invalid_backend_args with a directly callable details.help_call, without switching readers. Pagination, overflow catalog calls, recommended evidence calls, receipts, recovery and replay preserve backend_args. Explicit extension contents participate in semantic comparison.

Plugins must implement backend_name and configure_backend(). A reader without advanced features accepts {} and returns {}, accepts "help" and returns {"options": {}}, and rejects other nonempty dictionaries. A reader with advanced features documents types, defaults, result locations, bounds and usable examples in help; validates and stores options on the current reader; then generates query/load extensions. Never return native handles, secrets or unbounded data.

docs.title: Extensions and optional output
docs.text:
get_matched_signals requires signals, total, offset, and limit in its result dictionary; load_value_changes requires mapped. Both can omit extensions or return an empty dictionary. Nonempty extensions contain backend-defined fields with string keys at every level and only JSON objects, arrays, scalars, or null as values. Do not include Python tuples, native descriptors, handles, NaN/Infinity, or sensitive information. Query extensions belong to the current query page and can describe its hierarchy/relationships or bounded query-wide facts. Do not bypass pagination by including details for every omitted signal in extensions. Value-change extensions describe the signal, mapping, and read window. Bound their size to their respective scope: max_points limits only the standard timeline and does not truncate extension dictionaries. Malformed output fails the current query or analysis and produces operator diagnostics.

Local analyze() and local/MCP tool calls support include_extensions: bool = False. The default hides extension contents. Nonempty extensions add field names in extensions_available and an extensions_hint so the LLM can decide whether to inspect them. Outputs use the following scope groups, omitting empty groups:

  • backend: call-scoped results or explicit help from configure_backend().
  • signal_queries: extensions from the latest page keyed by the exact query string, including **; page bounds are in signal_query_summary.
  • value_changes: value-change extensions keyed by full signal path and value / x_mask / z_mask channel.

For example, the relevant default output is:

extensions_available:
  signal_queries:
    TOP.dut.result: [hierarchy, related_signals]
  value_changes:
    TOP.dut.result:
      value: [quality]
extensions_hint: "Additional signal information is available in the listed fields. If it would help your analysis, repeat this WaveInfo call with the same arguments and include_extensions=true to view its contents."

To inspect the contents, repeat the same TC, signals, window, and other query arguments with include_extensions=true. The result adds extensions under the same groups, retains extensions_available, and omits the viewing hint:

extensions:
  signal_queries:
    TOP.dut.result:
      hierarchy:
        TOP.dut.result:
          parent_scope: TOP.dut
      related_signals:
        TOP.dut.result: [TOP.dut.valid, TOP.dut.ready]
  value_changes:
    TOP.dut.result:
      value:
        quality:
          source: native
          gaps: []

Query extensions come only from queries actually executed and do not require loading signal values, so signal-catalog and other metadata calls can return them. Value-change extensions come only from signals actually loaded, including alignment clocks and context signals. File inventory does not open a reader and has no extensions. An unmatched query can retain related-candidate information without treating candidates as matched signals. If there are no extensions, all three extension-related fields are absent regardless of the option. The option does not change standard events, timeline, or window.

Explicitly returned contents from all groups are stored with the tool call's signed receipt and participate in semantic replay comparison; default calls store only available field names. The central waveform record format in dynamic Bug documents retains its existing contract.

When adding a backend, test registration and analysis without wavekit, query hierarchy/relationships, unmatched queries and metadata without traces, four-state mapping, window boundaries, empty traces, large integers, omitted/optional extension output, and cleanup after exceptions. Relevant regressions:

python -m pytest -q tests/test_waveform_backends.py tests/test_waveform_formats.py tests/test_waveform_tool.py

docs.title: RTL2Spec Documentation Generation
docs.text:
RTL2Spec is an on-demand UCAgent plugin located in plugins/RTL2Spec/. The current workflow targets the XiangShan module, combining Chisel/Scala source code with the corresponding RTL generated in the same commit and configuration, to deliver Chinese design and functional verification point documentation and quality reports.

The workflow consists of three stages:

  1. Generate Evidence: Check the tool environment and source code, generate RTL, port lists, and an evidence list.
  2. Write Documentation: Organize module behavior, interfaces, and verification plans according to templates; content that cannot be confirmed is retained as OPEN-*.
  3. Acceptance: Preserve the Mermaid source and verify the consistency of the document structure, evidence, and references.

To begin, install UCAgent, then install the plugin from the repository root directory:

python -m pip install ./plugins/RTL2Spec
ucagent --validate-plugin rtl2spec

Complete input preparation, Sbuffer execution examples, output paths, and environment requirements are centrally maintained in the RTL2Spec README. After document acceptance passes, human review of design intent is still required; it does not represent SVA compilation or formal proof success.

For extending the plugin, refer to Plugin Development and Release.

docs.title: Concurrent Execution of Multiple Instances
docs.text: When verifying multiple DUTs simultaneously, each instance must have an independent workspace, state directory, and service port. Do not allow two Agents to share the same .ucagent/, unity_test/, or MCP port, as this will cause history, artifacts, and tool calls to overwrite each other.

docs.title: 1. Select Execution Mode
docs.text:
Mode Model Connection Suitable Scenario Standard Mode Concurrent Each UCAgent uses the LangChain backend Running multiple tasks locally via script or tmux Command-line Backend Concurrent Each instance uses an independent MCP port and invokes the Code Agent Tasks requiring an external Agent Master A single Master manages multiple sub-Agents Centralized scheduling, queueing, and web monitoring requirements

Running multiple instances simply splits tasks; it does not alter the stages or Checker semantics of individual tasks.

docs.title: 2. Standard Mode: Independent Workspaces
docs.text:
Prepare an independent directory for each DUT:

workspaces/
├── adder/
│   └── Adder/          # DUT package and README exported by picker
└── mux/
    └── Mux/

Start them separately:

ucagent workspaces/adder Adder --output unity_test --tui --loop
ucagent workspaces/mux Mux --output unity_test --tui --loop

Since the workspaces of the two processes are different, there will be no conflict even if both use the default output directory unity_test. Production scripts should record the PID, log path, and exit code for each task; do not delete the shared output/ directory within a loop.

The CWD override in the Makefile can also be used in the source repository:

make test_Adder CWD=output/adder
make test_Mux CWD=output/mux

test_<DUT> will run init_<DUT> in their respective CWD and copy examples/<DUT>. If source files come from another location, manually prepare the workspace or modify SRC first.

docs.title: 3. MCP/Code Agent Concurrent Execution
docs.text:
Each instance requires:

  1. An independent workspace;
  2. An independent MCP port;
  3. An independent client configuration directory (e.g., .iflow/, .qwen/, .codex/);
  4. Independent logs and sessions.

Example:

ucagent workspaces/adder Adder \
  --mcp-server-no-file-tools --mcp-server-port 5001 --tui

ucagent workspaces/mux Mux \
  --mcp-server-no-file-tools --mcp-server-port 5002 --tui

The corresponding clients must point to:

http://127.0.0.1:5001/mcp
http://127.0.0.1:5002/mcp

Do not reuse a client configuration that contains an old port simply by copying it; check the configuration files and command preview before starting. The client timeout may cover the time required for compilation and testing.

docs.title: 4. Managing Sessions with tmux
docs.text:
You can place each instance in a separate tmux pane:

tmux new-session -d -s ucagent_multi

tmux send-keys -t ucagent_multi:0.0 \
  'ucagent workspaces/adder Adder --tui --loop' C-m

tmux split-window -h -t ucagent_multi:0.0
tmux send-keys -t ucagent_multi:0.1 \
  'ucagent workspaces/mux Mux --tui --loop' C-m

tmux attach-session -t ucagent_multi

Do not rely on a fixed sleep 10 to determine if a task is ready; use logs, port checks, or Agent status confirmation. When stopping, terminate the corresponding process in the pane first, then close the tmux session.

docs.title: 5. Master Multi-Tasking
docs.text:
When the number of tasks is large, start a Master and let the Launch page create an independent workspace for each task, then launch sub-Agents via process, Docker, Docker Swarm, or Kubernetes. The Master's master_api.max_task_count controls the number of concurrent tasks; exceeding this limit puts tasks into a waiting queue.

The Master is suitable for centralized status and log viewing; tasks should still use independent outputs, ports, and client configurations. See Master Mode and Web Master Usage Guide for more details.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Port Conflict: Assign a different --mcp-server-port to each MCP Server, or use -1 to auto-select a port, and write the actual port to the client configuration.
  • Artifacts Overwriting: Check if the workspace, --output, .ucagent/, and client configuration directory are independent.
  • Task Stuck in Waiting: Check the Master's concurrency limit and Launch Queue; in standard mode, check processes, logs, and model API rate limits.
  • Client Cannot Connect: Confirm that UCAgent has started with the corresponding MCP parameters, the client uses the /mcp endpoint, and the host/port match the permissions.

See Batch Execution for batch processing and hook-driven unattended workflows; it is not recommended to copy unverified client-specific scripts from this page.

docs.title: Batch Execution
docs.text: The core of batching is for a task to exit upon completion, then start the next task; in MCP scenarios, you can also use the Code Agent's Stop hook to automatically send continue or exit prompts. Each task must use an independent workspace to avoid confusion with history and artifacts.

docs.title: 1. Automatic Exit
docs.text:
Add the following when starting UCAgent:

--exit-on-completion

# Short form

-eoc

It exits only when the Agent successfully calls Exit and all phases are completed. It does not treat Checker failures, process crashes, or network disconnections as success; batch scripts must check exit codes and actual artifacts.

Minimal serial example in normal mode:

set -e
ucagent workspaces/adder Adder --tui --loop --exit-on-completion
ucagent workspaces/mux Mux --tui --loop --exit-on-completion

Run with different workspaces; do not rm -rf output inside the loop while directories are still in use. When restarting, explicitly select a new workspace for the current task or clean its dedicated directory according to project conventions.

docs.title: 2. Source Repository Example
docs.text:
The repository provides examples/BatchRun/README.md and Makefile that can be read and modified directly. They include:

  • api_batch: Runs Adder, Mux, and FSM sequentially, copying results after each task;
  • mcp_batch: Assigns ports for each MCP task and schedules them sequentially;
  • iflow_batch_auto_tmux: Uses tmux to drive both the UCAgent MCP process and the iFlow client simultaneously.

The exited.txt in the example is a completion marker written by the Makefile itself, not a generic status file from UCAgent. Production scripts should prioritize checking process exit codes, .ucagent/ucagent_info.json, and test reports.

docs.title: 3. MCP + Hook
docs.text:
MCP batching typically involves two terminals:

  1. UCAgent starts with --mcp-server-no-file-tools and --exit-on-completion;
  2. Code Agent connects to /mcp and, at each stop, retrieves the next prompt via the hook and sends it to the client.

UCAgent provides:

ucagent --hook-message 'continue|quit'

The format of --hook-message is [config_file.yaml::]continue_key[|stop_key]:

  • Without a file, it reads from the hooks in the current layered configuration;
  • continue and quit are default keys in the built-in configuration;
  • You can also write config.yaml::my_continue|my_stop to read custom YAML keys;
  • The command only outputs the prompt and does not send messages or operate tmux.

In shell hooks, correctly quote prompts containing spaces and explicitly specify the target tmux pane. Hook schemas and timeout units differ across Code Agents; refer to client documentation.

Example command to add MCP for Claude Code:

claude mcp add --transport http unitytest http://127.0.0.1:5000/mcp

For complete hook configurations in clients like iFlow, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI, refer to their respective documentation and the BatchRun examples in the repository; do not directly use one client's JSON for another.

docs.title: 4. Reliable Batch Verification
docs.text:
Each task must record at least:

  • workspace, DUT, configuration file, and MCP port;
  • startup command, start/end time, and exit code;
  • .ucagent/ status, test report, and major phase results;
  • logs and next actions for failed tasks.

Batch scripts should stop or enter a clear failure queue upon encountering failures, rather than continuing to copy half-finished artifacts that may overwrite successful results. Before retrying, determine whether the failure is due to model/API issues, test infrastructure, configuration, or DUT defects.

docs.title: 5. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Task does not exit automatically: Verify that all phases passed, the Agent called Exit, and --exit-on-completion was passed.
  • Hook not triggered: First run ucagent --hook-message 'continue|quit' alone to check output, then verify the client hook command, tmux pane, and permissions.
  • MCP connection fails: Check --mcp-server-port, client /mcp address, host, firewall, and client timeout.
  • Repeated execution overwrites results: Assign an independent workspace or a result directory with a timestamp to each task; do not treat old output/ as a global temporary directory.

Run a single task first, then add the same command to the batch; for parallel instead of serial execution, see Multi-instance Concurrent Execution.

docs.title: Workflow Builder Documentation Center
docs.text: This directory serves as the complete entry point for Workflow Builder usage and maintenance documentation. The responsibility of Workflow Builder is not to directly complete a specific business task, but rather to generate a UCAgent sub-workflow that can run independently, be verified, evaluated, and maintained incrementally, based on requirement documents and sample inputs provided by users. When reading the documentation, it is crucial to distinguish between two layers of objects: the "build workflow" within the current repository and the "business workflow" ultimately generated into the business workspace. Both possess a Makefile, configuration files, and execution phases, but they differ in working directories, input/output, and modification boundaries.

docs.title: Documentation Sections
docs.text: Section Target Audience Main Content QuickStart First-time users Complete generation, evaluation, incremental repair, and console approval using a DOCX workflow case Usage Daily users and project leads Input/output contracts, full commands, approvals, version management, and collaboration prompts Develop Users performing secondary development on the Workflow Builder parent workflow 24 stages, all Tools/Checkers/GuideDocs, incremental evaluation, console, regression testing, and secondary development of generated artifacts Q&A_Experience Troubleshooting and long-term maintenance personnel Issues encountered during actual runs, verification methods, repair mechanisms, and design experiences resource/ Documentation maintainers Workspace, TUI, evaluation, incremental, and console screenshots

docs.title: Recommended Reading Path
docs.text:
Upon first use, read the QuickStart Overview, complete environment configuration, and then sequentially execute the run, evaluation, approval, and incremental processes. For long-term operation of new business, subsequently read the Complete Usage Overview and input/output contracts. When preparing to modify the generator, tool protocols, or Checker, enter the Developer Documentation Overview; do not infer parent workflow rules solely by reversing-engineering a single generation artifact.

When processes fail continuously, show no artifact changes for extended periods, or exhibit repeated context compression, first locate the issue in Q&A & Experience based on the phenomenon, then decide whether to continue supervision, take over the current stage, or modify Workflow Builder. Do not directly modify the UCAgent core source code simply because a business artifact contains errors.

docs.title: Three Types of Workflows
docs.text:
1. Build Workflow: Reads <business_root_dir>/input/guide.md and test_input/, generating the business workflow in <business_root_dir>/workspace/workflow/. The entry point is make WS=... run.
  2. Evaluation Workflow: Reviews tools, Checkers, process configurations, and environment facilities, and optionally executes expensive runtime evaluations. Reports are written to eval/ in the workspace and do not directly modify workflow/.
  3. Incremental Workflow: Reads approved issues and user suggestions, establishes the candidate directory for this iteration, implements repairs, runs deterministic checks, deploys, and saves old versions. The entry point is make WS=... run_inc.

Evaluation and approval, build design, incremental reports, and historical versions can be viewed and managed via the "Workflow Build and Evaluation Console". The console binds only to the local address, defaulting to port 8765.

docs.title: Directory Hierarchy Terminology
docs.text:
This document uses ~/work/UCAgent as the source directory and ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx as the case business root directory. Replace with actual paths as needed and confirm source, Python, and business workspace configurations in setup.py.

This document uses the following fixed terminology:

  • Workflow Builder Directory: The parent directory of this README, i.e., examples/workflow_builder/.
  • Business Root Directory: For example ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/, containing input/ and workspace/.
  • Build Workspace: The workspace/ under the business root directory, which is the location where UCAgent build, evaluation, and incremental processes run.
  • Generated Workflow Root Directory: The workflow/ under the build workspace, which is the independent workflow delivered to the business user.
  • Business Execution Target: input/<TARGET>/ within the generated workflow, which must not be confused with the input/ in the build workspace.

docs.title: Environment Entry
docs.text:
For first-time use, run:

cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
export UCAGENT_HOME="$HOME/work/UCAgent"
python setup.py
make configure-check

Configuration is saved in .workflow_builder/local.mk, belonging only to the current machine and ignored by Git. Command-line arguments can still override defaults:

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run

Agent credentials, model tokens, and other secrets must not be written to this configuration file; they should be injected via the current shell or a trusted secret management system.

docs.title: Documentation Maintenance Rules
docs.text:
• Commands must match current Makefile targets; do not record deleted targets.
  • Path examples must specify the relative directory to avoid ambiguity like just workspace/.
  • Screenshots must include alternative text and contextual explanations; the main text cannot rely solely on images to convey critical steps.
  • Q&A must distinguish between "causes confirmed by logs" and "possible causes yet to be verified".
  • Tool and Checker documentation must reference real source code entry points and explain core business logic, not just list class names.
  • After modifying workflow contracts, check if QuickStart, Usage, Develop, and Q&A sections need updates.

docs.title: Quick Start Overview: Using the DOCX Workflow
docs.text: This set of documents guides users from an empty business directory to generate a UCAgent workflow that "produces DOCX documentation based on text, images, and layout requirements," then executes static evaluation, approval issues, and incremental repair, while observing the entire process through a graphical console. The case focuses on how to use the Workflow Builder and does not prescribe the unique implementation of the DOCX generation tool.

docs.title: Required Dependencies
docs.text:
