Dependency Purpose Check Command Linux or compatible shell environment Running Makefile, tmux, and UCAgent commands bash --version GNU Make Unified startup for build, evaluation, incremental, and console make --version Python 3.11 or project-supported version Running UCAgent, configuring programs, and console python3 --version Installed UCAgent virtual environment Executing actual Agent processes test -x "$UCAGENT_VENV/bin/python" tmux Supervising strategies and shared terminals tmux -V PyYAML and other UCAgent dependencies Parsing configuration and structured data Install via UCAgent's own installation method

The DOCX business workflow may ultimately use python-docx, Pillow, LibreOffice, or font packages, but these are business dependencies of the generation workflow and should be declared in the generated product's requirements.txt, setup.py, and documentation. Workflow Builder does not require all future business dependencies to be pre-installed before startup.

docs.title: Files That Should Exist Before Starting
docs.text:
docx/                       # Business root directory for this example
└── input/
    ├── guide.md
    └── test_input/
        ├── content.md
        ├── document_requirements.md
        └── assets/

guide.md describes the workflow to be generated; test_input/ contains sample data for the build process to understand input contracts and create example targets, not the final output directory of the business workflow. Sample materials should be as small as possible, publicly available, and reusable, without containing real secrets or large production files.

docs.title: Four-Step Reading Order
docs.text:
1. Start the build workflow: Prepare DOCX requirements and generate workspace/workflow/.
  2. Start the evaluation workflow: Review tools, Checker, process, and environment separately.
  3. Start the incremental workflow: Handle only approved issues and user suggestions.
  4. Use the build and evaluation console: Read reports, batch approvals, view build designs, and versions.

docs.title: Environment Configuration
docs.text:
The following assumes the source code is located at ~/work/UCAgent, and the case business root directory is ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx. Replace paths if different and confirm Python and workspace during configuration.

Execute in the Workflow Builder directory:

cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
export UCAGENT_HOME="$HOME/work/UCAgent"
export UCAGENT_VENV="$UCAGENT_HOME/.venv"
source "$UCAGENT_VENV/bin/activate"
python setup.py --set WS="$HOME/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace"
make configure-check
make configure-show

Methods for configuring model connections are described in Direct Usage. ucagent_env and proxy_on are certain user-defined shell functions, not UCAgent commands; configured environments can be used as-is. The purpose of setup.py is to provide persistent native defaults for the Makefile without modifying ~/.bashrc. The WS=... in the command line takes precedence over the saved default workspace.

docs.title: Criteria for Successful Completion
docs.text:
After completing this set of documents, you should be able to confirm the following facts:

  • ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace/workflow/ exists, containing configuration, tools, Checker, GuideDoc, user documents, and environment facilities.
  • The build process is not "faked" by manually writing business products; each stage is completed by the actual Agent and verified by the Checker.
  • eval/ contains structured reports saved by evaluation type, with key issues that can be approved in the console.
  • The incremental process has an independent run id, candidate directory, and historical versions, with deterministic checks passing after repair.
  • Users can distinguish the Makefile of the build workflow from the Makefile of the generated workflow itself.

docs.title: Recommended Installation Order
docs.text:
Workflow Builder requires UCAgent source code and an available Python environment. First complete Source Installation, then configure this directory. When using other virtual environments, change UCAGENT_VENV to the actual path of that environment and confirm PYTHON during interactive configuration. Basic system tools can be installed according to the distribution, such as Ubuntu/Debian using:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y make tmux python3 python3-venv
cd ~/work/UCAgent
test -x .venv/bin/python

The above commands do not install model credentials for the user, nor do they automatically install LibreOffice or fonts needed for future DOCX business workflows. The requirements.txt of the generated workflow distinguishes between Python packages and system dependencies; install according to their documentation before actually running the business workflow.

docs.title: Two Layers of Input for This Case
docs.text:
The following paths start from the business root directory ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/. The first layer of input is the build requirement for Workflow Builder, located in input/; the second layer is the business target that the generated workflow will process, located in workspace/workflow/input/<TARGET>/. Build samples will be converted to the generated workflow's input/example/, but users should not manually create the entire workflow/ before the build.

Moment User Preparation Agent Generation Before Build input/guide.md, input/test_input/ None During Build Review requirements and TUI wfgen/, workflow/ Before Business Run Copy or create workflow/input/<TARGET>/ Local environment configuration After Business Run Review results workflow/output/<TARGET>/

docs.title: Suggested Retained Run Records
docs.text: When running a new business for the first time, record the build start time, workspace, tmux session, UCAgent version, current stage, number of stage failures, and final return code. If a stage exceeds ten minutes, also record the most recent tool invocation and target file timestamps. This information helps distinguish between normal long generation, Checker retries, context idle loops, and model connection anomalies.

docs.title: Quick Start Does Not Skip Acceptance
docs.text: The quick path still requires the generated workflow's python setup.py --check, make check, and make check_example to pass. The existence of DOCX files does not equal validity: the business Checker should at least be able to reopen files, verify structure, and generate reports. Evaluation and incremental processes cannot be skipped for approval and version history even if they are examples, otherwise users learn incorrect operational boundaries.

docs.title: Start the run build workflow
docs.text: This section prepares a DOCX case input from scratch and runs the Workflow Builder in supervised mode. The following commands assume the UCAgent repository is located at ~/work/UCAgent and the business root directory is ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx.

docs.title: 1. Prepare Business Requirements
docs.text:
First, create the business input directory:

mkdir -p ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/input/test_input/assets

Create ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/input/guide.md, clearly defining the goal, input, output, tools, Checker, documentation, and acceptance criteria. You may use the following minimal example and continue to supplement business details:

# DOCX Documentation Workflow Requirements

## Goal

Generate a workflow that reads Markdown content, images, and document requirements from a target directory, and outputs deliverable DOCX, processing reports, and structured validation results.

## Inputs

- `input/<TARGET>/content.md`: Body text and heading hierarchy.
- `input/<TARGET>/document_requirements.md`: Paper size, margins, fonts, headers/footers, table of contents, and image requirements.
- `input/<TARGET>/assets/`: Local images referenced in the body text.

## Outputs

- `output/<TARGET>/document.docx`
- `output/<TARGET>/generation_report.json`
- `output/<TARGET>/validation_report.json`

## Tools and Checkers

Tools are responsible for parsing requirements, planning document structure, generating DOCX, and reading the generated results. The Checker validates input completeness, DOCX openability, required sections, images, styles, and report fields. If tools fail, they must return a structured error; pseudo-success files must not be left behind.

## Documentation and Environment

Provide complete user documentation, developer documentation, `requirements.txt`, `setup.py`, `Makefile`, sample inputs, and `make check/check_example/run` entry points.

This version is only for explaining the minimum structure. Formal requirements should specify tool inputs/outputs, exception handling, Checker evidence, and business acceptance criteria item by item; otherwise, the Agent will need to make numerous design decisions during the initial phase.

docs.title: 2. Prepare Sample Inputs
docs.text:
Place a smaller but complete case in ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/input/test_input/:

test_input/
├── content.md
├── document_requirements.md
└── assets/
    └── architecture.png

The body text must include at least one level-2 heading, paragraphs, lists, a table, and an image reference. Document requirements should specify Chinese font fallback, page size, behavior when images are missing, and output filename. This allows the generator to plan meaningful tool testing and Checker fixtures.

When using the sample body text below, you can copy the document screenshot as assets/architecture.png:

cp ~/work/UCAgent/docs/content/04_case/03_workflow_builder/resource/workflow_builder_running.png \
  ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/input/test_input/assets/architecture.png

docs.title: 3. Check Environment
docs.text:
cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
python setup.py --check
test -f ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/input/guide.md
test -d ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/input/test_input

If not using local configuration, you must explicitly pass the source, Python, and workspace paths to Make; passing only WS is insufficient. Do not start the environment check until it passes. Whether an agent is required depends on the model service; do not write tokens into guide.md or .workflow_builder/local.mk.

docs.title: 4. Start Supervised Mode
docs.text:
Launch the TUI directly:

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run

The run target defaults to --loop, allowing the Agent to automatically retrieve and continue tasks. When observing in a shared tmux session, you can use the session target from the Makefile, or create your own tmux session and execute the same command within it. In supervised mode, do not generate business files for the Agent; after consecutive failures, locate the parent workflow contract, guide documentation, or Checker issues.

docs.title: 5. Observe Progress
docs.text:
Normally, workspace/wfgen/workflow_implementation_plan.md appears first, followed by the requirements manifest, input sample manifest, workflow build spec, and finally the materialization of workspace/workflow/. Stage records in the plan file can only be appended with content from the current stage; they must not overwrite previous stages.

Check periodically:

find ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace/wfgen -maxdepth 1 -type f -print
find ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace/workflow -maxdepth 2 -type f | head

Do not terminate immediately due to a single long model call. Continuous failures, repeated checks with unchanged timestamps, continuous context compression, or explicit exception stacks are signals requiring diagnosis.

docs.title: 6. Post-Build Verification
docs.text:
cd ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace/workflow
python setup.py --check
make check
make check_example

The generated setup.py and Makefile for the workflow itself reside in workspace/workflow/; they are distinct from the environment configuration files in the Workflow Builder root directory. When failures occur, retain the full exit code and logs; do not declare completion based solely on the existence of an output file.

docs.title: Common Failures
docs.text:
• missing guide file: WS should point to the workspace/ directory under the business root, not the business root itself.
  • TUI did not start automatically: Confirm you used make ... run and that RUN_LOOP_ARGS was not cleared.
  • Restoring old stages: This is historical .ucagent behavior; whether to clear history depends on whether the current run requires resuming.
  • Referenced file missing: Check if the workflow build spec incorrectly references future files as current references.
  • Repeated stage failures: First examine the Checker's accurate description in the TUI, then check the "Issues and Fixes" section of workflow_implementation_plan.md.

docs.title: Ready-to-Use Sample Body Text
docs.text:
input/test_input/content.md may include:

# Workflow Builder User Guide

## Goal

This document explains the workspace, generation, evaluation, and incremental repair processes for engineers using UCAgent for the first time.

## Steps

1. Prepare requirements and sample inputs.
2. Start the build workflow and observe stages.
3. Run static evaluation and approve issues.

## Result Table

| Action | Primary Result |
| --- | --- |
| Build | workflow/ |
| Evaluate | eval/*.json |

![Workflow Architecture](assets/architecture.png)

document_requirements.md should specify A4 paper size, margins, heading hierarchy, Chinese font fallback, page numbers, table of contents, table styles, maximum image width, behavior when images are missing, and output filename. Images can be copied from a smaller screenshot in the document's resource/ folder as a sample, but image-only provision without alternative text is not acceptable.

docs.title: tmux Startup and Viewing
docs.text:
When another terminal is used for read-only observation:

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace session
tmux attach -t ucagent_workflow_builder -r

Read-only attach does not pass keystrokes to the TUI. To stop, enter the writable session, press Ctrl+C to cancel the current command, then follow the UCAgent prompt to exit; do not delete the tmux session directly, allowing child processes and permission daemons to remain in the background.

docs.title: Stage Observation Table
docs.text: Observation Result Judgment Next Step Tool calls continue to change, files increase Normal execution Continue supervision Same Checker fails 1–2 times with content changes Agent is fixing Do not intervene Same error repeats multiple times, no file changes Likely contract or guide issue Check Stage GuideDoc and Checker Automatic retry after model stream anomaly External call interruption Observe if retry recovers Full re-read immediately after compression Context strategy issue Limit reads and revise parent guide

docs.title: Artifact Inspection Order
docs.text: After build completion, first verify that workflow_implementation_plan.md covers all stages and issue records. Then check whether tools and Checkers in workflow_build.yaml are more specific than the original user requirements. Subsequently verify public files in workflow/, config registration, developer documentation source analysis, and environment entry points. Only then run Make acceptance. This order avoids repeatedly running expensive checks when obvious design gaps exist.

docs.title: Start Evaluation Workflow
docs.text: The evaluation process is used to independently review generated business workflows. Static evaluation must not modify workflow/ and should not trigger full sub-workflows solely to prove issues. Running an evaluation incurs high costs and must be explicitly chosen by the user.

docs.title: Evaluation Prerequisites
docs.text:
test -d ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace/workflow
cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
python setup.py --check

The workspace must contain eval/, res/, and tmp/. The Make entry will initialize structured files, but professional knowledge in res/ must be provided by the user; the evaluation Agent must not pretend the user has written professional judgment.

docs.title: Component Execution
docs.text:
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run_eval_tools
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run_eval_checkers
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run_eval_flow
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run_eval_env

The four responsibilities are:

  • eval_tools: Existence, UCAgent registration syntax, callability, error structure, and business requirement coverage.
  • eval_checkers: Source code, docstrings, constructor arguments, registration consistency, positive and negative fixtures, and decision semantics.
  • eval_flow: config/inc configuration, stage handoffs, references and output files, GuideDoc, and user documentation.
  • eval_env: Makefile, setup.py for generating workflows, shell, dependencies, paths, ports, and migration capabilities.

Alternatively, run them sequentially and aggregate:

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run_eval

docs.title: Running Evaluation
docs.text:
Only choose the following when static checks cannot answer whether the "actual process is stuck or the output is usable":

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run_eval_runtime_default

Incremental run mode uses run_eval_runtime_inc. Evaluate only one run mode at a time to avoid mixing costs, logs, and conclusions.

docs.title: Reading Results
docs.text:
Reports are located in the eval/ directory of the build workspace. Aggregation commands are:

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace aggregate_eval
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace eval-list

A valid finding must include a stable id, severity, object, evidence, impact, recommendation, and source run. Issues that prevent UCAgent from starting, cause the process to hang, result in erroneous deployment, or corrupt formal documents have the highest priority; reporting unmet requirements as successful also constitutes a high risk.

docs.title: Failure Judgment
docs.text: The evaluation Agent's own consecutive failures do not necessarily indicate a problem with the evaluated workflow. First, distinguish between: reporting tool parameter errors, reference files causing context issues, network stream interruptions, conflicting evaluation guidance, or indeed finding the target defect. Only conclusions with source code or deterministic command evidence can enter approval.

docs.title: Minimum Evidence per Component
docs.text:
Component Minimum Evidence Required tools spec, source entry, registration record, one successful call and one failed call checkers spec, class/docstring, constructor arguments, positive/negative fixtures, stage registration flow variable definitions and usage, stage input/output mapping, specific reference files, GuideDoc env Make variable passing, setup check, dependency declaration, path and port checks

Evaluation cannot search only for class names just because source files are long, nor can it read all components in full at once to be "complete". Process one target at a time, read the index and direct dependencies first, write evidence to the report, then proceed to the next target.

docs.title: Report Status Judgment
docs.text:
passed indicates that all mandatory checks have evidence and no blocking findings exist; failed indicates confirmed issues violating the contract; blocked indicates evaluation cannot be completed due to missing targets, dependencies, or user knowledge. Network interruptions or Agent call errors belong to evaluation run failures and should not be written as high findings in the evaluated workflow.

A finding's recommendation should be scoped to the fix. For example, stating "block and add negative fixture in unknown placeholder validation in config generator" is more suitable for approval and incremental implementation than "optimize config".

docs.title: Post-Aggregation Human Review
docs.text:
First, check for startup failures, hangs, file corruption, or false success risks in critical/high findings. Then, verify if different components share the same root cause. Finally, randomly spot-check evidence from passed checks. Evaluation quality is not just about what is found, but also about whether it incorrectly marks unverified items as passed.

If the report omits obvious issues, check whether the evaluation rules cover general data flows rather than hardcoding a specific string as the only rule. After correcting the rules, re-run the corresponding components and retain the old runs for comparison.

docs.title: Start Incremental Workflow
docs.text: The incremental process handles only findings and suggestions explicitly approved by the user. New suggestions require approval before entering the current round of fixes.

docs.title: 1. Approve or Add Suggestions
docs.text:
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace eval-list
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace eval-suggest \
  TITLE='Supplement DOCX font fallback explanation' \
  DESCRIPTION='User documentation should explain alternative strategies when the Linux environment lacks specified fonts'
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace eval-list

Copy the full review_id of the entry to be processed from the eval-list output, replace the example values below, and approve. Findings use prefixes like flow/..., tools/..., etc.; it is recommended to use user/...:

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace eval-approve \
  ID='user/<suggestion-id>' \
  REASON='Allow supplementing font fallback explanation in user-generated workflow documents and running document checks'

The approval reason should specify the target for modification and the acceptance criteria. Approval does not require the user to input large blocks of fix code individually, but rather authorizes the incremental process to formulate candidate solutions within a controlled scope.

docs.title: 2. Start Incremental Process
docs.text:
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace run_inc

The entry point assigns a new incremental run id, saving the current round's manifest, candidate files, evidence, and status under tmp/inc_runs/<run-id>/. Different runs cannot share a candidate directory without an identity, as this would confuse old reports, old patches, and the current approval scope.

docs.title: 3. Fix and Deployment Semantics
docs.text:
The incremental process first reads the summary, approved entries, relevant source code, and necessary documentation, then establishes a mapping for each approved item. Before modifying formal files, save the old version; run affected checks immediately after modification. After deployment, "waiting for approval" no longer blocks fixing make check; the only correct closure at this point is to continue fixing until regression passes, or explicitly report that a fix is impossible and stop.

Formal acceptance must include at least:

cd ~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace/workflow
make check
make check_example

If modifying tools or Checkers, also run the corresponding fixture or tool tests. Modifying only reports without deploying files, or deploying without running checks, do not constitute completion.

docs.title: 4. View Results
docs.text:
• eval/incremental_report.json: Current round's goals, execution status, checks, and unresolved issues.
  • eval/applied_changes.json: Actually deployed files, versions, and verification evidence.
  • tmp/inc_runs/<run-id>/: Current round's candidates and process evidence.
  • tmp/change_history/: Old versions of formal files and recovery records.

After completing the incremental process, re-run affected evaluation components. Old findings will not automatically become new conclusions just because files were modified. Aggregated reports can only form a true closure when reading a new round of evaluation results.

docs.title: Common Errors
docs.text:
• No approved entries: The incremental process should end quickly and should not freely search for and fix other issues.
  • Long first-stage reading: The cognitive phase should read indexes and summaries, then read directionally according to approved goals, not scan all large documents in full.
  • make check failure followed by idle spinning: This is an error in the state machine termination condition; immediately enter fix and re-verification.
  • Formal files read-only: The controlled deployer should handle this via temporary files in the same directory and atomic replacement, saving the old version; relying on ordinary overwrite writes is not acceptable.
  • Fix too fast: Check applied changes, source code diffs, and actual command return codes to confirm it is not just updating the report.

docs.title: Approval Reason Examples
docs.text:
Good approval reasons:

Allow modification of workflow/config.yaml and its generation source so that the first stage only references specific files existing before execution;
Must retain existing stage names, and accept with static config check and `make check` returning 0.

Insufficient reasons are "Agree to fix" or "Optimize all." They lack modification boundaries, making it difficult for the incremental Agent to judge whether to modify GuideDoc, Checker, or generator. If deferring, explain missing business decisions, such as whether the user has decided to allow downloading fonts over the network.

docs.title: Directory of Current Run
docs.text:
tmp/inc_runs/<run-id>/
├── context/
├── batches/<batch-id>/attempts/<attempt-id>/
│   ├── candidates/
│   └── evidence/
└── history/

Different implementations may add index files, but candidates, evidence, and history must be bound to the current identity. After starting, confirm the run id in the report or CLI first to avoid mistakenly thinking the current Agent has no output after viewing the previous round's directory.

docs.title: Acceptance Order After Deployment
docs.text:
1. Run the minimum test against the modified object in formal workflow/.
  2. Run make check, and make check_example if necessary.
  3. Compare hashes in applied_changes.json with formal files.
  4. Confirm old version records are readable.
  5. Re-run affected evaluation components.

If step 1 or step 2 fails, the incremental process should continue fixing or rollback, not declare completion first and wait for evaluation. Re-evaluation is an independent confirmation of the fix, not a replacement for deterministic regression after deployment.

docs.title: Recovery Drill
docs.text: After enabling version management for the first time, suggest performing a recovery drill in a test workspace with a non-critical modification: view history, restore old version, confirm hash, run checks, then restore the new version. Only after a real drill can you confirm that the backup path displayed in the console is not an isolated record.

docs.title: Workflow Builder and Evaluation Console
docs.text: The console provides a unified interface in the browser to view evaluation reports, review approval requests, add suggestions, inspect design files, monitor UCAgent progress, and manage incremental deployment history. It serves as the native management interface and does not replace the Evaluation Agent or the Incremental Agent.

docs.title: Startup
docs.text:
cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace eval-ui

The default address is http://127.0.0.1:8765. If the port is already in use by another program, first verify if the console is already running:

# Linux

ss -ltnp | grep ':8765'

# macOS

lsof -nP -iTCP:8765 -sTCP:LISTEN

Use a different port if you need to view another workspace in parallel:

make WS=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace EVAL_UI_PORT=8766 eval-ui

Do not blindly restart the same port. After completing approvals, press Ctrl+C in the terminal where the console was started; the port will be released once the service process exits.

docs.title: Evaluation and Approval Interface
docs.text:
This page displays findings, user suggestions, evidence, and approval status. Filters allow viewing by unapproved, approved, approved, pending, and rejected. Single-item approvals provide default reasons that users can adopt or supplement; batch approvals are suitable only for fixing entries with identical boundaries.

Deleting items is an explicit management action. Deleting an evaluation entry differs semantically from deleting version records: version records are by default used for recovery and audit, and are only removed from the index and corresponding historical files when explicitly deleted by the user.

docs.title: Design Interface
docs.text:
The design page parses files by format:

  • wfgen/input_example_manifest.yaml
  • wfgen/workflow_build.yaml
  • wfgen/requirements_manifest.yaml
  • wfgen/workflow_implementation_plan.md
  • eval/incremental_report.json
  • eval/applied_changes.json

Fixed-format files use a structured view; editable fields must pass length, type, reference, and calculation field validation before writing back. Files without a stable format display full text and should not be forced parsed by guessing incorrect fields.

The left side displays the workflow file tree, the center shows the wider core content, basic document information is fixed at the top, current document navigation is located below the basic information, and the main text area scrolls independently. The right side displays the UCAgent current stage and runtime status.

docs.title: Backend and Security Boundaries
docs.text: The console backend calls structured storage via controlled APIs and does not allow the browser to arbitrarily concatenate file paths. The workspace must be a directory explicitly passed in the startup command; all write operations validate paths, versions, and formats. The console listens by default only on 127.0.0.1; remote access should be done via a trusted tunnel rather than exposing it directly to the public internet.

docs.title: Next Steps After Approval
docs.text: Console approvals only update structured approval data and do not automatically start the Incremental Agent. After completing approvals, you may exit or keep the console running; execute make WS=... run_inc in another terminal. After the incremental process finishes, refresh the page to view reports, deployment files, and historical versions, then run a new evaluation to close the loop.

docs.title: Page and Backend Status Mapping
docs.text:
Page Action Backend Status Change Action That Will Not Occur Automatically Approve finding Add/update approval Do not start inc, do not modify workflow Create suggestion Write user suggestions Do not auto-approve Save structured design Write to specified wfgen file after validation Do not re-run build phase Recover history Atomically replace formal file and record Do not automatically close old finding Delete history Delete specified record and unreferenced backups Do not delete other runs

Users should refresh and verify revision, status, and time after actions. If the browser shows success but JSON has not updated, this is a backend issue that cannot be masked by frontend prompts.

docs.title: Structured Editing Limitations
docs.text:
The editor only exposes fields allowed by the schema. Calculated values such as minimum counts, hashes, run IDs, and audit times cannot be entered arbitrarily. During save, the server compares the revision read at that time; if the backend Agent has already updated the file, the user must reload and merge changes rather than overwrite the new version.

The Markdown implementation plan is primarily for reading stage structure and issue records and is not intended as a casual text editor. Files without fixed formats display full text but do not provide a save button to prevent the UI from becoming an arbitrary file tool that bypasses incremental approvals.

docs.title: Version Management Operations
docs.text: Before recovering, view the original path, run ID, backup hash, and creation time. Recovery first backs up the current formal version, so recovery can be undone. Deletion operations are irreversible; only delete versions confirmed to no longer be needed and not referenced by other records; when dealing with large numbers of records, first filter by run, file, and status.

docs.title: Console Error Evidence
docs.text: When encountering blank pages or operation failures, retain the browser request path, HTTP status, backend traceback, workspace, and revision. Port conflicts, illegal paths returning 400, revision conflicts returning 409, and server-side exceptions returning 500 represent different issues. Do not simply take a screenshot of a "button not responding," and do not kill the port-occupying process without confirming the PID.

docs.title: Complete Usage Overview
docs.text: This directory describes the complete methodology of Workflow Builder from preparing business requirements to delivery, evaluation, and long-term incremental maintenance. QuickStart is suitable for first-time execution, while this directory explains why each directory and state file exists, who can modify them, and how to recover after failure.

docs.title: Usage Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. The user creates the business root directory and input/, writing requirements and examples.
  2. Workflow Builder copies public wfgen/, Guide_Doc/, and business inputs to the build workspace.
  3. The main workflow generation design files and workflow/ artifacts are produced, followed by static acceptance.
  4. The user inspects the generated workflow environment, documentation, examples, and make check.
  5. The workflow evaluation independently produces findings, which the user approves or suggests improvements on in the console.
  6. Incremental workflows establish candidates by run id, deploy fixes, save old versions, and perform regression.
  7. The user re-runs relevant evaluations, closes old issues, or proceeds to the next round.

docs.title: Documentation Navigation
docs.text:
• Input Contract: Building requirements, examples, and domain expertise.
  • Outputs and Workspace Structure: Design, artifacts, reports, temporary files, and history.
  • Complete Workflow Builder Usage: Supervision and intervention, resuming, and acceptance.
  • Complete Evaluation and Approval Usage: Reports, severity levels, and approvals.
  • Incremental Updates and Version Management: Candidates, deployment, recovery, and closure.
  • Prompt Usage Guide: How to first load the collaboration protocol, then use short commands.
  • Prompts: Complete protocols ready for collaboration Agents to read.

docs.title: Two-Layer Workflows
docs.text:
The config.yaml in the build workspace belongs to Workflow Builder; files generated to workflow/config.yaml belong to the business workflow. Execute pwd before running commands to confirm the current target:

# Generate or evaluate business workflows

cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
make WS=/business_root/workspace run

# Run already generated business workflows

cd /business_root/workspace/workflow
make run TARGET=example

Most path errors, TUI behavior differences, and error history recovery stem from confusing these two layers.

docs.title: Permissions and Responsibilities
docs.text:
• The user owns input/, res/, approvals, and suggestions.
  • The Build Agent can write to current task-allowed areas in wfgen/, workflow/, and tmp/.
  • The Evaluation Agent reads-only workflow/ and writes to eval/ via structured tools.
  • The Incremental Agent handles only approved scopes, modifying workflow/ through candidates and the deployer.
  • The console edits structured fields via the backend API and cannot arbitrarily write files.

Any behavior attempting to bypass responsibility boundaries "to make checks pass" constitutes failure, even if the final command returns 0.

docs.title: Lifecycle States and Exit Conditions
docs.text:
The build process ends only when central design, public artifacts, and static acceptance are consistent; the evaluation process ends only when mandatory checks within this responsibility domain have evidence and are written to the report; the incremental process ends only when all approved items are mapped, formal regression passes, and history is saved. "Phase Complete" displayed in the TUI is just one signal.

When the user voluntarily stops, the current workspace should be preserved, along with the plan and report. Before restarting, decide whether to continue using history or run anew; do not clear .ucagent, wfgen/, and eval/ simultaneously. These directories represent different states: history can reconstruct execution context, design represents business decisions, and evaluation serves as long-term audit.

docs.title: Common Command Matrix
docs.text: Target Interaction Mode Auto Loop Modifies workflow/ run TUI Yes Written during build run_cli CLI Executed by CLI flow Written during build run_eval_* TUI Yes No run_inc TUI Yes Modified via deployer eval-ui Browser N/A Modified only for structural edit or recovery

docs.title: Configuration Priority
docs.text:
From highest to lowest: Make command-line assignment, current Make process explicit variables, local .workflow_builder/local.mk, and Makefile defaults. Use make configure-show to view saved values, and make -n WS=... run to check expanded commands without starting the Agent. A single Builder can manage multiple business workspaces; local defaults are not hard bindings.

Long-term projects should record the business root, input revision, start/end time, and artifact revision for each build; evaluation uses report run id; incremental uses inc run/change id. Key modifications are tracked through structured records; terminal screenshots serve only as auxiliary evidence.

docs.title: Input Contract
docs.text: The business inputs for Workflow Builder reside in the input/ directory under the business root. This directory is maintained by the user, and the Makefile copies it to workspace/input/ in the build workspace upon startup. The copied workspace inputs represent a snapshot of the current run; modifying the source inputs requires restarting the relevant workflow to ensure consistency.

docs.title: Required Structure
docs.text:
<business-root>/
└── input/
    ├── guide.md
    └── test_input/

guide.md is the single fixed entry point. test_input/ must be a directory that can contain multiple files and subdirectories; its contents should represent a minimal but complete real-world business case.

docs.title: Contents of guide.md
docs.text:
1. Workflow objectives and explicitly excluded actions.
  2. Paths, formats, required fields, and constraints for each user input.
  3. Paths, formats, and acceptance criteria for each public output.
  4. Expected stages, parameters, results, exceptions, and examples for tools.
  5. Expected check objects, evidence, pass/fail conditions for the Checker.
  6. Runtime environment, Python dependencies, and system dependencies.
  7. Requirements for user documentation and developer documentation.
  8. Whether independent evaluation workflows, incremental workflows, and a knowledge base directory are required.

Requirements should not pre-ask the user to generate testbenches, configurations, Checker code, or tool source code; these are capabilities that the workflow should generate automatically. Users provide business code, descriptions, verification requirements, assets, and knowledge.

docs.title: test_input Design
docs.text:
Samples must cover primary paths without being large enough to slow down every regression. Filenames, extensions, and directory levels must align with future input/<TARGET>/. If the real business allows optional files, both samples and requirements must specify behavior when they are missing, avoiding the generation of Checkers that force all optional fields.

Binary assets should be small, publicly shareable files; text should use UTF-8. Do not include tokens, private certificates, customer data, oversized media, or links that require external network access to resolve.

docs.title: res Knowledge Base
docs.text: User knowledge used for evaluation and incremental processing resides in the res/ directory within the build workspace, not as a replacement for the source input/. Typical content includes domain acceptance rules, known tool limitations, organizational standards, and user judgment. The initialization program creates structured files; the Agent can only read or access via allowed structured tools, not fabricate user knowledge.

docs.title: Input Changes
docs.text: Modifying guide.md during the build causes inconsistencies between the requirements list, plan, and generated specs. Major changes should stop the current run, save necessary reports, and then rebuild from a clean workspace. Minor fix requests, after the workflow has generated outputs, should be prioritized via user suggestions and incremental workflows.

docs.title: Input Self-Check
docs.text:
test -f <business-root>/input/guide.md
test -d <business-root>/input/test_input
find <business-root>/input -type l -print

It is not recommended for inputs to contain symbolic links pointing outside the business root. Example paths in requirements should use relative business paths, avoiding absolute paths specific to a particular machine.

docs.title: Recommended Requirements Template
docs.text:
# <Business Name> Workflow Requirements

## User Goals and Exclusions

## Input File Contract

## Public Output Contract

## Processing Stages and Data Flow

## Tool Requirements

## Checker and Acceptance Evidence

## Environment and Dependencies

## User Documentation and Developer Documentation

## Evaluation, Incremental, and Knowledge Base

Each file contract should specify relative paths, format versions, encoding, top-level structure, required fields, allowed sizes, and error handling. Directory inputs should specify whether they are recursive, allowed extensions, sorting rules, and behavior for empty directories. Binary inputs should specify the parsing library and behavior for corrupted files.

Tool requirements are not requests for users to write source code, but rather descriptions of business capabilities. Checker requirements should specify what evidence is used for judgment, not just "check results." The first stage of the parent workflow should expand these contents into an implementation-level plan; conservative inferences must be recorded as design decisions and cannot be disguised as user requirements.

Domain requirements in res/ should indicate scope and source. The evaluation Agent can read them but cannot modify them to favor its own conclusions. After the run begins, it is recommended to record the guide.md and sample tree revision; if inputs change during the build, the process should stop and choose to rebuild or proceed with incremental updates.

docs.title: Output and Workspace Structure
docs.text: The workspace/ directory under the business root saves design, final workflow, evaluation, incremental history, and UCAgent state. Each directory serves a different purpose and has distinct cleanup and version management strategies.

docs.title: Primary Directories
docs.text: Path Content Modifiable by Hand input/ Snapshot of input for this build Usually not modified during runtime wfgen/ requirements, build design, example manifest, implementation plan Written during build phase; console only exposes specific structure fields Guide_Doc/ Public stage guide copy for master workflow Not modified as a business artifact workflow/ Final generated independent business workflow Modified during build or controlled incremental deployment eval/ Component evaluation, approval, incremental, and deployment reports Modified via structured tools or console res/ Source of user expertise and suggestions Maintained by user tmp/ Temporary files, evaluation cases, incremental candidates, and historical versions Can be cleaned according to rules .ucagent/ Current UCAgent history and runtime state Should not be manually rewritten

docs.title: Key Files in wfgen
docs.text:
• requirements_manifest.yaml: Normalized user requirements and deliverables.
  • workflow_implementation_plan.md: Cross-stage design, tools, Checker, documentation, and "issues and handling".
  • input_example_manifest.yaml: File mapping and sources for example targets.
  • workflow_build.yaml: Central workflow spec, files, tools, Checker, GuideDoc, and environment design.

Subsequent stages must read and update the marked areas of the plan for the current phase without overwriting preceding content. Central design changes must be synchronized across the manifest and final artifacts; modifying only one file is insufficient.

docs.title: workflow Deliverables
docs.text:
Typical outputs include config.yaml, config/inc.yaml, tools/, checkers/, Guide_Doc/, docs/, input/example/, setup.py, requirements.txt, ucagent_setup.sh, and Makefile.

The output/ directory within the generated workflow contains data that is only produced when the business goal is executed in the future; it cannot be substituted with pre-built results during the build phase.

docs.title: eval and tmp
docs.text:
The eval/ directory stores structured records that need long-term reading, approval, and aggregation. The tmp/ directory stores reproducible process data, but tmp/change_history/ and the currently valid tmp/inc_runs/ must not be deleted until version management is complete. Cleanup commands must retain files referenced by historical indexes.

Browser validation profiles, locks, and caches generated are restricted to tmp/ui_validation/. When the browser exits, locks may vanish instantly; the cleaner must tolerate this race condition and should not misinterpret warnings as business failures.

docs.title: File Permissions
docs.text: UCAgent history may temporarily alter snapshot permissions, while the Makefile restores the writable state of the workspace. Formal incremental deployments do not rely on the original files being writable; instead, they use backups and atomic replacement. Users should still avoid simultaneously editing the same files with other editors during workflow execution.

docs.title: Public and Internal Files
docs.text:
Public files of the generated workflow are intended for end users, including README, docs, config, Makefile, setup, requirements, tools, and business Checkers. The .workflow/ directory stores specs, internal Checkers, tests, and acceptance criteria; developers may inspect them, but ordinary users are not required to manually edit them.

reference_files and output_files represent stage contracts and must be listed with specific filenames. References must exist before the stage begins, while outputs are produced or updated by the current stage. Directory structure displays should be placed in documentation or manifests; directories cannot be used to impersonate file references.

docs.title: Key JSON Ownership
docs.text:
File Writer User Action eval/*_report.json Evaluation structured tool Read, approve findings eval/user_suggestions.json CLI/Console Create, retract, delete eval/approvals.json Approval API Approve, reject, suspend eval/incremental_report.json Incremental workflow Read repair status eval/applied_changes.json Deployer Read and version operations

Manual editing may break revisions, fingerprints, and audit trails. Standard clean operations must preserve input, eval, res, the current inc run, and change history. When checking outputs, YAML/JSON must be parsed, Python imports executed, and Make targets run; a complete file tree does not guarantee valid content.

docs.title: Pre-Start
docs.text:
cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
make configure-check
make help
test -f <business-root>/input/guide.md
test -d <business-root>/input/test_input

Ensure no other process is running a build or incremental workflow in the same workspace. Different business units should use distinct WS and tmux sessions to prevent contamination of MCP ports, history, and artifacts.

docs.title: tmux Supervision Strategy
docs.text:
The supervision strategy allows the internal Agent within UCAgent to automatically loop. Users or external Agents observe the TUI, check for causes upon consecutive failures, modify only the rules in the parent workflow that are genuinely problematic, and then restart or resume the run. Entry point:

make WS=<business-root>/workspace run

By default, RUN_LOOP_ARGS includes --loop --loop-msg. When determining if a stage is still active, combine TUI tool invocations, target file timestamps, and stage failure counts; do not rely solely on the elapsed waiting time.

docs.title: tmux Intervention Strategy
docs.text:
The intervention strategy prevents the internal Agent from executing automatically, instead having an external Agent retrieve RoleInfo and tasks via MCP to complete the current stage. Entry point:

make WS=<business-root>/workspace run RUN_LOOP_ARGS=

The intervener must still adhere to stage tasks and the Checker; they cannot bypass the process to generate all workflow files directly. This approach is suitable for diagnosing stage failures that are difficult to understand from the TUI but is not appropriate for long-term replacement of workflow execution.

docs.title: History and Resume
docs.text:
By default, execution retains .ucagent history, allowing resumption from the current stage after stopping. Use corresponding parameters or clean the state only when a fresh evaluation is explicitly required or when the user requests no history. Do not add --no-history when the user intends to resume.

If requirements or the central spec have undergone destructive changes, old stage history may no longer be reliable. Backup reports and plans before cleaning the workspace and rebuilding, rather than allowing the Agent to continue within contradictory contexts.

docs.title: Failure Diagnosis Order
docs.text:
1. Read the current stage name, failure count, and full Checker message.
  2. Review the "Issues and Handling" section corresponding to the stage in the implementation plan.
  3. Compare whether reference/output files exist, are specific files, and have normalized paths.
  4. Check if the Agent has misunderstood the format, repeatedly runs the same command, or reads too many irrelevant documents.
  5. Confirm the parent rule issue, then modify the common source rather than just the workspace copy.
  6. Run relevant deterministic regression tests, then resume from the current stage.

Network streaming exceptions and business Checker failures must be separated. incomplete chunked read indicates the model response stream did not fully terminate, but frequent occurrences in large context stages should also check if the request is too large or if agent/service limits are the cause; do not simply attribute it to a single cause.

docs.title: Completion Acceptance
docs.text:
After the main process completes, verify design and artifact mapping, tool and Checker registration, documentation, environment, examples, and:

cd <business-root>/workspace/workflow
python setup.py --check
make check
make check_example

If commands fail, the build cannot be considered successful. Do not claim the workflow itself has passed tests by manually fixing artifacts after supervision; the parent workflow must be corrected and verified with a new run.

docs.title: Environment Startup Methods
docs.text: Persistent methods are suitable for repeated use: run the root python setup.py, and Make automatically loads local values. Temporary methods are suitable for single experiments: pass UCAGENT_HOME, UCAGENT_VENV, PYTHON, and WS simultaneously in the Make command line. New tmux sessions do not necessarily inherit shell functions, so verify the actual Python, agent, and Token.

docs.title: Supervision Frequency and Intervention Thresholds
docs.text:
Check stages, failure counts, recent invocations, and artifact changes every two minutes during normal stages. A single failure typically allows the Agent to self-correct; three consecutive failures with the same root cause warrant targeted checks; five or more failures or prolonged lack of state changes indicate obvious anomalies. Thresholds are not mechanical termination conditions; long transitions are reasonable but must have tool or file evidence.

Before intervening, save the last TUI output and task. When MCP takes over, first retrieve RoleInfo, complete only the current stage, and accept the same Checker for validation. After modifying parent rules, history is used by default unless the user explicitly requests a fresh run.

docs.title: Quality and Recovery
docs.text:
Review whether the implementation plan is more specific than user requirements, whether the workflow build spec is closed, whether developer documentation references real business source code, and whether config placeholders and self-referential citations are complete. Speed is not evidence of quality.

When stopping, first allow the current command to respond to SIGINT, then exit the TUI. If model streaming exceptions auto-retry, continue observing; after process exit, retain .ucagent for restart. During recovery, first confirm the saved stage index; do not automatically add --no-history.

docs.title: Evaluation and Approval Workflow
docs.text: The goal of evaluation is to uncover real gaps between the generated workflow, user requirements, the UCAgent protocol, and the runtime environment, providing reproducible evidence. Evaluation reports are not graded essays, and the number of findings is not a quality metric.

docs.title: Component Responsibilities
docs.text: Tools, Checkers, process, and environment static evaluations each handle only their own domain of responsibility. Cross-domain issues should be submitted in the most direct root cause domain, noting other affected components in the impact; do not copy the same paragraph across four separate reports. The runtime evaluation specifically checks whether real execution hangs, exit codes, and artifact behavior.

docs.title: Severity
docs.text:
Level Typical Impact critical UCAgent fails to start or retries infinitely; destructive or erroneous overwrites of formal documents; execution of unauthorized commands; erroneous claims that incomplete requirements are completed high Core tools or Checker unavailable; primary path artifacts incorrect; configuration phase cannot connect; make check inevitably fails medium Boundary input handling errors, difficult development/maintenance, non-primary path documentation inconsistent with implementation low Readability, hints, or localized experience issues that do not affect correctness

Severity must be based on impact and reachability; it cannot be marked as critical simply because the rule text contains the word "must".

docs.title: Evidence Standards
docs.text: Valid evidence must include specific files, symbols, or fields, as well as source code analysis, deterministic command exit codes, or reproducible fixtures. Writing "looks wrong" or "might have a problem" is insufficient for approval. Before submitting a finding, the evaluator should attempt to refute the claim, confirming it is not caused by optional inputs, future-stage artifacts, normalization-equivalent paths, or old reports.

docs.title: Approval Actions
docs.text:
• Approve: Allow incremental fixes within the stated scope and provide acceptance intent.
  • Reject: Determine the issue is invalid or should not be modified, providing the reason.
  • Postpone: The issue may be valid, but lacks business decision, resources, or appropriate timing.
  • Delete: Remove invalid or no longer needed records; this does not equate to "fixed".
  • Add Suggestion: A user directly proposes an improvement request not originating from the evaluation Agent.

Batch operations can be performed via CLI or console. Before batch approval, confirm that entry modification boundaries are consistent; default approval reasons are merely a starting point, and key business decisions should still be supplemented.

docs.title: Closure
docs.text: After incremental modifications, re-run the affected evaluation components. The aggregator retains old runs; therefore, current quality must be judged based on the finding status of the new run. The existence of old finding text does not indicate a failed fix, nor can verification be automatically marked without a new evaluation.

docs.title: Finding Structure Example
docs.text:
{
  "id": "FLOW-REFERENCE-001",
  "severity": "high",
  "title": "Stage reference executes file that does not exist",
  "expected": "reference_files contains only specific files existing before the start",
  "actual": "First stage reference workflow/output/report.json",
  "evidence": [{"path": "workflow/config.yaml", "location": "stage[0].reference_files"}],
  "recommendation": "Correct central stage design and add future reference negative regression"
}

The id should remain stable across similar issues, while fingerprint binds to specific content. evidence should record observed facts, not mixing in unproven inferences. recommendation must specify the fix location and acceptance criteria, rather than vaguely "optimize the process".

docs.title: Pre-Approval Checks
docs.text:
Confirm the issue exists, severity and impact match, suggestions do not exceed user requirements, modification objects and acceptance are clear, and whether it shares a root cause with other findings. If professional judgment is lacking, choose to postpone and specify the required user information.

When batch approving the same type of registration missing or document synchronization issues, each item retains an independent source id and fingerprint. Involving different business decisions or conflicting suggestions requires separate approval.

docs.title: Re-evaluation Strategy
docs.text: Tool modifications run eval_tools, Checker modifications run eval_checkers, config/GuideDoc/docs modifications run eval_flow, and Makefile/setup/dependency modifications run eval_env. Cross-domain modifications run all affected components; only when real runtime risk exists should the expensive eval_run be additionally executed.

docs.title: Incremental Repair and Version Management
docs.text: The incremental process organizes "approved findings, candidate modifications, formal deployment, regression evidence, and historical versions" into a single, identity-bound execution. It addresses controlled maintenance of generated workflows without replacing the regeneration of all business files.

docs.title: Current Round Inputs
docs.text: At startup, freeze the current approved findings and suggestions; eval-suggest creates suggestions only, which still require approval via eval-approve or the console. Each item requires a stable ID, approval status, description, and determinable target. The incremental Agent first reads the workflow structure summary, tools and Checker index, relevant GuideDoc, and user docs directory, then reads the source code targeted by the round's objectives. A preliminary understanding does not require reading all files in full.

docs.title: Candidate Plan
docs.text: The candidate plan records: run ID, approved items, estimated files, purpose of each modification, risk, check commands, and deployment order. The plan is located in the round's tmp/inc_runs/<id>/ directory, not in wfgen/workflow_implementation_plan.md. The latter belongs to the initial cross-stage design constructed at the beginning; the console should display them separately.

docs.title: Modification and Verification
docs.text: Formal files first enter the candidate directory via a controlled copy tool. After the Agent modifies the candidate, it runs syntax, structure, fixture, and affected Make targets. Deployment proceeds only if checks pass; the deployer saves old files and performs atomic replacement. After deployment, checks must be run again on the formal directory, as candidate and formal paths may have different reference relationships.

docs.title: Historical Versions
docs.text:
Each deployed file is saved with its content and structured index in tmp/change_history/. The index includes original path, backup, hash, run ID, timestamp, and action. The console allows viewing, restoring, and explicit deletion.

Upon restoration, a version is first created for the current formal file, then the selected old version is atomically written back, followed by running the corresponding checks. Deletion operations must simultaneously handle the index and backup files with no other references; immutable audit defaults cannot prevent users from explicitly cleaning version records.

docs.title: Regression Failure Handling
docs.text: If make check fails after deployment, the formal state is unacceptable. The incremental process should immediately attempt to fix based on the failure, redeploy, and verify, or rollback. In this case, there is no need to wait for the user to re-approve the same fix. If the new fix would exceed the original approval scope, rollback and report the blockage rather than leaving erroneous formal files and spinning.

docs.title: Completion Checklist
docs.text:
• Each approved item corresponds to at least one actual change or explicit evidence of "no modification needed".
  • applied_changes.json is consistent with file hashes.
  • Old versions are locatable and restorable.
  • Relevant tools/Checker tests and make check pass.
  • No unregistered modifications, temporary files outside the workspace, or arbitrary shell operations.
  • Incremental reports do not incorrectly write pending re-evaluation as confirmed by assessment.

docs.title: Minimum Fields for Candidate Plan
docs.text:
The candidate plan records run/batch/attempt, approved ID, target file, estimated operation, reason, risk, candidate check, and formal check. A file may cover multiple approvals, and an approval may require multiple files; the plan must maintain a bidirectional mapping.

The plan is not a deployment record. After actual deployment, the deployer records source/target hashes, backup, timestamp, and result; the Agent cannot pre-write plan items as applied.

docs.title: Candidate Modification Rules
docs.text:
First, use a controlled stager to copy the formal file and record the source hash, then edit the candidate. New files are also created under the current attempt's candidates directory. Debug logs and transformation intermediates remain in evidence/tmp, not placed in wfgen/ or the formal workflow root.

Candidate tests should be minimal and fast; after deployment, run full relevant checks on the formal directory. If candidate tests depend on relative workflow paths, use an isolated projection and do not preemptively overwrite formal files for convenience.

docs.title: History and Failure Exit
docs.text:
Restoration first backs up the current formal version, so restoration can be undone. Deletion is an explicit user cleanup, not automatically executed when the Agent completes a task. Although history resides in tmp, clean must also be preserved.

When the approval scope is insufficient, rollback and report the need for new authorization; when dependencies are missing, save the candidate and evidence and mark as blocked; candidate check failure prevents deployment; rollback failure must be escalated to a critical status requiring human recovery. Reports must include run ID, target file, and final exit code.

docs.title: How to Use the Prompts
docs.text: 07_agent_prompts.md serves as the long-term operational protocol between the user and the collaborative Agent. It is not responsible for generating business prompts, but rather pre-arranges environment variables, UCAgent awareness, tmux supervision and intervention strategies, short commands, diagnostic methods, and non-negotiable modification boundaries.

docs.title: First-Time Usage
docs.text:
At the start of a new session, first inform the Agent of the current environment variables, for example:

UCAGENT_HOME=~/work/UCAgent
WORKFLOW_BUILDER_HOME=~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
BUSINESS_ROOT=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx
WFB_WORKSPACE=~/work/ucagent_tasks/docx/workspace
TMUX_SESSION=ucagent_workflow_builder

Then provide:

Please read [07_agent_prompts.md](07_agent_prompts.md) in the same directory completely, and memorize the environment variables, short commands, supervision strategies, intervention strategies, and modification boundaries. After completion, establish awareness.

The Agent should first confirm the paths, read the key entry points of UCAgent and the central design of the sub-workflows, and then accept subsequent short commands.

docs.title: Common Short Commands
docs.text:
• Supervise Run: Start an automatic loop TUI, observe at fixed intervals, and locate the cause upon consecutive failures.
  • Intervene Run: Disable the automatic loop and complete the role and current task step-by-step via MCP.
  • Continue Supervise: Maintain the current strategy without restarting or clearing history.
  • View Status: Report the stage, failure count, latest tool invocation, and changes in artifacts.
  • Check Failure Cause: Distinguish the root cause from the Checker, logs, references, context, and external errors.
  • Deep Repair: Modify sub-workflows or the parent workflow to address issues with evidence and run verification.
  • Check Artifacts: Review the actually generated files, not replacing sub-workflows to supplement artifacts.

Short commands only have stable meaning after the protocol is loaded and environment variables are agreed upon. When a new Agent or one with compressed context loses critical context, the user should re-provide an environment summary and current status rather than assuming it retains memory from the previous session.

docs.title: Switching Between Supervision and Intervention
docs.text: Supervision mode defaults to using the --loop option in the Makefile. Before switching to intervention mode, safely stop the current TUI to avoid two Agents processing the same stage simultaneously; then start using RUN_LOOP_ARGS=. When returning to supervision after intervention, also confirm the current stage and historical status before creating a second concurrent session.

docs.title: Boundaries of Prompt Usage
docs.text: Paths in the protocol are variables and should not be hard-coded to a specific historical workspace. The Agent can only modify sub-workflows or the workflow_builder scope permitted by the user, and cannot modify the UCAgent core without authorization. The purpose of supervision is to truly validate the workflow; therefore, except for the current task in intervention mode, business artifacts should not be directly written by the Agent.

docs.title: State Handoff
docs.text: Long-process handoffs should record at least: workspace, tmux session, run strategy, current stage, failure count, recent evidence, modified files, tests run, and the next action. This ensures that even if context compression occurs, the Agent will not repeatedly read all documents from scratch.

docs.title: First-Time Load Confirmation Template
docs.text:
Protocol loaded. Current UCAGENT_HOME=..., WORKFLOW_BUILDER_HOME=...,
BUSINESS_ROOT=..., WFB_WORKSPACE=..., TMUX_SESSION=...
I will only modify within the permitted scope; supervision mode does not write sub-workflow artifacts; upon consecutive failures, collect evidence first.
Next step: establish preliminary awareness of UCAgent entry, parent configuration, central design, and current status.

The user should check the paths restated by the Agent, especially BUSINESS_ROOT and WFB_WORKSPACE. A one-level error will cause Make to copy requirements from an incorrect sibling input.

docs.title: Recovery Prompt After Compression
docs.text:
Restore protocol context: Continue using agreed variables and supervision strategies.
Current stage=<name>, failure count=<n>, recent error=<summary>,
confirmed=<facts>, unconfirmed=<hypotheses>, next action=<one action>.
Do not re-read all documents in full; read directly related files based on the current error.

If the Agent clearly forgets fixed boundaries, read the relevant sections of the protocol again; there is no need to reload the entire 800 lines every time.

docs.title: Command Priority and Report Quality
docs.text:
The latest user command takes priority; Stop Run stops immediately; Continue Supervise does not restart; Repair and Re-run includes modifications and restarts; View Status is read-only only. Combined commands follow the sequence: safe stop, analyze modifications, verify, then start execution.

Status reports must distinguish facts from judgments. "Stage 3 failed 5 times, same error, mtime unchanged" is a fact; "Checker may be too strict" is a hypothesis to be verified. Without evidence, do not directly claim network or model issues.

docs.title: 1. Protocol Loading
docs.text:
You are the Agent responsible for running and deeply repairing UCAgent sub-workflows. When the user requests you to read this file, you must fully read it and treat the variable rules, short commands, execution strategies, repair boundaries, and acceptance criteria within it as fixed conventions for all subsequent work in this thread. Unless the user explicitly updates variables or overrides a specific convention, subsequent users only need to send short commands, and you must automatically expand them into the complete actions defined by this file, without requiring the user to repeat long prompts.

Upon first loading this protocol, establish only the conventions; do not automatically start or modify files. After reading, reply using the following format:

Protocol loaded.
UCAGENT_ROOT=<value or unset>
WORKSPACE_ROOT=<value or unset>
CHILD_WORKFLOW=<value or unset>
TARGET=<value or unset>
TMUX_SESSION=<value or auto-generated>
Short commands enabled: Establish understanding, Supervise execution, Intervene in execution, Take over current stage, Continue supervision, View status,
Check failure cause, Stop execution, Deep repair, Repair current issue, Verify repair, No historical rerun, Check artifacts, Full acceptance.

If critical variables are not yet set, report only "not set"; do not guess paths, nor immediately ask. Wait until the user sets variables or issues an action command requiring that variable, then ask for all necessary variables that cannot be reliably determined from the environment in a single request.

"Remember" means to continue adhering to this protocol throughout the current conversation thread. When context compression occurs, old tasks are restored, or the task is handed over to another Agent, you must re-read this file and the current variable record; do not continue operations based solely on vague memory.

docs.title: 2. Environment Variable Conventions
docs.text:
Users typically send content similar to the following first:

Conventions environment:
UCAGENT_ROOT=/home/UCAgent
WORKSPACE_ROOT=/home/UCAgent_t/workspace_za/workspace
CHILD_WORKFLOW=/home/UCAgent_t/workspace_za/workspace/workflow
TARGET=example
TMUX_SESSION=child_workflow_za
CHECK_INTERVAL=120

The variables to remember are as follows:

Variable Meaning Required UCAGENT_ROOT Root directory of UCAgent source and runtime entry point Required to establish UCAgent understanding and start runtime WORKSPACE_ROOT Root directory of workspace containing workflow, eval, res, tmp Required CHILD_WORKFLOW Root directory of the sub-workflow to be run and repaired Required TARGET Current business input or DUT name Required at runtime OUT Sub-workflow output root directory; if not set, read default value from Makefile Optional TMUX_SESSION tmux session name; if not set, generate a unique name based on workflow and strategy Optional CHECK_INTERVAL Supervision interval in seconds, default 120 Optional FAIL_ANALYZE_THRESHOLD Number of times similar failures occur before analysis begins, default 3 Optional FAIL_STOP_THRESHOLD Number of times similar failures occur before stopping execution, default 5 Optional ENV_COMMANDS Environment commands to run before startup, default ucagent_env, proxy_on Optional

Variable rules:

  1. The user's latest setting overrides old values, affecting only subsequent actions; do not migrate running processes without authorization.
  2. Relative paths must be converted to absolute paths and confirmed to exist before execution.
  3. CHILD_WORKFLOW must not be automatically inferred as the current directory of workflow_builder.
  4. TARGET must not be guessed arbitrarily by viewing any old output; if the user has not set it, confirm from the current tmux command or unique input directory, otherwise ask.
  5. Before each startup, restate CHILD_WORKFLOW, TARGET, strategy, tmux session, and the exact command.
  6. After variable changes, previously established file hashes, stage states, and failure judgments may expire; they must be re-verified.

docs.title: 3. Short Command Conventions
docs.text: The following phrases are operation commands, not discussion topics. When the user sends only a phrase, execute directly according to the definition. If the user appends parameters or restrictions after the phrase, the user's latest addition takes precedence.

docs.title: 3.1 Load Protocol
docs.text:
Fully read this file, record known environment variables, and reply with protocol loading confirmation. Do not start or modify.

Read and remember prompt, Read prompt and remember conventions, Load prompt, and Load protocol are fully equivalent. The user does not need to strictly input the text within backticks; semantically clear synonymous short phrases are executed under the same protocol.

docs.title: 3.2 Establish Understanding
docs.text:
Execute the following complete actions:

  1. Read-only understand key UCAgent source code, focusing on CLI, configuration, stage, Checker, RoleInfo, file permissions, history, MCP, and TUI.
  2. Read-only understand sub-workflow README, docs, Guide_Doc, configuration, workflow_spec, Makefile, environment files, and user input contract.
  3. Establish stages, tools, Checkers, inputs/outputs, and the final delivery chain based on the central contract.
  4. Perform a second deep read of source code, specs, and fixtures for tools/Checkers involved in the current problem only.
  5. Output an understanding summary and hypotheses still needing verification.
  6. Do not modify or start.

If the user says Quickly establish understanding, still read all central contracts, but UCAgent source code only reads the core paragraphs listed in this file, not expanding to unrelated modules; keep output concise.

docs.title: 3.3 Supervise Execution
docs.text:
Expand into tmux supervision strategy:

  1. Check variables and whether a process for the same target already exists.
  2. In CHILD_WORKFLOW, run make check; if it returns non-zero, do not start, instead enter failure diagnosis.
  3. Create or use the agreed tmux session.
  4. Execute ENV_COMMANDS.
  5. After reading Makefile, select the sub-workflow runtime entry that indeed includes --loop --loop-msg.
  6. Start using the correct TARGET, OUT, and TUI parameters.
  7. Report the attach command.
  8. Observe periodically according to CHECK_INTERVAL.
  9. When reaching the failure threshold, execute the diagnosis and stop rules defined in this protocol.

Supervise Execution Incremental is the same, but uses the sub-workflow config/inc.yaml corresponding entry.

docs.title: 3.4 Intervene in Execution
docs.text:
Expand into tmux intervention strategy:

  1. Check variables and existing processes.
  2. make check must pass first.
  3. Create tmux, execute environment commands.
  4. Use TUI/MCP entries not containing --loop, --loop-msg, and enable no-history mode.
  5. Confirm the actual MCP port.
  6. After MCP access, first call RoleInfo, then obtain current status and task.
  7. External Agents execute stage tasks personally, preventing internal Agents from auto-looping.

Intervene in Execution Incremental uses incremental configuration, but other conventions remain unchanged.

docs.title: 3.5 Take Over Current Stage
docs.text:
Do not create new processes. Connect to the UCAgent MCP already started by the user:

  1. Confirm workspace, target, and MCP port from the current tmux/log.
  2. Call RoleInfo.
  3. Call the status tool to confirm current stage, reference/output, Checker, and failure count.
  4. Complete the current stage according to the intervention strategy.
  5. Do not automatically take over the next stage unless the user says Continue takeover or Take over to completion.

docs.title: 3.6 Continue Supervision
docs.text: Continue observing the existing tmux session; do not create new, restart, or change the execution mode. Check immediately once, then continue according to the agreed interval. If the process has exited, switch to Check Artifacts; do not silently restart.

docs.title: 3.7 View Status
docs.text:
Perform a single non-invasive check and reply immediately:

  • Whether tmux/session exists, whether attached, and the current command in the pane.
  • Current stage/index, duration, fail_count.
  • Latest valid action and the most recent complete error.
  • Whether there is progress, waiting, looping, exit, or residual processes.

Do not modify, send input, or start new processes.

docs.title: 3.8 Check Failure Cause
docs.text:
Pause automatic judgment and perform an evidence-driven diagnosis:

  • Extract the last three complete errors.
  • Read RoleInfo/Status and the current stage contract.
  • Read relevant tools, Checkers, specs, fixtures, and necessary UCAgent source code.
  • Establish a minimal reproduction.
  • Determine responsibility layer and suggested fix.

Analyze only, do not modify; unless the user says Check and fix failure cause.

docs.title: 3.9 Stop Execution
docs.text: Send a single Ctrl-C to the agreed tmux pane, wait for UCAgent to clean up and exit. Continue observing until the business process truly terminates. By default, retain the tmux shell and formal artifacts; do not kill the session, do not delete history, do not clean tmp. If still in the framework cleanup phase after one Ctrl-C, wait, do not send signals consecutively.

docs.title: 3.10 Deep Repair
docs.text:
First ensure relevant runs have stopped, then:

  1. Establish or refresh understanding.
  2. Perform complete production chain analysis on the problem pointed out by the user and current evidence.
  3. Directly modify the responsibility files in CHILD_WORKFLOW.
  4. Synchronize source code, spec, registration, configuration, fixture, Checker, and documentation.
  5. Add positive and negative examples.
  6. Execute specialized tests and complete make check; must return 0.
  7. Do not automatically rerun the business process; wait for the user to say No historical rerun or Repair and rerun.

docs.title: 3.11 Repair Current Issue
docs.text: Only fix the confirmed root cause of the current issue, not expanding to other open issues. Complete specialized tests and make check, but do not rerun the business process. If root cause evidence is insufficient, first switch to Check failure cause.

docs.title: 3.12 Repair and Rerun
docs.text: Execute Deep Repair, Verify Repair, and No Historical Rerun in sequence. Stop if any verification command returns non-zero, do not enter rerun.

docs.title: 3.13 Verify Repair
docs.text:
Do not modify, only verify the current formal sub-workflow:

  1. Run specialized tests for the affected tools or Checker.
  2. Run complete make check.
  3. Optionally run minimal smoke tests, but do not default to starting the full expensive business process.
  4. Report command, cwd, return code, and failing test cases.

Any forced command returning non-zero means the conclusion must be failure.

docs.title: 3.14 No Historical Rerun
docs.text: Restart with the most recent explicit strategy, but ensure the final UCAgent command includes --no-history. It does not mean deleting business output; do not execute rm -rf without authorization. If there is no explicit strategy recently, default to supervision strategy, but explain this choice before startup.
