docs.title: 3.15 Check Artifacts
docs.text:
Do not modify, do not rerun. Verify:

  • .ucagent/ucagent_info.json
  • Formal output/<TARGET>/
  • Declarations in config/workflow_spec
  • Results from tools and Checkers
  • Consistency among final JSON, Markdown, JUnit, etc. reports
  • Whether user input and res have been modified
  • Whether temporary files are only in allowed areas

Conclusions use "Pass, Partially pass, Fail, Blocked".

docs.title: 3.16 Full Acceptance
docs.text: Execute Check Artifacts, then run Verify Repair, and check residual processes, historical states, environment entries, final report consistency, and user requirement coverage. Full acceptance performs more real commands than Check Artifacts.

docs.title: 3.17 Clean Temporary Files
docs.text: Only clean temporary content in WORKSPACE_ROOT/tmp/ allowed by the protocol. List the cleanup scope before execution; do not delete change_history, logs explicitly required by the user, or profiles used by running processes. When involving historical versions, obtain explicit user permission first.

docs.title: 3.18 Command Combinations and Priority
docs.text:
• Establish understanding first, then supervise execution: Execute two commands in sequence.
  • Supervise until Stage N: Stop automatic execution and report upon reaching this stage.
  • Supervise only, do not fix: Stop and report after reaching the threshold without modifying.
  • Diagnose and fix failure causes: Diagnose first; repair and verify only if evidence is sufficient, without automatic rerun.
  • Take over until completion: Execute in intervention mode through all stages until completion.
  • Continue: Continue the most recent incomplete action; if the recent action is ambiguous, report the current status first.
  • Restrictions such as Do not modify, Do not start, and View only take precedence over all default actions.
  • User messages override old conventions, but uncovered protocols remain valid.

docs.title: 4. Fixed Boundaries
docs.text:
1. The repair target is the configuration, tools, Checker, specifications, documentation, Makefile, and environment support facilities within CHILD_WORKFLOW.
  2. UCAgent source code may be read to understand framework behavior, but modification of UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/ and UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent.py is prohibited without explicit user authorization.
  3. Do not research or modify the five eval_*.yaml files of the parent workflow to replace analysis of the child workflow.
  4. Do not directly modify output/<TARGET>/ generated by a single run to fabricate workflow success. Repair the true producers: child workflow configuration, tools, Checker, task descriptions, or environment entry points, then rerun.
  5. WORKSPACE_ROOT/res/ contains user-maintained professional knowledge; it is read-only by default and not automatically deployed by the Agent.
  6. Temporary scripts, fixtures, logs, browser profiles, and experimental artifacts must be placed in WORKSPACE_ROOT/tmp/.
  7. User input must remain unchanged. Do not modify CHILD_WORKFLOW/input/<TARGET>/ to accommodate tool implementations.
  8. A non-zero return code from a command indicates failure. Do not rewrite facts based on partial PASS lines, TUI completion messages, or Agent self-reports.

docs.title: 5.1 UCAgent Essential Files
docs.text:
These files are for understanding the framework only and are not default modification targets:

File Content to Understand UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/cli.py CLI parameters, especially loop, TUI, MCP, history, config, output, guid-doc-path UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/verify_agent.py Configuration initialization, template overwrite, tool registration, permission settings, and Verify Agent lifecycle UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/stage/vstage.py Stage creation, reference file read tracking, output file checks, Checker invocation, and Complete conditions UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/stage/vmanager.py Stage switching, tool commands, Complete, history synchronization, and failure handling UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/checkers/base.py Checker base class, return protocol, and description requirements UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/tools/uctool.py Interfaces and return content of UCAgent tools such as RoleInfo UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/tools/fileops.py Read/Edit/Write tools and write_dirs/un_write_dirs boundaries UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/util/config.py YAML configuration objects and recursive replacement methods for template_overwrite UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/server/api_mcp.py How MCP service starts, thread lifecycle, and port behavior UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/tui/app.py TUI prerequisites, terminal display, and interaction entry points UCAGENT_ROOT/ucagent/setting.yaml UCAgent default settings and global behaviors that may affect execution

Read specifically when encountering concrete issues:

  • Path expansion or reference_files tracking anomalies: Continue reading template, path search, and directory synchronization functions in ucagent/util/functions.py.
  • History recovery, permissions, or .ucagent/history anomalies: Continue reading hist_sync, hist_commit, and UCAgent information saving logic in vstage.py and vmanager.py.
  • MCP integration issues: Continue reading the service startup section in server/api_mcp.py and verify_pdb.py.
  • TUI not appearing or color anomalies: Read tui/ and the CLI handling of --tui, and check for a real TTY; do not modify business configuration first.

docs.title: 5.2 UCAgent Understanding Prompt
docs.text:
In this phase, read UCAgent only, do not modify source code, and do not start the child workflow.

Read in order:
1. Definitions and passing locations of --loop, --loop-msg, --tui, --no-history, --mcp-server,
   --mcp-server-port, --config, --output, --guid-doc-path in ucagent/cli.py.
2. Config loading, template_overwrite, RoleInfo registration, write_dirs/un_write_dirs, and stage manager construction in ucagent/verify_agent.py.
3. reference_files initialization, ReadTextFile callback, output_files lookup, checker execution, fail_count, Complete, and history status in ucagent/stage/vstage.py.
4. Check/Complete/Status, stage switching, and history commit in ucagent/stage/vmanager.py.
5. Checker/RoleInfo protocols in ucagent/checkers/base.py and ucagent/tools/uctool.py.
6. Read/write permission checks in ucagent/tools/fileops.py.
7. Template replacement model in ucagent/util/config.py.
8. MCP lifecycle in ucagent/server/api_mcp.py.

Produce a framework understanding summary, answering:
- When does UCAgent consider a stage complete?
- How are reference_files marked as read?
- Does output_files check only existence or also content?
- What Checker return value increases fail_count?
- What problem does --no-history solve, and what cannot it solve?
- Who drives the Agent in --loop mode versus no-loop mode?
- Is write_dirs/un_write_dirs a general file tool restriction or a system sandbox for all Python code?
- What can MCP RoleInfo obtain, and why must it be called before intervention?

Do not provide generic summaries; provide source code paths and key class/function names, but do not copy large blocks of UCAgent source code.

docs.title: 5.3 Pitfalls to Avoid When Establishing Understanding
docs.text:
1. Do not treat reference_files as ordinary prompt text. UCAgent tracks whether they are read via the read file tool.
  2. Do not equate the existence of output_files with correct artifacts; business semantics are still guaranteed by Checkers or specialized tests.
  3. Do not consider write_dirs as an OS-level security boundary; it primarily constrains UCAgent's general file tools.
  4. Do not assume --no-history clears business output; it only affects UCAgent history recovery.
  5. Do not judge path equivalence by string appearance. Confirm whether UCAgent normalizes paths at the corresponding location.
  6. Do not equate TUI exit with all stages passing; still check ucagent_info.json and actual command return codes.

docs.title: 6. Establish Understanding of the Child Workflow
6.1 First Round Essential Reading
docs.text:
Read the central contract and user entry points first:

CHILD_WORKFLOW/README.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/docs/README.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/docs/01 Quick Start.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/docs/02 Input/Output.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/docs/03 Steps and Checks.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/docs/04 Developer Docs-tools.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/docs/05 Developer Docs-checkers.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/Guide_Doc/
CHILD_WORKFLOW/config.yaml
CHILD_WORKFLOW/config/inc.yaml
CHILD_WORKFLOW/.workflow/workflow_spec.yaml
CHILD_WORKFLOW/Makefile
CHILD_WORKFLOW/setup.py
CHILD_WORKFLOW/ucagent_setup.sh
CHILD_WORKFLOW/requirements.txt

Then check target input, but read-only:

CHILD_WORKFLOW/input/<TARGET>/

If the following design memories exist, they must be read:

WORKSPACE_ROOT/workflow_implementation_plan.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/workflow_implementation_plan.md
CHILD_WORKFLOW/.workflow/build_report.md

The "Issues and Handling" for each stage in workflow_implementation_plan.md is crucial for repairing the child workflow. It explains trade-offs made during generation, which constraints are prone to failure, and the original design intent of tools/Checkers.

docs.title: 6.2 Second Round Directed Reading by Problem
docs.text: Read a complete chain based on the failed component, do not read just one file:

docs.title: Tool Issues
docs.text:
tools/<Tool>.py
.workflow/tool_specs/<Tool>.yaml
Tool invocation stage in config.yaml or config/inc.yaml
Tool contract in .workflow/workflow_spec.yaml
Positive examples, negative examples, and fixtures in .workflow/tool_tests/
docs/04 Developer Docs-tools.md
Related Guide_Doc

docs.title: Checker Issues
docs.text:
checkers/<checker>.py
.workflow/checker_specs/<Checker>.yaml
Checker parameter binding in config.yaml and config/inc.yaml
Checker planning in .workflow/workflow_spec.yaml
.checker_tests/ or corresponding fixtures in .workflow/
docs/05 Developer Docs-checkers.md
Tools and stages producing the checked artifact

docs.title: Stage or Path Issues
docs.text:
Simultaneous comparison:

config.yaml
config/inc.yaml
.workflow/workflow_spec.yaml
workspace, TARGET, OUT, and config passed in Makefile
Actual input/<TARGET>/ and output/<TARGET>/ layouts

Key checks:

  • Stage order and Checker timing.
  • Whether reference_files are determined to exist before this stage.
  • Whether all output_files are specific files.
  • Whether {OUT}, {DUT}, and custom template variables are declared and not concatenated redundantly.
  • Whether default and incremental flows maintain consistent stage names.
  • Whether tool actual read/write paths match declared configurations.

docs.title: 6.3 Sub-Workflow Understanding Prompt
docs.text:
Currently, only establish understanding of the sub-workflow without modification.

Read README, docs, Guide_Doc, config.yaml, config/inc.yaml,
.workflow/workflow_spec.yaml, Makefile, and environment files. Based on these files, draw:

1. User input contract: which files the user must provide, and which content is automatically generated by the workflow.
2. Main flow stage diagram: tools, inputs, outputs, and Checkers for each stage.
3. Incremental flow stage diagram: shared and different contracts compared to the main flow.
4. Tool list: registered name, source code, spec, called stage, and primary artifacts.
5. Checker list: class name, parameters, bound stage, and actual check object.
6. Environment entry: how setup.py, ucagent_setup.sh, and Makefile combine to start UCAgent.
7. Final deliverables: file paths, producers, and final acceptors.

Afterwards, read the most recent failed TUI output, .ucagent/ucagent_info.json, related logs, and formal output.
Conduct a second round of complete reading only for source code/spec/fixtures involved in the failure chain.

Output the difference between "declared behavior" and "actual behavior," and do not claim the root cause before running a minimal reproduction.

docs.title: 7.1 Definition
docs.text:
The tmux supervision strategy allows the internal Agent within the sub-workflow to execute automatically using a loop. The external Agent is responsible for starting, periodically observing, and diagnosing. After detecting the same issue failing repeatedly, it stops execution, repairs the sub-workflow itself, and then restarts for verification.

Under supervision, the following can be repaired:

  • CHILD_WORKFLOW/config.yaml, config/inc.yaml
  • CHILD_WORKFLOW/tools/
  • CHILD_WORKFLOW/checkers/
  • .workflow/tool_specs/, .workflow/checker_specs/, workflow_spec.yaml
  • Guide_Doc/, docs/
  • Makefile, setup.py, ucagent_setup.sh, requirements.txt

Under supervision, the following must NOT be done:

  • Directly modify output/<TARGET>/ to make the current run pass.
  • Modify user inputs.
  • Modify the core UCAgent source code.
  • Complete the task for the internal Agent after a single failure; first give it the opportunity to self-repair based on the Checker.

docs.title: 7.2 Supervision Prompt
docs.text:
This time, the tmux supervision strategy is adopted. The repair target is <CHILD_WORKFLOW>.

Before startup:
1. Preliminary understanding of UCAgent operation mechanism and sub-workflow contract is completed.
2. cd <CHILD_WORKFLOW>.
3. Read the help, run, run_tui, run_inc commands and environment initialization in Makefile to confirm the accurate commands.
4. Execute ucagent_env and proxy_on; if the sub-workflow requires sourcing ucagent_setup.sh, execute it via the real contract in Makefile, not by guessing.
5. First run make check; it must return 0. Otherwise, repair basic checks first without starting the business process.

Startup:
- Create a unique tmux session.
- Use the automatic run entry of the sub-workflow with --loop/--loop-msg.
- Specify the correct TARGET, OUT, and working directory.
- Maintain a real TTY/TUI; do not replace the interactive terminal with tee or redirection.
- Inform the user of the tmux attach command.

Supervision:
- Capture the most recent output approximately every two minutes.
- Report stage name, stage index, duration, fail_count, and the latest tool and Checker errors.
- 0 to 2 failures usually allow the internal Agent to self-repair.
- Begin root cause analysis when the same error occurs continuously 3 times.
- Stop execution when the same error occurs continuously 5 times, with no new evidence or obvious loops.

After stopping:
- Do not modify the current output artifacts.
- Read the corresponding tool, Checker, spec, configuration, fixture, and UCAgent framework related source code.
- Modify the root cause file in CHILD_WORKFLOW.
- Add or update positive and negative examples for the sub-workflow itself.
- Run make check and specific tests; the return code must be 0.
- Restart using a no-history mode to avoid continuing from an old stage index.

After the process ends, do not rely solely on TUI. Verify .ucagent/ucagent_info.json, formal output, Checker results, and Make command return codes.

docs.title: 7.3 Supervision Startup Example
docs.text:
The specific target follows the sub-workflow Makefile. Common methods:

cd /home/peter/FDocB/UCAgent_t/workspace_za/workspace/workflow
tmux new-session -s child_supervise
ucagent_env
proxy_on
make run TARGET=<TARGET>

If a user-visible TUI is required but run is a non-TUI loop, add a supervision target in the sub-workflow Makefile that includes both --tui and --loop, or use the supervision entry it already provides. Do not misuse run_tui without a loop and claim the internal Agent will execute automatically.

View:

tmux attach -t child_supervise
tmux capture-pane -pt child_supervise -S -180

docs.title: 8.1 Definition
docs.text:
The tmux intervention strategy starts the sub-workflow UCAgent TUI and MCP but does not enable automatic loops. The external Agent calls RoleInfo via MCP first, then personally executes the current stage. This mode is suitable for:

  • When the automatic Agent misunderstands the same task for a long time.
  • When the complete structured return of tools and Checkers needs to be observed.
  • When verification of how UCAgent actually tracks reference/output is required.
  • When the user requires the Agent to take over a step.

docs.title: 8.2 Intervention Prompt
docs.text:
This time, the tmux intervention strategy is adopted. The target is the sub-workflow, not workflow_builder.

1. cd <CHILD_WORKFLOW>.
2. Create a unique tmux session.
3. Execute ucagent_env and proxy_on.
4. Use the TUI/MCP entry without --loop and --loop-msg according to the sub-workflow Makefile.
   Common targets are make run_tui TARGET=<TARGET>, but the Makefile must be read first to confirm.
5. Use --no-history or the target's built-in no-history parameter to ensure starting from the expected stage.
6. Confirm the actual MCP port; do not guess.
7. After MCP access, call RoleInfo first to obtain the role and system prompt.
8. Then call Status/task information to confirm the current stage, reference_files, output_files, Checker, and fail_count.
9. Use ReadTextFile to fully read the reference files required for this stage, ensuring UCAgent correctly records the read status.
10. Call the business tools registered by the sub-workflow according to the task; do not fake tool results with manual scripts.
11. Call SetCurrentStageJournal to save evidence, then call Check/Complete.
12. On failure, read the complete last_check_result and correct according to structured errors; do not invoke the same error repeatedly.
13. After completion, read the status again to confirm the stage index has advanced.

The intervention Agent can complete the output artifacts required for the current run because it is playing the role of the internal Agent of the sub-workflow;
however, it must not bypass registered tools, Checkers, and stage contracts to forge content. If the root cause belongs to sub-workflow design, stop the current run, modify sub-workflow configuration, tools, Checkers, specs, or documentation, execute make check, and restart.

Do not modify the core UCAgent source code. If framework behavior is suspicious, first provide a minimal reproduction and evidence based on UCAgent source code, and let the user decide whether to open a separate UCAgent repair task.

docs.title: 8.3 Intervention Startup Example
docs.text:
For the current common generation workflow:

cd /home/peter/FDocB/UCAgent_t/workspace_za/workspace/workflow
tmux new-session -s child_intervene
ucagent_env
proxy_on
make run_tui TARGET=<TARGET>

After startup, confirm that TUI does not execute automatically. If automatic Agent messages appear, check if the final command still contains --loop or --loop-msg.

docs.title: 9. Continuous Failure Diagnosis Prompt
docs.text:
The sub-workflow current stage has failed continuously. Do not lower Checker standards, nor manually modify output to fake success.

Please execute the following diagnosis:
1. Record session, TARGET, cwd, config path, output root directory, stage name/index, fail_count, and time_cost.
2. Extract the last three complete last_check_result to determine if it is the same error.
3. Call or read RoleInfo/Status to confirm the actual task received by the Agent, not guessing based on config fragments.
4. Verify reference_files exist and are indeed read via ReadTextFile.
5. Verify output_files are specific files produced by the current stage, and check content, not just existence.
6. Read the current Checker source code, docstring, spec, args binding, and positive/negative fixtures.
7. Read the source code and actual return structure of the artifact-producing tool, checking if the Checker uses the correct fields.
8. Compare with UCAgent's vstage/vmanager implementation to determine if the failure comes from business Checker, reference file tracking, output existence check, history synchronization, or tool invocation.
9. Run the tool or Checker independently with a minimal fixture:
   - Correct artifact rejected: Checker may be misjudging.
   - Incorrect artifact accepted: Checker may be missing detection.
   - Tool unable to produce declared fields: Tool and contract inconsistent.
   - Checker bound before artifact generation: Stage timing error.
10. When checking paths and templates, verify based on UCAgent's actual replacement model, not subjective string equivalence.
11. Identify the root cause layer: sub-workflow task/Guide, configuration, tool, Checker, fixture, Makefile, environment, or UCAgent framework.

Stop the process when the same failure reaches five times with no new information. After repairing CHILD_WORKFLOW, run make check and affected specific tests, confirm return code 0, and restart using no-history mode.

docs.title: 10. Sub-Workflow Deep Repair Prompt
docs.text:
Perform a deep repair on the sub-workflow; do not apply one-off patches that merely allow the current output to pass.

Establish a complete chain for each issue:
User input and requirements
-> stage tasks in config/config.inc
-> registered tools and tool specs
-> intermediate artifacts
-> Checker source code, checker spec, and parameter binding
-> subsequent stages
-> final deliverable
-> Makefile and user documentation.

Simultaneously verify framework facts using UCAgent source code:
- When template variables are replaced.
- How reference_files match and mark as read.
- How output_files determine existence.
- When Checkers are invoked and how failures are accumulated.
- How history, permissions, MCP, and TUI affect execution.

Repair Priority:
1. Failures to start, hang, infinite retries, or exit codes being masked.
2. Sub-workflows deviating from user requirements yet reporting completion.
3. Checkers accepting erroneous artifacts or rejecting correct ones.
4. Inconsistencies between tool declarations, implementations, registration, specs, and actual outputs.
5. Errors in stage sequencing, paths, template variables, and input/output contracts.
6. Inconsistencies between documentation and actual commands or source code.

Each repair must include at least:
- Minimal reproduction.
- Root cause file and framework basis.
- Formal sub-workflow source code or configuration modification.
- Corresponding positive and negative examples.
- Necessary Guide_Doc and developer documentation updates.
- `make check` returning 0.
- Affected specialized tests returning 0.

Do not modify UCAgent core source code. Do not read the parent workflow eval YAML. Do not modify user res/. Do not cover defects by deleting tests, lowering Checker standards, or modifying output results.

docs.title: 11. Tool Repair Checklist
docs.text:
When repairing a sub-workflow tool, verify each item:

  1. name matches the registered name and spec filename.
  2. Classes and entry methods comply with UCAgent external tool specifications.
  3. input_schema matches stage invocation parameters.
  4. output_schema matches the actual returned ok/data/errors/warnings/meta.
  5. Both success and failure returns are structurally complete.
  6. Path restrictions are bounded by the sub-workflow root directory; absolute paths and .. escapes are prohibited.
  7. Upon failure, no partial formal artifacts remain that could be misread by subsequent stages.
  8. Temporary files must reside in WORKSPACE_ROOT/tmp/ or a clearly defined temporary area within the sub-workflow.
  9. Positive examples verify real business values, not just key existence.
  10. Negative examples cover missing, malformed, out-of-bounds, and downstream unconsumable results.
  11. .workflow/tool_specs/, configuration registration, workflow_spec, and developer documentation are synchronized.
  12. Pass make check_tools, make test_tools, and the full make check.

docs.title: 12. Checker Repair Checklist
docs.text:
When repairing a Checker, verify each item:

  1. The class inherits UCAgent's Checker base class.
  2. The docstring clearly describes the check object; otherwise, registration may result in "No description provided".
  3. Constructor parameters match config, inc config, and checker spec completely.
  4. Every received parameter is actually used in do_check, or removed from the contract.
  5. Missing files, malformed JSON/YAML/XML, empty content, and permission anomalies cleanly return failure without raising unhandled exceptions.
  6. Checkers bind after artifact generation; they cannot inspect future files prematurely.
  7. Do not redundantly check the same immutable artifact across multiple stages without meaning.
  8. Positive examples cover complete actual paths; do not bypass core logic via optional parameters.
  9. Negative examples separately cover different error causes; a single fixture must not contain multiple defects.
  10. Checkers cannot only verify file existence; they must validate business semantics of interest to the user.
  11. Source code, spec, workflow_spec, config, inc config, and developer documentation are synchronized.
  12. Pass make check_checkers, make test_checkers, and the full make check.

docs.title: 13. Environment and Makefile Repair Prompt
docs.text:
When repairing the sub-workflow environment, first read the Makefile, setup.py, ucagent_setup.sh,
config/environment.schema.yaml, requirements.txt, and quick-start documentation.

Verify:
- Declared targets in `make help` actually exist.
- setup.py interactions, --check, --dry-run, --non-interactive, and --set behaviors are consistent.
- Controlled environment blocks do not overwrite user manual content.
- ucagent_env and proxy_on take effect correctly in the sub-shell.
- UCAGENT_HOME, virtual environment, PYTHONPATH, TARGET, OUT, and workspace are passed correctly.
- run, run_tui, run_inc, run_inc_tui loop/TUI/history semantics match their names.
- Commands using tee truly propagate underlying exit codes.
- clean only removes allowed temporary areas; it does not delete input, output, res, or evaluation records.
- Non-zero return codes from `make check` are not masked by subsequent grep, tee, or shell structures.

Record all verification details including real argv, cwd, and returncode. Do not judge Make target success solely based on PASS appearing in logs.

docs.title: 14. Post-Run Acceptance Prompt
docs.text:
Perform independent acceptance after sub-workflow execution:

1. Confirm UCAgent has exited in tmux, with no residual Agent, MCP, or business subprocesses.
2. Read .ucagent/ucagent_info.json and verify all_completed, stage index, and failure count.
3. Verify formal output/<TARGET>/; do not treat tmp candidates as formal results.
4. Verify declared artifacts against actual artifacts stage by stage according to config and workflow_spec.
5. Re-run `make check`, saving the actual return code; it must be 0.
6. Run affected tool/checker specialized tests, saving the actual return code.
7. Cross-verify pass count, fail count, verdict, and JUnit/JSON/Markdown in the final report.
8. Verify user input has not been modified.
9. Verify res/ has not been automatically overwritten by the Agent.
10. Verify no temporary files are scattered in tools/, checkers/, wfgen/, or the sub-workflow root directory.

Final conclusion must be one of:
- Pass: All mandatory commands return 0, and final artifacts meet requirements.
- Partial Pass: Some repairs are effective, but non-gatekeeping observations remain, and all mandatory commands return 0.
- Fail: Any mandatory command returns non-zero, critical artifacts are erroneous, or the report contradicts facts.
- Block: Missing user input, external dependencies, or permissions prevent obtaining valid evidence.

docs.title: Under Supervision
docs.text:
Repair Target: <CHILD_WORKFLOW>
tmux session: <SESSION>
Strategy: Supervise / Intervene
TARGET: <TARGET>
Current Stage: <NAME> (<INDEX>/<TOTAL>)
Duration: <DURATION>
Failure Count: <FAIL_COUNT>
Latest Tool or Checker: <NAME>
Latest Error: <STRUCTURED_ERROR>
Current Judgment: Self-repair normal / Sub-workflow configuration issue / Tool issue / Checker issue / Environment issue /
UCAgent framework doubt
Next Step: Continue observing / Minimal reproduction / Stop and repair sub-workflow

docs.title: Repair Complete
docs.text:
Modified sub-workflow files:
- <PATH>: <BEHAVIOR_CHANGE>

UCAgent Framework Basis:
- <UCAGENT_SOURCE_PATH>: <CONFIRMED_BEHAVIOR>

Verification:
- <COMMAND>, cwd=<PATH>, returncode=<CODE>
- <COMMAND>, cwd=<PATH>, returncode=<CODE>

Final Artifacts:
- <PATH>: <RESULT>

Unresolved Issues:
- <SEVERITY>: <ISSUE>

Conclusion: Pass / Partial Pass / Fail / Block

docs.title: 16. Unbreakable Conventions
docs.text:
1. The repair target is the sub-workflow, not the parent workflow workflow_builder.
  2. There is no requirement to read the parent workflow's five eval_*.yaml files.
  3. Read UCAgent source code to establish understanding, but do not modify UCAgent without authorization.
  4. tmux supervision mode allows internal Agents to auto-loop, while external Agents observe periodically.
  5. tmux intervention mode removes the loop; after MCP access, call RoleInfo first.
  6. Execute ucagent_env and proxy_on before startup.
  7. Use real TTY/TUI; do not fake TUI via pipes.
  8. Use history-less mode for new tasks to avoid erroneously restoring old stages.
  9. Do not modify user input.
  10. Do not modify user-maintained res/.
  11. Do not directly repair output artifacts to mask production chain issues.
  12. Temporary files must only enter WORKSPACE_ROOT/tmp/.
  13. reference_files/output_files declare specific files only, not directories.
  14. Non-zero commands must not be written as passed.
  15. After repair, the sub-workflow's own make check and specialized tests must be run.

docs.title: Workflow Builder Parent Workflow Secondary Development Overview
docs.text: This set of documents is intended for users preparing to perform secondary development on the parent workflow located in examples/workflow_builder/. The goal is to assist developers in modifying the parent workflow stages, generators, evaluation control, incremental deployment, console, and delivery contracts, rather than guiding how a specific sub-workflow Agent should complete business tasks. The generated workflows, business Tools, business Checkers, and GuideDoc mentioned in this text are output objects of the parent workflow code, used to explain the impact of a single parent code modification.

docs.title: Secondary Development Goals
docs.text:
After reading this set of documents, developers should be able to locate the actual modification entry point within the parent workflow from a requirement or defect, understand module interfaces and call relationships, design backward-compatible data structures, supplement deterministic regression, and verify generation effects using independent business validation. A single business generation failure may originate from the requirement, parent stage description, GuideDoc, generator, Checker, UCAgent runtime, or external services; parent code should only be modified after confirming the responsibility domain. Modifying the UCAgent core or manually supplementing sub-artifacts to mask problems is not acceptable.

We do not repeat the daily startup steps found in Usage, nor do we treat stage prompts as developer tutorials. Developers are concerned with: which YAML defines the stage, which UCTool exposes the tool, how to write core functions to files, which schemas and regressions must be synchronized, and how to ensure any future business obtains the fix.

docs.title: Reading Order
docs.text:
1. Workflow Introduction: Understand the data flow of construction, evaluation, incremental, and console.
  2. Tool Introduction: Understand tool registration, invocation, return structures, and write boundaries.
  3. Checker Introduction: Understand stage acceptance, parameter injection, and evidence semantics.
  4. GuideDoc Introduction: Understand GuideDoc templates, stage FAQs, and minimal examples.
  5. Evaluation and Incremental Control: Understand approval, candidates, deployment, and version history.
  6. Testing and Regression: Determine which deterministic checks must run after modification.
  7. Secondary Development Guide for Workflow Artifacts: Understand components, ownership, extension order, and criteria for judging whether to feed back to the parent generator.

docs.title: Parent Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text: Secondary development typically begins with one of four entry points. Process behavior modifications involve config.yaml, inc.yaml, eval_*.yaml, and their Guide_Doc/ directories; product generation capability modifications involve tools/workflow_builder/ and the four generators; evaluation, approval, deployment, or UI modifications involve tools/workflow_evaluation_control/; and runtime and environment entry modifications involve the root Makefile and setup. After determining the entry point, read the corresponding source code analysis, do not edit a historical workspace_x/workflow/ first.

docs.title: Primary Source Code Areas
docs.text: Area Responsibility tools/workflow_builder/ Read construction design, create skeleton, environment facilities, configuration, and inline Checkers tools/workflow_tool_generator/ Generate and register tools according to tool spec tools/workflow_checker_generator/ Generate Checker source code, fixtures, and registration information tools/workflow_config_generator/ Generate main configuration and incremental configuration, inject stage contracts tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/ Generate and register GuideDoc tools/workflow_evaluation_control/ Structured reports, approval, incremental run, deployment history, and console Guide_Doc/ Parent workflow stage execution rules, FAQs, and evaluation rules regression/ Model-independent protocols, boundaries, and regression tests

docs.title: Development Boundaries
docs.text:
• Prioritize modifying the parent workflow within examples/workflow_builder/; do not modify the UCAgent core to mask generator issues.
  • Business-specific filenames cannot be written to generic GuideDoc unless it is explicitly marked as an example.
  • New tools or Checkers must synchronize updates to spec, registration, tests, configuration, and generated documentation.
  • reference_files and output_files can only list files, not directories; referenced files must exist before execution in that stage.
  • All temporary files enter the workspace tmp/; evaluation reports enter eval/; user expertise enters res/.
  • Long documents should use indexing and on-demand reading strategies; do not require the Agent to read all materials in full every round just to "establish understanding."

docs.title: Problem Statement Before Modification
docs.text: It is recommended to clearly write observable symptoms, minimal reproduction commands, failed stages, Checker messages, related artifacts, and expected behavior. For performance issues, also record stage start time, actual tool invocations, whether artifact timestamps have changed, and whether context compression has occurred. This allows distinguishing real computation, model waiting, and stateless idle loops.

docs.title: Completion Definition
docs.text: Development modification is only considered complete when all the following conditions are met: code implementation and documentation are consistent; target regressions pass; no other generators are broken; new fields have a compatibility strategy; generated artifacts can be accepted by make check; and during real workspace verification, no sub-workflow artifacts are hand-written by the parent Agent.

docs.title: Entry Map from Command to Source Code
docs.text:
Developers must first clarify which layer of entry they are running. The run, run_eval_*, and run_inc commands in the root Makefile all start UCAgent within the business construction workspace, but the loaded configurations come respectively from config.yaml in the Workflow Builder root directory, evaluation configuration, and inc.yaml. The Makefile is responsible for preparing the workspace, copying public inputs, selecting the output root, setting PYTHONPATH, starting the permission daemon, and passing TUI/loop parameters. UCAgent then invokes the UCTools registered in this directory according to the stages in the configuration; these tools then enter the various generators or evaluation control modules.

Key entry points can be located using the table below:

User Action Make Entry Python Entry Main Persistence Result Generate business workflow run workflow_builder.core.build_workflow and respective UCTools wfgen/, workflow/ Generate business Tool Internal call during build stage workflow_tool_generator.core.generate_tools_from_specs workflow/tools/, tool registration Generate business Checker Internal call during build stage workflow_checker_generator.core.generate_checkers_from_specs Checker, fixture, stage registration Generate configuration Internal call during build stage workflow_config_generator.core.generate_config workflow/config.yaml, config/inc.yaml Generate GuideDoc Internal call during build stage workflow_guidedoc_generator.core.generate_guidedocs workflow/Guide_Doc/, registration Write evaluation report run_eval_* StructuredJsonStore, json_store.mutate_document eval/*.json Incremental deployment run_inc incremental.deploy_incremental_changes workflow/, tmp/change_history/ Console eval-ui review_server.serve Update approval, suggestions, and structured design via API

If the issue occurs in generated artifacts, still trace upward along this table: which template or spec generated the artifact file, which parent stage wrote the spec, which Checker should have intercepted earlier. Fixing a single line in the last generated file might pass the current workspace, but cannot improve the next business.

docs.title: Core Data Object Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_builder/core.py, symbols WorkflowBuildError and BuildReport.

class WorkflowBuildError(RuntimeError):
    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str):
        super().__init__(f"{code}: {message}")
        self.code = code
        self.message = message

@dataclass
class BuildReport:
    workflow_name: str = ""
    created_dirs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    created_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    skipped_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

These two types reflect the error and result boundaries of the generator. WorkflowBuildError uses stable error codes to distinguish issues like "configuration cannot be parsed", "path out of bounds", "Checker generation failure", etc., from ordinary Python stack traces. Callers can write the code into the UCTool's structured error, allowing stage tasks to obtain actionable reasons without parsing natural language. When adding new validation rules, choose an error code prefix consistent with the responsibility domain, and ensure one error code represents only one type of fix action.

BuildReport is not the final business report, but a change list of a materialized operation. created_files and skipped_files support determining if overwrite strategy is effective, and warnings are used to record non-blocking issues that need developer handling. New generation steps must append actual writes to the report; otherwise, although UCTool returns success, Agent and regression cannot confirm what was produced. Conversely, do not pre-register success before file write failure.

docs.title: Environment Configuration Invocation Analysis
docs.text:
The setup.py in the Workflow Builder root directory only generates .workflow_builder/local.mk. The Makefile optionally loads it before default variable definitions, so saved values can become local defaults, while the command-line make WS=... retains higher priority. This configuration is oriented towards "how to start the parent workflow", containing UCAgent source, virtual environment, default workspace, MCP/console port, and optional proxy.

The workflow/setup.py in generating business workflows comes from the WORKFLOW_ENVIRONMENT_SETUP template in tools/workflow_builder/core.py. It reads the business workflow's own config/environment.schema.yaml, saves .workflow/local/environment.yaml, and updates the controlled sections of the generated product Makefile and ucagent_setup.sh. While both share the same name, their state directories, schemas, and modification objects are completely different. Development documentation, tests, and error messages must use qualifiers like "Workflow Builder root setup" or "generated workflow setup".

The risk of environment configuration modifications focuses on three aspects: first, whether Make variable priority changes; second, whether sensitive values are written to commit-able files; third, whether half-controlled sections are left when configuration fails. Any modification should be tested for first write, repeated execution, dry-run, illegal input, command-line override, and atomic replacement.

Source location: root Makefile, local configuration load entry.

WORKFLOW_BUILDER_DIR := $(patsubst %/,%,$(dir $(abspath $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST)))))
LOCAL_CONFIG ?= $(WORKFLOW_BUILDER_DIR)/.workflow_builder/local.mk
-include $(LOCAL_CONFIG)

UCAGENT_HOME ?= $(HOME)/FDocB/UCAgent
WS ?= $(WORKFLOW_BUILDER_HOME)/workspace

First calculate the Makefile's own directory rather than relying on the caller's cwd, so local configuration can still be found when starting from the business workspace using make -f .... The -include allows the file to be missing on first use; ordinary assignments in the configuration override subsequent ?= default values, while command-line variables remain at highest priority maintained by GNU Make. Modifying this order directly affects cross-workspace startup and must be verified via three dry-runs: no configuration, with configuration, and command-line override.

docs.title: Data Ownership and Write Boundaries
docs.text:
The input/ directory is the source of user requirements; the parent Agent can only copy and read from it. The wfgen/ directory is the central design, where components are appended by responsibility during the build phase. The workflow/ directory contains public business workflows. The eval/ directory can only be updated via structured storage. The res/ directory holds user expertise. The tmp/ directory stores temporary test cases, incremental candidates, and historical versions. The write boundary is not a documentation suggestion but a security contract preventing the evaluation Agent from modifying the object being evaluated, preventing incremental Agents from exceeding their approval scope, and preventing temporary files from polluting the formal delivery.

When developing new tools, first determine which ownership category it belongs to. A standard evaluation command executor cannot write to workflow/. A candidate stager can copy from formal files to the current run directory but cannot deploy in reverse. Only a deployer can replace formal files after verifying the approval source and candidate mapping. Merging these actions into a "universal file tool" renders approval, auditing, and rollback meaningless.

docs.title: Complete Localization Example for a Single Defect
docs.text:
Assume the generated config.yaml references a non-existent {INPUT} in the first phase. Do not simply change it to an absolute path. First, read wfgen/workflow_build.yaml in the generation workspace to confirm whether the variable is declared in the runtime contract or template coverage. Then, check if workflow_config_generator.core._find_unknown_runtime_placeholders() and _inject_planned_stage_contracts() should intercept the issue. Next, verify if the parent phase GuideDoc requires a self-review after generation. Finally, add a negative fixture to the config generator containing undefined placeholders.

The correct fix ensures that all unknown placeholders fail during the generation phase and provide the field location. The current workspace can obtain the new configuration by re-running the corresponding phase or incremental process. Acceptance is not just YAML parseability; it also includes config generator regression, delivery contract, actual make check, and new business builds. This process illustrates that developers fix the mechanism producing the error and the missing defense, not a string in a historical file.

docs.title: Compatibility and Change Review
docs.text:
When modifying public spec fields, answer whether the old workspace can continue to read them. New optional fields must have clear default values; required fields must appear simultaneously in the schema, minimal example, and migration notes. Renaming fields must provide compatible reading or a clear version gate; updating only the generator while leaving the console, Checker, and regression readers using the old name is insufficient.

During review, check at least: input schema, generated files, configuration registration, user documentation, development documentation, error codes, regression fixtures, and incremental compatibility. A small number of lines of code does not imply a small impact scope; for example, changing the path rule for reference_files affects config generation, UCAgent reference tracking, evaluation, and console parsing simultaneously.

docs.title: Extension Points Summary
docs.text: This system prioritizes extension through the central schema, template renderer, UCTool wrapper, structured storage API, and console editor schema. New capabilities should choose the narrowest correct extension point: business rendering enters the corresponding generator, cross-component invariants enter central validation, manual approval enters evaluation control, and no logic should be dumped into tools/workflow_builder/core.py or arbitrary shells.

docs.title: Mother Workflow Execution Architecture and Phase Secondary Development
docs.text: This document guides developers in modifying the stage structure and end-to-end call chain of the current Workflow Builder mother workflow. The Workflow Builder generates business workflows using the "Requirement Extraction, Central Design, Component Generation, Integration Acceptance" structure; the Central Design resides in wfgen/, and the final published artifacts are located in workflow/. Understanding these execution results is necessary for safely adjusting the mother configuration, phase Checkers, and generation call order, not for readers to manually execute a specific sub-phase.

docs.title: Secondary Development Goals
docs.text: Typical tasks include adding or merging mother phases, adjusting phase inputs and outputs, modifying the central workflow spec, integrating new generators, changing evaluation blocking strategies, optimizing context reading, or fixing incremental termination conditions. Every modification must enter from the mother configuration, traverse UCTool to core, then reach generated files and Checkers, forming a closed impact analysis.

docs.title: Mother Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text:
• Main Build Phase: Root config.yaml and Guide_Doc/stages/.
  • Incremental Phase: Root inc.yaml, incremental GuideDoc, and tools/workflow_evaluation_control/.
  • Evaluation Phase: eval_tools.yaml, eval_checkers.yaml, eval_flow.yaml, eval_env.yaml, eval_run.yaml.
  • Build Execution: tools/workflow_builder/core.py and its uc_tools.py wrapper.
  • Orchestration Startup: Root Makefile.

When modifying phases, first draw the reference, output, tools, and Checker of the old phase, then design the new structure. Inserting a stage directly into YAML without updating plan markers, GuideDoc, variables, Checkers, and regression tests will result in a formally existing process that cannot execute stably.

docs.title: Build Data Flow
docs.text:
input/guide.md + input/test_input/
  -> requirements_manifest.yaml
  -> workflow_implementation_plan.md
  -> input_example_manifest.yaml
  -> workflow_build.yaml
  -> workflow/ tools, Checkers, GuideDoc, configuration, documentation, and environment facilities
  -> make check / make check_example

requirements_manifest.yaml is the normalized requirement list; workflow_build.yaml is the central build design, which must declare phases, files, tools, Checkers, GuideDoc, and execution contracts in advance. The implementation plan facilitates cross-phase communication; subsequent phases can only append questions and handling within their own marked areas and cannot override prior decisions.

docs.title: Phase Execution
docs.text:
The root config.yaml defines the mother workflow phases. Each phase contains a task description, reference files, output files, tools, and Checkers. The Agent first acquires the current task via RoleInfo, then reads necessary references for the phase, calls tools to generate or update artifacts, and finally has the Checker verify. If the Checker fails, the same phase retries; therefore, the task description must provide an accurate repair direction to avoid the Agent repeatedly guessing formats.

A phase's reference cannot point to files generated by future phases. Directories cannot serve as substitutes for references or outputs, because UCAgent's reference tracking, permissions, and existence checks operate on a per-file basis.

docs.title: Evaluation Data Flow
docs.text:
Static evaluation is divided into four responsibility domains: tools, checkers, flow, and env. Each evaluation Agent reads a compact execution guide, the current report index, user resources, and target source code, then appends checks/findings via structured storage. The aggregator does not re-evaluate the source code; it only summarizes individual reports and approval statuses.

eval_run is an optional expensive runtime evaluation, separate from static evaluation. Static review must not secretly launch the full sub-workflow, and runtime evaluation should not simultaneously run both default and inc modes.

docs.title: Incremental Data Flow
docs.text:
approvals + user suggestions
  -> start-inc-run  assign run id
  -> read target summary and related source code
  -> tmp/inc_runs/<id>/  candidates
  -> deterministic check
  -> save old version and atomic deploy
  -> make check / related tests
  -> incremental_report + applied_changes
  -> re-evaluate

The incremental process must maintain a mapping of "approved items to modified files, check evidence." After deployment, the process cannot remain in a "pending approval" state; when formal files have changed, it must continue fixing regressions or explicitly fail. Version management addresses recoverability, not re-approving files already deployed.

docs.title: Console
docs.text: The console is provided by tools/workflow_evaluation_control/review_server.py as a local HTTP service. Pages read structured JSON, construct design YAML/Markdown, workflow file trees, and UCAgent status. Write operations must pass server-side validation; browsers cannot directly write raw files.

docs.title: Extension Principles
docs.text: Before adding a phase, determine if it can be merged into an existing core phase. Excessive specifications, lists, and cognitive verifications consume context without increasing business quality. Prioritize ensuring tools, Checkers, GuideDoc, config, and user documentation are correct; introduce new structures only if they eliminate real ambiguities or support deterministic verification.

docs.title: Build Design Loading and Basic Validation
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_builder/core.py, symbols load_yaml_config(), get_nested(), and validate_build_config().

def validate_build_config(data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    for key, expected_type in REQUIRED_FIELDS.items():
        value = get_nested(data, key)
        if not isinstance(value, expected_type):
            raise WorkflowBuildError("BUILD-CFG-003", ...)
    if "tmp" not in data["directories"]["public"]:
        raise WorkflowBuildError("BUILD-CFG-007", ...)
    validate_workflow_spec_contract(data)

The loading function accepts only YAML mappings to avoid subsequent code producing hard-to-understand attribute errors on lists or scalars. get_nested() uses dot-path reading for required fields, allowing errors to directly point to workflow.name or runtime_contract. validate_build_config() first validates the outer shape, then checks semantic constraints, and finally enters the central workflow spec validation. When developers add new fields, they should determine if it is a required field indispensable for Builder execution or an optional business extension; stuffing all fields into REQUIRED_FIELDS will break backward design compatibility.

The root-level tmp constraint reflects temporary file governance: all components share a controlled temporary root, prohibiting the re-introduction of .workflow/temp. Such cross-component invariants must be blocked in the earliest central validation, rather than relying on late documentation reminders.

docs.title: Central Workflow Spec Validation
docs.text:
validate_workflow_spec_contract() requires Checkers and phases to fully plan before building. It first collects shape errors and reports multiple structural missing items at once, then checks names, source entry points, fixtures, tests, and phase references. This strategy of "reporting all similar structural issues at once" reduces retries caused by Agents fixing only one field per attempt.

The core logic can be summarized as: establish a unique set of Checker names, files, classes, and fixtures; verify that every stage reference to a Checker can be found in the central definition; verify that references/outputs are specific files with no future references; and verify that stage registration parameters are traceable to definitions. If adding a Checker field, validation must occur here, synchronizing the checker generator, schema, minimal examples, and console structure views.

This stage cannot validate all business semantics. For example, "whether the Chapter Consistency Checker truly covers user requirements" requires fixture and evaluation process judgment. Central validation is responsible for proving design closure and materialization, not for inflating to running the entire business.

docs.title: Materialized Main Call Chain Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_builder/core.py, symbol build_workflow().

data = load_yaml_config(config_path)
validate_build_config(data)
root = check_path_safety(data, base_dir)
create_directories(root, data, report)
for group_name in ("public", "internal"):
    for item in data["files"][group_name]:
        content = render_file_by_template(...)
        write_file(root, rel_path, content, overwrite, report)
generate_planned_business_checkers(root, data, overwrite, report)

Order is critical. Path safety checks occur before any writes to avoid discovering root boundary violations after partial artifacts are created. Directories are created before files; both public and internal files are dispatched via the same template and write_file(), ensuring consistent overwrite, report recording, and path boundaries. Business Checkers are generated after the basic skeleton and config exist, because the checker generator needs to write source code and fixtures and may read the registered structure.

The template dispatch function render_file_by_template() is the centralized entry point for fixed deliverables. When adding new templates, the behavior of unknown templates must be explicitly defined. Currently, unknown templates generate empty files and append warnings; for mandatory business artifacts, warnings alone are usually insufficient, and subsequent acceptance must block empty shells from passing. Do not generate different semantic content via the same path in multiple branches, as path rules will mask template errors.

docs.title: Configuration Generation and Phase Injection
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_config_generator/core.py, symbols validate_config_spec(), _inject_planned_stage_contracts(), and generate_config().

The configuration generator first validates placeholders, scope leaks, parent workflow path leaks, body detail, and reference/output file contracts. _planned_stages() converts the central workflow spec into a structure indexed by phase names, and _inject_planned_stage_contracts() injects Checker, reference, and output constraints into the config spec. This ensures the config should not become a second set of manually maintained phase facts.

After generation, _validate_generated_config() reviews the final YAML rather than assuming the spec is correct implies the rendered result is correct. Common errors include undefined variables, double-bracket remnants, loop replacements, absolute parent workspace paths, directories written to the file list, and references to files not yet existing in the current phase.

docs.title: Evaluation State Machine Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/core.py, symbol evaluation_stage_decision().

if is_report:
    decision = "run"
elif stage_name in state.get("skipped_stages", []):
    decision = "skip"
elif state.get("status") in {"blocked", "terminated", "completed"}:
    decision = "skip"
else:
    decision = "run"

Report stages always run to persist failure reasons and suggestions even if preceding stages are blocked, rather than exiting without a report. Explicitly skipped stages take precedence over normal running; blocked and terminated statuses prevent expensive subsequent actions; completed status prevents redundant execution. evaluation_control_action() appends an event for each state change, making the reason for skipping auditable.

When modifying the state machine, prevent both extremes: running all expensive stages even after blocking, and skipping the report stage even after failure. The evaluation state machine is not a single state set with the incremental deployment state machine; do not directly apply evaluation pending/blocked semantics to an incremental process that has already replaced formal files.

docs.title: Incremental Deployment Call Chain
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/incremental.py, symbol deploy_incremental_changes().

The deployer sequentially validates the workflow root, change id, current run/batch/attempt, approval freshness, mapped fields, candidate paths, target paths, and approval coverage. It then performs a projected semantic audit, saves each target old version, uses atomic replacement with temporary files in the same directory, and writes applied_changes.json. If failure occurs midway, rollback proceeds in reverse order.

backup = _archive_target(workspace, history_root, target_root, target)
_atomic_copy(source, target)
...
_rollback_targets(workspace, target_root, archived)

_atomic_copy() uses os.replace(), so it does not require write permissions on the old file itself, only that the target directory allows creation and replacement. This is precisely why read-only config/Makefile files can still be deployed under control. Backup records include whether the original file exists, its path, hash, and timestamp, supporting both recovery of existing files and rollback of newly created files in the current run.

docs.title: File Producer and Consumer Matrix
docs.text:
File Producer Primary Consumer Allowed Update Timing requirements_manifest.yaml Initial requirement extraction Planner, design builder, console Append sync when requirement decision changes workflow_implementation_plan.md All build stages Subsequent stages, developers Write own marker zone per stage workflow_build.yaml Design stage Builder, generators, console Complete central closure before materialization config.yaml config generator UCAgent default business process During build or approval of incremental eval/*.json Structured storage Console, aggregation, incremental Via controlled CRUD applied_changes.json deployer Acceptance, version management Only after successful actual deployment

This matrix is used to determine "which file should be modified". For example, when tool source code and workflow build spec are inconsistent, editing the registered config alone is insufficient; first decide whether the central design has changed, then rematerialize or fully record deviations with incremental reports.

docs.title: Decision Methods for Extended Stages
docs.text:
New stages must satisfy at least one condition: they produce independent, verifiable, subsequently consumed artifacts; they have distinct write permissions; or they isolate high-cost/high-risk actions. Merely because a task description is long is insufficient to split stages. After splitting, calculate the added cost of new references, Checkers, GuideDocs, and context reading.

Conversely, tool generation and tool testing can be batched in the same responsibility stage: first independently generate multiple tools, then update registration and run comprehensive checks. Splitting each tool into "generate, read-back, check, read-back again" four stages amplifies model round-trips without adding deterministic evidence.

docs.title: Failure Paths and Partial Write Analysis
docs.text:
Exceptions in the main build chain may occur during central config loading, path checking, directory creation, template rendering, file writing, Checker materialization, or example copying. Developers should confirm whether each layer of error includes a responsibility-domain error code, and whether the report accurately reflects the writes that have already occurred when failure happens. The Builder is currently not a database transaction spanning all files, so mid-run failure may leave created files; retries depend on overwrite and idempotent recovery by each generator.

This means new generation steps cannot assume the workflow root is always empty. They should verify existing targets, adopt safe overwrite strategies, and not destroy user drifted files before failure. For shared files requiring overall consistency, such as config registration, generate and validate complete candidates in memory first, then write atomically, rather than appending in a loop and failing on the last item.

The UCTool wrapper layer should catch known WorkflowBuildError and return code/message/report; unknown exceptions retain traceback for development logs while returning a failure summary without sensitive content to the Agent. Do not catch all exceptions and return ok=True with a warning, as this would face the stage Checker with a half-finished product and cause misleading retries.

docs.title: Runtime Contract and Example Targets
docs.text:
runtime_contract connects the build design to the final Makefile. It defines input root, output root, example target, and required input. The Builder uses this to copy test_input to the working workflow example, generate input/output documentation, and let make check_example verify the same contract. If a generator assumes data/ or fixed target names independently, it will diverge from config and documentation.

When adding new input types, first update the runtime contract and input example manifest, then let the Builder copy actual samples, and finally have the Makefile and Checker read the same list. Example targets must represent real minimal business, not just empty JSON to provide false passes for structural checks.

docs.title: Observability and Stage Duration
docs.text:
The process layer should write key artifacts to the report or plan, not just print in the TUI. Long-stage troubleshooting requires knowing the current spec being processed, recent writes, check return codes, and remaining queue. During batch generation, first record total queue count and completed ids; after context compression, resume from structured progress without re-scanning the entire workflow.

Performance optimization should not eliminate the final comprehensive check. The correct approach is to reduce redundant full checks, limit irrelevant reads, and parallelize non-sharing write tasks. Any optimization should be evaluated by comparing different business scenarios across stage failure counts, tool invocation counts, context compression, and final quality.

docs.title: Main Workflow 24 Stages Step-by-Step Explanation
docs.text: The following stage order comes from the root config.yaml and represents the current parent workflow's public execution architecture. WorkflowPlanAppender spans almost all stages, used to append design records for the current stage only; the table lists only representative tools for this stage. When secondary developers modify stages, they must simultaneously verify config, corresponding Guide_Doc/stages/, implementation plan block, reference/output, and Checker parameters.

docs.title: First Group: Requirements and Central Design
docs.text:
Step Primary Purpose Key Artifacts and Checks Secondary Development Notes 00 extract_requirements_and_plan Convert user guide.md and sample inputs into normalized requirements, input example manifest, and complete implementation plan. Here decide subsequent tools, Checkers, docs, environment, and migration targets; plan detail must exceed user original text. Output requirements_manifest.yaml, input_example_manifest.yaml, workflow_implementation_plan.md; jointly checked by requirements, input example, implementation plan, and living plan Checker. New requirement fields must sync manifest schema, minimal examples, first-stage GuideDoc, Checker, and console parsing. Do not disguise implementation results confirmable in later stages as user requirements. 01 design_workflow_build_config Form the unique central workflow_build.yaml, organizing directories, public/internal files, runtime contract, tools, business Checkers, GuideDocs, environment, and acceptance into a materializable design. Output central build config and this stage's plan record; WorkflowBuildConfigChecker validates structure and requirement mapping against initial requirements. Modifying central schema is a high-impact change, requiring sync with Builder, four generator types, design editor, and delivery contract. Reference must be specific existing files.

The core of stage 00 is not "writing three files," but establishing a source of truth that subsequent stages will not arbitrarily redesign. If knowledge base, license, or new config type needs to be added, define the delivery contract here first. Stage 01 converts requirements into fields generators can consume; before adding top-level fields, first judge if existing workflow_spec, runtime_contract, or acceptance can express them, avoiding spec bloat.

docs.title: Second Group: Initial Skeleton and Tool Smoke Loop
docs.text:
Step Primary Purpose Key Tools and Checks Secondary Development Notes 02 build_initial_template Use WorkflowBuilder to create workflow skeleton, environment facilities, internal Checker, central business Checker spec/fixture, and minimal public files in one pass. WorkflowBuildOutputChecker checks 21 initial outputs; requirement coverage prevents skeleton from missing user-required deliverables. When modifying Builder template dispatch, fixed directories, or environment files, update this stage's output list and build regression. Do not supplement files that should be fixed by the skeleton in later stages. 03 verify_tool_generation_loop Verify that the Tool generator itself can generate source, register, test, and maintain generation state from spec, first opening the general loop before generating business Tools. Use WorkflowToolGenerator; WorkflowToolGenerationChecker checks spec, source, registration, and test loop. New Tool templates or override strategies should be verified with small fixtures here first. Shared registration and generation state must be written serially. 04 design_smoke_business_tool_spec Select minimal but representative smoke Tools from user business tools, designing real parameters, outputs, errors, and test specs. Output smoke tool spec and plan record; WorkflowGeneratedToolChecker focuses on spec quality at this point. Selected Tools should cover key libraries or input formats but not be complex enough to block the entire parent process. Update smoke baseline semantics when modifying selection rules. 05 implement_smoke_business_tool Materialize the smoke Tool via WorkflowToolGenerator, proving the parent generator can produce truly importable, registrable business implementations. Output tool source and generation state; Checker validates source, registration, normal/failure calls. Do not allow parent Agent to bypass the generator and write formal source manually. After adding a new renderer, verify template results in this stage, not just renderer string tests. 06 strengthen_smoke_business_tool_tests Supplement boundary, exception, repeated run, and path safety tests on the initial implementation to prevent "only one happy path" pseudo-passes. Update tool spec, cases, and state; same WorkflowGeneratedToolChecker uses strengthened parameters for stronger coverage. Strengthened tests should change one condition at a time. Avoid requiring all business tools to have unrelated tests when modifying strength thresholds. 07 initialize_smoke_workflow Integrate minimal workflow config, setup, Makefile, and run targets, perform environment pre-check, and establish a runnable smoke workflow. Use WorkflowEnvironmentPreflight, necessary Tool generation, and ChildWorkflowSupervisor; validate minimal init and environment setup Checker. This connects generation to the runtime environment. New Make targets, environment variables, or proxy strategies must simultaneously update Builder template, schema, GuideDoc, and environment regression. 08 verify_generated_tools_through_mcp Call generated Tools from UCAgent's actual MCP/adapter boundary, proving they are not limited to Python direct runner usage. Generate MCP test logs/reports; WorkflowMCPToolIntegrationChecker checks registration, calls, and structured results. Must update this stage after modifying adapter, --ex-tools, or MCP parameters. Do not replace MCP integration evidence with ordinary function calls. 09 freeze_smoke_baseline Form a smoke baseline of the already-passed minimal tools, config, tests, and environment, serving as a stable reference for subsequent full generation. Output smoke manifest and plan record; requirement coverage-like Checker verifies baseline. Baseline only freezes verified facts, should not include all future business tools. Provide old manifest compatibility or migration when modifying fields.

This group adopts a progressive design: "first verify the generator, then generate one business Tool, then call from real boundaries." During secondary development, do not merge 03, 05, and 08 into a single undiagnosable large stage; do not replicate the full smoke stage for each Tool. Full tools are handled in the batch stage later.

docs.title: Group 3: Complete Configuration and All Business Tools
docs.text:
Step Primary Purpose Key Tools & Checks Secondary Development Notes 10 design_complete_runtime_configs Design final default flows, incremental flows, and optional evaluation configurations based on the central spec, clarifying all variables, stages, GuideDoc injections, and Checker injections. Output config specs and plan records; this phase is primarily guaranteed by the living plan to ensure design additions. When adding a config type, update requirements and the workflow build schema first; prohibit restoring cancelled default/empty configurations. 11 generate_complete_runtime_configs Generate real YAML using WorkflowConfigGenerator and self-audit placeholders, paths, reference ordering, and registration via WorkflowArtifactInspector. Output config.yaml, config/inc.yaml, etc., and audit logs; WorkflowRuntimeConfigAuditChecker blocks unknown variables and erroneous references. Modifying placeholder rules, stage injections, or file contracts requires updating both pre-generation and post-generation validation in the config generator. 12 design_all_business_tool_specs Establish a complete spec queue for all business Tools except smoke tests based on requirements and implementation plans. Output tool specs/manifests and plan records. Reuse the interface patterns validated by smoke tests, but each tool must still have business algorithms, exceptions, and tests. Do not skip the generator after writing source code in this phase. 13 generate_all_business_tools Batch generate all business Tools using WorkflowToolGenerator, coordinating shared registration and state in a single pass. Output tool source code, registration, and generation state. Independent source code can be planned in parallel, while shared config/state is submitted serially. New tools must align with requirements, specs, and docs. 14 run_full_tool_test_suite Run specs, static imports, direct cases, and MCP integration tests for all tools to form a comprehensive test report. Output tool test summaries; full_mcp_tool_integration_check verifies that not only smoke Tools are tested. When modifying the test runner, retain single-tool location information and the total return code. Do not repeat the full test suite for every generated file.

10–11 Separate "designing configurations" from "generating and self-auditing configurations" to detect central design contradictions before any formal YAML write. Similarly, 12–14 complete the Tool spec queue first, then batch materialize and integrate tests. If a new business area involves only one Tool, these phases should still retain their semantics, but tasks can quickly confirm there are no additional items rather than generating empty shell files to meet a count.

docs.title: Group 4: Documentation, Dependencies, and Reusable Templates
docs.text: Step Primary Purpose Key Tools & Checks Secondary Development Notes 15 design_all_document_specs Plan all GuideDocs, user docs, developer source analysis, and dependency descriptions to establish a document spec. Output GuideDoc spec sets; WorkflowGuideDocSpecChecker validates sections, paths, lengths, and coverage. When adding a new document type, update the guidedoc schema, generator, and document regression. FAQ entries should only record cross-business confirmed experiences. 16 generate_all_documentation_and_dependencies Generate GuideDocs and user docs using WorkflowGuideDocGenerator, while completing requirements/system dependency declarations. Output GuideDocs, docs, requirements; Generated GuideDocs, User Docs, and Dependency Checker perform separate checks. User docs and Agent GuideDocs cannot be mixed in registration. Developer docs must analyze the final real source code; they cannot remain at the plan template level. 17 generate_all_reusable_templates Generate user-copyable input templates, resource structures, or business reusable files using the controlled template capabilities of WorkflowBuilder. Output reusable template manifest/files and plan records. Templates must originate from requirements and reside in public convention locations; temporary fixtures cannot masquerade as user templates. Unknown template names must be checked before materialization.

docs.title: Group 5: Release Completeness and Final Requirement Coverage
docs.text: Step Primary Purpose Key Artifacts & Checks Secondary Development Notes 18 complete_readme_and_makefile Summarize final commands, inputs/outputs, environment, tests, and tmux targets to ensure README and Makefile reflect actual delivery. Update README, Makefile, setup-related files, and plans. When modifying Makefile target generation, simultaneously update README, QuickStart, environment schema, and acceptance criteria. 19 mark_feature_complete Write feature completeness status after all planned features are materialized, prohibiting subsequent masking of omissions with "in planning". Output feature complete manifest/status and plan records. Completion status must derive from actual files and tests, not just phase numbers. New delivery categories must be included in completion calculations. 20 verify_final_requirement_coverage Re-map final workflow files, tools, Checkers, configurations, and documents back to each user requirement to identify omissions or semantic deviations. Output final coverage; WorkflowRequirementCoverageChecker checks in final mode. When modifying the coverage algorithm, retain the mapping of requirement refs to real files/evidence; do not rely solely on quantity comparison.

docs.title: Group 6: Cleanup, Migration, and External Verification
docs.text: Step Primary Purpose Key Tools & Checks Secondary Development Notes 21 clean_release_candidate Use WorkflowArtifactInspector to clear temporary logs, browser profiles, caches, and unregistered files, while preserving public delivery and necessary internal tests. Output cleanup reports and plan records. Changes to clean whitelist/keep rules must run the write boundary; never delete eval, res, input, or version history. 22 prepare_and_verify_migration_packages Build complete or partial migration packages and manifests, verifying paths, dependencies, and allowed contents within the package. Output migration packages, manifests, and check reports; WorkflowMigrationPackageChecker validates generated packages. Partial packages must not accidentally include Tools/Checkers; complete packages must cover environment, docs, examples, and installers. Modifying package formats must provide a version. 23 verify_migrated_release Unpack, configure, and verify the migrated workflow in an isolated target, rather than just checking compressed file names. Output final migration verification report; similar Migration Checkers verify installation, paths, and tests with final parameters. The verification environment must not rely on absolute paths from the original workspace. When adding new installation steps, update the installer, manifest, and this phase's command whitelist.

docs.title: How to Secondary Develop a Phase
docs.text:
1. Confirm the phase's unique responsibility, location, and alias in the root config.yaml.
  2. Modify or add the corresponding Guide_Doc/stages/<index>_<name>.md, providing tools, Checkers, and minimum formats.
  3. If the phase produces new central files, update the wfgen schema, design editor, and implementation plan markers.
  4. In reference_files, list only files existing before the phase; in output_files, list only files actually written by this phase.
  5. Register suitable Checkers; new Checkers follow the generation and regression path described in section 03.
  6. Update living plan rules to ensure this phase only appends its own block.
  7. Add configuration/GuideDoc/phase regression, and verify in a brand new business workspace.

Do not merely observe if a new phase passes; compare whether the context before and after phases repeats, whether it introduces new full-document reads, or if it can be merged into an existing responsibility domain. Deleting a phase requires cleaning Checker aliases, GuideDocs, plan markers, references, and all old phase assumptions in recovery history.

docs.title: Continue Reading
docs.text: Phases are executed deterministically by UCTool; please continue reading Tool Introduction to view the full tool list, registered context, and modification interactions for the master workflow.

docs.title: Mother Workflow Tool Generation Subsystem Secondary Development
docs.text:
This document explains how to perform secondary development on the Tool generation subsystem of the Mother Workflow, specifically modifying tools/workflow_tool_generator/, its UCTool wrapper, mother configuration registration, and related regression tests, to enable future generated business workflows to obtain new tool templates, spec fields, write policies, or registration capabilities. It does not teach business Agents how to invoke a specific tool.

A Tool is a deterministic capability exposed by the Mother Workflow to the UCAgent, and it is also the type of artifact delivered by the Mother Workflow generation to the sub-workflow.
