Developers must understand both "the UCTool of the generator itself" and "the business Tool produced by the generator," but actual modifications should focus on the source code, spec contract, and templates of the former.

docs.title: Secondary Development Goals
docs.text: Tasks suitable for completion in this subsystem include: adding generic tool templates, extending the tool spec schema, modifying preserve/replace policies, enhancing path safety, adjusting config registration, adding tool test baselines, or fixing generation states. Business-specific algorithms that serve only a single generation workflow should be provided as inline source code or business templates via the central spec, rather than being hard-coded into all workflows shared by the Mother Generator.

docs.title: Mother Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text:
• tools/workflow_tool_generator/core.py: spec validation, generation state, write, and registration.
  • tools/workflow_tool_generator/templates.py: built-in tools and generic source code renderer.
  • tools/workflow_tool_generator/uc_tools.py: parameter model and UCTool for calls to the Mother Agent.
  • Root config.yaml: which mother stage calls the generator and which specs are passed.
  • Guide_Doc/stages/: instructs the Mother Agent on how to prepare specs and perform batch generation.
  • regression/: tool descriptions, delivery contracts, and stability verification.

DOCX tool cases mentioned later should be understood as "how to verify that a Mother Generator extension can support a business," not a requirement for developers to write DOCX logic into the WorkflowToolGenerator.

docs.title: Real Generation Pipeline
docs.text:
The tool generation entry point is located in tools/workflow_tool_generator/. Tool specs in the central workflow_build.yaml first declare the name, purpose, parameters, output, errors, invocation stage, and tests, and then the generator writes them into the business workflow's tools/ directory and updates the registration. The core coordination logic of the Mother Builder is located in tools/workflow_builder/core.py; this file also generates the generic environment, README, and fixed skeleton.

When developers adjust the tool protocol, they should search simultaneously:

rg -n "tool_spec|GeneratedTools|tools\." workflow_builder workflow_tool_generator regression

Do not modify the generation result of a single workspace_x/workspace/workflow/tools/ instance, as that will not improve subsequent builds.

docs.title: Interface Structure
docs.text:
A tool should have a stable name, a clear docstring, serializable parameters, and a structured return value. The recommended return format is:

{
    "ok": True,
    "data": {"output_path": "output/example/document.docx"},
    "errors": [],
    "warnings": [],
    "meta": {"tool": "BuildDocument", "version": 1},
}

When failing, ok must be False, and errors should contain stable error codes, actionable messages, and related fields or paths. Do not catch exceptions and still return success, nor print terminal text and let the Agent guess the result.

docs.title: Key Business Code Analysis Requirements
docs.text:
The generated docs/04​开发者​文档​-tools.md must reference real source code snippets for each tool, not pseudo-code. Each tool must analyze at least:

  1. How the tool entry function or class receives parameters and performs type, path, and business pre-condition validation.
  2. How the core algorithm or third-party library call converts input into a business product.
  3. How file writing restricts to allowed directories, uses temporary files, and handles partial failures.
  4. How exceptions are mapped to structured errors, and which errors allow retries.
  5. How registration code allows the UCAgent to find the tool, ensuring parameter configuration and Python signatures are consistent.
  6. Which branches are covered by normal, boundary, and failure tests.

Source code references must note relative paths and symbol names. After the snippet, key variables and control flow must be explained; do not simply paste the entire file. If a tool is generated by a template, also indicate the template source and the actual file differences after generation.

docs.title: Write and Command Boundaries
docs.text:
Tools can only write to directories allowed by the business workflow. Temporary data from the build process enters the workspace tmp/ and should not be scattered in wfgen/ as debug scripts. When executing batch operations or external programs, use whitelists, parameter arrays, timeouts, and return codes; do not concatenate user input into arbitrary shells.

Path validation should occur after parsing and normalization to prevent .., symbolic links, and absolute path escapes. The existence of an output directory does not equal a valid product; tools must also verify size, format, or re-parsability.

docs.title: Parallelism and Performance
docs.text: Independent tools can be generated or tested in parallel by the Agent, but writes to shared registration files and central specs must be coordinated serially. The generation stage should not stipulate "only one tool can be called per response"; the real constraint is avoiding concurrent modifications to the same file and running a comprehensive check once after batch generation.

docs.title: Modification Checklist
docs.text:
• Update the central tool spec and requirements manifest.
  • Update generator templates or generic implementations, not just individual products.
  • Update registration, GuideDoc, and developer document generation rules.
  • Add positive, negative, boundary, and path escape tests.
  • Run tool generator regression and the total make regression.

docs.title: Complete Data Flow from Tool Spec to Source Code
docs.text:
Business tools are not written directly to tools/ based on natural language. In the first phase, tool responsibilities are clarified in the requirements manifest and implementation plan. In the design phase, stable fields are written into the central tool spec. The generator reads the spec, validates paths and interfaces, renders source code, updates registration, and saves generation state. Finally, the business config is exposed to the UCAgent via a dynamic adapter.

A maintainable spec must include at least: name, description, entry file, class name, input schema, output schema, errors, invocation stage, implementation template or inline source code, tests, and existing file policies. The description must answer what problem the tool solves in the business process, not just repeat the class name. Input fields need type, requiredness, and meaning; output fields must allow subsequent Agents and Checkers to stably read the data.

docs.title: Path Safety Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_tool_generator/core.py, symbol _safe_resolve().

def _safe_resolve(root: Path, rel_path: str) -> Path:
    candidate = Path(rel_path)
    if candidate.is_absolute() or ".." in candidate.parts:
        raise ToolGenerationError(...)
    target = (root / candidate).resolve()
    if target != root and root not in target.parents:
        raise ToolGenerationError(...)
    return target

The first layer rejects absolute paths and explicit .., and the second layer checks the true parent directory after resolve(), so symbolic links or path normalization cannot escape the workflow root. All specs, generated files, configurations, and test paths should go through this entry point. When adding tools like "copy resources," do not re-use string prefix checks in your own branch, because /root/workflow-old might incorrectly match /root/workflow.

Path safety verification only proves that the generator's write location is safe; it does not guarantee runtime safety of the generated business tools. Runtime tools still need to re-normalize user-provided paths relative to the business workspace and restrict allowed read/write roots.

docs.title: Generation State and Overwrite Strategy
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_tool_generator/core.py, symbols _load_generation_state(), _write_generated_file(), and _normalize_existing_policy().

The generator saves file content hashes and test baselines to distinguish three scenarios: the file is still the content from the previous generation, the file has been modified by the user or an incremental process, and the file appears for the first time. The existing file policy cannot be expressed by a single boolean overwrite, because automatically overwriting manually maintained code may cause data loss, while skipping everything would make spec updates never take effect.

The following is pseudo-code omitting implementation details; the full implementation is in the source code above.

policy = _normalize_existing_policy(existing_policy, overwrite)
if target.exists() and policy == "preserve":
    report.skipped_files.append(relative)
    return
...
state["files"][relative] = {"sha256": _sha256_text(content), ...}

When developers add a policy, they must define how to handle: target does not exist, target matches the last hash, target has drifted, and forced overwrite; how the report records these; and whether failures leave a new state. The state file must be updated only after successful actual writes and must use secure persistence; do not record the new hash before writing the file.

docs.title: Spec Validation Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_tool_generator/core.py, symbol _validate_tool_spec().

This function checks the spec top-level mapping, tool name, description, entry file and class, input/output, implementation type, and tests. The validation order should be structural before semantic: if entry is not a mapping, do not continue to read entry.file. Tool descriptions, parameter explanations, and error contracts belong to maintainable interfaces, not optional decorations.

When declaring inline source code in the spec, Python AST or compilation checks should also be performed, and the existence of the entry class confirmed. Template tools are generated by render_tool_from_spec(), but must also pass the tool static checker and direct runner after writing to prevent template string syntax correctness while having incorrect runtime protocols.

docs.title: Generic Template Rendering Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_tool_generator/templates.py, symbols _schema_from_inputs(), _output_schema_from_spec(), and _render_generic_tool().

def render_tool_from_spec(spec):
    template = spec.get("template")
    if template in BUILTIN_RENDERERS:
        return BUILTIN_RENDERERS[template](spec)
    return _render_generic_tool(spec)

Input specs are first converted to fields required by Pydantic/JSON schema, then written into the generated class. The output schema is not the runtime result itself, but the contract that the Agent and tests understand the data structure. Generic tool templates must retain the ok/data/errors/warnings/meta structure; otherwise, the upper-layer Agent cannot uniformly determine failure.

If the business subject in the generated class is just a placeholder NotImplemented or unconditionally succeeds, the static syntax may pass, but the tool is unusable. Therefore, the central plan should prefer explicit templates or provide real implementation source code, and invoke them with positive and negative cases using the direct runner. When adding a new template, add the template name to the allowed set, implement the renderer, add fixtures, record requirements, and update developer documents.

docs.title: Registration Process Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_tool_generator/core.py, symbols _tool_record_from_spec() and _register_tool_records().

Registration records convert spec entry points into runtime loadable module class paths while preserving tool names, descriptions, parameter schemas, and source specs. The generator should batch collect records before a single update to the config to prevent multiple parallel tool generations from overwriting the registration file.

Registration must satisfy three-way consistency: the Python class name and entry file exist; the class path recorded in the config is importable; and the tool parameter model matches the spec input fields. If files are created in tools/ without registration, UCAgent will not call them; registering non-existent files will cause failures at startup or upon first use.

Batch registration must also handle tools with duplicate names. Duplicate names should typically update the same record or fail explicitly; they cannot silently generate two sequentially dependent records. When modifying the registration structure, simultaneously check tools/mcp_adapters.py, the tool spec checker, the static runner, and the evaluation tool registration review.

docs.title: UCTool Wrapping Layer Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_tool_generator/uc_tools.py, symbols WorkflowToolGeneratorArgs and WorkflowToolGenerator.

The parameter model is responsible for converting JSON passed by the Agent into stable Python types. The actual run() should only perform parameter normalization, invoke the core, catch ToolGenerationError, and return a structured result, without duplicating business generation logic in the wrapping layer. This allows CLI, regression, and UCTool to share the same core.

The wrapping layer docstring becomes the tool description visible to UCAgent and must specify the generation location, spec requirements, overwrite strategy, and return content. Parameter default values should be handled carefully: setting overwrite=True as the default may cause the Agent to overwrite user-maintained code without awareness.

docs.title: Structured Error Design
docs.text:
Recommended failure result:

{
    "ok": False,
    "data": {},
    "errors": [{
        "code": "TOOL-GEN-SPEC-004",
        "message": "entry.file must be workflow-relative",
        "location": ".workflow/tool_specs/BuildDoc.yaml:entry.file",
    }],
    "warnings": [],
    "meta": {"generated": [], "skipped": []},
}

Error codes are used for stable association in FAQs, Checkers, and Agent fix prompts; the message explains the fact and fix direction; the location points to the spec field. Do not include full sensitive inputs or large stderr in errors. External command output should be truncated and saved in tmp/ logs; the returned structure should only provide summaries and paths.

docs.title: Secondary Development Case: Enabling the Parent Generator to Support New Business Tools
docs.text:
Assume enabling the parent workflow to stably generate DocumentStructurePlanner required by business DOCX. The secondary developer first determines if the existing generic renderer is sufficient; if so, only enhance the parent stage's spec planning and validation without adding public templates. If multiple businesses reuse the structure planning algorithm, add a template renderer in templates.py and allow the template name in the core. The tool spec defines content_path, requirements_path, and assets_index_path, outputting plan_path, chapter count, and warnings.

After generation, verify: missing body content returns a stable error; unknown heading levels form warnings; resource references do not escape paths; identical inputs yield stable plans; registered classes are importable; positive fixtures include headings, lists, and images; negative fixtures lack only one required file. GuideDoc explains call order and failure recovery, and docs/04​开发者​文档​-tools.md references the actual planning algorithm source code.

If later support for tables is added, do not just modify the Python implementation. Also update capability requirements, spec output schema, test samples, GuideDoc, user input descriptions, and developer code analysis. If output fields change, the Checker using them and subsequent DOCX renderers must also be synchronized.

docs.title: Correct Boundaries for Parallel Generation
docs.text:
Different tool sources and independent fixtures can be prepared in parallel as they write to different files. Central tool specs, generation state, config registration, and comprehensive reports are shared resources that must be submitted by a single coordination step. The recommended process is parallel generation of candidate content, followed by serial calls to the generator to write and register, with the final run performing tool static/direct/MCP comprehensive checks.

Do not enforce a global rule of "only one tool call at a time," as it would force serial execution of dependency-free workflows. Also, do not allow unconstrained parallel calls to multiple generators that would overwrite the same config. Parallel strategy should be based on whether write sets intersect, not on the number of tools.

docs.title: Extension Points, Modification Impact, and Regression Matrix
docs.text:
Modification Must Check New spec field schema, validation, templates, console view, old spec default values Path rule modification safe resolve, symbolic links, absolute paths, Windows/Posix expressions, write boundary regression Return structure modification UCTool, Agent guidance, direct runner, evaluation tool availability check Overwrite strategy modification generation state, hash, user drift, repeated runs and incremental compatibility New template renderer, requirements, positive/negative fixtures, registration and developer documentation Registration modification import test, MCP adapter, config generator, and eval_tools

After target tests pass, run total regression. During real business validation, let the sub-Agent call the generation tool to complete the stage; developers cannot manually place the final tool and pass the Checker as if the generator succeeded.

docs.title: Parent Workflow UCTool Complete List
docs.text:
The following table lists classes that truly inherit UCTool in the current source code. "Registration Context" indicates which configuration exposes it to the Agent; it does not mean every configuration uses all tools. After modifying class names, parameter models, or return structures, search config.yaml, inc.yaml, and eval_*.yaml for ex_tools and synchronize GuideDoc and regression.

Tool Source Registration Context Core Responsibilities and Side Effects WorkflowBuilder tools/workflow_builder/uc_tools.py Main config.yaml Reads central construction design, materializes sub-workflow skeletons, fixed supporting files, and reports; is the controlled entry point for the build core. WorkflowCommandRunner tools/workflow_builder/uc_tools.py Main config.yaml Runs whitelist commands within the build workspace, restricting cwd, timeout, parameters, and output; should not evolve into arbitrary shell execution. WorkflowArtifactInspector tools/workflow_builder/uc_tools.py Main config.yaml Structurally queries files, directory trees, summaries, and local content for evidence collection; read-only and size-limited. WorkflowEnvironmentPreflight tools/workflow_builder/uc_tools.py Main config.yaml Checks Python, Make, UCAgent, paths, dependencies, and optional external commands, outputting a distinguishable environment report for "missing" vs "optional skip". WorkflowPlanAppender tools/workflow_builder/uc_tools.py Main config.yaml Appends implementation plans with phase markers, preserving prior phase content; responsible for the living plan's non-overwrite constraint. WorkflowToolGenerator tools/workflow_tool_generator/uc_tools.py Main process and inc.yaml Validates tool spec, generates business tool source, fixtures, tests, and registration, maintaining generation state and overwrite strategy. WorkflowCheckerGenerator tools/workflow_checker_generator/uc_tools.py inc.yaml Generates or updates Checker, fixtures, and registration from checker spec; some Checkers in main builds can also be materialized directly by the Builder. WorkflowConfigGenerator tools/workflow_config_generator/uc_tools.py Main process and inc.yaml Generates or updates config.yaml and inc.yaml based on workflow spec, injecting Tools, Checkers, GuideDoc, and phase contracts. WorkflowGuideDocGenerator tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/uc_tools.py Main process and inc.yaml Validates document spec, generates GuideDoc and user/developer documentation, registering only against guidance needed by the Agent. ChildWorkflowSupervisor tools/workflow_child_supervisor/uc_tools.py Main process limited validation and eval_run.yaml Starts, queries, captures, or stops sub-workflows via independent tmux sessions, returning run id and observable state; should not be registered in static eval_tools/checkers/flow/env. IncrementalContextInventory tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_tools.py inc.yaml Inventories sub-workflows, reports, approvals, and resources under controlled reading budgets, producing a round-trip cognitive index rather than copying full text. StructuredJsonStore tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_tools.py All evaluation and inc.yaml Performs CRUD with schema, revision, and audit on allowed eval/*.json and res/*.json; is the sole conventional write channel for structured files. EvaluationCommandRunner tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_tools.py All static evaluation and inc.yaml Runs evaluation/regression whitelist commands, saving return codes and truncated evidence; does not allow static evaluation to start sub-workflows via it. StaticEvaluationAudit tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_tools.py All evaluation and inc.yaml Performs deterministic audit on Tools, Checkers, config, GuideDoc, environment, and write boundaries, outputting rule id and evidence. EvaluationControl tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_tools.py Control API/compatibility entry Encapsulates aggregation, approval, suggestion, and incremental run control; not all YAML ex_tools register it currently; do not assume Agent visibility upon modification. IncrementalCandidateStager tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_tools.py inc.yaml Safely copies approved targets from the formal workflow/ to the current run/batch/attempt candidate directory and records source hash. IncrementalChangeDeployer tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_tools.py inc.yaml Validates candidate mapping against current approval, backs up old versions, atomically replaces formal files, and rolls back on failure while writing applied_changes.json. ReadTextFileMCPTool tools/workflow_builder/core.py Generated sub-workflow MCP Reads text within the business workspace with path boundaries and chunk parameters; it is the generation source template, not a regular tool for the parent Agent build stage. WriteTextFileMCPTool tools/workflow_builder/core.py Generated sub-workflow MCP Writes text within the business-allowed root, maintaining output and temporary file boundaries. RunCommandMCPTool tools/workflow_builder/core.py Generated sub-workflow MCP Provides limited command execution for sub-workflows; the allowed set should be determined by business design and environment configuration.

docs.title: Secondary Development of Control Tools
docs.text:
The parameter layer of WorkflowBuilder should only accept workspace-relative design paths, override strategies, and optional phase ranges; materialization must be delegated to tools/workflow_builder/core.py. When adding a fixed deliverable, updates must be applied simultaneously to BuildReport, the initial skeleton, requirements manifest overrides, the delivery contract, and the secondary development documentation for artifacts. A file not recorded by the core must never be temporarily written inside run().

WorkflowCommandRunner and EvaluationCommandRunner share similar names but distinct permissions. The former serves the generation and verification of the build workspace, while the latter serves the evaluation of evidence and incremental regression. Adding allowed commands requires adding precise parameter rules to the whitelist of the corresponding executor; allowing arbitrary make <target> simply because make check is needed in one place is incorrect. Regression tests must cover non-whitelisted targets, timeouts, out-of-bounds current working directories, non-zero return codes, and excessively long outputs.

WorkflowArtifactInspector is used to reduce the need for Agents to perform full-text scans to establish understanding. When adding a new query type, it should return file count, size, hash, matches, and a truncation marker, rather than expanding content without limits. The check items in WorkflowEnvironmentPreflight must declare required/optional status, confirm commands, and provide installation suggestions; missing optional Verilator and Python failure to start cannot be set as equivalent blocking conditions.

WorkflowPlanAppender must use stable begin/end markers to locate the current phase block and refuse to overwrite other phases. When extending plan fields, compatibility reading of old plans without new fields, idempotency of retries within the same phase, and corresponding rules from WorkflowLivingPlanChecker must be checked.

docs.title: Secondary Development of Four Generator Tools
docs.text:
WorkflowToolGenerator, WorkflowCheckerGenerator, WorkflowConfigGenerator, and WorkflowGuideDocGenerator follow the same wrapping principle: Pydantic Args ensure basic types for Agent JSON, the core handles path normalization and business validation, and UCTool converts expected exceptions into structured failures. If new fields are added only to Args without passing them to the core, the Agent will mistakenly believe the parameters are active; if only the core is modified, the Agent cannot construct the parameter.

The deliverables differ among the four generators: the Tool generator maintains tool source code and generates hashes; the Checker generator also materializes positive and negative fixtures; the Config generator performs cross-file reference closure, placeholders, and phase connection audits; the GuideDoc generator distinguishes between Agent GuideDoc and human documents. A generic generator that merely "reads spec then writes file" should not be abstracted, as this would lose their respective semantic validations.

docs.title: Secondary Development of Evaluation and Incremental Tools
docs.text:
The output of IncrementalContextInventory should be a "navigable cognitive list": configuration phases, tool/checker indices, target findings, direct dependencies, and a read-order based on demand. It should not embed docs/, all source code, and historical reports into a single large report. When extending inventory items, set per-file and total byte budgets, and retain truncated evidence to prevent evaluation/incremental Agents from repeatedly reading after continuous compression.

Public operations of StructuredJsonStore include list/get/create/update/upsert/delete and must select a fixed schema via relative document ID. Adding a structured file requires synchronizing json_store.py to allow list, initial documents, collection/id rules, CLI, review API, UI, and regression. Agents must not bypass revision to directly cover JSON via WriteTextFile.

Each rule returned by StaticEvaluationAudit must have a stable id, scope, passed status, severity, evidence, and remediation. New rules must belong to the correct evaluation domain and provide minimal positive and negative fixtures. If EvaluationControl is registered as a new Agent entry point, its permissions overlapping with CLI/review server must be explicitly defined to avoid three inconsistent implementations of the same approval operation.

IncrementalCandidateStager and IncrementalChangeDeployer must be separated. The Stager only copies formal files to the current candidate and records hashes; the Deployer can then verify approval, backup, and atomic replacement. Merging them would pollute formal files before candidates are checked. When modifying the mapping format, synchronize incremental reports, applied changes, historical indices, consoles, and rollback tests.

Operations start/status/capture/list/stop of ChildWorkflowSupervisor are implemented in tools/workflow_child_supervisor/core.py, allowing only explicit Make targets like run_tui, run, run_inc, and run_inc_tui. Adding a target requires first determining it will not bypass the evaluation cost gate, and adding regression tests for session naming, run metadata, startup failures, timeouts, stopping, and residual tmux cleanup. When modifying capture, continue limiting line count, avoiding returning the entire long TUI log to the Agent context.

docs.title: Built-in MCP Tools for Generated Artifacts
docs.text:
ReadTextFileMCPTool, WriteTextFileMCPTool, and RunCommandMCPTool are defined in the generation source of tools/workflow_builder/core.py. Developers modifying them must simultaneously read the generated tools/mcp_adapters.py, config registration, security boundaries, and make test_tools. They represent the lowest-level capabilities of sub-workflows; arbitrary commands or out-of-bounds writes cannot be allowed simply because business tools are incomplete.

These classes appear in Builder source code but run within the generated sub-workflow. Therefore, after modification, not only must the parent code be compiled, but a brand new business workflow must be generated, importing the classes from the generation directory and executing out-of-bounds negative cases. Success of AST parsing in Builder source code alone does not prove the template string is runnable after generation.

docs.title: Standard Steps for Adding or Modifying UCTool
docs.text:
1. First, determine in the table above whether the tool belongs to parent build, generator, evaluation/incremental, or sub-artifact, clarifying its readable root, writable root, and caller.
  2. Add or modify the Args model and specific Tool in the corresponding uc_tools.py, maintaining consistent docstrings, defaults, core parameters, and structured returns.
  3. In the core implementation, perform path validation, business logic, and atomic writes, avoiding placing large logic blocks inside the UCTool run().
  4. Register only in the YAML ex_tools where truly needed, then update the parameter source, output, failure recovery, and Checker evidence in the GuideDoc for that phase.
  5. Add Args validation, direct invocation, out-of-bounds paths, repeated execution, partial failures, and configuration registration regression, then run component regression and total regression for related components.

docs.title: Continue Reading
docs.text: To understand how tool outputs are judged by phases, please continue reading Checker Introduction. To modify tools in the generated sub-workflow, also combine with Generated Workflow Development Guide to judge whether modifications should flow back to the parent generator or be retained as a single business extension.

docs.title: Secondary Development of the Parent Workflow Checker Generation Subsystem
docs.text:
This document explains how to modify the parent workflow Checker planning, generation, templates, fixtures, and registration system to ensure that subsequently generated business workflows possess the correct Checker. The target audience is developers maintaining tools/workflow_checker_generator/, the Builder center spec, and the parent stage acceptance, not the sub-Agent being checked by the Checker.

The Checker determines whether the parent stage or the generated business stage satisfies the contract. Secondary development must distinguish between two categories: parent Checkers registered in the root config verify wfgen/ and build progress; business Checkers planned in workflow_build.yaml are materialized into workflow/. Both categories inherit the UCAgent Checker protocol, but differ in source and delivery location.

docs.title: Secondary Development Goals
docs.text: Typical tasks include adding generic rule types, enhancing AST/docstring validation, modifying automatic fixtures, fixing registration parameters, adding path normalization, or improving Checker direct runner execution. Business-specific judgments should primarily be expressed by inlining sources within the center spec; only when multiple businesses share a rule and it is stable should it enter the public template.

docs.title: Parent Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text:
• tools/workflow_checker_generator/core.py: spec, source code, fixtures, registration, and reporting.
  • tools/workflow_checker_generator/templates.py: generic rule renderer.
  • tools/workflow_builder/core.py: materializes business Checkers directly from the center workflow spec.
  • Root config.yaml and parent Checker modules: self-acceptance of the parent stage.
  • Guide_Doc/stage_check_guide.md and stage GuideDoc: failure explanations and repair directions.
  • regression/run_checker_description_regression.py and delivery contract: protocol regression.

docs.title: Real Generation Pipeline
docs.text:
The center planning for Checkers is located in the workflow spec within workflow_build.yaml. The build stage should directly generate Checker source code, fixtures, and registration from this design, avoiding the need to guess what each stage requires later. Related implementations are primarily located in tools/workflow_checker_generator/, tools/workflow_builder/core.py, and tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_checkers.py.

rg -n "Checker|checker_spec|workflow_spec" workflow_builder workflow_checker_generator regression

docs.title: Docstring and Construction Parameters
docs.text:
UCAgent reads the Checker description; therefore, Checker classes must provide non-empty, specific docstrings. Descriptions like "Check output" do not explain the check object. The docstring should specify which files or fields are read, the core pass conditions, and the meaning of failure.

Parameter names, required status, and default values in the configuration registration must match the Python constructor exactly. Adding an extra parameter will cause instantiation to fail, while missing required parameters will prevent the stage from running. Directory parameters are only reasonable when the Checker design explicitly supports directory traversal; workflow stage reference_files must remain specific files.

docs.title: Judgment Semantics
docs.text:
Checkers should distinguish between: - Files that do not exist or cannot be parsed. - Missing or incorrectly typed structural fields. - Correct structure but unsatisfied business semantics. - Dependency conditions not yet met, such as future chapters or optional outputs that do not exist. - Exceptions encountered by the Checker itself.

Optional inputs should not be treated as mandatory files in early stages. Version or progress checks must be based on the current stage's true semantics, such as "version must match when the latest snapshot chapter equals the current chapter"; using globally unresolvable equalities will create false positives.

docs.title: Key Business Code Analysis Requirements
docs.text:
The generated docs/05​开发者​文档​-checkers.md must provide real source code and analysis for each Checker:

  1. Class definition, constructor, and check/entry call points.
  2. Input paths, fields, and normalization rules.
  3. Major conditional branches and error code mappings.
  4. Why these conditions prove user requirements rather than merely proving format existence.
  5. Positive fixtures, single-error negative fixtures, and boundary fixtures.
  6. Registration fragments in config and parameter mappings.
  7. Stages and tests that must be synchronized when modifying thresholds, fields, or dependencies.

Fragments must come from the final generated real files, annotated with relative paths and symbols near key lines. Analysis should point out the source of business rules; if requirements do not specify, it must state this is a design decision supplemented by the first-stage plan.

docs.title: Preventing False Positives and Negatives
docs.text:
The minimum fixture changes only one condition, making the failure reason locatable. A single negative fixture breaking five fields makes it impossible for developers to know if the Checker validates the target rule. Checkers must not rely on unstable time, random order, or absolute paths. Path comparisons should be normalized before comparison; .//workflow/x and workflow/x should not be incorrectly judged as different due to string differences.

Severity is not a decoration arbitrarily decided by the Checker. Issues that block UCAgent startup, cause infinite retries, corrupt formal files, or falsely claim completion are most dangerous; document wording, non-critical hints, and optional optimizations should not be upgraded to blocking stage issues.

docs.title: Modification Checklist
docs.text:
• Synchronize updates to the center checker spec, generation templates, registration, and stage parameters.
  • Ensure docstrings explain the actual check content.
  • Add instantiation tests and parameter registration consistency tests.
  • Provide positive and negative evidence for each business rule.
  • Verify that Checker self-exceptions do not masquerade as business failures.
  • Run Checkers to generate regression and related full-process checks.

docs.title: Central Role of Checker Spec
docs.text:
The Checker spec is the common source for judgment implementation, fixtures, tests, and stage registration. Each Checker in workflow_build.yaml should fully carry name, description, entry, rules or source code, fixtures, tests, and registration. The Builder first writes the center definition to .workflow/checker_specs/<name>.yaml, then calls the checker generator for materialization, avoiding the situation where stage config, Python files, and tests are each written by different steps.

Checker descriptions must explain "what evidence proves what business condition." For example, a "Check report" has no object, fields, or failure meaning; only "read validation_report.json's status, missing_assets, and output_sha256, confirming DOCX is parseable and no required assets are missing" is sufficient to guide the Agent and evaluator.

docs.title: AST and Docstring Validation Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_checker_generator/core.py, symbol _validate_spec().

This function first confirms the top-level mapping, name, detailed description, and entry, then validates rule type, register, fixtures, and tests. Paths must pass _safe_resolve(), test parameters must be mappings, and expected_pass must be a boolean. Duplicate or missing fields should fail before source generation to prevent leaving half-finished Checkers.

If the spec provides source, the validator cannot skip structural checks just because "the user has written code." Source and entry must still align, tests are still required, and registration parameters still need validation. Rule templates and inline source are just two ways to produce implementation and do not represent different quality standards.

docs.title: AST and Docstring Validation
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_checker_generator/core.py, symbol _validate_inline_source().

The following is pseudo-code omitting implementation details; the full implementation is in the source above.

tree = ast.parse(source)
class_node = next(
    node for node in tree.body
    if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == entry["class_name"]
)
if not any(base.id == "Checker" ... for base in class_node.bases):
    raise CheckerGenerationError(...)
method = next(node for node in class_node.body if node.name == entry["method"])
if method is None or not ast.get_docstring(method):
    raise CheckerGenerationError(...)

AST validation is more reliable than text search: class names in comments are not mistaken for implementation, aliases or base class attributes can be explicitly handled, and method docstrings can be obtained from the syntax tree. It still does not run tests, cannot prove import dependencies exist, construction parameters match, or check logic is correct, so a static checker and direct runner are still needed afterwards.

Current validation requirements check that methods have docstrings because UCAgent and diagnostic tools need explanations. Class-level description and method docstring responsibilities differ: description explains business checks to the stage and user, while method docstring explains calls and returns to maintainers. Neither can be empty.

docs.title: Automatic Fixture Generation Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_checker_generator/core.py, symbol _materialize_auto_tests().

The following is pseudo-code omitting implementation details; the full implementation is in the source above.

if rule_type == "json_required_keys":
    fixtures[valid_path] = json.dumps({key: 0 for key in keys})
    fixtures[invalid_path] = json.dumps({key: 0 for key in keys[:-1]})
    tests = [
        {"expected_pass": True, ...},
        {"expected_pass": False, ...},
    ]

Automatic tests establish minimal positive and negative examples for generic rules. The negative example for required keys deletes only the last key, resulting in a single failure reason; the negative value for numeric ranges exceeds only the upper bound; file exists creates a file and ensures another path does not exist; command exit code uses an allowed command to produce 0 and non-0.

Automatic fixtures are suitable for proving basic template behavior but cannot replace business fixtures. A "field exists" Checker might still need to validate semantic relationships between fields; in such cases, an explicit fixture or inline Checker should be provided. Do not continuously add business-specific examples to generic templates, as this makes templates difficult to understand and imposes additional complexity on all workflows.

docs.title: Template Code Analysis: JSON Required Fields
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_checker_generator/templates.py, symbol _render_json_required_keys().

target = self._resolve()
if not target.is_file():
    return False, {"error": "CHECKER-DATA-001: JSON result file not found"}
data = json.loads(target.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
if not isinstance(data, dict):
    return False, {"error": "CHECKER-DATA-002: JSON top-level must be mapping"}
missing = [key for key in self.required_keys if key not in data]

This code separates errors for missing files, parsing/type issues, and missing fields, allowing the Agent to take different remediation actions. _resolve() restricts the path to within the workspace, preventing the Checker from reading arbitrary system files via stage parameters. The return value is (passed, evidence), where the evidence retains the path and missing keys rather than simply returning False.

Note that "key exists" does not verify value type or meaning. If business logic requires status == completed or a non-empty hash, a more suitable rule should be selected or a business-specific Checker written. Stuffing all conditions into the description of required_keys creates inconsistency between documentation and implementation.

docs.title: Template Code Analysis: Numeric Range and Commands
docs.text:
The numeric range template explicitly excludes bool because bool is a subclass of int in Python. The upper and lower bounds are closed intervals; changing them to open intervals would alter business semantics and requires synchronizing the spec and fixture. Fields that do not exist and non-numeric values currently share the same error branch; if the Agent's fix requires distinguishing these, a new error code and a single negative case can be added.

The command exit code template only allows self.command[0] to appear in allowed_commands, using an array parameter to call subprocess.run(), setting cwd, capture, text, and timeout. It does not concatenate via shell, so user parameters do not become pipes or redirects. stdout/stderr are truncated to the tail to avoid the Checker returning massive context.

Command whitelists need to be precise to executable programs, but verifying only the program name may still allow dangerous parameters. This is suitable for python -m py_compile, specific make check, etc., where control is assured; handling user-controlled arbitrary parameters requires adding parameter mode, working directory, and output path restrictions.

docs.title: Registration Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_checker_generator/core.py, symbol _register_checker().

expected = {
    "name": spec["name"],
    "clss": f"{module_path}.{spec['entry']['class_name']}",
    "args": args if isinstance(args, dict) else {},
}
existing = next(item for item in checker_list if item.get("name") == spec["name"])

UCAgent configuration fields use clss instead of the usual spelling class. The generator is responsible for removing .py from file paths, converting slashes to dots, and then concatenating the class name. Manual registration easily misses this detail. Existing items with the same name are updated rather than appended repeatedly, ensuring stable stage invocation order.

The target stage is looked up before registration; if the stage does not exist, it must fail and cannot revert to the first stage. args must align with the Checker's __init__. The evaluation process should import the class, check the signature, and attempt instantiation to discover if the config passes or misses parameters.

docs.title: Checker Materialization Main Chain
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_checker_generator/core.py, symbol generate_checkers_from_specs().

The main chain parses each spec sequentially, performs structural validation, generates automated tests, writes explicit fixtures, selects inline source or template renderer, writes Checker source code, and optionally registers. Each action updates the CheckerGenerationReport. Any failure should point to the current spec to avoid ambiguity during batch generation regarding which item failed.

When Builder is invoked, update_config=False is typically used because the central stage contract injects configuration uniformly via the config generator; independent tools can register. Developers modifying the semantics of this switch must check for duplicate or missing registrations.

docs.title: Secondary Development Case: Extending Business Checker Generation Capabilities
docs.text:
The DocumentIntegrityChecker for DOCX workflows needs to prove the output is not merely an empty shell with a .docx suffix. Construction parameters include the workflow-relative document path, a list of required chapters, and a minimum image count. The check method uses zipfile or python-docx to parse the file, verifying ZIP integrity, body paragraphs, headings, relationship files, and image references, returning evidence for each.

Positive fixtures represent the minimal valid DOCX; negative fixtures separately cover damaged ZIPs, missing chapters, lost image relationships, and document path escape. The spec is registered to the stage after document generation, with the reference pointing to the specific DOCX and structured report. Developer documentation cites the actual parsing code, explaining why checking only file existence and size is insufficient.

If "page header must contain version" is added later, the requirement reference, Checker construction parameters, rules, fixtures, stage tasks, development documentation, and eval_checkers business coverage must all be updated. Adding a sentence in the description without changing the code is not sufficient.

docs.title: False Positive Diagnosis Methods
docs.text:
When encountering consecutive stage failures, first reproduce the Checker registration parameters in an independent direct runner. Then check sequentially: whether the input is already generated in the current stage; whether paths normalize to the same value; whether optional files are forced; whether the fixture represents the current schema; whether the Checker itself catches import/parsing exceptions; and whether the failure evidence corresponds to the actual branch.

Issues like .//workflow/x vs workflow/x being incorrectly judged by string comparison have occurred; such problems should be normalized at the path generation and comparison layer, not by requiring the Agent to read a strange string. Issues like "latest snapshot version must always equal current version" causing false positives during batch updates within the same phase should be limited to the same chapter or same checkpoint semantics.

docs.title: Extension Points, Modification Impact, and Regression Matrix
docs.text:
Modification Sync Scope New rule type spec validation, renderer, auto fixture, documentation, and regression Modified construction parameters template, register args, config, instantiation test Modified path rules _safe_resolve, template _resolve, symbolic links, and out-of-bounds fixtures Modified error codes FAQ, stage fix hints, evaluation evidence, and negative tests Modified clss registration UCAgent loading, config generation, static import regression Modified business semantics user requirements, central spec, positive/negative fixtures, stages, and development documentation

Checker regression must simultaneously prove that passing cases pass and failing cases fail. Running only positive examples will allow error implementations with unconditional return True to pass all tests.

docs.title: Parent Builder Checker Complete Index
docs.text:
The following class definitions are in tools/workflow_builder/uc_checkers.py. Most classes inherit WorkflowBuildConfigChecker, sharing workspace path normalization, YAML/JSON reading, and evidence structure, but each class has a different business proof object.

Checker Class Check Object Primary Failure Meaning Secondary Dev Note WorkflowBuildConfigChecker Basic structure, paths, and core contract of workflow_build.yaml Central design unparseable or unable to drive subsequent generation Yes, shared base class; modifying generic paths/reading behavior affects almost all parent Checkers. WorkflowInputExampleManifestChecker User sample list, file existence, and categorization in input_example_manifest.yaml Input contract incomplete regarding real samples New sample types must express unknown/optional classification; do not hardcode specific business extensions. WorkflowBuildOutputChecker Builder initial products, directories, and reports Builder returns success but fixed deliverables are missing New deliverables must sync BuildReport and delivery regression. WorkflowMinimalInitChecker Minimal runnable skeleton of smoke workflow Cannot complete generation loop before full implementation Minimal does not mean empty shell; check only files committed in this stage. WorkflowEnvironmentSetupChecker Generated Makefile, ucagent_setup.sh, setup.py, schema, and requirements Sub-workflow not portable or config ineffective Distinguish Python dependencies from non-Python installation notes; test dry-run and repeated execution. WorkflowMCPToolIntegrationChecker Tool source code, config registration, import, parameters, and direct/MCP calls Tool file exists but UCAgent unavailable New return structures or adapters must change both direct and MCP evidence. WorkflowGeneratedCheckerChecker Generated Checker source code, docstring, fixture, registration, and positive/negative runs Checker cannot load, parameters wrong, or judgment invalid Prevent unconditional pass while avoiding false positives from future products in current stages. WorkflowGeneratedConfigChecker Syntax, required fields, and basic registration of generated config/inc Runtime configuration unloadable New schema fields must define compatible defaults before modifying generator and this Checker. WorkflowRuntimeConfigAuditChecker Stage reference/output specific files, reachability, placeholders, Tool/Checker/GuideDoc closures Config parses but hangs at runtime or cannot read files Normalize path comparisons; reference/output directories prohibited; do not write exceptions for specific {INPUT} appearances. WorkflowGeneratedGuideDocChecker Semantic chapters, operation evidence, registration, and detail level of generated GuideDoc Agent can read docs but cannot execute steps Handle multi-language titles via stable section IDs; do not hardcode Chinese titles. WorkflowMigrationPackageChecker Migration package file list, relative paths, hashes, extractability, and post-migration checks Success on dev machine but fails on new system delivery Must verify in new temporary root; do not pass due to accidental absolute path existence. WorkflowToolGenerationChecker Tool spec, generation status, basic source/test structure Generation loop not established Base class for tool Checkers; generic rules should not include specific business filenames. WorkflowGeneratedToolChecker Single smoke business Tool source code, spec, fixture, and run result Representative Tool unavailable, batch generation untrustworthy Check parameters should be provided by current spec; do not assume accidental files like diag_checker*.py. WorkflowBusinessToolGenerationChecker Count, generation, registration, testing, and requirement coverage of all planned business Tools Only smoke Tools; business capability delivery incomplete Allow subsequent new Tools, but each must return to manifest/spec and test evidence. WorkflowGuideDocSpecChecker Document spec target path, type, section ID, detail level, and registration plan Batch document generation without planning Distinguish GuideDoc and human docs; word count rules cannot be bypassed by code block flooding. WorkflowRequirementCoverageChecker Traceable mapping from requirements in requirements manifest to Tool, Checker, config, GuideDoc, docs Products complete in form but deviate from user needs Same category used with multiple aliases at different times; thresholds should increase with stages, not require final products initially. WorkflowImplementationPlanChecker Initial implementation plan stages, Tools, Checkers, GuideDocs, products, and action descriptions Parent Agent fails to establish executable blueprint Class/method docstrings and plan body detail must be tested; minimum examples must indicate non-meeting of positive word count. WorkflowLivingPlanChecker Per-stage markers, appended content, and predecessors Subsequent stages disconnected from or overwrite predecessor design Sync appender, FAQ, UI parsing, and living-plan regression after marker modification. WorkflowUserDocsChecker README, 01–05 user/dev docs, directories, word count, and real source analysis Generated workflow unusable by humans or further development Format requirements must maintain content freedom; source snippets must come from actual generated files. WorkflowDependencyChecker Python dependencies in requirements.txt, non-Python tool comments, and installation methods Users cannot restore runtime environment Do not fabricate unverified versions; optional system tools must explain downgrade behavior.

docs.title: Complete Index of Evaluation and Incremental Checkers
docs.text:
The following class definitions are located in tools/workflow_evaluation_control/uc_checkers.py. They do not judge whether a business file is "good" or "bad," but rather verify whether evaluation/incremental reports collect evidence according to the contract, are bound by approval constraints, and are truly completed with deployment regression.

Checker Class Purpose Secondary Development Focus EvaluationJsonReportChecker Validates the schema, status, checks, findings, metrics, and run identity of a specified eval report New fields must provide backward-compatible defaults for old runs; JSON parsing alone is insufficient. EvaluationGuideCoverageChecker Validates whether the eval/incremental GuideDoc covers required rules, severity levels, and execution constraints New check IDs must synchronize with both the GuideDoc and the coverage list, but full long-form document reading per stage should not be required. StaticAuditCoverageChecker Confirms that static audit coverage includes all required rules within this evaluation domain Must compare rule IDs against actual evidence; a single "audit success" boolean value is insufficient. IncrementalAuditCoverageChecker Confirms that the incremental phase has performed approval freshness, candidate, boundary, deployment, and regression audits Audit rules must be synchronized after modifying the state machine to prevent scenarios where formal documents are replaced while awaiting re-approval. IncrementalContextReportChecker Validates the cognitive list, target approvals, index, and reading budget for the current inc run "Preliminary understanding" should not be implemented as a full file read check-in; it must verify navigability rather than byte volume. IncrementalApprovalChecker Validates the source, run, fingerprint, decision, and current status of approvals/suggestions Agents must not self-approve; old approvals must become invalid if the source finding changes. EvaluationStageGateChecker Checks whether the evaluation stage only executes allowed operations, writes reports correctly, and meets completion thresholds When changing eval responsibility splitting, the gate must be synchronized to prevent eval_tools from exceeding boundaries or starting sub-processes in the evaluation environment. EvaluationEvidenceChecker Checks whether evidence for findings/checks points to specific files, symbols, commands, or results Judgments without evidence cannot be used to deceive users into believing requirements are met; evidence paths must be traceable and non-invasive. IncrementalApplicationChecker Validates the mapping from approved targets to candidates, deployment records, hashes, backups, and incomplete item mappings Generating a candidate plan is not equivalent to fixing; formal file results must be verified. IncrementalRegressionChecker Requires formal make check and related target success on top of application evidence Regression failures must not be converted to pending solely due to deployment; they should continue to be fixed or rolled back within the original approval scope.

docs.title: Configuration Alias and Implementation Class Mapping
docs.text:
The Checker name in the configuration is a stage semantic alias, while clss is the Python implementation. A single class can be used across multiple stages with different arguments and aliases. Developers adjusting class signatures must search for all mappings below and cannot rely on only the first search result.

Implementation Class Current Primary Configuration Alias WorkflowLivingPlanChecker living_plan_update_check WorkflowRequirementCoverageChecker requirements_manifest_check, initial_build_requirement_coverage, initial_template_requirement_coverage, smoke_manifest_check, final_requirement_coverage WorkflowImplementationPlanChecker workflow_implementation_plan_check WorkflowInputExampleManifestChecker input_example_manifest_check WorkflowBuildConfigChecker workflow_build_config_check WorkflowBuildOutputChecker workflow_builder_output_check WorkflowToolGenerationChecker workflow_tool_generation_check WorkflowGeneratedToolChecker workflow_business_tool_spec_check, workflow_generated_tool_check, workflow_generated_tool_strengthened_check WorkflowMinimalInitChecker workflow_minimal_init_check WorkflowEnvironmentSetupChecker workflow_environment_setup_check WorkflowMCPToolIntegrationChecker workflow_mcp_tool_integration_check, full_mcp_tool_integration_check WorkflowRuntimeConfigAuditChecker runtime_config_reference_audit WorkflowGuideDocSpecChecker guidedoc_spec_check WorkflowGeneratedGuideDocChecker generated_guidedoc_check WorkflowUserDocsChecker generated_user_docs_check WorkflowDependencyChecker generated_dependency_check WorkflowMigrationPackageChecker generated_migration_package_check, final_migration_package_check

In inc.yaml, generated_workflow_context_complete maps to IncrementalContextReportChecker; approved_changes_deployed maps to IncrementalApplicationChecker; applied_changes_have_approval and all_current_approvals_deployed map to IncrementalApprovalChecker; incremental_report_complete maps to EvaluationJsonReportChecker; incremental_guide_complete maps to EvaluationGuideCoverageChecker; incremental_static_audit_covered maps to IncrementalAuditCoverageChecker; and incremental_make_check_passed maps to IncrementalRegressionChecker.

In each eval_*.yaml, report aliases tools_report_complete, checkers_report_complete, flow_report_complete, env_report_complete, and run_report_complete map to EvaluationJsonReportChecker; guide aliases tools_guide_complete, checkers_guide_complete, flow_guide_complete, env_guide_complete, run_guide_complete, and evaluation_contract_complete map to EvaluationGuideCoverageChecker; and deterministic_audit_covered maps to StaticAuditCoverageChecker. EvaluationStageGateChecker and EvaluationEvidenceChecker belong to composable gate capabilities; if newly registered in the configuration, they must supplement alias, args instantiation, and stage evidence regression.

docs.title: Standard Steps for Modifying Checkers
docs.text:
1. First, write a provable proposition stating "what exactly is proven when it passes," then determine whether this is a parent construction, an evaluation incremental, or a generated business Checker.
  2. List all specific files and fields that currently exist in this stage; set future outputs as post-stage checks or explicitly optional, prohibiting the use of directories to replace reference files.
  3. Implement stable docstrings, construct parameters, path normalization, branch error codes, and meaningful evidence; do not catch all exceptions and masquerade as business failures.
  4. Search all YAML files for the corresponding clss and alias, verifying that argument names, types, requiredness, and default values match the signature.
  5. Add minimal positive fixtures, negative fixtures destroying only one condition at a time, boundary fixtures, import/instantiation tests, and configuration integration tests.

docs.title: Continue Reading
docs.text: Checkers tell the Agent "what constitutes completion," while GuideDocs tell the Agent "how to achieve it repeatably." Please continue reading GuideDoc Introduction to understand how stage guidance, FAQs, minimal examples, and Checker semantics remain consistent.

docs.title: GuideDoc and Document Generation Secondary Development for Parent Workflows
docs.text: This guide is for developers maintaining the parent workflow Guide_Doc/ and tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/, explaining how to modify stage guidance contracts, common FAQs, user document generation, and registration logic. The actual readers of GuideDoc are the Agents executing the stage, but the purpose of this guide is not to teach Agents how to perform tasks, but to instruct developers on how to design and implement this guidance system.

docs.title: Secondary Development Goals
docs.text: Typical tasks include adding new parent stage GuideDocs, adjusting semantic chapter contracts, adding user document types, fixing detail algorithms, controlling reference document read volumes, updating common FAQs, or changing guide_docs registration. After modifications, it must be proven that the parent Agent reads the correct guidance, and that user documents generated for the workflow are not erroneously injected into each stage.

docs.title: Parent Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text:
• Root Guide_Doc/: Public and stage guidance actually loaded by the parent workflow.
  • Root config.yaml, evaluation/incremental YAML: GuideDoc registration and stage references.
  • tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/contract.py: Stable chapter semantics and compatible headings.
  • tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/core.py: Spec validation, rendering, writing, and registration.
  • tools/workflow_builder/core.py: Fixed user document templates.
  • regression/: GuideDoc, delivery document, and detail regression.

docs.title: Directory Structure and Generation Methods
docs.text: Parent workflow public guidance is located in the root Guide_Doc/. Stage-specific documents are typically located in Guide_Doc/stages/, while common issues are located in the same public directory and referenced by each stage. The implementation for generating business GuideDocs is located in tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/, with registration information entering the business configuration.

docs.title: What a Stage Document Should Contain
docs.text:
• Stage objectives and content not handled in this stage.
  • Specific reference files that must be read and their read order.
  • Tool names, parameter sources, outputs, and failure handling.
  • Specific files that need to be generated or updated.
  • Checker names, parameters, and the meaning of each check.
  • Minimum passing version, using stable placeholders rather than specific business filenames.
  • A realistic common example.
  • Common failures, confirmation methods, and fix order.
  • The format for appending records in this stage within the implementation plan.

The purpose of the minimum example is to eliminate ambiguities in YAML, JSON, Markdown markers, or registration formats; it does not represent an encouragement for Agents to generate only minimal content. When there are requirements for body text length, it should be explicitly stated after the example that "this snippet only demonstrates structure, and formal content must meet detail requirements."

docs.title: FAQ Positioning
docs.text:
Stage FAQs are stable experiences summarized after predecessors run, placed in the public Guide_Doc/ along with the Workflow Builder, and are not automatically rewritten on every business run. Only update the FAQ after confirming the issue is general, with causes and fix methods verified.

FAQ entries should include symptoms, true causes, incorrect practices, correct handling, and applicable stages. Business-specific filenames should only be placed in the "example" field and should not become universal mandatory artifacts. For example, if a business generates diag_checker.py once, it should not be required in general rules for all workflows to create it.

docs.title: Read Cost Control
docs.text: Stage tasks should directly reference short documents of this stage; do not stuff hundreds of lines of public contracts into each config stage. Agents should first read directories, summaries, and minimum examples, then direct-read FAQs or development documents when encountering specific problems. Evaluation and incremental cognitive stages also adopt budgeted reading; establishing a preliminary understanding does not mean scanning all docs in full.

docs.title: Modification Methods
docs.text:
1. First confirm the problem stems from missing guidance, not Checker implementation errors.
  2. Update public source documents and corresponding stage references.
  3. If format contracts change, synchronize updates to minimum examples, schemas, and Checkers.
  4. Check that text contains no business coupling, future file references, or contradictory steps.
  5. Run GuideDoc generation regression and configuration reference checks.

docs.title: Document Quality Checks
docs.text: Detail does not mean repeatedly saying "must be detailed." High-quality guidance provides fields, data flows, tool parameters, judgment conditions, and failure recovery. Stage descriptions should at least allow an Agent not involved in this conversation to execute, without guessing filenames, template names, or output locations.

docs.title: GuideDoc Spec and Document Types
docs.text:
The GuideDoc generator handles both stage operation guidance and final user documents, but the two document types use different contracts. Stage GuideDocs emphasize purpose, inputs, outputs, usage, execution, checks, and failure recovery; user documents emphasize effective body text length, commands, input/output, and development/maintenance information. When developers add new document types, they should first determine if it is executed by the Agent or read by humans; the same set of headers should not mechanically validate all documents.

The spec should clearly define target path, document type, chapter id, heading, content, and registration stage. The id is stable semantics, while heading can be localized or adjusted in wording. Relying solely on heading text would incorrectly treat "input", "Inputs", and "input/output" as different contracts, so the current implementation retains compatible mappings.

docs.title: Semantic Chapter Contract Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/contract.py, symbols REQUIRED_SECTION_IDS, LEGACY_HEADING_IDS, and section_id().

REQUIRED_SECTION_IDS = (
    "purpose", "inputs", "outputs", "usage",
    "execution", "checks", "failure_recovery",
)

def section_id(section):
    value = section.get("id")
    if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
        return value.strip()
    return LEGACY_HEADING_IDS.get(section.get("heading"), "")

Explicit id takes priority, ensuring Chinese heading changes do not affect validation. Only when the old spec lacks an id is it mapped by heading, providing backward compatibility. Adding new required chapters affects all existing GuideDocs, therefore requiring schema versions, default migrations, or sufficient regression; one cannot simply add a value to the tuple and expect the old workspace to pass automatically.

REQUIRED_OPERATION_MARKERS further checks if key chapters truly describe input/<TARGET>/, output/, make check_example, and make run. It addresses the issue of "complete headings but vague content." However, markers are just minimum evidence and should not evolve into all business documents pasting the same command block.

docs.title: Spec Validation Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/core.py, symbol validate_guidedoc_specs().

The validator first limits specs and output paths via _safe(), then loads the YAML mapping, distinguishing user documents from GuideDocs. For operation guidance, it builds a section id set, checks for missing or duplicate entries, content types, and markers; for user documents, it calls _effective_prose_length() to calculate body text after excluding code fences, headings, and formatting noise.

This order is critical: path safety must fail before reading or writing; do not continue building Markdown if the structure is illegal; length checks should be based on actual descriptions, not YAML serialization length. If a new "source analysis" document requirement is added, check real source paths, code fences, and analysis chapters, rather than counting code characters to meet length.

The validation function returns a normalized spec list for the generation stage. Developers should not read a set of unnormalized fields from the original YAML again after validation, otherwise validation and generation will diverge.

docs.title: Document Generation and Registration Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/core.py, symbol generate_guidedocs().

The following is pseudo-code omitting implementation details; see the source above for the full implementation.

specs = validate_guidedoc_specs(workflow_root, spec_paths)
for spec in specs:
    target = _safe(root, spec["path"])
    content = render_sections(spec["sections"])
    _write_text(root, target, content)
    ... update config guide_docs registration ...

The generator should use atomic writes to avoid UCAgent reading a long document halfway written. Registration applies only to GuideDocs the Agent needs to load; ordinary user documents should not all be stuffed into guide_docs, otherwise each stage context would meaninglessly increase. Registration records must use workflow-relative file paths and be consistent with stage references.

When multiple GuideDocs are batch-generated, it is best to validate all first before starting writes. This ensures that if the seventh spec has a format error, the first six new files and old config do not end up in a mixed state. If the current implementation cannot be transactional, the report must at least accurately list written files for failure recovery cleanup.

docs.title: Minimum Passable Structure for Stage Guidance
docs.text:
The following structure only demonstrates semantics and does not represent that formal content can be this abbreviated:

path: Guide_Doc/stages/prepare.md
document_type: guidedoc
sections:
  - id: purpose
    heading: Purpose
    content: Describe this stage's responsibility and explicitly excluded work.
  - id: inputs
    heading: Inputs
    content: List the files and fields available before execution and their source stages.
  - id: execution
    heading: Execution Steps
    content: Specify the tools, arguments, outputs, and plan update locations in order.

Formal specs must also include outputs, usage, checks, failure_recovery, and provide sufficient detail for each tool and Checker. The minimum example should be placed immediately after the reminder that "body text must meet detail requirements" to prevent Agents from copying the example verbatim as the final document.

docs.title: FAQ Maintenance Linkage
docs.text:
After stage failures are evidenced, first record the business scene in this stage's "Issues and Handling" in the implementation plan. After the process completes, categorize: if it is a business-specific constraint, keep it in the business plan or business GuideDoc; if it is a generator defect, modify the code and regress; if it is a cross-business stable misconception, then write it to the public FAQ.

FAQ entries must provide symptoms, impact, confirmation steps, root cause, correct fix, and incorrect practices. For example, the universal root cause of "Checker reports unread .//workflow/x" is that the path is not normalized; .// should not be treated as the correct format that future Agents must mimic. After FAQ updates, check which stages need to reference them, ensuring not all stages default to reading all FAQs.

docs.title: Reading Budget and Context Design
docs.text:
The goal of GuideDoc is to reduce Agent decision costs, not add reading rituals. A stage should directly reference short, complete documents of this stage; shared long contracts should be consulted on-demand via indexes and rule ids. Evaluation and incremental processes should first read directories, manifest summaries, and target object indexes, then read source code by finding.

Instructions like "fully understand the entire process" in task descriptions can lead to full scans of tools, checkers, docs, and reports, which then compress and repeat reading. More reliable instructions specify which indexes to read in the first round, what cognitive summary to output, and which direct dependencies are allowed to be appended when processing a specific object.

docs.title: Secondary Development Case: Adding Stage Guidance to Parent Workflow
docs.text:
Assume the addition of a "Material License Audit" stage. The developer first declares in the central workflow spec that the input is a specific material list file, the output is a license report, the Tool is the license metadata parser, and the Checker is the license status checker. The stage GuideDoc explains the source whitelist, unknown license behavior, network failure recovery, and report evidence.

Adding only the GuideDoc without the central stage and Checker means the document will not be executed; adding only the config stage without a GuideDoc means the Agent will guess tool parameters; registering the entire docs/ directory causes stage context explosion. The correct approach modifies and covers the spec, tool, Checker, GuideDoc registration, minimal fixture, and regression simultaneously.

docs.title: Extension Points and Testing
docs.text:
Testing explicit IDs, old heading mappings, missing sections, duplicate sections, and unknown IDs when adding new chapter semantics. Testing code blocks, tables, links, Chinese and English body text when modifying the length algorithm. Testing that user documents are not injected into the Agent, GuideDocs are readable, paths do not escape, and repeated generation is idempotent when modifying registration.

Real-world business acceptance requires reading the generated documents, not just checking the checker return code. A structure that is correct but inconsistent with the actual tool signatures in the steps remains a serious document defect.

docs.title: Cross-Cutting Complete GuideDoc Index
docs.text:
All files in the table below are located in the parent workflow Guide_Doc/. They represent the execution contract of the parent Agent, not the content of the developer's documents. Before modifying, query referenced stages in YAML to avoid unintentionally injecting a long document into all stage contexts.

docs.text:
Guide_Doc/stages/README.md is the stage document directory and shared structure description. The following files correspond one-to-one with the 24 stages in the main config.yaml; the numbers and stage names in the filenames must remain synchronized.

docs.title: Standard Process for Adding or Modifying GuideDoc
docs.text:
1. Identify whether this is a cross-cutting contract, an evaluation/incremental contract, or a main phase operation guide, and query the current YAML reference scope.
  2. Write steps using specific files, fields, Tool parameters, Checker judgments, and failure evidence; descriptive content should be in Chinese, while class names, fields, commands, and identifiers must remain in their original form.
  3. Include a minimal passing structure and a common complete example immediately followed by a reminder: "The minimal example does not meet the depth/length of the main text," to prevent the Agent from copying a brief example verbatim.
  4. Write stable, generic failures into the corresponding FAQ, retaining only symptoms, root cause, verification, correct fix, and incorrect practices; do not automatically modify the parent FAQ during every business run.
  5. Synchronize stage task, guide_docs registration, corresponding Checker, document generation rules, and document regression, then verify whether a new business observation Agent can execute independently.

docs.title: Continue Reading
docs.text: Beyond evaluation and incremental GuideDoc, there are JSON state, approval freshness, candidate deployment, and rollback contracts. Please continue reading Evaluation and Incremental Control, and do not leave an inconsistent state machine by modifying only natural language guidance.

docs.title: Parent Workflow Evaluation, Incremental, and Console Secondary Development
docs.text: This guide instructs users on secondary development of the parent workflow evaluation suite, incremental state machine, controlled deployment, and the "Workflow Build and Evaluation Console". Modifications focus on tools/workflow_evaluation_control/ and root evaluation/incremental configurations, not on individual evaluation reports or sub-workflow source code.

docs.title: Secondary Development Goals
docs.text: Typical tasks include adding report types or check IDs, adjusting severity rules, adding approval actions, modifying incremental run/batch/attempt, extending candidate stagers/deployers, changing backup recovery policies, or adding console pages or structured edit files. All extensions must maintain backward JSON readability, traceable approval sources, rollable formal documents, and restricted API paths.

docs.title: Parent Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text:
• eval_*.yaml, inc.yaml, and corresponding GuideDocs: Agent phase and task boundaries.
  • tools/workflow_evaluation_control/json_store.py: structured file schema, CRUD, and atomic persistence.
  • approvals.py: finding/suggestion decision and fingerprint.
  • incremental.py, incremental_runs.py: candidates, deployment, history, and run identity.
