  • review_server.py, design_editor.py, and frontend resources: console API and UI.
  • uc_tools.py, uc_checkers.py: expose controlled operations and acceptance to the parent Agent.
  • evaluation split, review UI, write boundary regression: behavior protection.

docs.title: Report Model
docs.text:
Evaluation components write check results and findings to eval/. User approvals and suggestions possess stable IDs, status, reasons, timestamps, and sources. Aggregated reports retain history across different runs; old findings cannot represent modified new evaluation results.

Structured files must be created, updated, read, or deleted via the storage interface. When extending fields, provide default values and migration reads to prevent console crashes due to missing fields in old workspaces. Deleting entries is an explicit API; versioned deletions must also synchronize management of corresponding historical files and references.

docs.title: Incremental Run Identity
docs.text: Each run_inc invocation first calls start-inc-run, generating a unique ID and tmp/inc_runs/<id>/. All approvals snapshots, candidate files, check records, deployment lists, and final states for this round are associated with this ID. The Agent can only read candidates from the current run and cannot treat previous round residues as approved modifications.

docs.title: Candidates and Deployment
docs.text:
The parent workflow should provide controlled tools to copy formal files to the current candidate directory. Modifications occur in the candidate replica; subsequent runs perform syntax, fixture, and related Make checks. The deployer creates temporary files in the same filesystem, saves old versions, and atomically replaces formal files, even if the original file is not writable in-place.

Old versions are saved to tmp/change_history/, with index records containing original paths, backup paths, hashes, timestamps, run IDs, and recovery status. Recovery is also a controlled atomic deployment; deleting history records must be explicitly triggered by the user.

docs.title: State Machine Termination Conditions
docs.text:
• No approved targets: normal quick termination.
  • Candidate check failure: continue fixing candidates; do not deploy.
  • Deployed but make check failure: immediately continue fixing or rollback; do not wait for new approvals.
  • All approved targets have changes and evidence, regression passed: complete.
  • Unable to fix within approved scope: report blocking reasons and incomplete mappings, then fail exit.

Repeated execution of the same failed command with unchanged state, files, and evidence constitutes a spin loop; the cycle should stop and enter an explicit fix or block branch.

docs.title: Console Extensions
docs.text: The backend entry point is located at tools/workflow_evaluation_control/review_server.py, with structured design edit logic in design_editor.py. When adding new page fields, extend the server-side schema and validation first, then implement frontend presentation. File paths must be resolved from an allowlist and workspace root; arbitrary absolute paths passed by the browser are prohibited.

docs.title: Testing Priorities
docs.text:
• Concurrent report writes do not lose data.
  • Old format files are readable and migratable.
  • Unapproved entries cannot enter incremental snapshots.
  • Two incremental runs do not share candidates.
  • Old versions are saved before deployment; hashes match after recovery.
  • Deleting version entries maintains files and indices.
  • Illegal paths, symlinks, and out-of-bounds targets are rejected.
  • Failed post-deployment regressions do not remain pending.

docs.title: Structured File Model
docs.text:
Evaluation control uses a fixed allowlist to manage eval/ and res/. Each document possesses a format version, revision, and specific collection: evaluation reports use runs, approvals and suggestions use items, deployment records use entries, and audits use events. When the Agent calls tools, pass individual records, not entire JSON documents, to avoid overwriting all history with a single error.

Report runs contain run ID, contract version, status, timestamp, target revision, checks, findings, and metrics. Findings include stable ID/fingerprint, severity, evidence, impact, and suggestions. Approvals are bound to the source report, run ID, source ID, and fingerprint; if the source finding content changes, old approvals are no longer current.

docs.title: JSON Load and Validation Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/json_store.py, symbols load_document() and validate_document().

value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
return validate_document(relative, value)

This seemingly simple load function separates reporting "file not found", "JSON format error", and "invalid schema". validate_document() selects the corresponding structural rule based on the relative path, rejecting Agent-created unknown eval files. Developers adding new document types must simultaneously update the allowlist, base document, validation, collection name, record ID, template, CLI, and console.

Validation at load time means historical file corruption is immediately exposed upon reading, rather than silently overwriting during the next mutation. Error messages retain line and column numbers to facilitate user repair of manually corrupted files, but the normal flow should still write through structured tools.

docs.title: Atomic Write and Permission Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/json_store.py, symbol _atomic_write().

tmp_root = workspace / "tmp/json_store"
fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=tmp_root)
json.dump(value, stream, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
stream.flush()
os.fsync(stream.fileno())
os.replace(temporary, path)

Temporary files are uniformly placed in the root tmp/, flushed and fsynced after writing, then atomically replaced with os.replace(). The function temporarily restores parent directory and target user write permissions, then restores parent directory mode and removes group/other write bits on eval files after completion. This prevents half-written JSON and explains why direct editors might see files as read-only.

Read-only is not "permanently locked": controlled storage and deployers can update via directory-level atomic replacement. Developers cannot globally chmod -R 777 for convenience, as this would break audit boundaries. Exception branches must clean up temporary files and restore permissions.

docs.title: CRUD and Concurrency Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/json_store.py, symbol mutate_document().

expected_revision implements optimistic concurrency control. After the console reads the revision and submits edits, if the evaluation Agent has updated the document in the meantime, the server rejects the old draft, preventing post-write overwriting pre-write. Create rejects duplicate IDs; update/delete require record existence; upsert explicitly allows both.

Each successful mutation increments the revision, performs atomic write, and appends audit. List/get returns deep copies to prevent callers from modifying in-memory objects and bypassing persistence. When adding batch operations, they must still complete under a single lock and single revision; looping single API calls can lead to partial success.

docs.title: Approval Freshness Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/approvals.py, symbols _fingerprint(), decide_item(), and approval_is_current().

The fingerprint is calculated based on the stable business content of findings/suggestions, not just the ID. Approval records store the source run and fingerprint; during incremental deployment, the current source object is re-read and compared. If the evaluation regenerates the same ID but the problem content changes, the user must re-approve.

Approve, reject, and defer are user decisions; the Agent cannot approve its own findings. Default responses reduce input, but the console must allow user modification. Batch approvals apply only to user-selected records, saving sources for each item, avoiding an untraceable "big approval" for specific issues.

docs.title: Incremental Candidates and Run Identity
docs.text:
Each start-inc-run generates a run ID, below which batches and attempts are established. Candidate stagers only allow copying explicitly targeted files from workflow/ to the current attempt's candidate directory, recording source hashes. The Agent modifies candidates, not formal files, ensuring check failures do not pollute the public workflow.

Run ID resolves issues with old candidate mixing; batch represents a group of related approvals; attempt represents retry fixes within the same batch. Reports, candidates, evidence, and history must carry these identities. A single long-lived tmp/candidate/ directory covering all rounds cannot be used.

docs.title: Deployer Code Analysis
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/incremental.py, symbol deploy_incremental_changes().

The deployer first validates workflow_root, mapping, change ID, fixed manifest path, current run, and current approvals. Each mapping must include source, target, approval IDs, and rationale, with all approvals within the current authorization set. It then executes projected semantics, preventing candidates from introducing new deterministic high-risk findings.

approved = {
    item["id"]: item for item in approvals["items"]
    if approval_is_current(workspace, item)
}
if any(item not in approved for item in approval_ids):
    raise IncrementalDeploymentError(...)

This check prevents old approvals, forged IDs, or changed findings from being deployed. Mappings must also reference covering approvals, allowing applied changes to answer "why this file is allowed to be modified".

docs.title: Backup, Atomic Replacement, and Rollback
docs.text:
Source location: tools/workflow_evaluation_control/incremental.py, symbols _atomic_copy(), _archive_target(), and _rollback_targets().

_atomic_copy() creates a temporary file in the target parent directory, uses copy2 to preserve metadata, and then os.replace. The original target can be a read-only file because it is not written in-place. _archive_target() saves the pre-replacement file to a relative path under the current history/before and computes the SHA-256 hash; the new file records existed=False.

When a batch deployment fails midway, rollback restores existing files in reverse order and deletes files added in the current run. Reverse order is critical because subsequent targets may depend on preceding directories or configurations. Rollback should also record failures; if rollback itself fails, the report must be escalated to a critical state and cannot return a standard deployment failure.

docs.title: Restore and Delete History
docs.text:
restore_incremental_backup() searches records, verifies backup paths are within the allowed history root, checks hashes, and saves the current formal version before restoration. This allows users to undo restoration after restoring an older version. delete_incremental_backup() only responds to explicit user actions, updates the index, and deletes unreferenced backups.

Version records are immutable by default for Agents to support auditing; user deletion in the console is an explicit, controlled management action. Frontend buttons, backend APIs, reference checks, and file deletion must all be implemented together; removing only the UI entry would leave orphaned files.

docs.title: Incremental State Machine and make check
docs.text:
If a candidate check fails, continue fixing the candidate; if make check fails on the formal version after successful deployment, continue fixing or rollback. At this point, do not wait for new approval, as the target is already authorized by the current approval and formal files have already changed. Only rollback and report a need for new decision if the fix requires going beyond the original approval scope.

Anti-loop conditions should compare state, candidate hash, check return code, and new evidence. If the same command is executed consecutively and none of these values change, the process should enter a fix or block state, no longer treating stage prompts as new requests for repeated verification.

docs.title: Console Backend and Structure Editing
docs.text:
review_server.py binds the workspace to the handler, exposing only fixed APIs. design_editor.py provides editor schemas, drafts, cross-file validation, and save functionality by file type. The browser can only edit allowed fields; the server re-reads the original revision, applies the draft, validates all candidates, and then atomically saves.

The workflow file tree reading API must also restrict paths, symbolic links, size, and binary types. Files without a fixed schema display raw text only; guessing fields for a pretty interface and writing back is not allowed. When adding monitored files, simultaneously update the whitelist, artifact parser, frontend renderer, and API regression tests.

docs.title: Fault Scenarios and Testing
docs.text:
Test coverage must include: corrupted JSON, revision conflicts, duplicate IDs, expired approvals, candidate out-of-bounds, target out-of-bounds, backup hash mismatch, second run using old candidate, batch deployment failure midway, rollback failure, read-only targets, history restore and delete, and post-deployment regression failure. Each test runs in a temporary workspace without touching real business data.

For the console, also test: two workspace port conflicts, existing service detection, invalid path 400, unsaved draft, structure validation failure, batch approval, and explicit deletion. HTTP 200 only proves API response; business state correctness must be re-asserted by re-reading JSON and target files.

docs.title: Five Evaluation Workflows Itemized Responsibilities
docs.text:
The evaluation suite uses five independent YAML files. Splitting them limits reading scope, report writing, and tool permissions, avoiding the need to start high-cost sub-workflows for any single static evaluation.

Configuration & Stage Input/Output Must Check Explicitly Prohibited eval_tools.yaml / evaluate_tool_contracts Read tool source, register, spec, fixture, requirements, and res/; write eval/tools_report.json Verify all tools exist, comply with UCTool protocol, config correctly registered, source contains real business logic, fixtures/direct calls prove availability, requirements cover user needs Do not start sub-workflows, do not modify workflow/, do not declare tools available just because files exist. eval_checkers.yaml / evaluate_checker_contracts Read Checker source, config args, fixture, stage product contracts, and res/; write eval/checkers_report.json Checker exists, protocol/docstring, class import, constructor args match registration, positive examples pass and single-negative fails, determines if proof of requirement, does not reference future files or form unpassable thresholds Do not lower business semantics to make existing products pass, do not directly modify Checkers. eval_flow.yaml / evaluate_flow_contracts Read config/inc, workflow spec, Tool/Checker/GuideDoc index, and requirements; write eval/flow_report.json YAML parsing is just the start; also check placeholder declarations, reference/output specifics and timeliness, Tool/Checker/GuideDoc loadability, stage outputs support subsequent stages, documents match real signatures Do not just search for {INPUT} patterns; check all undeclared variables and closure references; do not start sub-processes. eval_env.yaml / evaluate_environment_contracts Read Makefile, setup.py, ucagent_setup.sh, requirements, schema, and environment docs; write eval/env_report.json Make targets and variable priorities, setup controlled updates, requirements distinguish Python/non-Python, paths portable, secrets not written to disk, port conflicts resolvable, permissions do not block atomic replacement Do not treat local absolute paths as portable, do not modify user res/checkers.json without authorization. eval_run.yaml / evaluate_requested_runtime Read user-specified runtime target, inputs, and existing static evidence; write independent runtime report Use ChildWorkflowSupervisor to start specified sub-process, record stage, duration, failure, product changes, stuck, and termination evidence Do not start high-cost business flows by default with run_eval, do not wait indefinitely without timeout/termination policies.

Severity ordering is: issues preventing UCAgent startup, infinite retries, destructive/out-of-bounds replacement of formal files, or inability to rollback are highest risk; products deviating from user semantics while claiming completion follow closely; deterministic check failures, missing critical evidence, and non-reproducible installs are high/medium risk; text not affecting results and optional improvements are low risk.

docs.title: Incremental Workflow Four Stages Itemized Explanation
docs.text:
inc.yaml stage Primary Input Tools & Products Checker & Pass Semantics understand_generated_workflow Current inc run ID, approved finding/suggestion snapshot, sub-workflow index, res/ index, and direct dependencies IncrementalContextInventory produces a budgeted context report, StructuredJsonStore records this run's state; read list and targets first, then source as needed generated_workflow_context_complete only proves sufficient preliminary understanding to plan this fix, does not require reading all docs/tools/checkers in full. plan_approved_changes Current approval snapshot, context report, source file hashes, and related requirements Build candidate plans for this run/batch/attempt, mapping each change to approval ID, source, target, reason, implementation, and acceptance commands; use stager to copy formal files applied_changes_have_approval checks that plans and subsequent records only reference current approvals; unapproved suggestions cannot be mixed in. deploy_approved_changes Current attempt candidate, mapping, approval snapshot, candidate check evidence Use generator or controlled editing to update candidates; after passing checks, IncrementalChangeDeployer backs up old versions and deploys atomically, writing applied_changes.json and history approved_changes_deployed, all_current_approvals_deployed require a deployed/skipped/blocked mapping for each current approval; passing is not granted just by generating a plan. verify_and_report_increment Formal files, applied changes, history, this run's check commands, and all approval acceptance conditions Run make check and related targets on formal sub-workflows; on failure, immediately return to candidate fix or rollback; on pass, write incremental_report.json with acceptance evidence incremental_make_check_passed, incremental_report_complete, incremental_guide_complete, incremental_static_audit_covered jointly prove formal products pass, reports are complete, and no out-of-bounds changes occurred.

Approval authorizes "the scope of fixes for the target issue," not "asking again for each file replacement." If formal files deployed after regression fail, iterative fixes within the same scope do not require new approvals, but each replacement must save versions and evidence. Changes to other unauthorized files require rollback or a report for new approval.

docs.title: Console Subsystem Secondary Development Map
docs.text:
The "Workflow Construction and Evaluation Console" has three types of data interfaces: evaluation and approval are structured JSON CRUD; construction design is field-level draft editing for YAML with fixed schemas, full-text read-only for unstructured Markdown; version management is restore and explicit delete for change history. These three cannot be merged into a single "turn any file into a JSON form" API.

review_server.py handles HTTP routing, workspace binding, error codes, and static resources; json_store.py and approvals.py manage evaluation data; design_editor.py manages editor schemas, drafts, and cross-validation for wfgen/input_example_manifest.yaml, wfgen/workflow_build.yaml, wfgen/requirements_manifest.yaml, and other allowed fields; artifact reader parses implementation plan markers, YAML outlines, JSON reports, and the workflow/ file tree. The server must re-verify every save; it cannot trust that the browser has already performed word count and cross-file checks.

When adding new editable fields, synchronize allowed fields, value types, create/delete rules, word counts/statistical derived values, cross-file references, revision conflicts, and save regression tests. Do not open raw full-text coverage to bypass the structural view. When adding new read-only monitored files, update the allowed list, parser, navigation outline, file size limits, and illegal/symbolic link path regression tests.

docs.title: Continue Reading
docs.text: Every invariant for evaluation and incremental control requires deterministic regression. Please continue reading Testing and Regression to understand the responsibility boundaries protected by each existing regression script.

docs.title: Second-Development Testing and Regression for Parent Workflows
docs.text: This guide directs second-developers to write, select, and run tests for the current Workflow Builder parent workflow. Since the model processes in Workflow Builder are time-consuming, parent code modifications should first be identified by deterministic regression tests for protocol errors, followed by a small number of real business runs to verify parent Agent behavior and generated artifacts. Complete generation should not be treated as the most basic unit test.

docs.title: Second-Development Goals
docs.text: Developers should be able to select the minimum regression based on the modified responsibility domain, establish fixtures that fail first then pass for defects, integrate new scripts into the regression Makefile, and record existing failures outside the scope. The testing focus is to prove the parent module's inputs, outputs, boundaries, and compatibility, not to achieve a green return code by manually fixing the test workspace.

docs.title: Parent Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text: The test entry points are the root make regression and regression/Makefile. Scripts directly invoke the parent generator or evaluation control core, checking artifacts within a temporary workspace. Tests involving UCAgent import must use the project venv; real process validation requires creating an independent business root to observe via supervision strategy whether the parent workflow can generate correct results autonomously.

docs.title: Regression Entry
docs.text:
cd ~/work/UCAgent/examples/workflow_builder
make regression

Scripts in regression/ cover design construction, delivery contracts, boundary writing, evaluation splitting, incremental control, console, and generator behavior. Developers should run the most relevant scripts first based on the modification scope, then run the total entry point.

docs.title: Layered Testing
docs.text:
1. Syntax Tests: Python compilation, YAML/JSON parsing, Makefile dry run.
  2. Unit Tests: Pure functions, schema validation, path handling, state transitions, and serialization.
  3. Component Regression: Run a specific generator with fixed test_data and check artifacts.
  4. Protocol Regression: Consistency between tools, Checker, GuideDoc, config, and environment facilities.
  5. Real Workspace Validation: Select a small business to run key stages, observing retries, latency, and final artifacts.

docs.title: Test Data Principles
docs.text: Fixtures should be small, stable, and contain a single error. Do not rely on network, model random output, current username, or absolute paths. Negative samples should break the target rule only once. When external commands are required, use a whitelist and detectable skip conditions, distinguishing "not installed" from "test failure" in reports.

docs.title: Documentation Regression
docs.text: Documentation checks should verify the existence of required files, Markdown relative links and images, necessary titles and commands. It cannot merely count words, nor count repeated code block content as proof of detail. Make targets in QuickStart must exist in the current Makefile.

docs.title: Minimum Test Set After Modifications
docs.text: Modified Area Minimum Validation Makefile or setup.py Config dry-run, check, variable coverage, Make help Tool Generator Tool component regression, registration test, total regression Checker Generator Instantiation, positive/negative fixtures, stage registration, total regression GuideDoc/config YAML parsing, reference existence, stage check regression Evaluation Control Report CRUD, aggregation, approval status, permission boundaries Incremental Deployment Run isolation, candidate copy, backup, atomic replacement, recovery Console API test, structure edit, filter, delete, port conflict

docs.title: Real-Run Acceptance
docs.text:
During real-time execution, record the start/end of each stage, failure count, Checker messages, and artifact changes. If a stage is slow, first confirm if it is still generating valid tool calls; only modify rules if a parent workflow issue is confirmed. The supervision Agent should not directly write sub-workflow artifacts, otherwise the run result loses its verification value.

After completion, check git diff to ensure workspace artifacts, .ucagent history, tmp/, local configurations, or browser profiles are not committed to the parent repository.

docs.title: Regression Makefile Code Analysis and Structure
docs.text:
The regression/Makefile defines independent targets for each type of protocol test, which are then aggregated by all. The root Makefile's regression target explicitly passes the UCAgent virtual environment Python, avoiding inconsistencies between system Python versions and dependencies and the project.

all: contract stability checker_descriptions requirement_templates \
     living_plan write_boundaries evaluation_split review_ui \
     documentation environment_setup

contract:
    cd $(ROOT) && PYTHONPATH="..." $(PYTHON) regression/run_delivery_contract_regression.py

Each target runs from the Workflow Builder root, ensuring relative test_data and module paths are consistent. New regression scripts must be added to .PHONY and all; otherwise, developers running only make regression will not execute them. Scripts depending on UCAgent modules must use the passed venv Python; pure documentation scripts can use the same interpreter for consistency.

docs.title: Delivery Contract Regression
docs.text:
run_delivery_contract_regression.py is the largest deterministic test. It constructs workflow build data, generates a complete workflow, and checks fixed deliverables, Make targets, config, environment, documentation, tools, Checker, and run contracts. It is suitable for discovering new templates that break the overall structure, but with many assertions; when failing, locate the specific contract rather than blindly updating expected strings.

Currently, this script has one existing assertion requiring the initial task to include "Prohibit calling non-existent ListFiles". If source rules have changed but the test is not synchronized, review separately whether it is an implementation regression or an outdated assertion. This round of documentation expansion only records it without modifying parent task semantics.

docs.title: Stability and Living Plan Regression
docs.text:
run_builder_stability_regression.py verifies repeated builds, existing file policies, and generation result stability. For tool generation states based on hashes, the first and second runs should produce interpretable created/skipped results, not unconditional rewrites every time.

run_living_plan_regression.py verifies implementation plan stage markers, append behavior, and protection of preceding content. New stage names or marker syntax must include corresponding fixtures to ensure subsequent stages cannot overwrite preceding stage "issues and handling".

docs.title: Checker and Requirements Regression
docs.text:
run_checker_description_regression.py generates a Checker, imports the class, and checks description/docstring, capable of discovering issues where "source exists but UCAgent reports No description". Running it must use the project virtual environment; otherwise, system Python may fail due to typing.NotRequired or dependency versions, which is a test environment error, not a Checker business failure.

run_requirement_template_contract_regression.py verifies that user requirement templates can express reusable templates, tools, Checkers, environments, and documentation requirements. When modifying guide templates or manifest schemas, add positive examples for new fields and negative examples for missing fields.

docs.title: Write Boundary and Evaluation Split Regression
docs.text:
run_write_boundary_regression.py checks workspace initialization, history permission recovery, tmp cleanup, and prohibition of out-of-bounds writes. When adding cleanup logic, prove it will not delete eval/, res/, input/, the current incremental run, or change history.

run_evaluation_split_regression.py verifies responsibilities of tools/checkers/flow/env, JSON store, approvals, incremental runs, candidate deployment, and report aggregation. It should not start expensive real model processes but use fixed workspaces and tools to directly invoke control logic.

docs.title: Console Regression Code Patterns
docs.text:
run_review_ui_regression.py starts a local service on a temporary port, checking meta, state, design files, structure editing, approvals, suggestions, history recovery, and deletion via HTTP requests. Tests also actively request symbolic links and ../ out-of-bounds paths, expecting a 400 response.

response = request("GET", "/api/design-files/workflow%2F..%2Feval%2Fsummary.json")
assert response.status == 400

Console tests should close the server and browser profile upon exit. If a lock in tmp is deleted by browser concurrency, the cleaner must tolerate FileNotFoundError; however, if service threads are not stopped and ports are still listening, it must fail.

docs.title: How to Write Single-Variable Fixtures
docs.text:
First construct a minimal legal baseline, then copy and only change the target field. For example, when testing that reference cannot be a directory, the valid spec uses reports/result.json, and the invalid spec changes only it to reports/. Do not simultaneously delete stage names, change templates incorrectly, and add absolute paths, as failures may stem from any rule.

Each negative test must assert a stable error code or key field, not just assert "an exception was raised". Positive tests must also check actual file content, registration, or hashes, not just that the function did not raise an error.

Source code pattern: Scripts like regression/run_write_boundary_regression.py use temporary workspaces, explicit calls, and assertions.

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
    workspace = Path(temporary) / "workspace"
    workspace.mkdir()
    result = operation(workspace)
    assert result["ok"] is True
    assert (workspace / "expected/file.json").is_file()
    assert not (Path(temporary) / "escaped.json").exists()

Temporary directories isolate machine state and clean up upon completion; tests assert both files that should be created and files that should not be created to prove write boundaries. If failure artifacts need to be retained for debugging, a directory can be retained via an explicit environment variable, but regression should not pollute the repository by default.

docs.title: Tool Test Design
docs.text:
Tools require at least spec validation, source compile/import, parameter models, normal calls, boundary calls, failure structures, path escape, and repeated runs. When involving external programs, use controllable small commands, timeouts, and temporary cwd. Network-acquired tools should separate the downloader from business parsing, testing with local response fixtures without relying on the public internet in regression.

For generator tests, also verify config registration and generation state. After modifying existing files, generate again, asserting that preserve/replace policies match the design. When multiple tools are batch-generated, check that registration does not lose items or have duplicates.

docs.title: Checker Test Design
docs.text:
Each business rule in Checker must have positive and single negative evidence. First test class importability, inheritance of Checker, non-empty description/docstring, and constructor parameter matching, then call check. Exceptional inputs should return (False, evidence) instead of causing the runner to crash.

Command Checker tests whitelist rejection, expected return codes, unexpected return codes, and timeouts. File Checker tests relative paths, absolute paths, .., symbolic links, and missing files. Structure Checker tests top-level types, field types, missing fields, and boundary values.

docs.title: GuideDoc and config Test Design
docs.text:
GuideDoc tests explicit section IDs, old title mappings, missing sections, duplicate sections, markers, valid content, and registration. Code blocks in user documentation should not be counted towards content length. After generation, read the Markdown to confirm commands and paths match the actual Makefile/config.

Config tests unknown placeholders, double braces, loop coverage, parent process path leakage, directory file contract, future references, unknown Checkers, parameter mismatches, and stage handoffs. YAML parsing is just the first layer; the final step must also execute static config checker.

docs.title: Incremental and Version Management Test Design
docs.text:
Initialize eval files and two formal files in a temporary workspace, create approval, start run, stage candidate, and deploy. Assert formal hash, backup hash, applied changes, run ID, and approval mapping. Then simulate a second file replacement failure, confirming the first rolls back. Finally, test recovery saves the current version, while deletion removes only the target record.

Post-deployment regression failure state machine tests must prove the process does not stall in pending or repeat the same command. Use fixed failure/success scripts and attempt counts to simulate two fixes.

docs.title: Complete Example from Defect to Regression
docs.text:
Problem: config generator allows reference_files: [docs/]. First write a minimal invalid spec and confirm old code passes the error; add specific file judgment in _file_contract_errors(); assert error includes field location; then add valid file paths to ensure no false positives. Subsequently run config component, delivery contract, evaluation split, and real generation workflow make check.

Documentation synchronization explains why directories cannot be references, how to list deterministically existing files, and why unknown future files cannot be referenced in advance. This protects the regression mechanism, guides the Agent, and evaluation rules can still discover historical artifacts.

docs.title: Performance and Authenticity
docs.text:
Deterministic regression should complete within seconds without invoking models. Real business tests are used to observe whether the Agent understands the task, whether it fails continuously, and product quality; the two cannot replace each other. To speed up real processes, batch generation followed by checks, limit reads, and parallel independent tools can be used, but results cannot be manually generated by the supervisor.

Test reports must record commands, interpreters, return codes, and known failures. If full regression stops early due to existing issues, run remaining targets separately and explicitly state which pass; do not vaguely write "regression failed" or "all passed".

docs.title: Regression Extension Rules
docs.text: When adding new components, prioritize adding tests to existing responsibility targets; only create new targets when forming independent protocols, runtime costs, or dependency boundaries. New targets must enter all, use the passed interpreter, isolate workspaces, and be documented in README explaining the protected behavior. When deleting features, simultaneously delete assertions for lost objects; do not let outdated tests force implementations to retain meaningless text.

docs.title: Complete Directory of Existing Regression Scripts
docs.text:
The following table is based on actual files regression/run_*regression.py. Secondary developers should first place defects into the script with the closest responsibility; only create new scripts when attribution is impossible.

Script Protected Parent Workflow Contract Extended Methods run_builder_runtime_directory_regression.py Sub-workflow runtime directories created by Builder, Python package/import skeleton, and basic path ownership When adding fixed runtime directories or packages, build and import real generation classes in temporary workspace, not just check filenames. run_builder_stability_regression.py Command limits, plan appending, GuideDoc contract, Tool generation safety, and repeated build stability For modifications to preserve/replace, hashes, paths, or detail algorithms, add first/second/file drift comparison groups. run_checker_description_regression.py Generated Checker class descriptions, method docstrings, imports, and basic runtime protocols When adding new renderers/rule types, generate and import that type to prevent runtime failures like No description provided. run_delivery_contract_regression.py Broad delivery contracts from central design to complete sub-workflows: skeleton, config, Tool, Checker, GuideDoc, docs, Make, and migration Only add true cross-component invariants; single-module details go into component scripts to avoid stale prompt strings becoming pseudo-contracts. run_documentation_regression.py This docs/ information architecture, links/images, development documentation detail, source analysis, and dynamic component lists New documents add REQUIRED; new stages/UCTool/Checker/GuideDoc/regression should pass dynamic inventory requirements corresponding to development document class or file names. run_environment_setup_regression.py Workflow Builder root setup.py, .workflow_builder/local.mk, interactive/non-interactive config, command line overrides, and secret boundaries Test defaults, persistence, show/check, invalid values, and old config compatibility for each new environment field. run_evaluation_split_regression.py Five evaluation splits, JSON store, approval freshness, inc run isolation, candidate, deploy, backup recovery, and report aggregation New JSON types, approval actions, state transitions, or deploy mappings go here first; must assert persisted results and file hashes. run_living_plan_regression.py workflow_implementation_plan.md stage markers, required sections, appending idempotency, and non-overlapping predecessors New stages or plan sections must have normal appending, same-stage retries, missing markers, duplicate markers, and predecessor coverage negative examples. run_requirement_template_contract_regression.py Requirements manifest/input guide templates' expressiveness for Tool, Checker, environment, documentation, templates, and requirement tracking New requirement categories add positive minimal mappings and single-field missing negative examples; do not treat a business name as a generic required item. run_review_ui_regression.py Console HTTP API, report filtering/approval/suggestions/deletion, design reading/editing, workflow tree, progress, history recovery/deletion, and path safety Frontend changes cannot only test DOM; read JSON/YAML/target files after API requests, covering revision conflicts and out-of-bounds paths 400. run_write_boundary_regression.py Parent Agent, evaluation, incremental, history permission guardianship, and tmp/ cleanup writable scope New tools' writable roots or cleanup rules must add positive examples and negative examples for .., absolute paths, symbolic links, and unrelated directories.

docs.title: Current Regression Makefile and Explicit Execution
docs.text:
The all target in regression/Makefile currently aggregates contracts, stability, checker descriptions, requirement templates, living plans, write boundaries, evaluation splits, review UI, documentation, and environment setup. During secondary development, do not assume scripts in the directory are executed by make regression; run_builder_runtime_directory_regression.py must confirm integration into the current Makefile. If not integrated, run explicitly:

PYTHONPATH="$(cd ../.. && pwd):${PYTHONPATH:-}" \
  python regression/run_builder_runtime_directory_regression.py

If a script is a mandatory delivery gate, correct modification is adding the target to regression/Makefile and including it in all, while updating this list; it should not rely solely on documentation telling users to manually run an extra command. For expensive, network/model-dependent, or hardware-specific tests, retain explicit targets and clearly annotate why they do not enter deterministic all.

docs.title: New Regression Code Pattern
docs.text:
Each script uses tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() or equivalent isolation, creates real artifacts via public core/UCTool, then reads back files to assert. The structure below is the minimal pattern; actual scripts should make specific assertions on error codes and persisted states:

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
    workspace = Path(temporary)
    create_valid_baseline(workspace)
    report = call_public_core(workspace)
    assert report.ok
    assert (workspace / "expected/file.yaml").is_file()

    break_exactly_one_rule(workspace)
    with pytest.raises(ExpectedContractError, match="STABLE-CODE"):
        call_public_core(workspace)

If the project does not use pytest, maintain the existing script's pure assert/main() style; do not introduce a new test framework for a single case. Subprocesses must pass argument arrays, cwd, timeout, text/capture_output, assert return codes, and retain limited stdout/stderr in failure messages. Threads, HTTP servers, or browser processes must be closed in finally, leaving no ports or profile locks.

docs.title: Secondary Development Acceptance Order
docs.text:
1. First run py_compile and YAML/JSON parsing for the modified module to exclude low-cost syntax failures.
  2. Run one to three closest responsibility regression scripts from the table above, confirming new negative examples fail old implementations and pass new ones.
  3. Run make regression; if known failures cause all to terminate early, record precise assertions and run subsequent targets separately.
  4. Generate a new, controlled-scale business workflow, using supervision strategy to observe failure counts, product timestamps, and context compression, without generating sub-products for the Agent.
  5. Run make check on the generated sub-workflow, then select corresponding evaluation and incremental loops to confirm parent modifications do not merely pass static regressions.

docs.title: Continue Reading
docs.text: After completing the parent workflow modification, developers also need to know "which components in the generated child workflows should be continued in development and how." Please continue reading the Workflow Product Secondary Development Guide.

docs.title: Secondary Development Guide for Generated Workflow Artifacts
docs.text:
This guide targets two types of developers: those who need to enhance a specific business sub-workflow after generation in Workflow Builder, and those who need to determine whether a change should be reflected back into the parent workflow in Workflow Builder. In this document, "Artifact Root" refers to the workflow/ directory under the business build workspace, and "Parent Root" refers to examples/workflow_builder/.

Generated workflows are deliverables that can be used, checked, and migrated independently; they are not immutable black boxes. However, when performing secondary development on them, you must maintain consistency across input/output contracts, Tool/Checker registration, GuideDoc guidance, Make targets, and evaluation/incremental capabilities. Modifying only a single Python file without updating its spec, tests, and documentation may make the manual run succeed this time, but subsequent incremental maintenance will become incomprehensible.

docs.title: Secondary Development Goals
docs.text:
The goal of artifact secondary development is to add or adjust capabilities for a specific business that has already been generated, while preserving runnability, checkability, evaluability, rollback capability, and migratability. Typical tasks include adding new business Tools, adding formats or algorithms to existing Tools, adding new stages or adjusting stage input/output, adding Checkers that can prove new requirements, expanding the business knowledge base, GuideDoc, or user documentation, and configuring external dependencies for the new system.

Tasks that do not belong to artifact secondary development include: modifying the UCAgent core to bypass a business config error; manually forging reports to make a Checker pass; directly overwriting structured eval/*.json files; scattering temporary scripts in wfgen/, the artifact root, or the source directory; and writing all business-specific edge cases back into the parent generator.

docs.title: Parent Workflow Modification Entry Points
docs.text:
If errors in the artifacts recur across multiple unrelated businesses, or if the root cause lies in the Workflow Builder's generic templates, schemas, path rules, generation state, evaluation control, or stage guidance, you should modify the Parent Root. The corresponding entry points are tools/workflow_builder/core.py, tools/workflow_tool_generator/core.py, tools/workflow_checker_generator/core.py, tools/workflow_config_generator/core.py, tools/workflow_guidedoc_generator/core.py, tools/workflow_evaluation_control/, and Guide_Doc/.

If changes belong only to a business's algorithms, fields, knowledge, style, website visual rules, audio processing strategies, or dedicated external tools, they should remain in the Artifact Root. To enable reuse of similar businesses in the future, prioritize expressing generic capabilities as templates/specs that the parent workflow spec can accept, only moving the implementation up to the parent template once the protocols and algorithms of multiple businesses are stable.

docs.title: Component Ownership and Data Ownership in Artifact Root
docs.text:
Different businesses can add directories, but standard artifacts typically include the following responsibility areas. Read the artifact README and docs/02​输入输出​.md before secondary development, as specific sub-workflows can further subdivide input/<TARGET>/ into requirements, source data, domain knowledge, and optional resources.

Artifact Component Ownership and Role Primary Coupling on Modification config.yaml Main execution stages, tasks, reference/output, Tool, Checker, and GuideDoc registration Stage order, file accessibility, parameter signatures, GuideDoc, Make run/check and flow evaluation. config/inc.yaml or equivalent incremental config Business content extension/update process, not the Workflow Builder's outer inc.yaml Business state, version, input contract, Checker, and user documentation. tools/ Business Tools, parameter models, shared runtime libraries, and MCP adapters Tool spec, config ex_tools, fixtures/tests, requirements, GuideDoc, and docs/04​开发者​文档​-tools.md. Checker source directory Business invariants, output integrity, and stage acceptance Checker spec, config checkers, args, fixtures/tests, GuideDoc, and docs/05​开发者​文档​-checkers.md. .workflow/ Generator spec, fixtures, generation state, and deterministic test support; belongs to maintainable metadata Sync central spec and state strategy when modifying real source code to avoid generator overwriting or skipping next run. Guide_Doc/ Sub-agent stage operation guidance, business constraints, and failure recovery Config guide_docs, real Tool/Checker signatures, input/output and business knowledge indexing. docs/ Documentation for human users and subsequent developers README directory, quick start, input/output, stage checks, and real source code analysis for Tools/Checkers. knowledge_base/ or business knowledge directory General business knowledge delivered by the workflow, readable by Agent via index Index, source/license, version, GuideDoc read strategy, and related Checkers; do not inject the full database into every stage. Makefile, setup.py, ucagent_setup.sh, requirements.txt Runtime entry, cross-system configuration, controlled environment updates, and dependency installation Environment schema, variable precedence, Make help/check/test/migration, non-Python installation notes, and eval_env. input/<TARGET>/ Data, requirements, and optional domain knowledge provided by business users for each run Input schema, quick start examples, missing file errors, and path boundaries; Tools must not overwrite user input. output/ Business run results and structured intermediate artifacts Output contract, atomic writes, hash/parsable verification, Checker, and cleanup strategy. tmp/ The only allowed root for storing debug info, browser profiles, download caches, candidate cases, and temporary outputs Cleanup at run start/end, concurrency lock fault tolerance, and version history to retain; do not clear profiles in use.

docs.title: Code Analysis of Builder Generation Boundaries
docs.text:
The parent workflow's tools/workflow_builder/core.py uses BuildReport to record materialized operations and restricts artifact targets via safe path functions. Secondary developers should not copy these internal parent classes into sub-workflows, but must understand why generation state distinguishes created/skipped/warnings:

@dataclass
class BuildReport:
    workflow_name: str = ""
    created_dirs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    created_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    skipped_files: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

An artifact already modified by the user is marked as skipped, typically indicating that the preserve strategy is protecting it, not that the generator failed. To make spec updates take effect, use the generator's supported replace or incremental candidate deployment, saving the old version first and running regression tests. Do not delete the entire .workflow/ to force generation, as this will also lose specs, fixtures, and drift evidence.

docs.title: Tool Artifact Extension Steps
docs.text:
Before modifying a tool, locate it in .workflow/tool_specs/ or the artifact's actual central spec directory. If a spec exists, it should be the single source of truth for name, description, inputs, outputs, errors, implementation, registration, and tests; modify the spec first, then update the real source code via the generator in the artifact or the Workflow Builder incremental process. If the artifact does not retain a replayable spec, explicitly mark the modified file as manually maintained in the modification record to prevent future generator overwrites.

Each Tool's stable return should allow subsequent stages to avoid parsing terminal text:

return {
    "ok": True,
    "data": {"artifact": "output/result.json", "records": record_count},
    "errors": [],
    "warnings": warnings,
    "meta": {"tool": self.__class__.__name__, "schema_version": 1},
}

When adding parameters, sync Args/Pydantic models, Tool signatures, spec input schemas, config registration, GuideDoc call examples, and positive/negative fixtures. When adding outputs, sync output schemas, subsequent references, Checkers, and documentation. When introducing third-party libraries, sync requirements.txt. When introducing non-Python tools like Verilator, FFmpeg, or LibreOffice, document Linux/macOS installation commands, version verification, and failure/degradation behavior in the requirements comments.

Tool writes must be restricted to explicit output/state/tmp roots, with paths normalized using resolve() and ownership checked before writing. When involving network resource acquisition, place domain whitelists, protocols, response sizes, MIME types, redirects, license records, and caches in the checkable contract; do not implement "searchable online" as an arbitrary URL downloader.

docs.title: Checker Artifact Extension Steps
docs.text:
New Checkers must answer a verifiable proposition, such as "the output JSON is parseable, all required records have stable IDs, and the total error count matches the summary," rather than just "checking the output." Class docstrings should describe the check object and pass conditions; method docstrings should describe calls and returns. Construct parameters should only accept workflow-relative paths and structured thresholds; config args must exactly match signatures.

Check methods are recommended to return (passed, evidence), where evidence includes error codes, target paths, failed fields/rules, and limited context. File not found, unparsable, structural errors, business semantic errors, and Checker self-exceptions should be distinguishable. Each rule must have at least one positive fixture and one negative fixture that breaks only that rule. Placeholder implementations using unconditional return True must not pass all tests.

After modifying a Checker, also verify the artifact timing of the stage it resides in. A file generated in subsequent stages cannot be used as a required input by the current Checker. Path comparisons must be completed after normalization; do not misjudge due to string differences between .//workflow/a and workflow/a. In reference/output, list specific files; directories can only be passed if the Checker explicitly supports directory traversal in its construction parameters, which does not change the stage file contract.

docs.title: config and Stage Extension Steps
docs.text:
Before adding a new stage, map out input files, output files, called tools, passed Checkers, guidance documents, and failure recovery. Descriptive content in tasks should be in Chinese; class names, fields, commands, and file paths must remain in their original form. New stages should not just be "run cognition again," "write another spec," or "check again"; if it does not produce new state, new artifacts, or independent acceptance evidence, merge it into an existing stage.

Perform closure audits on stage references: reference files must come from user input or be explicitly output by previous stages; outputs must be specific files, not directories representing unknown results; Tool and Checker registration classes must be importable with consistent args; GuideDoc files must exist and inject only necessary documentation; any {NAME} placeholders must have clear definitions, defaults, or startup parameter sources.

After modifying config, complete YAML parsing, unknown placeholder checks, reference accessibility, directory file contracts, Tool/Checker imports, and Make dry-run checks. Then execute the relevant stage with a minimal business input, rather than waiting to discover the first missing reference after running the full long process for dozens of minutes.

docs.title: GuideDoc, docs, and Knowledge Base Extension Steps
docs.text:
GuideDoc is for Agents executing sub-workflows and should specify the phase objectives, specific inputs and outputs, tool parameters, verification conditions, minimum passing structures, common complete examples, and failure recovery. User docs are for humans and should cover quick start, inputs and outputs, each phase, and the Checker. Developer docs should reference real business source code for every Tool and Checker, explaining parameters, core algorithms, writes, errors, registration, and testing.

The Knowledge Base stores general professional knowledge required by sub-workflows itself. Project-specific knowledge added by users each time should remain in inputs or agreed-upon resources directories. The Knowledge Base must have an index, annotating topics, scope, source, license, version, and related files. The Agent first queries the index, then reads direct entries according to the current task; do not read the entire knowledge base at the start of each stage, otherwise long workflows may repeat reading after compression and spin uselessly.

docs.title: Environment, Makefile, and setup Extension Steps
docs.text:
The generated workflow's setup.py should read its own environment schema, interactively define or update local values, then controlled update markers in the Makefile or ucagent_setup.sh. Default users should be able to run it, but secrets, tokens, and agent credentials should not fall into commit-able files. Make variable priority is typically command line highest, local configuration second, and ?= code default last; modify include order only after confirming with dry-run.

When adding external commands, synchronize environment schema, setup prompts and verification, requirements comments, Make variables/targets, Tool whitelist, Checker installation probe, QuickStart, and eval_env. External commands must be executed with parameter arrays, setting cwd, timeout, and output limits, never concatenating user input into a shell. When a business needs to generate multiple independent products in parallel, disjoint write sets can be executed in parallel; config, registration, shared state, and aggregated reports must be submitted serially.

docs.title: Compatibility of Evaluation and Incremental Delivery
docs.text:
After secondary development of sub-workflow outputs is complete, first run its own make check, make test_tools, and relevant business examples, then run corresponding eval_tools, eval_checkers, eval_flow, or eval_env from the outer Workflow Builder. Evaluation reports do not modify outputs; only after the user approves findings in the console or proposes suggestions does the outer inc.yaml modify, check, backup, and deploy in the current candidate directory. The atomic deployment entry for formal files is IncrementalChangeDeployer; ordinary file tools and evaluation Agents must not replace it in writing to workflow/.

If human secondary development bypasses the incremental deployer to directly modify outputs, subsequent incs can still work, but developers must treat the current file as a new baseline, check generator state and spec for drift, and provide their own Git or another version backup. Do not treat the outer tmp/change_history/ as a permanent version library; it is used for incremental deployment recovery, and users should still manage long-term business source code with Git.

docs.title: Complete Order of Secondary Development on One Product
docs.text:
1. Run existing make check in the product root and record the baseline, read README, input/output docs, target stage GuideDoc, and related Tool/Checker development docs, avoiding blind full-library scans without objectives.
  2. Clearly define requirement id, current behavior, expected behavior, inputs/outputs, invariants, affected components, minimal positive/negative examples, and acceptance commands.
  3. Decide if the change belongs only to the current product or exposes a generic defect in the parent template/generator; if both are needed, fix the parent mechanism first with regression, then use incremental flow to fix historical products.
  4. Fix the central spec/manifest first, then Tools, Checkers, config, GuideDoc, docs, and requirements. Temporary test data goes only to tmp/; formal fixtures go to test directories specified by the contract.
  5. Verify in order: syntax, unit/fixture, Tool direct/MCP, Checker positive/negative, config closure, documentation, and make check; fix the layer if it fails at any point, without re-running the same long command without state changes.
  6. Run corresponding evaluations and review reports; high-risk issues must have concrete evidence. When deploying via incremental flow, confirm each approval has change mapping, old version backup, new hash, and formal regression results.
  7. Update the product's version, change notes, and migration package; execute configuration and checks in the new temporary root, confirming no dependencies on developer machine absolute paths.

docs.title: Failure, Rollback, and Regression Strategies
docs.text:
Syntax failures, Tool direct call failures, Checker negative example false passes, unreachable config references, and formal make check failures cannot be replaced by "known issues" in docs or reports. For candidates not yet deployed, continue fixing the candidate; if deployed and within the same approval scope, save a new version of old files before continuing fixes; if exceeding the approval scope, rollback or report needing new approval. Do not stop at pending when a deployed regression fails and infinitely repeat the same command.

Product-level regression must include: full Python source compilation; YAML/JSON parseable and schema-valid; each Tool's normal, boundary, failure, path, and repeated runs; each Checker's import, args, positive examples, and single-error negative examples; stage reference closure; GuideDoc with real signatures; Make dry-run/check; setup first, repeated, invalid values, and command-line override; minimum run after migrating to new root. External dependencies that do not exist must be clearly marked skip/unavailable, not disguised as business success.

docs.title: Completion Definition
docs.text:
Secondary development on a generated workflow is considered complete only when all the following conditions are met simultaneously: user requirements have stable ids and tracking mappings; spec/source code/config/GuideDoc/docs are consistent; Tools are truly callable and passable via UCAgent; Checker positive/negative evidence is valid; make check returns 0 for formal products; old versions are recoverable; evaluations have no unresolved blocking issues; migration to new directories does not depend on original absolute paths.

If a modification fixes a generic parent mechanism defect, also add deterministic regression in the Workflow Builder parent root, update corresponding Guide_Doc/, and update this group's developer docs. Only then will the fix automatically take effect in the next unrelated business, rather than existing only in the current historical workspace.

docs.title: Continue Reading
docs.text: When needing to modify specific components in the parent workflow, locate the phase from Workflow Introduction, then read Tool Introduction, Checker Introduction, GuideDoc Introduction, Evaluation and Incremental Control, and Testing and Regression.

docs.title: Q&A and Experience Summary
docs.text: This directory compiles common issues encountered in Workflow Builder during real-world business construction, evaluation, and incremental execution. Entries prioritize verifiable methods and do not package one-off anomalies as universal rules. When troubleshooting, first locate the documentation closest to the phenomenon, then collect evidence following the "Verification Method."

docs.title: Categories
docs.text: Document Primary Issues Installation and Environment Issues UCAgent paths, virtual environments, agents, dependencies, and local configuration Runtime and Stage Failures TUI, history, Checker, references, continuous retries, and stage hangs Evaluation, Approval, and Incremental Updates Report omissions, approvals, candidates, idle loops, deployment, and closure Console and Ports Port conflicts, exits, filtering, editing, and version deletion Performance, Context, and Stability Long stages, continuous compression, streaming interruptions, and browser lock Workflow Design Quality Formalism, design plans, tools/Checkers/docs, and path contracts

docs.title: Troubleshooting Evidence Priority
docs.text:
1. Inputs, outputs, and return codes of deterministic commands.
  2. Complete Checker descriptions, parameters, and source code branches.
  3. Target file contents, hashes, timestamps, and structured reports.
  4. TUI tool invocations and model responses.
  5. Speculations regarding network, model, or business complexity.

When relying solely on fifth-category evidence, do not immediately modify large sets of rules. First, design small experiments capable of distinguishing different causes.

docs.title: Recording New Experiences
docs.text: New entries must include: phenomenon, impact, possible causes, verification method, handling steps, and preventive measures. Confirmed causes should be noted with evidence; items that have not been reproduced or are only relevant should be marked as "To Verify." Business-specific details belong in examples and should not be elevated to mandatory rules for all workflows.

docs.title: Standard Issue Recording Template
docs.text:
## Issue Title

**Phenomenon**: Directly observable outputs, counts, and timestamps.
**Impact**: Blockage, erroneous artifacts, performance, or maintenance impact.
**Status**: Confirmed / High Probability / To Verify.
**Possible Causes**: Ranked by evidence strength.
**Verification Method**: Commands, files, fields, and expected differences.
**Handling Steps**: Begin with minimal, reversible actions.
**Preventive Measures**: Rules to modify, tests, or documentation.

When recording return codes, preserve the command and cwd; when recording files, preserve relative paths, mtime, or hashes; when recording TUI, preserve the stage and failure count. Without this context, the same error message may represent different causes across different workspaces.

docs.title: Severity and Public Experience
docs.text: Address issues that prevent startup, infinite loops, destruction of formal files, or false completion first, followed by core requirement deviations and unavailability of key tools, then edge cases and experience. For a single business issue, write an implementation plan first; only after cross-business reproduction or proof of a universal defect in code should it enter the public FAQ, with deterministic regression tests added.

docs.title: Missing UCAgent or Python
docs.text:
Symptom: make reports that ucagent.py is missing, Python is not executable, or importing examples.workflow_builder fails.

Impact: Workflows cannot start; this is a blocking issue that must be resolved before execution.

Verification Method:

python setup.py --show
python setup.py --check
test -f "$UCAGENT_HOME/ucagent.py"
test -x "$UCAGENT_VENV/bin/python"

Resolution Steps: Re-run python setup.py in the root directory to configure the actual UCAgent source and virtual environment paths. Command-line overrides can be used temporarily for validation, but permanent values should be saved in local configuration. Do not write absolute paths from a specific machine into the public config or GuideDoc.

Prevention: After migrating machines, run make configure-check in the root directory before starting the business workspace.

docs.title: Relationship between ucagent_env and setup.py
docs.text:
ucagent_env is typically a function already present in the user's shell, used to activate PATH, PYTHON, and PYTHONPATH. The Workflow Builder root setup.py saves the native default paths required by the Makefile into .workflow_builder/local.mk. These two can coexist; setup.py does not write to ~/.bashrc, so it does not permanently inject environment variables into the parent shell.

Another setup.py located in the workflow root directory (workflow/setup.py) configures the business workflow execution environment. Before execution, it is necessary to distinguish between the two programs using pwd.

docs.title: Connection Failures After Proxy Enablement
docs.text:
Possible Causes: Incorrect proxy address, missing credentials, server disconnection, inherited incompatible ALL_PROXY, oversized model requests, or proxy instability.

Verification Method: Check the HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, and ALL_PROXY actually inherited by the current process; perform a short request using the same environment; compare results with and without the proxy. Do not assume the issue is unrelated to request size or the server simply because the network changed.

Local configuration rejects saving URLs with embedded credentials. When authentication is required, set it in the current shell or a secrets management system; do not write it to the version control system or document screenshots.

docs.title: Missing Ports or Tool Dependencies
docs.text: MCP and console ports must be between 1 and 65535. System tools like tmux, LibreOffice, and Verilator must be checked using their respective version commands. Missing business tools should be reported by the requirements.txt and environment documentation generated when creating the workflow, not by Workflow Builder attempting to install unknown system packages.

docs.title: Mixing Virtual Environment and System Python
docs.text:
Symptom: A regression can run via the root make regression, but direct python3 fails due to typing.NotRequired, langgraph, or missing packages.

Verification Method: Compare which python3, $UCAGENT_VENV/bin/python --version, and the sys.path of both. The root regression passes the venv Python, but manually entering the regression directory may revert to the system interpreter.

Resolution: Explicitly execute make -C regression PYTHON="$UCAGENT_VENV/bin/python" <target>. Do not modify business Checkers based on interpreter dependency errors.

docs.title: Local Configuration Not Taking Effect
docs.text: Use make configure-show to check saved values, then observe expansion with make -n WS=... run. Command-line variables take precedence over local configuration; if local files are manually corrupted, re-run python setup.py rather than directly editing Make syntax.

docs.title: Proxy Credentials and Business Dependencies
docs.text: setup rejects saving proxy URLs containing account and password. Secrets are injected via the runtime environment and must ensure tmux inheritance. Clear tokens and authentication URLs before sharing logs. "Command exists" only proves installation, not that the version and functionality meet requirements; business setup/check should also verify version and key capabilities.

docs.title: No Auto-Execution After Startup
docs.text:
Symptom: TUI opens but hangs waiting for input.

Verification: Check if the actual command originates from make run and whether RUN_LOOP_ARGS is empty. Supervision mode requires --loop --loop-msg; intervention mode intentionally omits these parameters.

Resolution: In supervision mode, re-use the default make WS=... run. Do not manually input loop in the same session and then start a second automatic Agent.

docs.title: Restored Old Phases
docs.text: UCAgent defaults to reading .ucagent history. This is correct behavior when resuming; history should only be cleared or disabled when a completely independent, fresh evaluation is required. Arbitrarily adding --no-history will lose the context of already completed phases.

docs.title: First Phase Fails Multiple Times
docs.text:
Common Causes: The implementation plan lacks mandatory sections, phase block markers are invalid, the level of detail is insufficient, the tool/Checker plan merely rewrites user text, or the Checker has hidden requirements for minimum formatting.

Verification: Read the full Checker message and the minimum passable example in Guide_Doc/stages/00...; compare generated file titles, markers, body length, and required items. Do not assume repetition is needed just because of "word count"; missing elements are often data flow, exceptions, tests, or extended analysis.

Prevention: The Phase FAQ explicitly states strict rules, and after the minimum example, it clarifies that the formal body must be more detailed.

docs.title: Cited Files Misjudged as Unread
docs.text: It previously occurred where configuration wrote .//workflow/... but actually read workflow/...; string tracking failed to normalize, leading to a misjudgment. The correct approach is to eliminate duplicate slashes when generating paths and normalize before comparison. Both reference_files and output_files should list specific files, not directories; do not cite files that are uncertainly present in the current environment.

docs.title: Phase Stuck for Long Duration
docs.text:
First observe if there are new tool invocations, file timestamps, Checker results, or context compression. If the Agent runs a full make check_docs for every batch of documents as each file is written, it should be changed to complete the batch of files first, then run a comprehensive check once. Independent tools can generate in parallel, but shared registration files must be serialized.

If the same failure check repeats and the state does not change, it is a spin, not "still working". Stop and locate the state machine or task description.

docs.title: TUI Suddenly Disappears
docs.text: Check if the tmux session still exists, the command return code, and the terminal's last output. It may be user interruption, Make recipe completion, remote exception recovery failure, or the startup command was originally CLI. Do not infer workflow failure solely because "the interface is not visible".

docs.title: Checker Reports Missing Description
docs.text: Check the configuration registration pointing to the actual class, the class-level description, and the Checker method docstring, then regress using the checker description. The configuration may register another class with the same name, so checking only the currently open file is insufficient. Fix the central spec or template, and increase regression tests; do not just add temporary comments to historical artifacts.

docs.title: Fails Many Times but Eventually Passes
docs.text: If errors gradually decrease, the Agent may be making valid repairs. If the same format is repeatedly guessed, the GuideDoc lacks a minimum example or error messages are insufficient. If the product is correct but misjudged by path string, it is a Checker issue. The number of failures itself cannot be directly attributed to body length.

docs.title: Long Phase Confirmation Commands
docs.text:
find <workspace>/wfgen <workspace>/workflow -type f -mmin -5 -exec ls -l {} +
tmux capture-pane -pt <session> -S -200

Continue observing if new files or different invocations appear; optimize batches if full re-reading or full checks are repeated. Check context and service links only when stuck at a model node with stream exceptions.

docs.title: Post-Fix Re-Run
docs.text: First run relevant deterministic regressions, stop old processes, then start with the same WS while preserving history. Clear history only if phase structure is incompatible with old history or the user explicitly requests it. Setting WS itself does not close TUI; if no interface is visible, check if CLI, pipes, or non-TTY were used.

docs.title: Evaluation, Approval, and Incremental Fixing Issues
Configuration Errors Not Detected During Evaluation
docs.text:
Phenomenon: For example, a phase uses a non-existent variable, references future files, or a Checker checks an error object, but the evaluation report contains no findings.

Root Cause Types: Evaluation guidelines list only a few surface-level rules; the evaluation Agent searches for keywords without performing phase data flow verification; the evidence budget is exhausted; or a specific component considers the issue belongs to another responsibility domain.

Remedy: Enhance general check dimensions rather than simply adding variable names. The evaluation process should establish mappings from variable definitions to usage, phase inputs to outputs, reference existence timelines, and Checker objects to artifacts, and perform refutation. Severity should be judged based on actual impact.

docs.title: How Users Approve and Propose Suggestions
docs.text: Users can use the console or execute eval-approve, eval-reject, eval-defer, and eval-suggest. Approval reasons should describe the allowed modification boundaries and acceptance objectives; users do not need to provide full patches. New suggestions are used when users proactively propose issues not found in the evaluation report.

docs.title: Incremental Phase Takes a Long Time to Read
docs.text: The goal of the cognitive phase is to understand the current workflow and the scope of approval for this round, not to read all tools, checkers, GuideDoc, docs, and reports in full. First, read indexes, directories, and summaries, then read directly relevant files according to the approval target. Tool outputs should also be limited to the required intervals to avoid compression followed by immediate quota exceedance.

docs.title: Incremental Process Does Not Complete All Approvals
docs.text: Check the approval snapshot of the current run and the "item to modification/evidence" mapping. Completion conditions must cover every id; passing make check after fixing only the first item does not represent that other suggestions are complete. Entries without modifications must also record why no modification is needed and the supporting evidence.

docs.title: make check Fails After Deployment but Process Waits
docs.text: This is a serious state machine issue. After formal files are replaced, the approval status no longer acts as a gate blocking repairs. The process must continue fixing and re-verifying, or rollback and fail out. Version backups are responsible for recovery; a second round of human approval for the same approved target is not required.

docs.title: Old Findings Remain After Fix
docs.text: Aggregated reports retain history. To conclude, one must re-run eval_tools, eval_checkers, eval_flow, or eval_env using the new run. Directly deleting old findings loses audit information and cannot prove the fix is effective.

docs.title: Fix Completed Abnormally Quickly
docs.text: Check applied_changes.json, formal file diffs, candidate evidence, and actual command return codes. The issue may only require minor changes, or the report may not have been deployed. Speed itself is not evidence of quality.

docs.title: Evaluation Agent Continues to Fail
docs.text: First, distinguish between a reported Checker failure and a target finding. Read the last tool invocation, JSON store errors, required check id, and report status. If the tool only accepts records but the Agent passes the entire document, the guideline example should be fixed; if evidence is missing, source code or commands should be added, not the Checker lowered directly.

docs.title: Finding Quality Assessment
docs.text: High-quality findings are reproducible, cite requirements, include source code or return codes, have justified severity, and have clear suggestion scopes. Low-quality findings merely state "there may be risks," set format preferences as critical, cite non-existent paths, or suggest rewriting the entire system. Merge duplicate items with the same root cause before approval.

docs.title: Candidate Plan and Build Plan
docs.text: wfgen/workflow_implementation_plan.md belongs to the initial build; the current candidate plan is located in tmp/inc_runs/<id>/. The console can display both simultaneously, but they cannot be mixed into a single system. Writing the candidate back to the build plan will pollute historical design.

docs.title: Read-Only Formal Files and Early Termination
