docs.text: The deployer deploys via temporary files in the same directory and os.replace. Standard read-only files can be handled, but if the directory is not writable or backup fails, it blocks. If the inc terminates early, compare the approval snapshot, candidate plan, incremental report, and applied changes to confirm that every approved id has a change or evidence of no modification; passing make check alone cannot prove all suggestions are complete.

docs.title: Address already in use
docs.text:
Symptom: When starting eval-ui, the error 127.0.0.1:8765 is already in use is displayed.

Cause: The same port is already being listened to by the console or another program. An HTTP service cannot bind to the same address and port multiple times.

Verification:

# Linux

ss -ltnp | grep ':8765'

# macOS

lsof -nP -iTCP:8765 -sTCP:LISTEN

If a correctly functioning workspace console already exists, open it directly. If parallel consoles are required, set EVAL_UI_PORT=8766. Do not allow the Makefile to automatically kill unknown processes.

docs.title: How to release the port after approval
docs.text: Return to the terminal where make ... eval-ui was started and press Ctrl+C. After the service exits, verify again using ss or lsof. If the terminal is lost, first confirm the process is indeed this project's console based on the PID, then send a normal termination signal.

docs.title: Missing Plan or Report
docs.text: The console uses the WS passed at startup as the root, reading wfgen/workflow_implementation_plan.md, three YAML manifests, eval/incremental_report.json, and eval/applied_changes.json. Do not search for these design files in the Workflow Builder source directory or within the generated workflow.

docs.title: Incorrectly Structured Design Page Layout
docs.text: Fixed-format YAML/JSON uses structural parsing; Markdown plans are parsed by phase markers and headings; files without fixed formats display full text. If parsing fails, display the error and raw text instead of rendering an empty page. Navigation belongs to the current document and should appear below the fixed basic information, with the main body scrolling independently.

docs.title: Version History Deletion Prompt Invariant
docs.text: Version history is by default immutable and cannot be silently modified by the Agent, but explicit deletion requests initiated by the user in the version management interface should be allowed. The backend must validate user actions, record IDs, and reference relationships, deleting indexes and any unreferenced backups. Changing only the frontend to hide errors does not alter the backend's immutability policy.

docs.title: How Structured Editing Takes Effect
docs.text: Page editing creates drafts for allowed fields; these are only sent upon clicking Save. The backend re-validates types, body length, references, computed fields, and concurrent versions before atomic write. Leaving the page without saving should prompt a warning; the original file cannot be arbitrarily rewritten via the generic text interface.

docs.title: Blank Page or Data from Wrong Workspace
docs.text: First, request /api/meta and verify the returned workspace against the startup command. Old browser tabs may still be connected to another port; the console name being the same does not imply the workspace is the same. Also check /api/state and the background HTTP status. Do not mask backend root path errors by modifying the frontend title.

docs.title: revision conflict
docs.text: After a user opens a design file, the background Agent may update the same file. When saving, if the revision/hash is inconsistent, the operation should be rejected and a reload with merge required. Directly overwriting will lose the Agent's new phase records. When confirming a conflict, save the current draft to a user-visible area, but do not bypass validation to write the original file.

docs.title: Filtering and Batch Operations
docs.text: Filtering only affects display and does not change state. Batch approval must use the ID explicitly selected by the user after applying the current filter; hidden records cannot be submitted together. Approve, defer, reject, and unapproved are mutually exclusive view dimensions; "approved" is a higher-level collection. Refresh after operation and verify each source ID.

docs.title: Background Process Management
docs.text: Pressing Ctrl+C in the startup terminal is the preferred way to exit. If the terminal is lost, use ss to find the PID, then verify the command line and workspace before sending TERM. Do not use broad pkill python. After the service exits, confirm the port is released and check for no lingering browser verification processes.

docs.title: Is a 20-40 minute single-stage run normal?
docs.text:
Business complexity affects tool, Checker, and documentation generation times, but duration alone cannot determine normality. Effective long-running tasks continuously generate diverse tool invocations, file changes, or progressively shrink the failing set; ineffective long-running tasks typically repeatedly read the same large files, perform full checks, compress consecutively, or restate conclusions without state changes.

Recording the stage start time, the last five tool invocations, the target file mtime, failure count, and compression timestamp is more reliable than observing the TUI display.

docs.title: Continuous Context Compression
docs.text:
Mechanism: Compression only summarizes existing history. If compression triggers a task to immediately read large amounts of reports, contracts, docs, and source code, the new context will quickly exceed limits again, and the Agent may continuously build understanding without modification.

Handling: Convert assessments and incremental tasks to index-first, responsibility queues, single target per run, and evidence-to-disk. The compression summary saves the current ID, read index, pending items, and the next action, avoiding redundant full-text insertion. GuideDoc provides a short execution version, while detailed contracts are read directionally based on the issue.

Prevention: Limit single tool output, use line ranges and structured queries; do not interpret "fully understanding the process" as reading every file verbatim.

docs.title: incomplete chunked read
docs.text:
This exception indicates that the HTTP stream was closed by the peer before the complete response ended. It may involve the model service, proxy, network link, timeout, or connection stability under large requests. It is not a Python file write error directly caused by a business file being locked.

If the exception consistently occurs after reading a specific file, the file may simply be the last tool result of the next model request, not proving that the read action itself crashed. Compare request context size, whether it consistently occurs at the model node, whether short requests succeed, and different proxy paths and service logs. Editing too much content at once increases generation time and response body, which is a risk factor, but the stack trace alone cannot confirm it as the sole cause.

docs.title: config.yaml and Makefile appearing locked
docs.text: UCAgent historical snapshots may alter permissions, or another process may be processing the same workspace. File locks/read-only and model stream interruptions operate at different layers. Check stat, processes, history permission daemons, and actual write errors. The Makefile is responsible for restoring history and writable workflow status; incremental deployments use atomic replacement and do not rely on in-place writing of the original file.

docs.title: Browser profile lock warning
docs.text: When the UI automatically exits verification, the browser deletes the lock in the profile, and concurrent thread cleanup may result in ENOENT. If only the lock in tmp disappears and the verification return code is normal, this is a cleanup race warning. The cleanup routine should ignore non-existent paths and delete the entire tmp/ui_validation/ directory after stopping UI verification.

docs.title: Performance Optimization Principles
docs.text:
• Generate independent files in batches, performing a comprehensive check on the final run.
  • Share specs and register files for serial writes; independent business tools can prepare in parallel.
  • After failure, only re-run affected checks, then perform a full check before stage completion.
  • Read summaries, indexes, and related source code without re-reading full text.
  • Stop repeating commands when state shows no change, entering repair or blocking branches.

docs.title: How to Distinguish Network, Request Size, and Business Errors
docs.text:
Model stream exception stacks typically stop at httpx/openai streaming; business errors usually return structured results from Tools or Checkers; local file permission errors appear as specific PermissionError or replace failures. Record the exception occurrence node, the size of the last tool result before the request, and behavior after automatic retry.

Stable short requests repeatedly experiencing stream interruption within the same stage while carrying large documents indicate that context or response scale are high-probability factors, but proxy and service limits must still be compared. Failure persists after switching networks, which can only partially rule out link issues and cannot prove a single root cause.

docs.title: Context Budget Practices
docs.text: Read only the manifest, directory, and target index in the first round; read direct source code and one layer of dependencies for each issue; limit tool results to line counts; write evidence to structured reports promptly; save completed IDs and next actions in the compression summary. Do not embed 300 lines of assessment contracts within each stage prompt.

docs.title: Batch Check Strategy
docs.text: When generating ten documents, complete this batch first, then run make check_docs once. After failure, only fix the failed files and run specific checks; perform a full check before stage completion. Tools and Checkers with independent source code can prepare in parallel, while shared configs/specs must be submitted serially. This reduces model rounds without sacrificing final evidence.

docs.title: Performance Recording Table
docs.text: Record at least: stage, start time, last change time, invocation count, failure count, compression count, target file count, and final return code. Compare these metrics across business scenarios to determine if new rules truly improve speed, rather than relying solely on subjective experience.

docs.title: Most Critical Deliverables
docs.text: The core of Workflow Builder consists of tools, Checkers, GuideDoc, config/inc, and user documentation. Manifest, schema, and implementation plans hold value only when they constrain these core deliverables, reduce ambiguity across stages, or support deterministic verification. Before adding a new spec, answer which real error it resolves and who reads and updates it.

docs.title: Why Implementation Plans Matter
docs.text:
workflow_implementation_plan.md serves as the carrier of dialogue between preceding and subsequent stages. The initial phase should expand user requirements into more concrete tool data flows, Checker judgments, documentation, dependencies, tests, and failure recovery. Subsequent phases' "Issues and Handling" record templates are incompatible, Checker false positives, reference ordering, and design adjustments are among the most valuable evidence for optimizing the parent workflow.

Plans should not merely repeat user text nor stack grand designs that cannot be executed. Each plan must map to the workflow build spec, actual files, and acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Avoid Formalism
docs.text:
Common formalisms include: adding a spec for every minor action; repeatedly performing cognitive verification; requiring full-document reading at every stage; creating numerous empty shell tools; satisfying length through repetitive text; and running a full check after generating every document.

A better approach is to maintain a small set of central sources of truth, provide indexes and minimal examples, perform comprehensive checks in batches, and allocate time to real source code analysis of business algorithms, Checker evidence, and development documentation.

docs.title: Tool and Checker Plan Quality
docs.text: Tool plans must at least specify input, output, core algorithm, exceptions, path boundaries, invocation stages, registration, and testing. Checker plans must at least specify the target, fields, pass/fail conditions, evidence, positive/negative fixtures, construction parameters, and false positive risks. Plan detail should exceed user requirements, not require users to pre-write implementations.

docs.title: Self-Review of config and inc
docs.text: Review before and after generating configuration: are variables defined; are reference/output specific files; do files exist in the corresponding stage; are paths normalized; are tool and Checker registration parameters consistent; do write/un_write boundaries contradict; can stages derive input from previous stage artifacts; and could task descriptions cause the Agent to retry infinitely.

docs.title: User Documentation Quality
docs.text: User documentation requires stable structure, complete commands, and real input/output. Developer documentation must also reference actual business source code. Simple statements like "This tool handles data" do not guide maintainers in modifying algorithms. Detail is conveyed through fields, code, control flow, failures, and extension points, not merely character count.

docs.title: How to Absorb New Business Experience
docs.text: After business execution, read all "Issues and Handling" in the implementation plan completely. Categorize issues as business-specific, GuideDoc missing, generator defects, Checker defects, and external instability. Only content reproducible across businesses enters the public FAQ or general rules. Verify with new, different businesses after modification to avoid overfitting to historical cases.

docs.title: Decision Table: Is a Spec Necessary?
docs.text: Before adding a new structure, answer: does it have an independent consumer; does it eliminate real ambiguity between two components; can it be deterministically verified; is update responsibility clear; and is it simpler than expanding an existing central spec. If you cannot answer, do not add a spec. Spec count is not a measure of engineering quality.

docs.title: Detailed but Not Overly Detailed Plans
docs.text: Detailed plans focus on data flow, business algorithms, errors, tests, and extension points. Meaningless detail repeats "read, confirm, confirm again" for every step or pre-specifies many unused states. Every plan must map to deliverable files and Checkers; otherwise, it is merely formalism.

docs.title: Key Code Analysis Standards
docs.text: Developer documentation must reference real files and symbols for each component, excerpt minimal critical fragments, and explain input, control flow, return, exceptions, path boundaries, and modification impact. Pasting full source code is not analysis; listing only paths is insufficient. Business workflow-generated docs/04 and docs/05 apply equally.

docs.title: Cross-Business Verification
docs.text: After fixing the parent workflow, verify with at least one new business of a different type. Observe first-stage failures, generation time, document quality, tool/Checker registration, and final make check. Verifying only in historical workspaces that caused problems is prone to overfitting existing files, history, and approval states.

docs.title: Quality Review Output
docs.text: Summarize effective issues, false positives, failure counts, time hotspots, human interventions, missing documentation, and reusable experiences after the process concludes. Each suggestion should state benefits and potential added complexity. Suggestions deferred by users should retain decision rationale and not be automatically reintroduced in the next round.
